Prophets and sibyls in Rome (罗马的先知与西比尔女先知)


Papal Rome, like Washington, Canberra, or Brasília, has been less a city than a bureaucracy issuing administrative documents and guidebooks [ 367 ]. The marketplace for artists born anywhere else, Renaissance Rome illustrated books so fitfully that several styles vacillate in two sets of Roman cuts of the prophets and sibyls who foretell the coming of Christ. The author, Barberiis, describes the style and colors of costumes that he might have seen on girls dressed as sibyls in some Christmas procession or miracle play. He was probably absent in Sicily when a relative in Rome published his manuscript, so ill penned that Gideon’s request to God in Iudici (Judges) was printed as from “Ione”-for which the illustrator (reading no Latin) copied the whale spewing up Jonah [66] from a northern blockbook Bible of the Poor. (This alone shows how far blockbooks traveled and were consulted.) 27 years later, when Michelangelo started to fresco the Sistine Chapel with five of the sibyls and seven of the prophets
罗马的先知与西比尔女先知教皇统治下的罗马，如同华盛顿、堪培拉或巴西利亚，与其说是座城市，不如说是个发布行政文件与指南手册的官僚机构[367]。这座文艺复兴时期的罗马虽零星地为各地艺术家提供创作市场，却仅零星地为艺术家们提供创作市场，以至于在两组描绘预言基督降临的先知与西比尔女先知的罗马版画中，竟出现了数种风格的摇摆不定。 作者巴尔贝里斯所描绘的服饰风格与色彩，或许源自他曾在圣诞游行或奇迹剧中见过的女巫装扮少女。 当罗马的亲属出版其手稿时，他可能远在西西里岛。手稿笔迹潦草，致使《士师记》中基甸向上帝的祈求被误印为"伊翁"——插图画家（不懂拉丁文）便照搬北方贫民版木刻圣经中鲸鱼吐出约拿的画面[66]。 （仅此便可窥见木版书传播之广及被查阅之频。）二十七年后，当米开朗基罗开始在西斯廷教堂壁画中描绘五位西比尔女先知与七位先知时——
Figure 24: Prophets and sibyls in Rome
图 24：罗马的先知与西比尔女先知
illustrated in Barberiis’ book, he put Jonah thrown up out of the whale’s jaws (instead of Gideon and the fleece) centrally over the altar. After 22 years this commanding symbol of the Resurrection suggested frescoing the wall below with the Resurrection of Christ, which developed into Michelangelo’s stupendous Last Judgment.
在巴贝里斯的著作中，他将约拿从鲸鱼口中被吐出的场景（而非基甸与羊毛）置于祭坛正上方。二十二年后，这个象征复活的威严符号启发了在下方墙壁绘制基督复活的湿壁画，最终发展成米开朗基罗那幅宏伟的《最后的审判》。
A second edition of Barberiis was printed by one of the many Germans who dominated printing in Rome before 1500. One of its cuts bears the mark of Riessinger of Strassburg, who shaded with short parallels as he had learned to do at home under Dutch influence. Some of the cuts are the earliest datable prints in the manner of Botticelli [ 67 ], who arrived from Florence to fresco the Vatican in 1481, just as Barberiis returned to the Vatican from a five-year absence. Barberiis’ second edition also contains the first prints based on antique statues [68], the start of a specialty that Romans continue to this day [69] with picture postcards.
巴贝里乌斯的第二版由 1500 年前在罗马印刷业占据主导地位的众多德国人之一印制。其中一幅版画带有斯特拉斯堡里辛格的印记，其阴影处理采用短平行线技法——这种技法是在荷兰影响下于本土习得的。 部分版画可确认为波提切利风格的最早可考印品[67]——这位艺术家 1481 年从佛罗伦萨来到梵蒂冈创作壁画时，恰逢巴贝里斯结束五年流放重返梵蒂冈。巴贝里斯第二版还收录了首批以古希腊雕像为蓝本的版画[68]，由此开创的特色领域，罗马人至今仍通过明信片延续着[69]。

Contrast of temperaments (气质对比)


Venetian publishers used so many illustrations that they bought secondhand woodblocks from as far away as Paris and copied any kind of print from anywhere. A year after the publication of a Swiss cut [70], Venice published a copy [71]. No two pictures more directly oppose the Teutonic and Italian temperaments. The Swiss cut, with its windblown banderoles and its big figures gesticulating over a jumble of gables, whirls in the storm of emotion that agitates Germanic art whenever it escapes from Italian balance, whether in the Middle Ages, the baroque, or 20th-century expressionism. The Venetian adapter, shading his cut more than usual to approximate the northern “color,” has tamed this tempest under the discipline of architecture by shrinking the figures to a more factual size against the buildings, drawing forms impersonally, dividing the picture proportionally, and laying the letters as straight as moldings. (In Italy, architecture and picture-making interpenetrated so much that a woodcut page [ 72 ] resembles a contemporary facade, while the façade [ 73 ] in turn is carved in perspective like a painting.) The northern woodcut has the virtue of a blazing tem-
气质的对比威尼斯出版商大量使用插图，甚至远至巴黎收购二手木刻版，并复制各地各类印刷品。瑞士版画出版一年后[70]，威尼斯便推出了复刻版[71]。 再没有两幅画作能如此鲜明地对立德意志与意大利的艺术气质。瑞士版画中，风卷的彩旗与巨型人物在错落的屋脊间挥舞姿态，恰似情感风暴的旋涡——每当德意志艺术挣脱意大利式的均衡，无论是中世纪、巴洛克时期还是二十世纪表现主义，总会掀起这般汹涌。 威尼斯改编者为贴近北方"色彩"而比往常更重地渲染了版画，却在建筑的规制下驯服了这场风暴：人物缩小至与建筑更相称的真实尺寸，造型以非人格化的方式勾勒，画面按比例分割，文字排列得如装饰线脚般笔直。 （在意大利，建筑与绘画相互渗透到如此程度，以致木刻版画[72]宛如当代建筑立面，而建筑立面[73]又如绘画般以透视法雕刻而成。）北方木刻则具有炽烈激情的优点——
perament, the southern of intellectual clarity. The difference explains why so many prints can be attributed to individual artists in Germany, so few in Italy.
永久性，即南方的思想明晰度。这种差异解释了为何德国能将众多版画归功于个体艺术家，而意大利却寥寥无几。
This diversity of style matches the diversity of backgrounds from which all kinds of men entered an occupation that expanded too unexpectedly for guilds to shut out adventurers. Before 1500 German printers had been booksellers, merchants of various kinds, physicians, an astronomer, a priest, and a monk. Germans seeking work in northern Italy made the densest concentration of presses anywhere in the 1470s. Less is known about the lives of Italian printers. There was a sculp-tor-printer in Florence, whose foundry experience must have helped him to cast type, and there were patrician printers everywhere, including a 15 -year-old count. In Italy, where princes had lived in the tumult of cities since Roman times, not in hilltop castles like the French and German aristocracy, many books were financed by and dedicated to prominent Italians.
这种风格的多样性，恰恰反映了从业者背景的多元性——各类人士涌入这个行业，其扩张之迅猛令行会无暇排斥外来者。1500 年前，德国印刷商中既有书商、各类商人、医师，也有天文学家、神父和修士。1470 年代，前往意大利北部谋生的德国人形成了当时全球最密集的印刷中心。而意大利本土印刷商的生平则鲜为人知。 佛罗伦萨曾有一位雕塑家兼印刷师，其铸造经验必然助益了活字铸造；各地亦不乏贵族出身的印刷商，其中包括一位年仅 15 岁的伯爵。在意大利——自罗马时代起诸侯便栖居于喧嚣都市而非如法德贵族般居于山巅城堡——众多书籍由显赫的意大利人资助并献给他们。
Since speakers of Italian slip into Latin more easily than speakers of German or even French, Italy produced more books in Latin than other countries, reducing its
由于意大利语使用者比德语甚至法语使用者更容易切换到拉丁语，意大利出版的拉丁语书籍数量超过其他国家，从而减少了其

incunabula in Italian to about one fifth of its total production. Italian illustrations, though choice, were few, since literary stylists have never respected pictures as much as casual readers do. (Even children observe less after they learn to read.) In Paris, the many Sorbonne graduates and associates imposed a monotony of type and woodcut. In all countries one profession, the scriveners, took naturally to printing and to designing type faces in the style of the local lettering that they had learned to write. This beginning diversity coalesced as printers sold fonts and matrices to each other at the international book fairs in Lyons, Frankfurt, and Leipzig, ultimately leaving only the few faces in universal use today.
意大利的初版印刷品约占其总产量的五分之一。意大利插图虽精美却寥寥无几，因为文学家们从未像普通读者那样重视图画（即便是儿童学会阅读后也较少留意）。在巴黎，众多索邦大学毕业生及其同侪使印刷体与木刻版式趋于单调。 在各国，抄写员这一职业群体自然投身印刷业，并以他们习得的本土字体风格设计字体。这种初期的多样性在里昂、法兰克福和莱比锡的国际书展上逐渐融合——印刷商们相互买卖字体与印版，最终仅留下今日通用的少数字体。

Ratdolt


In 1462 the sack of Mainz scattered young printers trained by Gutenberg and his partners. The refugees, who disseminated their revolutionary skill throughout Europe, included an Augsburg sculptor’s 15-year-old son, Erhard Ratdolt. The most inventive printer after Gutenberg himself, Ratdolt was to lead with the first sheet of type specimens, list of errata, decoration in white on black [ 74 ], printing in gold, probably the first metal casts of woodblocks, the first modern title page [ 211 ], and the first pictures printed in three colors. In Venice during his 305 he also printed the first geometry with diagrams.
拉特多尔特 1462 年美因茨遭劫掠，古腾堡及其合伙人培养的年轻印刷工四散奔逃。这些将革命性技艺传播至全欧的难民中，包括奥格斯堡一位雕刻师的十五岁儿子埃尔哈德·拉特多尔特。 作为古腾堡之后最具创造力的印刷师，拉特多尔特开创了多项印刷技术：首份活字样本、勘误表、黑白装饰[74]、金箔印刷、可能是最早的木版金属铸件、首个现代式标题页[211]以及首幅三色印刷图版。三十五岁时在威尼斯，他还印制了首部附有图解的几何学著作。
About 300 b.c. Euclid had written voluminously because he had to describe each step in words that scribes could copy but could not refer to diagrams that they would deform. From some manuscript in which a student had worked out his own diagrams, Ratdolt reproduced over 600 geometrical figures by bending metal strips and setting them in plaster or lead [ 74 ]. Once printing had standardized these diagrams for everybody, they eroded Euclid’s text to the telegraphic syllabus that plagued us all at school.
约公元前 300 年，欧几里得撰写了大量著作，因为他必须用文字描述每个步骤——抄写员只能照抄文字，却无法参照他们会变形的图示。 从某份学生亲绘图示的手稿出发，拉特多尔特通过弯折金属条并将其嵌入石膏或铅中，复原了 600 余幅几何图形[74]。印刷术使这些图示得以标准化传播后，欧几里得原著却被简化成电报式教学纲要——正是这种教学模式曾令我们所有人在校园里备受折磨。
In Venice, Ratdolt saw liturgical texts being printed in black and red through stencils. He took the next step when he illustrated the phases of the moon [ 75 ] by printing black, red, and yellow brown from three woodblocks. Even though this necessitated placing the paper exactly in the press three times, it saved labor over hand coloring for big editions. Imagine Günther Zainer’s toil in Augsburg if he had hand-painted his illustrations in 1472 when he printed 284 woodcut illustrations in five publications. A normal edition of 300 would have meant painting 85,200 woodcuts in eight months! After Ratdolt had mastered the registering of colors in Venice, the Bishop of Augsburg summoned him home to modernize German churchly printing. In Ratdolt’s ensuing book the first real color print imitates a painted Gothic woodcut by printing patches of red, olive, and yellow, and then surcharging them with a complete design in black line [76]. The book’s success established Augsburg as Germany’s center for color printing and expensive church books.
在威尼斯，拉特多尔特目睹了通过模板以黑红双色印刷礼仪文本的过程。他更进一步，运用三块木刻版分别印制黑色、红色和黄褐色，生动呈现了月相变化[75]。尽管这要求将纸张精准放置于印刷机中三次，但相较于手工上色，这种方式在印刷大批量书籍时显著节省了人力。 试想 1472 年奥格斯堡的冈特·扎伊纳若以手工绘制插图的辛苦——当时他在五部出版物中印制了 284 幅木刻插画。以常规 300 册的印量计算，八个月内需手绘 85,200 幅木刻！当拉特多尔特在威尼斯掌握色彩套印技术后，奥格斯堡主教便召他归国，以革新德国教会印刷业。 拉特多尔特后续出版的书籍中，首幅真正意义上的彩色印刷品通过叠印红、橄榄绿与黄色块，再以黑色线条覆盖完整图案，成功复刻了哥特式彩绘木刻效果[76]。该书的成功使奥格斯堡奠定了德国彩色印刷与高价宗教书籍中心的地位。

Shortly after 1500 Germans reproduced drawings made in black ink and white paint on colored paper. The white paint was imitated by grooving the woodblock to let lines of bare paper show through a printing of solid color. Such a tone block might also be printed independently [ 77 ], just as a black-line block might. About 1530, after Dürer had demonstrated the subtleties possible in black and white
约 1500 年后，德国人开始在彩色纸上复刻用墨水绘制、白漆描摹的画作。白漆效果通过在木版上刻出凹槽实现——当整块木版印出纯色时，凹槽处的裸露纸面便透出白色。这种色调版画也可独立印刷[77]，如同纯黑线条版画般独立成章。约 1530 年，在丢勒展现黑白技法可能达到的精妙境界后——

“color,” Germans stopped printing in colors. Yet the solid German tone block proved handy for glossing over damages in a black and white block to keep Dürer’s cracked woodcut [ 78 ] in print for some 200 years as the best available picture of a rhinoceros. (Dürer, by the way, did not see the actual beast, which drowned while being shipped from Portugal to the Vatican.)
“色彩”一词消失后，德国人便不再进行彩色印刷。然而，这种实心的德国色块却意外地派上了用场——它能巧妙掩盖黑白版块的损伤，使丢勒那幅开裂的木刻版画[78]得以持续印刷约两百年，成为当时最逼真的犀牛图像。（顺带一提，丢勒本人从未见过真正的犀牛，那头动物在从葡萄牙运往梵蒂冈途中溺水身亡了。）

Bookplates (藏书票)


When a man commissioned a manuscript, he had his arms blazoned on the opening page at the bottom of a decorative border. The earliest massproduced woodcut borders often included a blank shield for the purchaser to fill
藏书票当某人委托制作手稿时，会在开篇页的装饰边框底部镌刻其家徽。最早批量生产的木刻边框常预留空白盾形区，供订购者填入纹章。
with his arms [ 74 ]. Then, in the 1480s, the south German picture-printing indus- try invented a still more convenient way of marking ownership: pasting a bookplate into any book at will. The first such label to survive in quantity [ 79 ] marks some 40 incunabula that a monk gave to, or bought for, a south German monastery that he entered about 1494. The woodcut looks as though it had been made at Ulm
用他的臂章[74]。随后在 1480 年代，南德图像印刷业发明了一种更便捷的标记所有权的方式：随意将藏书票粘贴到任何书籍上。 现存最早的大量书签[79]标记着约 40 册古版印刷本，这些书籍由一位僧侣于 1494 年左右入修道院时捐赠或购入。该木刻版画的制作地疑似乌尔姆。

It is no bigger than most bookplates, but the contemporary cut of the arms of Henneberg (Hen Hill) [ 80 ], too large for any book smaller than a folio, probably marked saddles, shields, and trunks as family property. The Hennebergs used enough of these labels to make it worth while cutting stencils for the coloring. Such large armorial stickers were dramatically elaborated by Dürer and his contemporaries.

Almanacs for wall and pocket (挂历与袖珍日历)


We slaves of the clock jot engagements in calendars that regulate our minutes like school bells. Medieval man, reminded of vaguer calls by cockcrow and church chime, referred to almanacs to know the seasons for sowing and harvesting and being bled, the saints’ days, and above all the astrologers’ predictions. Beginning in the 1470s, wall almanacs as large as today’s bank calendars printed the saints’ days in red: red-letter days. Almanacs also appeared as small sheets folded in pocket-size envelopes and as booklets that must have been given as New Year presents the way we now give Christmas subscriptions to magazines. The almanac cuts often show the occupations of the months [ 83 ], familiar from reliefs on cathedral doors. For anxious reference, the cut of a naked man in almanacs and prayer books [ 84 ] showed which veins were safe to open under each zodiac sign. Under Louis XIV, over half a dozen yearly wall calen-
挂历与袖珍历我们这些时钟的奴隶，在日历上记录着像学校铃声般支配我们分秒的约会。中世纪的人们，在鸡鸣与教堂钟声的模糊召唤下，翻阅历书来了解播种、收割与放血的时节，圣徒的纪念日，以及最重要的——占星家的预言。 自 1470 年代起，墙历尺寸渐趋今日银行挂历之大，圣徒纪念日以红字标注：即红字日。年历亦以袖珍折页形式装入口袋信封，或制成册册相赠，恰似如今我们以圣诞杂志订阅礼相赠般，成为新年馈赠之物。 年历插图常展现月份象征的职业[83]，这些形象常见于大教堂门扉浮雕。为解忧虑，年历与祈祷书[84]中的裸体人插图标明了各星座下可安全放血的静脉。路易十四时期，每年发行逾半打的挂历——

Lacking such headline events (they were rarely lacking in so amorous a royal family), the calendar might celebrate the visit to Paris of Spanish musicians [85]. To show that they came from the first empire on which the sun never set, the quartet of girls in this touring group dressed their hair in the styles of the four parts of the world. In England in 1674 the Oxford University Press began to decorate calendars with college buildings in a series that continues to this day. Wall calendars, being bulky to store and too big for scrapbooks, were usually discarded after the year’s exposure had yellowed and flyspecked them. At the other extreme of size, 18th-century courtiers at Versailles pocketed almanacs too tiny to bulge a fitted coat, where they lurked at hand to verify the hours of opening of the king’s library and who was who at court and in the army. The fragility of their painted, gilded, and spangled bindings [ 86 ] had to be protected by slipcases.
达尔斯用去年皇家洗礼或婚礼的大幅版画服务于国王的专制统治。若无此类重大事件（在如此多情的王室家族中实属罕见），日历便会庆祝西班牙音乐家访问巴黎[85]。 为彰显其来自"日不落帝国"，巡演乐团中的四位少女将发髻梳成象征世界四方的造型。 1674 年，牛津大学出版社在英格兰开创以学院建筑装饰日历的传统，该系列延续至今。壁挂日历因体积臃肿不便收纳，尺寸又超出剪贴簿承载范围，通常在经年曝晒泛黄生虫后便遭弃置。 尺寸的另一极端，18 世纪凡尔赛宫廷贵族随身携带的年历小巧得不会撑起合身外套，随时可查阅国王图书馆开放时间及宫廷军中人物名录。这些绘有彩饰、镀金镶钻的精装本[86]极为脆弱，必须置于护封盒中保护。

Prints for pasting (用于粘贴的印刷品)


Prints not only transmitted images between painters and decorators, they often served as decorations in themselves or substituted for paintings. When monks in the Austrian monastery of Mondsee wrote little prayer books for home use, they illustrated them by pasting in tiny moon-round woodcuts, so roughly made by a great artist in his earliest years that they were often stuck in sideways [ 8 7 8 7 8_(7)8_{7} ]. Much larger prints, mostly Parisian, served as life insurance on the rough-and-tumble Gothic roads when they were pasted inside the lids of couriers’ dispatch boxes [ 88 ]. Outside, iron bands took the knocks while iron loops
用于粘贴的印刷品印刷品不仅在画家与装饰师之间传递图像，本身也常作为装饰品或替代绘画存在。奥地利蒙德塞修道院的僧侣们为家庭使用编写小祈祷书时，便用微型圆月木刻版画进行插图装饰——这些版画出自某位伟大艺术家早年粗糙之手，常被歪斜地粘贴上去[ 8 7 8 7 8_(7)8_{7} ]。 尺寸更大的版画（多产自巴黎）则被贴在信使箱盖内侧，在崎岖的哥特式道路上充当"生命保险"[ 88 ]。箱体外部由铁箍承受撞击，铁环则固定箱体。

colored to resemble the sweet, serious paintings with which Fra Filippo Lippi and Alesso Baldovinetti were then charming Florence. These inexpensive approximations of fashionable paintings must have sold well, for the coppers wore enough to need re-engraving twice. Much rarer is the sheet of engraved borders to be cut apart for framing the prints into a row [ 93 ].
这些铜版画的色彩模仿了弗拉·菲利波·利皮和阿莱索·巴尔多维内蒂当时风靡佛罗伦萨的甜美而庄重的画风。这些廉价的时尚画作复制品想必畅销甚广，因为铜版磨损严重，不得不重新刻制两次。更为罕见的是那张刻有边框的版画，可裁剪成条状装裱成一排印刷品[93]。
The French and Florentine series, made only about 40 years apart, demonstrate how totally styles differed before prints circulated along trade routes for everybody to copy. When printed pictures began to merge styles into the present homogenized world style, printed words began to impose and petrify dialects of capital cities uniformly within national boundaries, the way radio imposes pronunciation today. Before printing, the dialect of the Ile-de-France shaded imperceptibly eastward into Burgundian, which in turn merged into Rhineland German. The centralizing government of France consciously employed printing to impose Parisian French all the way to the Rhine, where Luther’s blend of German dialects took over. But printed pictures, deaf to language, have gradually made Europe and then the Americas, Australia, and Japan into one condominium of the eye.
法国与佛罗伦萨的版画系列相隔仅约四十年，却展现出风格迥异的图景——这发生在印刷品沿贸易路线传播、人人皆可模仿之前。当印刷图像开始融合风格形成当今同质化的世界风格时，印刷文字也开始在国界内统一强加并固化首都方言，正如今日广播统一发音规范。 印刷术出现前，法兰西岛方言向东与勃艮第方言无缝衔接，后者又与莱茵河德语相融。法国中央政府有意识地运用印刷术，将巴黎法语强行推行至莱茵河流域——该地区最终被路德融合的德语方言所取代。但印刷图像无视语言差异，逐渐将欧洲乃至美洲、澳大利亚和日本塑造成视觉的共同体。

Aesop The weakness or absence of a central government fragmented medieval Germany and Italy into self-governing, fiercely independent towns. So, although the first four illustrated Aesops appeared within a nine-year period, they differ from each other as much as modern illustrations from different decades and different continents. Despite the variations in treatment, Aesop illustrations descend from Eastern prototypes. (Greece and Rome pictured only the inhospitable meals of the fox and the stork.) In the 30 years before 1500 Aesop’s Fables were printed more often than the Bible. 123 Aesop editions survive out of many more that must be lost, whereas, in the 45 years before 1500 the Bible (which everybody saved) appeared in only 127 editions. The two first illustrated Aesops came out simultaneously in Germany and Italy. The German cuts [ 94 ], which also begin personal draftsmanship in typographic books, may have been drawn by Jörg Syrlin, who was then carving the cathedral choir stalls at Ulm with the same crinkling idiosyncracy. These 205 Aesop blocks passed in a few months from Ulm to Augsburg for three reprints there, and then were copied or adapted in some 20 German editions. Some of the Ulm woodcuts are related by a common manuscript ancestry to the metal cuts published at the same time at Mondovi in north Italy [ 95 ], where a
伊索寓言中央政府的薄弱或缺失使中世纪的德国和意大利分裂成众多自治的、极具独立性的城镇。因此，尽管首批四部插图版《伊索寓言》在九年间相继问世，它们之间的差异却如同不同年代、不同大陆的现代插画般迥异。尽管表现手法各异，伊索寓言插画仍源自东方原型。 （古希腊罗马时期仅绘制过狐狸与鹳鸟的恶劣餐宴场景。）在 1500 年前的三十年间，《伊索寓言》的印刷量甚至超过《圣经》。现存 123 种伊索版本，而更多版本已湮没无踪；反观 1500 年前的四十五年间，《圣经》（人人珍藏之书）仅出版 127 个版本。 首批插图版《伊索寓言》在德国与意大利同步问世。德文版木刻[94]开创了印刷书籍的个性化绘制风格，可能出自约尔格·西尔林之手——这位艺术家当时正在乌尔姆大教堂雕刻唱诗席，其作品同样带有独特的褶皱特质。 这 205 块伊索寓言木刻版在数月内从乌尔姆传至奥格斯堡，经三次重印后，又被德国约 20 种版本所仿制或改编。部分乌尔姆木刻版与同期在意大利北部蒙多维出版的金属版画[95]存在共同手稿渊源——当地工坊
surprising number of villages had presses, probably subsidized by local bigwigs wanting a fling at the novelty of printing. This rustic booklet with 65 smudgy little cuts is the earliest survivor of the innumerable Italian chapbooks designed to catch the masses with profuse illustrations. However, it did not start the Italian family of Aesop illustrations, which was founded three years later at Verona [ 96 ], where Pisanello’s tradition survived in the lithe and lively animals, so often copied throughout Italy. The splintery brilliance of these Veronese illustrations looks as though the illustrator had cut his own blocks in his own way. The cuts are bordered with the kind of type ornament that first became common on Victorian handbills and broadsides. The layout of these Veronese illustrations, but not their sparkle, was adapted six years later in metal cuts for a rich man’s hobby press at Naples [ 97 ]. Here the frames, arched like Neapolitan doorways and wall tombs, are filigreed with white-on-black scrollwork in the style of earlier books produced in Barcelona, which then ruled Naples. Since Dutch woodcut practice shows in the
令人惊讶的是，许多村庄都设有印刷作坊，这些作坊很可能由当地权贵资助，他们想借此尝试印刷这项新奇事物。这本粗糙的小册子内含 65 幅模糊的小插图，是意大利无数通俗读物中现存最早的实例——这类读物凭借大量插图吸引大众。 然而它并非意大利伊索寓言插图的开端——该流派三年前始于维罗纳[96]，皮萨内罗的传统在此得以延续：那些灵动生动的动物形象被全意大利广泛模仿。这些维罗纳插图的碎裂式光彩，仿佛出自独具匠心的刻版师之手。 版画边缘饰以维多利亚时期传单和海报上常见的字体装饰。 六年后，那不勒斯某富商的业余出版社[97]在金属雕版中沿用了这些维罗纳插图的版式布局（但未复刻其光彩）。此处的画框如那不勒斯门廊与壁墓般拱形，饰以黑白相间的卷草纹细密花边，承袭了当时统治那不勒斯的巴塞罗那早期书籍风格。而荷兰木刻技法则体现在

Woodcut in Aesop, fabellae, Verona (Alvise), 1479
伊索寓言木刻版画，维罗纳（阿尔维斯），1479 年
short, straight strokes and the floors bricked with hyphens, the “Germani fidelis- simi” who printed for Francesco del Tuppo may have been Dutchmen who traveled through Spain to Naples. This masterpiece of provincial eccentricity closed the first outburst of original Aesop illustrations.
笔触短促而笔直，地板铺满连字符，为弗朗切斯科·德尔·图波印刷的"Germani fidelis- simi"可能是途经西班牙前往那不勒斯的荷兰人。这部充满地方怪诞色彩的杰作，为早期原创伊索寓言插图的爆发式创作画上了句点。
After 1485 the old fabulist began to yield place to the beginnings of the modern novel and drama. Then, about 1670, Aesop suddenly jumped back into favor when La Fontaine taught his animals to speak French with inimitable point and grace. Nearly a century later Oudry’s illustrations [ 98 ], though a financial disaster for the publisher, promptly became a classic to be copied in countless French paintings, carvings, and tapestries. La Fontaine’s tradition has remained local because his effortless accuracy refuses to decant into any other language. Sir Roger L’Estrange, his contemporary, put Aesop into an English journalese rough and ready enough to remain readable to this day, in which it has inspired illustrations as witty as any in the past [ 99 ].
1485 年后，古老的寓言家逐渐让位于现代小说与戏剧的萌芽。约 1670 年，当拉封丹以无可比拟的机锋与优雅让动物们说起法语时，伊索寓言突然重获青睐。 近一个世纪后，奥德里绘制的插图[98]虽令出版商蒙受经济损失，却迅速成为经典范本，被无数法国绘画、雕刻与挂毯所效仿。 拉封丹的传统始终扎根本土，因其浑然天成的精准性拒绝被任何其他语言所稀释。其同时代的罗杰·勒斯特兰奇爵士将伊索寓言转化为粗粝而生动的英语期刊体，至今仍可读性十足，并由此催生出不逊于往昔的机智插画[99]。

Herbals and scientific illustration (草药与科学插图)


When patients knew almost as much medicine as their doctors, they searched the fields with pictures of healing plants in their hands. However, the copyists who redrew manuscripts inevitably degraded drawings of plants into unintelligibility, as old Pliny lamented in his Natural History, wherein he recommended describing plants instead of using inadequate pigments for pictures that copyists would smooth out of shape. For centuries after a Byzantine had copied a living plantain to illustrate a herbal, copyists copied copies, shirking the hard analysis of drawing from the idiosyncracies of nature. Their game of visual gossip evolved bunches as useless as wallpaper posies in a manuscript preserved near Rome. In the 1480s a Roman printer, as lazy as the scriveners, copied these abridged symmetries in 132 cuts for the first herbal printed with illustrations [100], which thus did not start a new trend but concluded an inheritance of apathy. The metal-cutter must have been the same bungler who had recently mangled the cuts of prophets and sibyls printed at the same press [ 66 ]. A man bitten by a scorpion or snake could identify the prescribed plantain from more accurate cuts in two herbals published a year apart by Gutenberg’s last surviving partner, Peter Schoeffer. Some of the woodcuts in his herbal of 1485 must have been copied from manuscript pictures [101], while others were evidently drawn from nature, probably by Erhard Reuwich on his return from the Holy Land [ 43 ]. These two versions of “Every Man His Own Doctor” were so much used that they were reprinted and pirated long after more accurate pictures of plants had appeared.
草药与科学插图当患者对医学的了解几乎与医生相当时，他们手持药用植物图谱在田野间寻觅。然而抄写员在重绘手稿时，总会将植物图稿蹂躏得面目全非——正如老普林尼在《自然史》中哀叹的那样。他建议用文字描述植物，而非使用劣质颜料绘制图稿，毕竟抄写员总会把图稿涂抹得变形难辨。 自拜占庭画家以鲜活的车前草为本绘制草药图谱后，数个世纪间抄写者仅复刻复刻，逃避了从自然奇特性中提炼绘画精髓的艰辛。这种视觉传言游戏最终演变为毫无价值的簇状图案——正如罗马附近保存的手稿中那些壁纸花束般的装饰。 1480 年代，一位罗马印刷商与抄写员同样懒惰，竟将这些简化对称图案直接复制到 132 幅版画中，用于首部带插图的印刷本草书[100]。此举非开创新风潮，实为惰性传承的终章。 负责金属雕刻的匠人，想必就是那位近期在同一印刷厂将先知与西比尔女神版画毁得面目全非的拙劣工匠[66]。若有人遭蝎蛇蛰伤，从古腾堡最后一位合伙人彼得·舍弗尔相隔一年出版的两部草药图鉴中，通过更精确的版画便能辨识出处方所载的车前草。 他 1485 年药草书中的部分木刻画显然抄袭了手稿插图[101]，另一些则明显取材于自然，很可能是埃尔哈德·罗伊维希从圣地归来后所绘[43]。这两版《人人皆可自医》广为流传，即便更精确的植物图谱问世后，它们仍被反复重印和盗版。
The botanists’ demand for exactitude cramped Western flower painting with literalness. In time the academic statements of external fact drove weavers and embroiderers to their drawing boards, where they hybridized lilies and daisies with feathers, shells, and fur. Chinese and Japanese designers, on the other hand, simplified and emphasized without distorting the flower’s individuality. An iris on a kimono is unmistakably an iris.
植物学家对精确性的追求，使西方花卉绘画陷入了刻板写实的桎梏。随着时间推移，对外部事实的学术性陈述驱使织工与刺绣师们伏案创作，他们在画板上将百合与雏菊与羽毛、贝壳和毛皮进行混搭。而中日韩设计师则通过简化与强调手法，在不扭曲花卉个性前提下进行创作。和服上的鸢尾花，依然是无可辩驳的鸢尾花。
Botany developed from practical quackery toward science in 1530 to 1550 when the first botanical gardens received plants from the New World, and botanists were exchanging enough pressed specimens to make the comparisons that led to the notion of genera. Botanical illustrations improved as publishers competed for an ever more crowded market by hiring better illustrators. The draftsman dominated the cataloguer for the first time in 1530 when a forceful Strassburg publisher yoked a learned physician, Otto Brunfels, with a brilliant and stubborn artist, Hans Weiditz. The uneasy partnership created the first modern-looking botany at about the same time that a similar northern team in Italy was beginning to create modern anatomy [ 394 ]. Weiditz, the artist, took the whip hand by drawing plants just as he found them in woods and fields-wilted, broken, chewed-for the physician to annotate, and the publisher to print at once in the order of receipt so as to forestall competitors. In these first known portraits of individual plants [ 102 ], Weiditz felt his way into the stems’ and leaves’ growing, as Leonardo had done a generation
1530 至 1550 年间，植物学从实用性伪科学向科学领域迈进：首批植物园接收了来自新大陆的植物，植物学家们交换了足够多的压制标本进行比对，由此催生了属的概念。随着出版商为争夺日益拥挤的市场而聘请更优秀的插图画家，植物图谱的绘制水平也日益精进。 1530 年，斯特拉斯堡一位强势出版商将博学医师奥托·布伦费尔斯与才华横溢却固执的画家汉斯·魏迪茨强行结为搭档，使绘图师首次凌驾于编目者之上。这段不安的协作关系催生了首部现代风格的植物学著作，几乎同时，意大利北部一支类似团队也开始创立现代解剖学[394]。 画家魏迪茨掌握主动权：他将林野间真实采集的植物——枯萎的、折断的、被啃食的——原样绘制，由医师标注解说，出版商则按接收顺序立即印刷，以抢占先机。在这些已知最早的单株植物肖像[102]中，魏迪茨如同前代的达·芬奇般，逐步摸索出茎叶生长的韵律。

before him. Though he never perceived beyond the particular specimen into the swing of the species with Leonardo’s mystery of exquisiteness (who has?), Weiditz harmonized exact likeness with rhythmic elegance in such a novel way that his publisher named him in the preface, thus rescuing him from the oblivion of ES and the Housebook Master. The publisher, however, suppressed the dissections of flowers and seed pods that fascinated Weiditz as much as they had Leonardo.
在他面前。尽管他从未像达·芬奇那样洞悉物种的韵律之美（谁能洞悉？），仅止于对个别标本的观察，但魏迪茨以如此新颖的方式将精确的相似性与韵律般的优雅融为一体，以致出版商在序言中点名提及他，从而使他免于沦为 ES 和《家庭手册大师》的无名之辈。 然而出版商却删去了花卉与荚果的解剖图——这些令韦迪茨着迷的画作，当年同样令达·芬奇痴迷不已。
Pressed plants were first illustrated when Fabio Colonna, a 25 -year-old Neapolitan botanist, etched them in what he called “a new way that I have devised.” Their impersonal exactitude suggests that a pantograph traced flattened specimens directly onto his copperplates [103]. A pantograph could also have enlarged the anatomical details, which he was the first botanist to publish, thus laying the basis for the modern classification by structure. These first copperplates of plants changed all botanical illustration from woodcut to the more detailed engraving on metal.
压制植物标本首次被绘制成图，是那不勒斯植物学家法比奥·科隆纳以他自称"新创技法"进行蚀刻所致。其冷静精准的笔触暗示，可能是通过描图仪将压平的标本直接转印至铜版上[103]。 拓印机还可能放大了解剖细节——他作为首位发表此类图谱的植物学家，由此奠定了现代结构分类学的基础。这些最早的植物铜版画彻底改变了植物插图的制作方式，从木刻版画转向更精细的金属蚀刻工艺。
German botanical woodcuts began the illustrated printing that enabled descriptive scientists of all sorts to publish their findings on numbered pages of comments written around exactly duplicated pictures. When two observers could discuss an image at a distance as clearly as though they were shoulder to shoulder, science emerged from Plinian fumbling into modern certainty.
德国植物学木刻版画开创了插图印刷术，使各类描述性科学家得以在精确复制的图版周围撰写编号页面的评注，发表研究成果。当两位观察者能隔空讨论图像，其清晰度犹如并肩而立时，科学便从普林尼式的摸索中脱胎，迈向现代的确定性。
The printing of words accelerated what scribes had long been doing adequately, though expensively, but Pfister’s 1461 innovation of printing typographic texts with pictures [ 27 ] provided man’s mind with a fresh and soon indispensable tool. Printed books stimulated the growth of universities, while actually making it unnecessary to gather information by sitting out most lectures. New ways of picturemaking changed the very basis of knowledge. The Greeks and Romans, as they perpetuated words through exact copying, came to think that stability resided in ideas, which writing preserves like blocks of knowledge. They scorned the instability of appearances, whose images shifted when repeated through the only replication then known. Today the emphasis is reversed. Now that photography explores works of art by ultraviolet light and X-rays, tracks particles of energy, and detects nebulae and viruses, images, not words, have become the building blocks of research.
印刷术加速了抄写员们长期以来虽耗资巨大却完成得相当称职的工作，但普菲斯特 1461 年创新性地将图文并茂的印刷品投入使用[27]，为人类思维提供了崭新且很快不可或缺的工具。印刷书籍不仅推动了大学的发展，更使人们无需再通过听课获取信息。 绘画技艺的革新颠覆了知识的根基。古希腊罗马人通过精确抄写延续文字，逐渐形成这样的认知：稳定性存在于思想之中，文字如同知识的石碑将其保存。他们鄙夷表象的易变性——当时唯一可知的复制方式会导致图像在转印时产生位移。 如今强调的重点已然逆转。当摄影技术能以紫外线和 X 光探索艺术作品，追踪能量粒子，探测星云与病毒时，图像而非文字已成为科研的基石。

Engineering illustrated (工程图解)


Romans built the Colosseum by heft and feel that workman transmitted to workman, because their practice could not have been published pictorially until the 15th century started to print words with pictures, nor codified precisely until the 17th began to calibrate instruments exactly and invent modern mathematics. Technical pictorial publication began with engineering, which attracted an inventor by associating him with important people. The first engineering woodcuts [ 104 ], like blueprints for condottieri, illustrate a catalogue of military hardware in a gathering of tracts on soldiering. The huge, antique wooden
罗马人建造斗兽场全凭体力与经验传承，技艺在工匠间口耳相传——因其实践无法以图示形式传播，直至 15 世纪印刷术诞生才得以图文并茂；更未被精确规范，直至 17 世纪仪器校准技术成熟与现代数学诞生。 技术图示出版始于工程学，它通过将发明家与重要人物关联来吸引人才。最早的工程木刻版画[104]如同雇佣军首领的蓝图，在军事手册汇编中展示着各类军械目录。巨大的古董木制

engines may have been transmitted through drawings in some now lost Byzantine manuscripts for woodcuts that Leonardo da Vinci studied. The Veronese printer was himself not very mechanical, for he made his woodblocks so much wider than his lines of type that both would not fit into the same form for printing together, thus forcing him to stamp his blocks by hand.
这些印刷技术可能通过达芬奇研究过的拜占庭木刻版画手稿（现已失传）中的图稿得以传承。维罗纳的印刷商本人并不精通机械，他制作的木刻版比印刷字体宽得多，导致两者无法同时放入同一印刷版中，迫使他不得不手工敲印木版。
The first survey of industrial engineering treated mining, a problem ever since prehistoric times. The author practiced as a physician among Saxon and Bohemian miners, whose occupational diseases got him interested in mining itself. Some 275 woodcuts illustrated the machinery of mining as clearly as its discomforts and dangers [ 105 ].
首部工业工程学调查报告探讨了采矿业——这一自史前时代便存在的问题。作者曾以医师身份服务于撒克逊与波希米亚矿工群体，其职业病问题使他开始关注采矿业本身。书中约 275 幅木刻版画清晰展现了采矿机械的运作，同时也揭示了该行业的艰辛与危险[105]。
Even before man began to mine, he was proud that his pigmy muscle could as-
早在人类开始采矿之前，他就为自己那微不足道的肌肉力量能够——
semble pyramids in Egypt and Mexico and lever gigantic stones together in Britain and Japan. Similar shows of strength celebrated the resurgence of the papacy in the later 1500s. Popes, being old men in a hurry, raided antique ruins for quick effects to create baroque Rome. In 1586, when the city’s biggest unbroken obelisk ( 326 tons) was moved from the side of Saint Peter’s to the front, the feat was proclaimed by publishing the first exhaustive book on one single engineering problem [106]. The text avoids speculating on how wind and men’s muscles, a millennium or two before, had split 75 feet of granite from the bedrock, sailed it down the Nile, across the Mediterranean, up the Tiber, and into the city. Thousands of slavish arms may then have wasted effort with antique rollers, levers, and wedges, but they accomplished more than the Renaissance engineer did by adding horsepower, capstans, and block and tackle.
在埃及和墨西哥建造金字塔，在英国和日本合力搬运巨石。16 世纪后期，教廷复兴之际也上演了类似的壮举。教皇们虽年事已高却心急如焚，为速成巴洛克式罗马，大肆掠夺古迹遗址。 1586 年，当这座城市最大的完整方尖碑（重达 326 吨）从圣彼得大教堂侧翼移至正门时，这项壮举通过出版首部针对单一工程难题的详尽著作而广为传颂[106]。 该文献刻意回避了千百年前如何仅凭风力与人力，将 75 英尺的花岗岩从岩床劈离，经尼罗河漂流，横渡地中海，逆台伯河而上运抵罗马的谜题。 当时或许有成千上万奴隶徒劳地使用古旧滚轮、杠杆和楔子，但他们所完成的成就，远超文艺复兴时期工程师借助马力、绞盘和滑轮组所能达到的高度。
His machinery went as far as invention could go before coal and steam forced the great breakthrough. This produced one of its first triumphs in Isambard Kingdom Brunel’s iron steamship, the Great Eastern [ 107 ], so huge-nearly 700 feet long, displacing nearly 19,000 tons-that she would loom large even beside yesterday’s biggest liners. This wood engraving appeared on one of the first illustrated broadsides distributed to industrial investors-for whom she lost more money than any ship ever. However, the Great Eastern laid the first Atlantic telegraph cable, and demonstrated that the steamship’s quick, cheap, and punctual transport was
他的机械装置在煤炭与蒸汽引发重大突破之前，已将发明推向了极限。这项技术在伊斯梅巴德·金德姆·布鲁内尔的铁制蒸汽船"大东方号"[107]上初尝胜利果实——这艘巨轮长近 700 英尺，排水量达 19000 吨，即便与当今最大的邮轮相比仍显庞大。 这幅木刻版画曾刊载于早期面向工业投资者的宣传画册——而这艘船给他们造成的损失，远超历史上任何船舶。然而"大东方号"铺设了首条大西洋海底电报电缆，并证明了蒸汽船具备快速、廉价且准时的运输能力。
Engineering illustrated  工程图解

图 36：108 布鲁克林大桥落成典礼，1883 年。A·梅杰根据纽约柯里尔与艾夫斯公司作品制作的彩色石版画
to bridge the oceans for man’s global migrations. Steel, the other prerequisite for modern life, first displayed all its strength by suspending a long, busy highway from wires in the Brooklyn Bridge [ 108 ]. The bridge’s esthetic lesson-that undisguised steel structure can be handsome-has still to be learned in all its consequences.
为人类的全球迁徙架起跨越海洋的桥梁。钢铁——现代生活的另一项必需品——首次在布鲁克林大桥[108]上展现其全部力量：它将一条繁忙的长长公路悬挂在钢索之上。这座桥的美学启示——裸露的钢结构也能优雅动人——其深远意义至今尚未被完全领悟。
Since modern technology advances through theory and experiment, any remotely helpful discovery is immediately published. This did not happen while technology relied on craft lore. Thus, before the age of Galileo, Descartes, and Newton, printers tended to leave scientific innovations in manuscript. Commercially, they were right, for in 1543, when Johann Kepler proved that the planets circle around the sun, and not around the earth, his founding treatise of modern astronomy sold so slowly that it did not need reprinting for 23 years.
由于现代科技通过理论与实验不断进步，任何稍有价值的发现都会立即公之于众。而在科技依赖手工艺秘传的时代，情况则截然不同。因此在伽利略、笛卡尔和牛顿之前的年代，印刷商往往将科学创新保留在手稿中。 从商业角度看，他们的做法是正确的。1543 年，约翰·开普勒证明行星围绕太阳而非地球运行时，其奠定现代天文学基础的论著销量惨淡，整整 23 年都无需再版。

The beginnings of engraving (雕刻的起源)


Cavemen scratched reindeer bones with designs that one today might fill with ink and print on paper. The oldest long series of printable incised (intaglio) designs on metal began in the 6th century b.c. when
雕刻的起源远古人曾在驯鹿骨上刻画图案，这些图案如今可填入墨水印在纸上。最早的金属凹版（凹雕）可印刷图案系列始于公元前 6 世纪，当时——
the Etruscans grooved bronze boxes and mirror backs with lines as limber as any drawn with a ballpoint pen [ 109 ]. They sank these grooves by hammering narrow chisels vertically or plowed rougher furrows by tapping a nail point at a driving slant. They sometimes also filed punches to shaped points for dotting backgrounds. When medieval metalsmiths began to use more copper than bronze, they decorated the softer metal by pushing a graver with the mere strength of one hand against the metal held with the other, the way engravers do today [110]. Unlike the freerunning hammered Etruscan lines, these engraved lines swing formally as the graver sweeps curves. Such geometric engraving decorates the chandelier that Emperor Frederick Barbarossa ordered for Aix-la-Chapelle when he exhumed Charlemagne’s body there in 1165. 700 years later, when the chandelier was dismounted for cleaning, the gilded copperplates were found untarnished enough to print excellently [ 111 ].
伊特鲁里亚人用笔尖般灵活的线条在青铜盒和镜背上刻出凹槽[109]。他们或用窄凿垂直敲击压出细纹，或以钉尖斜向敲击刨出粗犷的沟壑。有时还会将冲头磨成特定形状，用于点刻背景纹饰。 当中世纪金属匠开始更多使用铜而非青铜时，他们采用单手持刻刀、另一只手按压金属的技法装饰这种较软的金属——这与现代雕刻师的手法如出一辙[110]。不同于伊特鲁里亚人锤击形成的自由流畅线条，这些刻痕在刻刀划过曲线时呈现出规整的弧度。 1165 年，腓特烈一世（红胡子皇帝）在亚琛迁移查理曼大帝遗体时，曾下令为该城打造一盏饰有几何雕刻的枝形吊灯。七百年后，当这盏吊灯被拆卸清洁时，人们发现镀金铜板竟未受氧化侵蚀，其表面光洁度足以实现精美印刷[111]。
109
Odysseus Threatens Circe, Who has Turned His Companions into Swine. Chased bronze mirror back, Etruscan, 375-325 B.C.

To make such prints requires paper (which began to be plentiful in Europe only around 1400), and a thick, oily, densely black pigment. Oily printer’s ink suddenly appeared a couple of decades after the Van Eycks had perfected oil painting, and a short distance southwest of them, when an unknown somebody started to rub this newfangled pigment into grooves engraved in copper, wiped the unwanted ink off the smooth unworked metal, and transferred the inked lines to paper by pressing
制作这类版画需要纸张（欧洲直到 1400 年左右才开始大量生产）以及一种浓稠、油性、深黑的颜料。 就在范艾克兄弟完善油画技法后二十余年，油性印刷油墨突然问世。在他们工作室西南不远处，某位无名匠人开始将这种新式颜料揉入铜版凹槽，擦去光滑金属表面多余的油墨，再通过压印将带墨的线条转移到纸张上。

113

The Magdalene. Niello engraving on silver by Baccio Baldini, on a processional cross, Florence, 1464/65
《抹大拉的马利亚》。巴乔·巴尔迪尼银质黑镌工艺，游行十字架，佛罗伦萨，1464/65 年
metal and paper hard together. Just then, in the 14305 or 40s, Johann Gutenberg needed this same thick black ink for his experiments with printing from cast lead type. Could Gutenberg, the professional inventor, have boiled down something like the new oil paint into printer’s ink for his relief printing, and then passed it on to the engravers? In the time and the region of Gutenberg’s experiments, an engraver marked the earliest surviving date-1446-on any intaglio print [112]. The faceted distinctness of the detail in most of these earliest engravings shows the training of a silversmith, not a painter. Some early engravings represent the chalices, patens [119], and censers that the silversmiths made for their steadiest patron, the Church. Florentine and Bolognese silversmiths sheathed crosses [113] and boxes in little silver plates decorated in black with the very ancient technique of niello: melting a black compound of sulfur into engraved grooves. Before filling the grooves, they often recorded their engraving by casting it in pure sulfur (like pressing a seal into sealing wax), then rubbing ink on the raised sulfur ridges to make them show. After about 1450 the Italians engraved niello plates with letters in reverse especially for printing with the new northern oil ink. Pollaiuolo, whose Florentine shop made nielli, grandly expanded the niello contrasts in his Battle of the Naked Men [ 184 ].
金属与纸张紧密结合。就在那时，约翰·古登堡在 1430 年代或 40 年代进行铸铅活字印刷实验时，同样需要这种浓稠的黑色油墨。身为专业发明家的古登堡，是否曾将类似新型油画颜料的物质熬制成凸版印刷用的油墨，继而传授给雕刻师们？ 在古腾堡实验的时代与地域，一位雕刻师在凹版印刷品上标注了现存最早的日期——1446 年[112]。 这些早期雕版作品中多数细节呈现的棱角分明特征，彰显出银匠而非画家的训练痕迹。部分早期雕版描绘了银匠为其最稳定的赞助者——教会——制作的圣杯、圣盘[119]与香炉。 佛罗伦萨与博洛尼亚的银匠们采用古老的镌刻工艺——将硫磺熔合黑釉填入雕刻凹槽——为十字架[113]与匣盒镶嵌银质饰板。填充凹槽前，他们常先用纯硫磺铸造浮雕图案（如同在封蜡上按压印章），再将墨汁涂抹于凸起的硫磺棱线上使其显影。 约 1450 年后，意大利工匠开始为配合北方新兴油墨印刷技术，在镂刻镌刻板上反向雕刻字母。波拉伊奥洛的佛罗伦萨作坊专产镌刻工艺品，他在《裸体男子之战》[184]中将镌刻工艺的明暗对比效果推向了极致。
Engravings cost more than woodcuts because the graver takes longer to master than the woodcutter’s knife, copper costs more than wood, and plate printing requires more equipment, time, and skill of hand. In 1520 Dürer’s price per sheet for his engraved Passion was four and a half times that for his little woodcut Passion. Early engravings, therefore, were generally made in towns for the well-to-do, while woodcuts were peddled to poorer folk. Since early engravings were usually smaller than woodcuts, thrifty people saved more of them by pasting them into books. The typical engraving of the later 1400 s has survived in two or three impressions, the typical single-sheet woodcut in one.
铜版画比木刻画昂贵，因为刻刀的掌握比木刻刀耗时更长，铜材成本高于木材，且铜版印刷需要更多设备、时间和手工技艺。1520 年，丢勒的铜版《受难图》每幅售价是其小型木刻《受难图》的四倍半。 因此早期铜版画多在城镇面向富裕阶层制作，而木刻则面向贫民兜售。由于早期铜版画尺寸通常小于木刻，节俭之人常将其粘贴于书册中保存。15 世纪后期典型的铜版画现存多为两三版复本，而单幅木刻则多仅存一版。

Dotted prints (点状印花)


Dotted prints were printed from relief blocks of pewter or copper. Gravers scooped into the soft metal to make lines of white, drills made round white dots, and punches of various shapes were hammered in to print white repeated ornaments, using a technique as old as the Etruscans [ 109 ]. Metal relief prints differ from woodcuts in that the punched dots are never oval like the wormholes in wood [ 217 , right border ], and the metal lines curve more smoothly than lines in wood and do not end in splinters. Mishandling knocks a metal edge inward [ 249, right border ], but chips out a wooden edge altogether [50] and often splits along the grain in a white slash [ 78 , lower left].
点状版画采用锡或铜质凸版印刷。雕刻师在柔软金属上凿出白色线条，钻头打出圆形白点，再以各种形状的冲头锤印出重复的白色装饰纹样——这项技艺可追溯至伊特鲁里亚时期[109]。 金属凸版印刷与木刻的区别在于：冲压的圆点绝不会呈现木料蛀洞般的椭圆形[217，右边框]，金属线条的曲线比木质线条更流畅，且不会产生木刺。 不当操作会使金属边缘向内凹陷[249，右边框]，而木质边缘则会完全碎裂[50]，并常沿木纹裂开形成白色裂痕[78，左下角]。
Metal reliefs were rare in Italy [100, 397 ] but appeared in the Netherlands and Germany from about 1470 to 90 . Cologne advertised its specialty in them by
金属浮雕在意大利较为罕见[100, 397]，但在荷兰和德国约 1470 至 1490 年间出现。科隆通过宣传其金属浮雕工艺的专长来推广该技艺。

marking some with the city’s arms of the three crowns of the Magi. The painterly Flemings worked the white into the black for a richer darkness and more dramatic design [114]. Copper relief plates, nailed to woodblocks to make them the same height as the type, illustrated Parisian prayer books [249] from before 1480 to 1540. Then the graver was practically abandoned for relief blocks until around 1700, when Englishmen began to use it on type metal for cheap illustrations. At the same time, Englishmen and Frenchmen were clumsily trying the plank-cutting knife on the end grain of boxwood or pear. About 1780 Thomas Bewick in Newcastle combined methods by turning the metal graver to the end grain of boxwood for a white-line style [636] as richly dark as the old dotted prints. His modification had consequences that he could never have imagined.
在某些印版上刻有该城的三王徽章。擅长绘画的佛兰德工匠将白色融入黑色，营造出更浓郁的暗色调与更富戏剧性的设计[114]。 铜质凸版被钉在木板上，使其与活字高度一致，用于印刷 1480 年前至 1540 年间的巴黎祈祷书[249]。此后雕刻刀几乎被凸版取代，直至 1700 年前后，英国人开始将其用于活字金属板制作廉价插图。 与此同时，英法工匠正笨拙地尝试用板材切割刀处理黄杨木或梨木的端面纹理。约 1780 年，纽卡斯尔的托马斯·比威克创新性地将金属刻刀转向黄杨木端面，开创出白线风格[636]——其深邃暗调堪比古老的点刻版画。这项改良带来的深远影响，远超他当时的想象。

The Master of the Playing Cards (扑克牌之主)


The first engraver to abandon the silversmith’s primitive niggling was the painterly Master of the Playing Cards, whose simple parallels model a sidelight sliding around untroubled bulk [115], as light was later to do in paintings by the Swiss Conrad Witz. The master is named
扑克牌大师首位摒弃银匠粗犷刻画技法的雕刻师，是绘画风格的扑克牌大师。其简洁的平行线条勾勒出侧光在沉稳体量间流转的轨迹[115]——这种光影处理手法后来亦见于瑞士画家康拉德·维茨的作品。这位大师被称为

Some of these pips were also painted in the margins of manuscripts written at Mainz from 1452 to 82 and in the 42-line Bible that Gutenberg printed there between 1452 and 55 [117]. The marginal drawings and the engraved cards were both most likely copied from some lost craftsman’s model book of designs in which a bear climbed a tree, as he would have room to do in the tall format of a page, but not where a crowded playing card forced his paws to semaphore inanely.
约六十张雕刻卡片分为五组花卉、飞禽、鹿类、猛兽[116]及野人图案。其中部分点数图案亦见于 1452 至 1482 年间美因茨手稿的页边装饰，以及古腾堡 1452 至 1455 年间在当地印刷的 42 行圣经[117]。 无论是边饰绘画还是雕刻纸牌，其原型极可能源自某本已失传的工匠设计图册——其中熊攀树的姿态得以在竖版纸页中舒展，而拥挤的纸牌设计则迫使熊掌做出笨拙的手势。
The jumble of the model-book page probably carries over into the disorderly congestion of the playing cards [116], slowing the player’s recognition of the card’s value. For some of these cards, each pip was engraved on a separate scrap of copper, then ganged on a woodblock or copperplate. A painter turned engraver might have economized his graver work so cumbersomely, but hardly a profes-
模特画册页面的杂乱无章，或许延续到了扑克牌的混乱拥挤中[116]，延缓了玩家对牌面点数的识别。某些扑克牌的点数图案，每枚点数都单独刻在铜片上，再组合到木版或铜版上。画家转行当刻工时，或许会如此笨拙地节省刻刀工序，但专业刻工绝不会——
sional metal craftsman. Or was the Master of the Playing Cards close enough to Gutenberg to try composing little coppers into pictures the way Gutenberg was composing slugs of lead type into words?
职业金属工匠。抑或纸牌大师与古登堡关系密切，得以效仿古登堡将铅字排版成文字的方式，将小铜片拼成图案？

Master ES


Early woodcutters, who reproduced other men’s designs, showed local but not personal styles. In contrast, some early northern engravers invented their own designs and signed their quite individual work. The earliest engraver’s signature is an e, E, or ES on 18 engravings. 16 are dated 1461, 66, or 67. Since the ten plates dated 1467 are the most elaborate, ES probably died then. On the basis of these 18 initialed engravings, some 300 more have been attributed to ES. Since 50 of these have survived in two impressions, and 95 in only one, ES must have engraved quantities more that have disappeared altogether. To engrave so many plates-say 500-ES needed assistants, and indeed, two hands show in an ornamental leaf intended as a model for craftsmen [ 118 ]; EŚ short, light strokes clothe the wild man with down, while the leaf curves with the long sweeps of Martin Schongauer’s manner. Though Schongauer might not sign work while still an apprentice, he must have made many unsigned plates before maturing the style that appeared fully formed in all the engravings that he signed MS, in imitation of ES.
早期木刻工匠们复制他人设计，展现出地域特色却缺乏个人风格。相较之下，北方早期雕刻师则开创了独特设计，并在极具个人特色的作品上署名。最早的雕刻师签名为 e、E 或 ES，出现在 18 幅版画上，其中 16 幅标注 1461 年，6 幅标注 1466 年或 1467 年。 鉴于 1467 年题年的十幅版画最为精美，ES 可能于该年逝世。基于这 18 幅署名版画，另有约 300 幅作品被归为 ES 所作。其中 50 幅存世两版，95 幅仅存一版，可见 ES 曾刻制过大量现已湮灭的作品。 要完成如此庞大的版画量——约 500 幅——ES 必然需要助手。事实上，在为工匠制作的装饰叶片样本中[118]可见双人协作痕迹：ES 以短促轻盈的笔触为野人描绘绒毛，叶片轮廓则沿袭马丁·施恩高尔的流畅弧线。 尽管尚在学徒期的施恩高尔可能尚未署名作品，但在其风格成熟之前，他必然创作过大量无署名版画。其成熟风格最终以"MS"署名完整呈现于所有版画中——此署名方式正是效仿 ES 的署名方式。

After the painterly Master of the Playing Cards [ 115 ] had used the graver like a quill to create shadows with simple parallels, ES brought engraving back to its origins in the metal crafts. He decorated the garments of some of his figures with a metalworker’s tiny punches [ 121 ], and he supplied silversmiths with the ornamental layout for a paten [ 119 ], though without the prescribed scenes of the Passion. He made things look like crinkled metal in a style organized exclusively for engraving with curves, flicks, dots, and crosshatching. His technical revolution was purified by Schongauer and then elaborated by Dürer into a basic grammar that all subsequent engravers had to learn.
在绘画风格的《纸牌大师》[115]用刻刀如鹅毛笔般勾勒出简洁的平行阴影后，ES 将雕刻技艺回归至金属工艺的本源。 他用金属工匠的微型冲头装饰人物衣饰[121]，为银匠提供圣盘的装饰布局[119]——尽管省略了规定的受难场景。他以曲线、飞溅线、点状纹与交叉阴影构筑的独特技法，使物体呈现金属褶皱般的质感。 其技术革新经施恩高尔提炼，再由丢勒发展为所有后世雕刻家必须掌握的基石语法。
However, no one continued ES’ most singular innovation of hatching highlights instead of shadows for printing in white pigment on blackened paper [120]. He thus imitated manuscripts painted from about 1370 to 1470 in silver and gold on blackened vellum-and imitated them so clearly that all four surviving impressions of his Madonna were at one time catalogued as drawings. Round engravings recur after about 1460 for decorative applications. In Germany some served as playing
然而，无人延续 ES 最独特的创新——用白色颜料在墨黑纸上印刷时，以明线替代阴影来表现高光[120]。他因此模仿了约 1370 至 1470 年间在墨黑羊皮纸上以银金绘制的手稿，且模仿得如此逼真，以致其《圣母》四幅现存拓印本曾一度被归类为素描作品。 圆形雕版画约于 1460 年后为装饰用途再度流行。在德国，部分作品被用作游戏道具。

有些图案用于卡片，另一些则可能被复制到金属盘、盒子或镜背上，或是绘制在箱柜和窗玻璃上。在佛罗伦萨，许多圆形雕刻装饰着盒盖[89]，而镌刻银盘则被嵌入金属器物之中。
ES, unlike Schongauer, engraved all kinds of subjects, producing up to six variations on popular images like the Annunciation. Following the 500th anniversary of Christ’s dedication of the monastery of Einsiedeln near Zürich, he engraved the earliest copperplate pilgrim souvenirs in three sizes for three prices [121]. Since the miraculous Virgin looks different in each engraving, ES, if he ever saw her statue, probably scorned mere fact as much as the woodcutters of the first three views of Venice [ 40 − 42 40 − 42 40-4240-42 ]. He must have kept the largest of the three coppers himself, and sent only impressions to Einsiedeln, for some 30 years later the plate got to a north Italian who shortened and ground it almost smooth for engraving the hero of a popular romance [122]. ES’ plate must have been engraved on both sides (like many surviving early coppers), for if there had been an unworked side,
与施恩高尔不同，ES 刻画了各类题材，甚至为《圣母领报》等流行图像创作了多达六种变体。在苏黎世附近艾因西德伦修道院奉献基督五百周年之际，他制作了最早的铜版朝圣纪念品，分三种尺寸对应三档价格[121]。 由于每幅版画中的圣母形象各异，若埃斯曾见过圣母雕像，他大概与最初三幅威尼斯风景木刻画家一样，对写实手法嗤之以鼻[ 40 − 42 40 − 42 40-4240-42 ]。 他必定将三版中最大的一版铜版留作己用，仅向艾因西德伦寄送印品。约三十年后，该版落入北意大利人手中，对方将其截短并打磨近乎光滑，用于刻印某部通俗小说的主人公[122]。ES 的铜版应属双面雕刻（如许多现存早期铜版），若存在未加工面，
the Italian would have saved himself trouble by using that. For the middling rich, who bought engravings as well as the cheaper woodcuts, ES designed knightly courtships, mostly out of doors where he did not have to contend with the perspective of a room. The briskest of his lovers [123] snuggle in the kind of medieval garden that had to be squeezed into some southward angle of a town wall or castle, where boards bank up a square of grass and violets, set with a potted shrub. ES ′ ES ′ ES^(')\mathrm{ES}^{\prime} engravings were the first to be adapted all over Europe in paintings, embroideries, carvings, and metalwork. Individual details of his richest ornamental design [ 119 ] inspired more adaptations than any other Gothic engraving.
那位意大利人若采用这种方式，本可省去不少麻烦。对于那些既购买版画又购买廉价木刻的中产阶层，ES 设计了骑士式的求爱场景，多在户外进行——这样他便无需处理室内空间的透视问题。 他笔下最活泼的情侣[123]依偎在中世纪花园里——这类园圃总被挤在城墙或城堡朝南的角落，木板围起方寸草地与紫罗兰，间或点缀盆栽灌木。 ES ′ ES ′ ES^(')\mathrm{ES}^{\prime} 这些铜版画率先在欧洲各地被改编为绘画、刺绣、雕刻及金属工艺品。其最繁复的装饰设计[119]中，单个细节所引发的改编数量远超其他任何哥特式版画。

The Housebook Master and drypoint (《家书》大师与干刻版画)


The greatest of the unidentified printmakers gets his name from his drawings of medieval household gear and other subjects in a manuscript known as the Housebook. He used to be called the Master of the Amsterdam Cabinet, from the collection that treasures all but nine of his known prints. While he seems to have worked in Germany, he is Netherlandish in the modeling of his shadows [124] and the bizarre elegance of his skinny fig-
《家居手册》大师与干刻版画这位最伟大的无名版画家因其在中世纪手稿《家居手册》中描绘的家用器具及其他题材而得名。他曾被称为阿姆斯特丹内阁大师，因该馆珍藏了其所有已知版画作品，仅缺九幅。尽管他似乎在德国工作，但其阴影塑造手法[124]与瘦削人物所展现的怪诞优雅皆具尼德兰风格。
ures. He was possibly, perhaps probably, the Erhard Reuwich of Utrecht who illustrated the Pilgrimage to the Holy Land [ 43 ] in Mainz, and very likely the Speyer Mirror [ 22 ], with the same stylish quirks. But whether we have here three artistic cousins or one artist, the Housebook Master, like the earlier Master of the Playing Cards [ 115 ], certainly came to printmaking from a painter’s studio and not from a metal workshop. He and Mantegna finally transformed printmaking by freeing
他很可能——或许确是——乌得勒支的埃尔哈德·罗伊维希，正是这位艺术家在美因茨为《圣地朝圣记》[43]绘制插图，并极可能创作了《施派尔镜》[22]，其风格特质如出一辙。 但无论我们面对的是三位艺术表亲还是同一位艺术家，这位《家谱集大师》——如同早先的《纸牌大师》[115]——显然是从画室而非金属工坊踏入版画领域的。他与曼特尼亚最终通过解放版画创作，彻底革新了这一艺术形式。

it from its origins in engraving metal and woodblocking cloth to bring it for good and all under the dominance of the painter.
它从金属雕刻和布料木版印刷的起源中脱胎换骨，彻底将其纳入画家的统治之下。
For painterly purposes, the Housebook Master flouted the tidiness of professional metal practice by inventing drypoint. The stout drypoint needle [125] scratches the plate without removing substance (unlike the graver), simply deflecting metal up out of the grooves into flanking ridges [126]. These ragged ridges
为追求绘画效果，版画大师摒弃了专业金属工艺的规整性，开创了干刻法。粗壮的干刻针[125]在版面上划出痕迹却不剥离金属（与刻刀不同），仅将金属从凹槽中推挤至周边形成棱脊[126]。这些参差不齐的棱脊

The Housebook Master inspired Dürer to make three drypoints [127]; these are among his rarest prints. Dürer made no more, partly because his silversmith father had conditioned him to neatness, partly because he had too shrewd a business head to invest much time in a process that yielded such meager returns. But a business

Drypoint by  干刻版画
Dürer, 1512  丢勒，1512 年
idiot like Rembrandt turned more and more to drypoint after he was about 40 , because he could get effects without waiting for acid to bite, and because he had developed the command of hand to dominate the almost ungovernable scratching in so hard a metal as copper. Drypoint enabled him to accent his etchings [ 493 ] and to attack the copper directly [478] for the smoky majesty of his greatest paintings.
像伦勃朗这样的天才，年过四十后愈发倾心于干刻技法，既因无需等待腐蚀液作用便能呈现效果，更因他已练就精湛技艺，能驾驭铜板这般坚硬金属上近乎无法控制的刻划。干刻技法使他得以强化蚀刻作品的视觉效果[493]，更能直接攻克铜板[478]，从而在巅峰画作中呈现出烟雾缭绕的恢弘气势。
Drypoint became commercially rewarding after the 1850 s when copperplates could be electroplated with iron to reinforce the burr. Then Seymour Haden and Whistler in his Thames set [702] took advantage of this “whiff of steel” to launch drypoint in the so-called revival of etching in Britain. But back in the 1480s, the Housebook Master’s plates (possibly of soft pewter) printed fewer impressions than those of any great artist. Only 31 of his 91 drypoints have survived in two to five impressions, while 60 are unique. Some 30 more of his lost prints (or drawings?) seem to have been copied by Israhel van Meckenem [139].
干刻版画在 1850 年代后开始获得商业回报，当时铜版可通过电镀铁层来强化刻痕。随后西摩·海登与惠斯勒在其《泰晤士河组画》[702]中，便借助这种"钢铁气息"推动干刻版画在英国所谓蚀刻版画复兴运动中崭露头角。 然而早在 1480 年代，"家书大师"的铜版（可能是软锡材质）印制量远低于任何伟大艺术家。其 91 幅干刻版画中仅存 31 幅（存世量 2 至 5 份），其余 60 幅均为孤本。另有约 30 幅失传版画（或素描？）似乎被伊斯拉埃尔·范·梅克内姆[139]临摹复制。
Rarity kept the Housebook Master’s work private for 400 years until photogravure reproductions finally published it in 1893. Only then did we see his passionate vision that vibrated to the medieval world of the young [128], shaken between the extremes of rapture and early death [129]: cabined in the shuttered room without window glass and released into the jeweled endlessness of the cathedral, agitated by the days of processions and the days of beheadings.
稀世珍宝将《家谱大师》的著作封存了四百载，直至 1893 年通过照相凹版印刷技术得以面世。 直到那时，我们才得以窥见他那充满激情的视野——它在年轻的中世纪世界中震颤[128]，在狂喜与早逝的两极间摇摆[129]：既被困在没有玻璃窗的密闭房间里，又被释放到教堂那宝石般的无垠空间中，既被游行庆典的日子所激荡，又被斩首处决的日子所震撼。

Schongauer (尚戈尔)


Schongauer Martin Schongauer is the first northern printmaker whose biography we know, and the first whose signed engravings have apparently all survived, even the rarest one existing in three impressions. He must have been born when engravings were first being printed, and he may have been apprenticed to ES [ 118 ], whose monogram suggested his own MS. Unlike ES, Schongauer never dated a print. Although ES engraved all kinds of subjects, Schongauer specialized in saints and the New Testament (107 prints) in preference to ornament and worldly life (eight prints).
马丁·施恩高尔是首位传记可考的北方版画家，也是首位其签名版画作品得以完整保存的艺术家——甚至包括现存三份印本的稀世之作。 他诞生于铜版画初现世间的年代，很可能曾师从 ES[118]——后者的签名缩写暗示其作品与施恩高尔的"MS"标记存在关联。不同于 ES，施恩高尔从不在版画上署名日期。尽管 ES 创作题材包罗万象，施恩高尔却专注于圣徒题材与新约故事（共 107 幅版画），远少于其创作的装饰图案与世俗生活题材（仅 8 幅）。
His father was a silversmith in Augsburg, but Martin settled in Colmar on the upper Rhine, where he died just when Dürer, aged 19, was about to visit him on his student wanderings. His father’s workshop must have trained him to an instinctive mastery of metal. After the first northern engravers had tentatively scratched, and ES had started to vary the strokes with method, Schongauer organized the basic rhythm of lines that all later engravings developed. Since his long strokes are the first to curve concentrically, he may have been the first to pivot his copperplate on a hard leather pillow, revolving the plate with his left hand against the graver, steadily held in his right. This active opposition plows out segments of circles with a regularity distinct from the caprices of the quill, pencil, or etching needle. Schongauer harmonized this ambidextrous geometry of sinuous sweeps with an exquisiteness that purified Gothic engraving to its last refinement of conscious simplicity. His reasoned delineation of shapes spread beyond the technique of engraving to the pen drawing of Ghirlandaio in Florence about 1490, and through him to his 15-year-old pupil Michelangelo.
他的父亲是奥格斯堡的一位银匠，但马丁定居在上莱茵河畔的科尔马。当 19 岁的丢勒正准备在求学旅途中探望父亲时，父亲却在此时离世。父亲的工坊想必使他本能地掌握了金属加工技艺。 在北方早期雕刻师试探性地刻划之后，ES 开始有意识地变化笔触，而施恩高尔则确立了所有后续雕刻作品都沿袭的基本线条韵律。由于他率先运用长笔触形成同心曲线，他很可能是首位将铜版置于硬皮革垫上旋转的艺术家——左手转动版面，右手稳稳持握刻刀。 这种动态对抗以羽笔、铅笔或蚀刻针无法企及的规整性，开凿出圆弧的分段轨迹。他将这种灵动流转的双向几何几何学与极致精妙相融合，将哥特式版画升华至自觉简约的终极境界。 他理性化的造型技法不仅影响了版画艺术，更延伸至 1490 年左右吉兰达约在佛罗伦萨的钢笔素描，并通过后者传授给其十五岁的学生米开朗基罗。
Besides being the first virtuoso engraver, Schongauer also somehow learned to paint and draw at the center of northern art in Flanders, mastering so much of the grace of Rogier van der Weyden that Vasari thought him a Fleming. Flemish training enabled him to make the first prints that situate furniture convincingly in a room and people the depth with complex and expressive groups [130]. His Death of the Virgin was copied in some 40 paintings, carvings, and textiles, showing a special wonder at the boldly foreshortened bed and the intricate linking of the two kneeling apostles. Metalsmiths must have found useful ideas in the candlestick that Schongauer designed with the mastery of a man born in a metal shop. For the most exquisite prayer books, Tory of Paris [ 182 ] adopted Schongauer’s splitting
除了是首位雕版艺术大师，施恩高尔还在弗兰德斯——这座北方艺术的中心地带——习得了绘画与素描技艺，他如此精通罗吉尔·范德韦登的优雅风格，以致瓦萨里曾误以为他是弗拉芒人。弗拉芒式的训练使他能够创作出首批将家具逼真置于室内、并以复杂而富有表现力的群体构图营造空间纵深感的版画[130]。 他的《圣母之死》被约四十件绘画、雕刻及纺织品所临摹，其中对大胆运用透视法处理的床榻，以及两位跪姿使徒精妙交叠的构图尤为惊艳。 金属匠们定从施恩高尔设计的烛台中汲取灵感——这位生于金属作坊的匠人展现出超凡造诣。巴黎的托里[182]在制作最精美的祈祷书时，便沿用了施恩高尔的分层技法。
130 The Death of the Virgin. Engraving by Martin Schongauer
130 圣母之死。马丁·施恩高尔的铜版画
Schongauer  尚戈尔



of a scene into two facing pages [ 131 ]. His Road to Calvary [ 132 ], one of the largest early northern copperplates, masses together more figures than any other Gothic print, and fuses them into a processional surge that inspired artists from Memling to Guido Reni.
将一幅场景印制于对开双页[131]。他的《通往各各他的道路》[132]作为北方早期最大型的铜版画之一，汇聚了比任何其他哥特式版画都更庞大的人物群像，并将它们熔铸成一股汹涌的游行浪潮，由此启迪了从梅姆林到圭多·雷尼的众多艺术家。

Schongauer’s most formative print was his Bedeviling of Saint Anthony [ 133 ], which sums up the spooky drolleries that the late Middle Ages shaped into gargoyles and misericords and painted on the margins of books. Monsters patched together out of giblets from fish and poultry stalls here congregate in one engraving
施昂高尔最具代表性的版画作品当属《圣安东尼受魔鬼折磨》[133]，它浓缩了中世纪晚期那些被塑造成怪兽雕像、雕花椅座，或绘于书籍页边的诡异滑稽之作。那些由鱼摊禽摊的内脏拼凑而成的怪物，在此刻版画中汇聚成群。

that spawned a whole category of art. Michelangelo copied this print when he was a boy, and developed its implications in his later grotesque drawings. Bosch [ 134 ] and the elder Brueghel hybridized its freaks all their lives, and Schongauer’s monsters haunted artists as recent as James Ensor, who died in 1949 [ 135 ].
由此催生了整个艺术流派。米开朗基罗少年时曾临摹此版画，并在后来的怪诞画作中深化其意蕴。博斯[134]与老布鲁盖尔毕生都在融合其怪诞元素，而尚高尔的怪物形象甚至萦绕着 1949 年逝世的詹姆斯·恩索尔[135]等当代艺术家。

Early Netherlandish engravers (早期尼德兰版画家)


The early Dutch and Flemish engravers, associating with northern Europe’s first great painters, adapted the German engraver’s technique to the painter’s vision. The ablest early Flemish engraver signed his prints FVB. Since his style resembles the paintings of Memling in Bruges, VB may stand for “of Bruges” (van Brügge). FVB perfected his skill by copying eight of Schongauer’s engravings with a darker blend of lights and shadows. He seems to have been one of the few early non-Italian engravers to copy paintings, and must himself have painted to be able to construct figures [136] more solidly than any Netherlandish engraver before Lucas of Leiden.
早期尼德兰版画家早期荷兰与佛兰德版画家与北欧首批伟大画家结缘，将德国版画技法融入绘画美学。最杰出的早期佛兰德版画家在作品上署名 FVB。因其风格酷似布鲁日梅姆林的绘画，VB 可能代表"布鲁日人"（van Brügge）。 FVB 通过临摹施贡瑙尔八幅版画精进技艺，其作品以更深邃的光影层次见长。他似乎是少数临摹绘画的非意大利早期版画家，其人物构图之扎实超越了莱顿的卢卡斯之前的任何低地版画家，足见其必曾亲身绘画。
A Dutch engraver with more flourish than FVB often signed himself IAM Zwott, which is interpreted as IA, Master of Zwolle. To show that he also worked metal, he signed beside a metal drill, worked like a yo-yo by spinning it back and forth with a string. IA saw like a sculptor or a hammerer of metal when he engraved a silversmith’s bright flanges on his armored figures [137], which much resemble the woodcuts in the Chevalier Délibéré [ 49 ]. He is the first engraver to display Dutch swagger, the vaulting exuberance of a people who successfully defend their independence and force the sea to keep its distance. The same victorious self-confidence was to alert the paintings of Dutch admirals and stadtholders, and to regulate the elegant uprightness of their houses.
一位比 FVB 更富装饰性的荷兰雕刻师常署名 IAM Zwott，被解读为"兹沃勒大师"。为彰显其金属工艺造诣，他将签名置于金属钻旁——这种工具通过绳索来回旋转，如同溜溜球般运作。 当 IA 在铠甲人物上刻画银匠般的亮边时[137]，其手法宛若雕塑家或金属锤工，与《深思骑士》中的木刻画极为神似[49]。他是首位展现荷兰式傲气的雕刻师——这种蓬勃的自豪感源于民族成功捍卫独立、迫使大海退守的壮举。 同样的胜利自信，将唤醒荷兰海军上将与执政官的画作，并规范他们宅邸优雅挺拔的姿态。

Van Meckenem (范·梅克内姆)


138 The Engraver and His Wife. Engraving by Israhel van Meckenem, 1490s

139 鲁特琴与竖琴二重奏。范·梅克内姆雕版画
Van Meckenem Israhel van Meckenem-the first engraver thought to be the son of an engraver-copied other men’s work in practically every print except his self-portrait [ 138 ]. He copied 145 engravings by ES, and added his IM or Israhel to 41 more coppers that ES himself engraved. He seems to have engraved some 30 lost drawings or drypoints by the Housebook Master, including half a dozen of couples dancing or playing music [139]. He probably went to the bottom margin of a late medieval manuscript for his egalitarian drollery of hares roasting a hunter [140]. And for his personal memorial to himself and his wife, he adapted the paired conjugal portraits of Roman gravestones.
范·梅克内姆·以色列·范·梅克内姆——首位被认为是雕刻师之子的雕刻师——除自画像外，几乎所有版画作品皆为临摹他人之作[138]。他复制了 ES 的 145 幅铜版画，并在 ES 亲手雕刻的另外 41 幅铜版画上添加了"IM"或"以色列"的签名。 他似乎还刻制了约 30 幅已失传的《家书大师》素描或干刻版画，其中包括六幅描绘情侣跳舞或演奏音乐的作品[139]。他可能借鉴了中世纪晚期手稿的下边框图案，创作了那幅描绘野兔烤猎人的平等主义滑稽画[140]。而为纪念自己与妻子，他则借鉴了罗马墓碑上成对的夫妻肖像进行改编。
Israhel’s wholesale expropriations accumulated a stock of over 600 copperplates, from which he sold so many impressions that he had repeatedly to retouch worn
以色列通过大规模征用积累了 600 多块铜版，他售出的印品数量如此之多，以致不得不反复修补磨损的版面。
140 Hares Roasting a Hunter. Engraving by van Meckenem
140 兔子烤猎人。范·梅克内姆版画

areas, even though he did his best to make the engraving last by driving his graver heavy-handed. To this day much of his work can still be collected, though usually in tired impressions. As if all this printmaking were not enough, Israhel also made the earliest silver objects by a northern engraver. Such industrial mass production required assistants. Did his wife, Ida, help? (IM, or IVM could also stand for Ida van Meckenem.) If people are to collaborate smoothly, they must share a teachable, and therefore impersonal, routine. This subjection to efficiency accounts for the mechanical competence of Israhel’s engravings, and-to be frank-of the numerical bulk of old copperplate prints wherever they came off the assembly lines that this brisk boss did so much to organize.
尽管他竭力用重手刻刀延长版画寿命，某些区域仍难免磨损。时至今日，他的作品仍有不少可供收藏，只是印痕往往已显疲态。仿佛这些版画创作尚不足够，伊斯拉赫尔还制作了北方雕刻师最早的银器作品。如此工业化的大规模生产需要助手协助。他的妻子伊达是否参与其中？（IM 或 IVM 也可能代表伊达·范·梅克内姆。） 若要协作顺畅，必须遵循可传授的、因而去个性化的流程。这种对效率的服从造就了伊斯拉赫尔版画机械化的精湛技艺——坦白说，也造就了大量铜版画的批量生产，这些作品源自这位干练老板精心构建的流水线。

Florentine engraving (佛罗伦萨雕版印刷)


Florentine engraving twice succumbed to German engraving. In the 1440 s the first German engravings changed the backgrounds of Florentine nielli from checkers or diapering, imitated from Parisian illuminations, to backgrounds of close hatching. The Florentines showed their dependence on German inventiveness by adopting the German oil ink and by combining two of ES ′ ES ′ ES^(')\mathrm{ES}^{\prime} apostles [141,142]
佛罗伦萨雕版画两次败于德国雕版画。1440 年代，首批德国雕版画将佛罗伦萨镌刻工艺的背景图案从仿照巴黎插图的棋盘格或菱形纹样，改为密集的阴影线条背景。 佛罗伦萨人通过采用德国油墨并组合两位使徒形象[141,142]，展现出对德国创新精神的依赖。
Florentine engraving  佛罗伦萨雕版印刷
into a prophet seated on a homemade Renaissance throne [ 143 ]. This first importation of silversmiths’ niggling, the so-called Florentine fine manner of engraving, cannot have pleased the Florentine painters, whose different example of the painter’s way of drawing soon inspired broad-manner engraving [ 144 ]. For a decade or so, different shops must have practiced the silversmith’s fine manner and the painter’s broad manner.
化身为坐在自制文艺复兴风格宝座上的先知[143]。这种最初传入的银匠式精细雕刻技法——即所谓的佛罗伦萨精细雕刻风格——必然令佛罗伦萨画家们不悦，而画家们独特的绘画方式很快催生了粗犷风格的雕刻艺术[144]。 约莫十年间，不同作坊必然同时实践着银匠的精细技法与画家的粗犷风格。
Florentine painters drew with a silver wire on paper coated with fine white grit. They could hardly see what they were drawing until the silver trace oxidized into a moonstone image. The painter could erase nothing without scraping through the gritty coating onto the paper beneath. Thus forced to be both delicate and decided, Florentine painters outlined with crisp selectivity and shaded in close, straight parallels. Florentine engravers imitated such drawings so consistently that they often
佛罗伦萨画家在涂有细白砂粒的纸上用银丝作画。他们几乎看不清画笔痕迹，直到银线氧化形成月光石般的图像。画家若要擦除笔触，必须刮穿砂粒涂层触及底纸。这种技法迫使画家兼具细腻与果断，以鲜明的选择性勾勒轮廓，并用紧密平行的笔触进行阴影处理。佛罗伦萨雕刻师们如此忠实地模仿这类素描，以至于他们常常——
Figure 51: 144 The Prophet Ezekiel. Broad-manner engraving in style of Botticelli, 1475-90
图 51：144 先知以西结。博提切利风格的宽幅版画，1475-90 年
Figure 52: 144 The Prophet Ezekiel. Broad-manner engraving in style of Botticelli, 1475-90
图 52：144 先知以西结。博蒂切利风格的宽幅版画，1475-90 年
printed with an ink as gray as the silverpoint itself. The broad-manner engravers subordinated their unostentatious technique to grand pictorial effects in order to extend and popularize the work of painters. Collaborating in shops, they rarely signed their work. German engravers, on the contrary, showed that they, and not the painters, were the molding force by often initialing their work and by elaborating special quirks and strokes that suited the graver but would embarrass a pen or pencil. Thus, in the anonymous Florentine engravings, it is Baldovinetti and Filippo Lippi who give the considered clarity to the Life of Christ and the Virgin [ 92 ], and Botticelli who quickens an exquisite Triumph of Bacchus and Ariadne [ 145 ]. Vasari said that many Botticelli drawings were engraved, but all badly except for a Triumph of Savonarola, which is now lost.
采用与银尖笔同样灰暗的墨水印制。那些风格粗犷的雕刻师将朴实无华的技艺服从于宏大的画面效果，以此推广并普及画家的作品。他们在作坊里协作创作，却极少署名。 德国雕刻师则截然相反，他们通过署名作品并精心雕琢刻刀特有的笔触——这些笔触虽契合刻刀特性，却令毛笔或铅笔难以企及——彰显出自身才是塑造艺术的主导力量。 因此，在那些无名佛罗伦萨版画中，正是巴尔多维内蒂和菲利波·利皮赋予《基督与圣母生平》[92]深思熟虑的明晰感，而波提切利则为《巴克斯与阿里阿德涅的胜利》[145]注入了精妙生机。瓦萨里曾言许多波提切利素描被制成版画，但除现已失传的《萨沃纳罗拉的胜利》外皆属拙劣之作。
In the 1490s, when Florentine engraving had perfected its personality, it was
1490 年代，当佛罗伦萨的雕版印刷术已臻成熟，展现出其独特个性时，

Florentine engraving  佛罗伦萨雕版印刷

145 The Triumph of Bacchus and Ariadne, adapted from a Roman sarcophagus by a follower of Botticelli. Engraving, Florence, 1480s
145 巴克斯与阿里阿德涅的胜利，由波提切利门徒根据罗马石棺改编。铜版画，佛罗伦萨，1480 年代
disrupted-forever-by the impact of Dürer. In this second and last wave from Germany, Dürer’s irresistible virtuosity deflected the feeble dependence of the first Florentine engraver who signed many prints, Cristofano Robetta (who also made the last noteworthy prints in Florence until the work of Callot and della Bella a century later). Robetta concluded the sweet grace of the early Florentine Renaissance as he imitated Filippino Lippi’s febrile, mannered figures, often setting them against a landscape copied from Dürer’s engravings [ 146 ]. Though Robetta copied northern landscapes, like his contemporary Giulio Campagnola in Venice [ 267 ], neither of them, unlike the fine-manner engravers, copied northern figures. By Robetta’s time Mantegna, Pollaiuolo, Leonardo, and Michelangelo had perfected a supremacy of figure drawing that Italians taught to foreigners in contempt of foreign efforts. It thus caused a shock in 1522 when Pontormo frescoed the Passion from Dürer’s big woodcuts. He was, however, only initiating the future practice of baroque painters like Rubens and Rembrandt, who stocked all kinds of prints to get ideas. By 1712 some painters relied so much on borrowing that the Dutch artist Gérard de Lairesse remarked: “They cannot start any subject-history, allegory, or mythology-without first raking together bits and pieces of prints, drawings, and figure studies, taking here an arm, there a leg, a face, a garment, a torso to jumble together into a patchwork.”
杜勒的影响永远地颠覆了这一局面。在这股源自德国的第二波也是最后一波浪潮中，杜勒无可抗拒的技艺造诣，使首位在众多版画上署名的佛罗伦萨雕刻师克里斯托法诺·罗贝塔（他亦创作了佛罗伦萨最后一批值得注意的版画，直至一个世纪后卡洛与德拉·贝拉的作品问世）那脆弱的依附性荡然无存。 罗贝塔以模仿菲利皮诺·利皮那些病态矫饰的人物形象，为早期佛罗伦萨文艺复兴的甜美风韵画上句点，其作品常将人物置于杜勒版画复制的景观中[146]。尽管罗贝塔与同时代的威尼斯版画家朱利奥·坎帕尼奥拉[267]皆模仿北方风景，但二人与精致风格版画家不同，从未复制北方人物形象。 到罗贝塔时代，曼特尼亚、波拉伊乌奥洛、达·芬奇和米开朗基罗已将人物素描技艺推向巅峰，意大利人甚至不屑于向外国人传授这门技艺。因此当蓬托尔莫于 1522 年以丢勒大型木刻为蓝本创作《受难》湿壁画时，引发了巨大震撼。 然而他只是为鲁本斯、伦勃朗等巴洛克画家开创了先河——这些画家囤积各类版画汲取灵感。 到 1712 年，某些画家对借鉴的依赖已然泛滥，以致荷兰艺术家热拉尔·德·莱雷斯惊叹道："他们创作任何题材——无论是历史画、寓言画还是神话画——都必须先从版画、素描和人体研究中拼凑零碎元素，此处取一臂，彼处取一腿，再掺杂面容、衣饰与躯干，最终拼凑成一幅拼布画。"

The Triumphs of Petrarch and Maximilian (彼特拉克与马克西米利安的胜利)


In the 1350 s Petrarch began his popular poems on the Triumphs of Love, Chastity, Death, Fame, Time, and Divinity. A musician of rhetoric, but not an imagist like Dante, Petrarch supplied practically nothing visual to illustrate. Nevertheless, in 1441 Matteo de Pasti painted the Triumphs for the Medici, apparently in miniatures that are now lost. What did he find to paint? His handiest models could have been the frequent processions that the Medici staged to divert the fickle Florentines. Each of these street pageants dramatized a religious or literary theme through elaborate floats on wheels. (In northern medieval processions, priests carried images and relics in a long file, varied now and then by buffoons.) Whether or not Matteo de Pasti painted processional floats, they certainly represented Petrarch’s Triumphs in the earliest set of prints [ 147 ]. These six Florentine engravings solved a problem for
彼特拉克与马克西米利安的凯旋 1350 年代，彼特拉克开始创作广受欢迎的《凯旋诗集》，歌颂爱情、贞洁、死亡、声名、时光与神性的凯旋。 彼特拉克虽是修辞艺术家，却不像但丁那样擅长意象描绘，几乎未提供可供视觉呈现的素材。然而 1441 年，马泰奥·德·帕斯蒂为美第奇家族绘制了《凯旋》系列，据称是现已失传的微型画。他从何处汲取创作灵感？最现成的参照或许是美第奇家族为取悦善变的佛罗伦萨民众而频繁举办的游行。 这些街头庆典通过精巧的轮式花车演绎宗教或文学主题。（中世纪北方的游行中，神职人员列队抬着圣像与圣物，偶有丑角穿插其间。）无论马泰奥·德·帕斯蒂是否绘制过游行花车，最早的版画集[147]中呈现的形象无疑再现了彼特拉克的凯旋主题。这六幅佛罗伦萨版画解决了
Figure 54: The Triumphs of Petrarch and Maximilian
图 54：彼特拉克与马克西米利安的凯旋
Venetian publishers, who adapted them in three distinct sets of woodcuts in 148893 as the only illustrations for Petrarch’s complete poems. The first two copyists [148,149] approximated the engravings with typical Venetian outlines, while the third slavishly imitated even the Florentine broad-manner shading. At home in Florence, however, a woodcutter completely redrew the floats (from an up-to-date procession?) and departed entirely from any copperplate style into his own local knife style of woodcut [150]. Thus, because an alert Venetian publisher helped himself to ready copy for tacking some pretty pictures onto a text that offers nothing to illustrate, other publishers of Petrarch’s poems followed him for nearly 200 years, while Virgil, though evoking vivid tableaux [ 56 ], usually lacked pictures altogether.
威尼斯出版商于 1488-93 年间将这些浮雕改编为三套独立的木刻版画，作为彼特拉克全集诗歌的唯一插图。前两位抄写者[148,149]以典型的威尼斯轮廓线近似再现了雕版，而第三位则连佛罗伦萨粗犷的阴影技法都机械模仿。 然而在佛罗伦萨本土，一位木刻师完全重新绘制了花车（取材于当季游行？），彻底摒弃铜版画风格，开创了独具地方特色的刀工木刻技法[150]。 因此，由于一位机敏的威尼斯出版商擅自挪用现成版画——为缺乏插图的文本配上精美图画——此后近两百年来，其他出版彼特拉克诗集的商人纷纷效仿。而维吉尔的诗集虽能唤起鲜活画面[56]，却通常完全缺乏插图。
The sudden appearance of many illustrated Petrarchs after 1488 marked a financial crisis in book publishing. The earliest printers started by selling Latin grammars to schoolboys, who wore them to shreds that were then reused for patching bindings. The earliest surviving books were printed for priests and the next for lawyers and humanists. The glutting of these markets by the late 1480 s ruined printers here and there. Accordingly, about 1490, forward-looking publishers opened a new market by illustrating books to catch the general reader, the way the Augsburg publishers had so successfully done in the 1470 s and 14805 [ 34 ]. Thus, in the 1490s, Venice, Florence, Milan, Paris, Nuremberg, Basel, Lübeck, and other cities burst out with the first widespread crop of splendid woodcut illustrations.
1488 年后大量插图版彼特拉克作品的突然涌现，标志着图书出版业陷入了财务危机。最早的印刷商起家靠向学童销售拉丁语语法书，这些书被学生们翻得破烂不堪，最终只能用来补丁书脊。 现存最早的印刷书籍面向神职人员，其次是律师和人文主义者。到 1480 年代末，这些市场的饱和导致各地印刷商破产。因此，约 1490 年间，具有前瞻性的出版商效仿奥格斯堡出版商在 1470 至 1480 年代的成功模式，通过为书籍配图开拓大众读者市场[34]。 由此，1490 年代威尼斯、佛罗伦萨、米兰、巴黎、纽伦堡、巴塞尔、吕贝克等城市相继涌现出首批大规模精美木刻插图作品。
Successive sets of illustrations to Petrarch’s Triumphs kept so close to the look of processional floats that they inspired designs of dream processions on other
为彼特拉克《凯旋诗集》创作的系列插图，其风格与游行花车的视觉效果如此接近，以至于激发了其他艺术家对梦幻游行场景的设计灵感。

themes, and then actual pageants. The most sumptuous of the imaginary processions was drawn by Dürer in woodcuts for Emperor Maximilian’s program of paper grandeur [ 151 ]. Thereafter real floats, costing whatever money was available, appeared in processions in Italy, Germany, and Flanders. Fewer appeared in France, where royal entries kept closer to the simplicity of medieval church processions. Venice, always the exception, walked relics around the Piazza and over foot bridges, but floated its grand pageants on the Grand Canal.
主题，继而发展为实际的游行盛典。杜勒为马克西米利安皇帝的纸上宏图所绘制的木刻版画，展现了最富盛名的虚构游行场景[151]。此后，意大利、德国和法兰德斯地区的游行中出现了耗尽所有可用资金打造的实体花车。 法国出现的较少，其皇家入城仪式更接近中世纪教堂游行的简朴风格。威尼斯始终是个例外，它将圣物在广场和人行桥上巡游，却将盛大的庆典游行置于大运河之上。

Dante (但丁)


Dante as the oldest writer in any modern language who still molds thought, and the first modern classic to be printed in pocket format (1502), is the only supreme writer who fascinated a supreme artist. Vasari says that Botticelli’s obsession with the Divine Comedy caused him “infinite disorders,” and that he “figuró lo Inferno.” Botticelli’s vehemence struggles through 19 rough engravings of the Inferno made for the first illustrated printing of the Divine Comedy in 1481. Four years before, the German Nicolaus Laurentii had successfully printed three full-page copper
但丁作为现代语言中最古老的作家，其思想至今仍具塑造力，其作品更是首部以袖珍本形式印刷的现代经典（1502 年），这位至高无上的作家唯一令一位至高无上的艺术家为之倾倒。 瓦萨里记载，波提切利对《神曲》的痴迷使他陷入"无尽的困扰"，并称其"构思了地狱篇"。波提切利为 1481 年首版插图《神曲》创作的 19 幅粗粝版画中，可见其炽烈的情感挣扎。四年前，德国人尼古拉·劳伦提已成功印制三幅整版铜版画。

engravings [ 152 ] in the first illustrated book published at Florence. But the Dante faced him with the harder problem of printing the text on a screw press while reserving 100 gaps in which to center 100 small copperplates for the rolling press. When he forgot a gap on the first page, he had to add the illustration below the text, where the binder usually cropped it. The printer managed to introduce copperplates into the text for the next two or three cantos in a few copies of the book, then printed the illustrations through Inferno 19 on separate slips of paper numbered for pasting in later, and gave up entirely on the 81 remaining illustrations. (He tactfully omitted all attempts at illustration in the vellum copy presented to the city fathers.) This botch practically stopped Florence from illustrating books for eight or nine years, until the city found its true style in the magical woodcuts [153] of the 1490 s .
在佛罗伦萨出版的首部插图书籍中，共有[152]幅雕版画。但但丁的文本印刷面临更棘手的难题：既要在螺旋印刷机上印制正文，又需预留 100 处空白以容纳滚筒印刷用的 100 块小型铜版。当他在首页遗漏空白处时，只得将插图添加在正文下方——而该处恰是装订工通常裁切的位置。 此后两三章的铜版画，印刷商勉强在少数副本中嵌入文本；至《地狱篇》第十九章，他改用单独编号纸张印刷插图以便后期粘贴，最终彻底放弃了剩余 81 幅插图的制作。（他机智地省略了赠予市政要员的羊皮纸版本中所有插图尝试。） 这场混乱几乎让佛罗伦萨的书籍插画事业停滞八九年之久，直至 1490 年代这座城市在神奇的木刻版画[153]中找到了真正的艺术风格。
Some of the Dante engravings of 1481 show Dante and Virgil twice in the same picture, whose top and bottom edges overlap into the levels of hell above and below. Thus, the rebels against nature and art scratch off the rain of flames above Geryon, who pokes up his head from the ultimate abyss of Fraud [154]. These
1481 年版但丁版画中，有两幅画面同时呈现但丁与维吉尔的身影——画面上下边缘相互交叠，延伸至上下两层地狱。于是，那些违背自然与艺术的叛逆者，正从盖里翁头顶的火焰雨中挣扎爬出，而盖里翁的头颅正从欺诈的终极深渊中探出[154]。这些

engravings must therefore be snippets out of a panorama of the tiered funnel of hell in an earlier medieval version [ 152 ]. Botticelli, in his late 205 or early 30s, must have drawn or painted (Vasari’s figuró) such a funnel, to which he returned in middle age when starting his 100 exquisite vellum drawings for the elder Lorenzo di Pier Francesco de’ Medici [ 155 ].
因此，这些版画必然是中世纪早期版本中地狱阶梯漏斗全景图的片段[152]。 波提切利在二十五六岁或三十岁出头时，必定曾绘制过（瓦萨里称之为"人像"）这样的漏斗，中年时为年长的洛伦佐·德·皮耶尔·弗朗切斯科·德·美第奇创作百幅精美羊皮纸素描时，他再度回到了这个主题[155]。
Sometime between Botticelli’s early overall view and his late vellum drawings, the engraver of the 1481 Dante (Baccio Baldini?) must have prepared for his task by excerpting 34 Inferno scenes from Botticelli’s survey, which included bits above and below some of his subjects. These excerpts, or copies of them, inspired the Inferno cuts in three north Italian Dantes-two different but similar printings at Venice in March and November 1491, and a handsome folio at Brescia in 1487 [156]. The Brescia cuts are framed in black and white ornament in the Milanese style, and many of the Inferno illustrations are drawn with the open boldness of a Milanese illustrator trained to Mantegna’s rugged schemes for rocks and torsos. The successful Brescia cuts sparkle more happily with type than the smoky Florentine engravings, but the Brescia publisher evidently ran out of funds, for he changed to a jacknife slasher for the Purgatorio (for which Botticelli had not yet invented illustrations), and stopped all pictures after Paradiso I, stretching his 60 blocks with eight repeats. While adaptations allow a glimpse at Botticelli’s early Inferno picture, we have no clue at all to the even intenser intellect and passion that Michelangelo must have packed into drawings on the wide margins of a Dante that existed for two centuries and then disappeared at sea.
在波提切利早期全景图与晚期羊皮纸素描之间某个时期，1481 年版《但丁》的雕刻师（巴乔·巴尔迪尼？）必然从波提切利的全景图中摘录了 34 幅《地狱篇》场景作为创作蓝本——这些选段包含了部分主题上下方的延伸画面。 这些选段（或其复本）启发了三部北意大利版《神曲》中的地狱版画创作——包括 1491 年 3 月与 11 月威尼斯出版的两版不同但相似的印刷品，以及 1487 年布雷西亚出版的精美对开本[156]。 布雷西亚版画以米兰风格的黑白装饰框饰，其中许多《地狱篇》插图展现出米兰画师的开阔笔触——他们受过曼泰尼亚粗犷岩石与躯干技法的训练。 布雷西亚版画的成功在于其与活字排印的欢快碰撞，远胜于烟熏般的佛罗伦萨铜版画。但出版商显然资金告罄，转而为《炼狱篇》（此时波提切利尚未创作插图）启用廉价刻刀工，并在《天堂篇》第一卷后彻底停用插图，仅靠 60 块版材重复印刷八次勉强支撑。 虽然改编作品让我们得以窥见波提切利早期《地狱篇》的画作，但对于米开朗基罗在但丁手稿宽阔的页边空白处倾注的更深邃的智慧与激情，我们却毫无线索——那部存在了两个世纪的手稿最终在海上消失了。

Savonarola (萨沃纳罗拉)


157, 158
Figure 56: 157  图 56：157
Savonarola Preaching in the Duomo. Woodcut in Savonarola, compendio di revelazione, Florence (Pacini), 1496
萨沃纳罗拉在主教座堂布道。木刻版画出自《萨沃纳罗拉启示录纲要》，佛罗伦萨（帕奇尼出版社），1496 年
Savonarola preached in the cathedral of Florence from 1490 to 1498 to crowds so tightly packed that he had to stretch a curtain to keep the men from ogling the women [ 157 ]. His voice echoed down that stony chasm with a command that rang in Michelangelo’s ears for decades after Savonarola himself had vanished in flames. This Florentine uproar spread to the outside world and a future time when Savonarola printed his sermons with pictures so apt that he forced the papacy to counterattack. He published his brief, plain, eloquent tracts in pamphlets handy enough to pull out of a pocket while one waited for a ferry or a barber. The first and last leaves often display woodcuts to signal from a bookstall that the Frate had delivered a fresh blast. A generation later, Luther was to split Western Christendom with pamphlets that also fit any style of pocket, and also display distinctive woodcuts [ 300 ]. Luther’s covers were either decorative borders or violent satires, whereas Savonarola’s often reminded a man to contemplate his shortcomings.
萨沃纳罗拉于 1490 至 1498 年间在佛罗伦萨大教堂布道，听众拥挤得他不得不拉起帷幕，防止男性窥视女性[157]。他的声音在石砌深渊中回荡，那份威严在米开朗基罗耳畔萦绕数十年——即便萨沃纳罗拉本人已化作火焰消逝。 这场佛罗伦萨的宗教风暴蔓延至外部世界，更影响到未来时代——当萨沃纳罗拉将布道内容配以精准插图印刷成册时，迫使教廷发起反击。他将简洁而富有感染力的短篇论述印制成手册，小巧便携到人们在等渡轮或理发时都能从口袋中取出阅读。书页首尾常饰以木刻版画，在书摊上昭示着这位修士又一次震撼世人的呐喊。 一代人之后，路德同样以能塞进任何口袋的册子分裂了西方基督教世界，其封面同样印着醒目的木刻插画[300]。路德的封面要么是装饰性边框，要么是暴力讽刺画，而萨沃纳罗拉的封面则常提醒人们反思自身不足。
Battle by the printed word driven home by the printed picture was then as portentous as broadcasting is now, being as difficult for censors to jam. And indeed, Savonarola in the white silence of his cell [158] looked and acted like a radio broadcaster-a voice in a closet persuading millions.
印刷文字引发的论战，辅以印刷图像的冲击，其震撼力堪比当今广播，同样令审查者难以封锁。诚然，萨沃纳罗拉在牢房的寂静中[158]，其言行宛如广播播音员——一个密室里的声音，却能说服千万人。
