Savonarola Writing. Woodcut in Savonarola, della semplicita della Vita Christiana, Florence (Pacini), 1496
萨沃纳罗拉著作。木刻版画见于《萨沃纳罗拉论基督徒生活的简朴》，佛罗伦萨（帕奇尼出版社），1496 年

Florentine woodcut illustration (佛罗伦萨木刻插图)


Savonarola’s bonfires of vanities in 1497 must have consumed entire editions of Florentine stories and poems. Only three copies remain of a delicately saucy illustration to a love story written by a Renaissance pope [ 159 ]. Such lyric dalliance from the Holy Father would naturally have sparkled in a burning of worldly delights, but it is not so easy to explain the disappearance of early editions of the religious plays that Florence staged every Easter. Many of these sacre rappresentationi are known only in a 1555 reprint of 38 of them [ 160 ]. In this earliest gathering of miscellaneous plays ever published, each play opens with a cut of the angel who speaks the prologue, and then illustrates the action without showing any stage arrangements. At least one of these dramatic illustrations was copied from a little wood panel painted in Uccello’s workshop, probably for a chest or cupboard.
佛罗伦萨木刻插图 1497 年萨沃纳罗拉焚烧虚荣之火的行径，想必吞噬了整批佛罗伦萨故事与诗集。如今仅存三册文艺复兴时期教皇所著爱情故事的插图，其笔触既精致又带点俏皮[159]。 教皇的这般抒情嬉戏自然会在焚烧世俗享乐的烈焰中闪耀，但佛罗伦萨每年复活节上演的宗教剧早期版本消失之谜却难以轻易解释。这些"神圣剧作"（sacre rappresentationi）中，许多仅存于 1555 年重印的 38 部合集[160]。 在这部有史以来最早的杂剧合集里，每部剧作开篇都配有天使朗诵序幕的插图，随后通过画面展现剧情发展，却未呈现任何舞台布景。其中至少一幅戏剧插图源自乌切洛工坊绘制的小型木板画，很可能是为箱柜所作装饰。

Bronze statue by Andrea del Verrocchio at Or San Michele, Florence, 1478-80
安德烈亚·德尔·韦罗基奥创作的青铜雕像，位于佛罗伦萨圣米歇尔教堂，1478-1480 年
The longest series of Florentine woodcuts continued in use until printing wore out the blocks. For some 80 years, while German families were studying the Bible in German, Florentine families studied homilies on the Gospels and the Epistles in Tuscan, arranged as they were read in church during the year and always reprinted with the same 140 woodcuts. The publishers claimed that they had illustrated the folio so generously “to delight the buyer’s eye and to allow the senses to share in the consolation of the spirit.” Since most Florentine woodcuts were made while Botticelli was hypnotizing the town, his windblown grace naturally sweeps through many of these figures [161], raising the mirage of a return to adolescence with a magic that hovers between tenderness and impertinence.
佛罗伦萨木刻版画系列持续使用时间最长，直至印刷耗尽了木板。 约八十载光阴里，当德国家庭研读德文圣经时，佛罗伦萨家庭却在研习托斯卡纳方言的福音书与书信讲道集——这些经文按全年教堂诵读顺序编排，始终配以相同的 140 幅木刻版画。出版商宣称如此慷慨地为对开本配图，"既为悦目，亦为感官共享心灵慰藉"。 由于多数佛罗伦萨木刻版画诞生于波提切利令全城为之倾倒的时期，他笔下那股被风吹拂的优雅气质自然流淌于众多人物形象之中[161]，以游移于温柔与放肆之间的魔力，勾勒出重返青春的幻象。

Although the great Florentine artists seem just around the corner, none ever drew on a woodblock the way the great Venetians and Germans did. In Florence the guild shops of anonymous woodcutters transposed the discoveries of the major artists into a uniform style of knifework on blocks as wide as a narrow column of type (four inches), and all similarly bordered. These domestic miniatures lie in a civilized proximity to the disturbances of genius. When a woodcut of Doubting Thomas [ 162 ] appeared, Verrocchio’s bronze [ 163 ] had stood on the main street for over a decade, until Florentines could not imagine the miracle in the upper room taking place in any other way. The woodcut summarizes a monument the way some Athenian vase paintings summarize then familiar, now lost, Greek paintings and sculptures.
尽管伟大的佛罗伦萨艺术家们仿佛近在咫尺，却无人能像威尼斯与德国大师那样驾驭木版画技艺。在佛罗伦萨，匿名木刻工匠的行会作坊将大师们的艺术发现转化为统一的刻刀风格——木板宽度仅如窄版印刷字体（四英寸），边框亦千篇一律。这些本土微型作品与天才的颠覆性创作之间，存在着文明的距离。 当《多疑的托马斯》木刻版画问世时[162]，韦罗基奥的青铜雕像[163]已在主街矗立逾十年，以致佛罗伦萨人无法想象那间楼房里的奇迹以其他形式呈现。这幅木刻版画概括了一座纪念碑，正如某些雅典陶罐绘画概括了当时广为人知、如今却已失传的希腊绘画与雕塑。
Florence did not start to illustrate books with woodcuts until 30 years after Germany, and 60 years after a Florentine inventory had listed “woodblocks for playing cards and saints.” When at last, in 1490, the Florentines began to make up for lost time, they were so close to being beggared by wars and revolution that they had less than 15 years in which to make all the great illustrations they were ever to create. In contrast, Venice began a decade earlier, and kept quality for three centuries because the sea provided more dependably than banking, and the Venetian welfare state sedated civic unrest.
佛罗伦萨比德国晚了 30 年才开始用木刻版画装饰书籍，而早在 60 年前，佛罗伦萨的库存清单上就已记载了"用于制作扑克牌和圣徒画像的木刻版"。 当佛罗伦萨人终于在 1490 年开始弥补失地时，战争与革命已使他们濒临破产，仅剩不到十五年时间来完成所有伟大的插图创作。相比之下，威尼斯早十年起步，并凭借海运比银行业更可靠的收益，以及威尼斯福利国家对社会动荡的有效管控，在三个世纪里始终保持着卓越品质。

Business books (商业书籍)


Business books took on a modern look at Florence in 1491/92 when the first illustrated arithmetic published the present form of long division and illustrated the handsigns that still signal numbers across noisy auctions [164, 165]. About
1491/92 年间，佛罗伦萨的商业书籍呈现出现代风貌——首部插图版算术书不仅刊载了现代长除法的形式，更绘制了手势符号图示，这些至今仍在喧闹的拍卖场中传递数字信息[164, 165]。

164, 165

Woodcuts in Filippo Calandri, Aritmetica, Florence (Morgiani and Maganza), 1491/92
菲利波·卡兰德里《算术》中的木刻版画，佛罗伦萨（莫尔贾尼与马甘扎），1491/92 年


three years later Venice published the first instructions for double-entry bookkeeping. Florence managed to be the second Italian commercial center after Venice, and the second producer of books, in spite of lying away from the sea and aside from great trade routes. The city based her power on training the intelligence of her citizens, with more free schooling in 1400 than she was to have in 1800 . Her artists did not work for a court clique, but for hundreds of prosperous bankers and merchants who had an eye for a good thing, either in mortgages or Madonnas. The Florentine sense of industry and economy found pleasure in books of pocket size, and in the elegant sobriety of the first consistently uncolored woodcuts.
三年后，威尼斯出版了第一本复式簿记指南。尽管远离海岸且不在主要贸易路线旁，佛罗伦萨仍成功成为意大利第二大商业中心，以及第二大图书生产地。这座城市凭借培养市民智慧奠定根基——1400 年其免费教育资源远超 1800 年水平。 佛罗伦萨的艺术家们并非为宫廷小圈子服务，而是为数百位眼光独到的富庶银行家与商人创作——无论是抵押贷款还是圣母像，他们都懂得鉴赏价值。这座城市特有的勤勉与节俭精神，在袖珍书籍的精巧设计中得以彰显，更在首批始终如一的素色木刻版画中，展现出优雅的克制之美。
When American gold and silver shifted the base of Europe’s economy from land to cash, the new liquid coinage made Antwerp the first great international money market. To cope with fraud in the circulation of many kinds of currency, Flemish money-changers pocketed booklets hardly bigger than a cigarette lighter, containing woodcuts of current coins [166] and statements of their values in guilders. Larger Flemish coin indices were printed tall and thin to shelve with ledgers.
当美国金银将欧洲经济基础从土地转向现金时，新型流通货币使安特卫普成为首个国际金融中心。为应对多种货币流通中的欺诈行为，佛兰德兑换商随身携带的册子仅比打火机稍大，内含现行硬币的木刻版画[166]及其以盾币计价的价值表。 较大的佛兰德钱币索引则采用高瘦版式印刷，以便与账簿并排存放。
166
Venetian coin, obverse and reverse. Woodcut in les monnoyes d’or & d’argent, Ghent (Lambert), 1544
威尼斯硬币，正面与背面。木刻版画，载于《金银货币图鉴》，根特（兰伯特），1544 年

Lettering and writing (字体设计与书写)


The late Gothic letterers who deformed writing (sometimes to prevent forgery) or juggled letters out of men and animals [167] did not want to communicate so much as to decorate, the way Arabs decorated bowls and domes by swirling script. Germans, who clung to the semilegible Gothic black letter through the second World War, elaborated capitals in variations as labyrinthine as their musical variations [168]. To convolute this baroque B, the calligrapher said that he had “dipped his pen in his brains,” scorning the mechanics who drafted Roman capitals with ruler and compass. Italians felt otherwise as they gazed at the clarity of the great Roman letters that their triumphal arches display to this day like posters for a perpetual election. The ancient Roman letterer had first painted the stone with a flat brush that swelled and tapered curves, and ended straight strokes by neatly spreading them in thornlike serifs. (Greek letters are uniformly narrow.) The carver then grooved the stone to weatherproof the message, the way the Egyptian relief carver weatherproofed paintings.
字体与书写晚期哥特字体师们扭曲字形（有时为防伪造）或将字母变形为人形与兽形[167]，其目的与其说是传达信息，不如说是装饰——正如阿拉伯人以旋涡状文字装饰碗盏与穹顶。 德国人直至二战仍固守半可辨识的哥特黑体字，其大写字母的变体繁复如迷宫，恰似其音乐变奏的精妙[168]。 为使巴洛克式字母 B 更显繁复，书法家宣称自己"将笔尖浸入脑髓"，以此蔑视那些用直尺圆规绘制罗马大写字母的机械师。意大利人却另有一番见解——他们凝视着凯旋门上至今仍如永恒选举海报般清晰的伟大罗马字母时，便深有体会。 古罗马字匠先以平头刷在石上描绘，笔锋膨胀收束形成曲线，笔画末端则以荆棘状衬线收束整齐（希腊字母则统一狭窄）。随后石匠凿刻凹槽以防腐蚀铭文，其工艺与埃及浮雕师保护壁画如出一辙。
Lettering and writing  字体设计与书写
In the 1460s the archeologizing north Italians began to analyze the freehand antique capitals in rigid geometrical constructions, even as they began to codify Vitruvius’ Roman shop practice of architecture in the rigid regulations of the five orders of columns. Ever since the first publication in 1509 of capital letters constructed in Leonardo da Vinci’s circle at Milan [169], designers have labored to adjust hairbreadths in the matchsticks and washers of our printed letters without being free to reshape what must remain standard to be read without noticing. The lowercase letters you now are looking at derive from the script in which Charlemagne’s scribes copied Latin classics about 800 . When Renaissance scholars mistook these Carolingian manuscripts for autographs of Cicero’s contemporaries, they adopted the script for lowercase letters to go with the truly antique stone-cut capitals. This hybrid fossilized when the two sorts of letters were printed together
1460 年代，热衷考古研究的北意大利人开始将自由手绘的古风柱头纳入严谨的几何构造体系，与此同时，他们又将维特鲁威在罗马工坊实践的建筑理念，编纂成五种柱式体系的严苛规范。 自 1509 年米兰达·芬奇学派首次出版大写字母规范[169]以来，设计师们便致力于微调印刷字母中火柴棍与垫圈般的笔画间距，却始终无法自由重塑这些必须保持标准化的元素——唯有如此，字体才能在不被察觉的情况下被识别。 此刻映入眼帘的小写字母，其渊源可追溯至公元 800 年左右查理曼大帝抄写员誊录拉丁经典时使用的书体。当文艺复兴学者误将这些加洛林手稿视为西塞罗同时代人的亲笔原稿时，他们便采纳了这种书体作为小写字母，与真正古朴的石刻大写字母相配。当两种字体被并排印刷时，这种混合体便凝固成了活字印刷的化石。

170

《维琴察的卢多维科小手册：学习书写文书体》雕刻标题页，罗马（卢多维科·德利·阿里吉，人称维琴察人），1522 年

171
“Give others their due if you would enjoy your own.” Woodcut by Pedro Diaz Morante, Madrid, about 1630
“欲享其乐，当待人以礼。”佩德罗·迪亚斯·莫兰特木刻版画，马德里，约 1630 年

in Venice in the 1470 [ 211 ]. By then, Vatican scribes, perhaps following Venetian precedent, were beginning our modern handwriting by slanting and tying this book hand for swiftness and convenience. This new, elegant, compact lettering conquered Europe as italic when a papal scribe adapted it to cast type for printing the first, and instantly successful, pocket edition of a classic, the chubby little Virgil that Aldus published at Venice in 1502. Just 20 years later the same scribe published the chancery hand (cancellaresca) of the papal chancery itself in the first copybook for handwriting [170]. Many subsequent printed copybooks show how the fine Italian hand developed through the natural haste that saves lifting the pen off the paper by slurring more and more letters together.
在威尼斯的 1470 年[211]。 彼时梵蒂冈抄写员或许效仿威尼斯先例，开始将这种书写体倾斜连笔，由此催生现代手写体——既追求速度又注重便捷。当教廷抄写员将其改良为铸字体，用于印刷 1502 年阿尔杜斯在威尼斯推出的首部经典袖珍版《维吉尔诗集》（这部圆润小书甫问世即大获成功）时，这种优雅紧凑的新字体便以"斜体"之名风靡欧洲。 仅仅二十年后，同一位抄写员将教廷文书处的"教廷体"（cancellaresca）收录进首部书法练习本[170]。此后众多印刷版练习本清晰展现了意大利优雅字体的演变轨迹——为省去提笔动作，书写者通过将字母日益连贯地勾勒，在自然加速的书写过程中逐步发展出这种流畅书体。
Though Western handwriting can never depict character as forcibly as the Chinese script, the Spaniards at least made the chancery hand as decorative as-and more legible than-the Arabic flowed over their Moorish buildings [171]. Teutonic Europe showed its spirit again when a baroque Dutchman swung the tied Italian hand into a “strike” of swaggering illegibility [ 172 ]. Since publications of new hands did not immediately supersede old ones, the typical baroque penman wrote different hands for different uses, turning from a running chancery for the classics and polite correspondence to Gothic black letter for churchly texts and vernacular literature and to a crabbed, rapid “secretary” for accounts and inventories. A baroque painter, made aware through prints of many styles, seems like several artists when he draws-laboring over studies of anatomy, shading complete pictures of projects for submitting to patrons, jotting down ideas for compositions in a personal shorthand, or rendering pedantically for an engraver to copy without mistaking anything.
尽管西方的书写方式永远无法像汉字那样有力地展现性格，但西班牙人至少让公文体变得与摩尔式建筑上流淌的阿拉伯文同样富于装饰性——却更易辨识[171]。当巴洛克时期的荷兰人将意大利的连笔体挥洒成狂放不羁的"一笔挥就"时，日耳曼欧洲再次彰显了其精神[172]。 由于新字体问世后并未立即取代旧体，典型的巴洛克书法家会为不同用途书写不同字体：用流畅的公文体书写经典著作与礼仪信函，用哥特黑体书写宗教文本与通俗文学，用蜿蜒快速的"秘书体"记录账目与清单。 一位巴洛克画家通过版画接触多种风格，其创作过程宛如数位艺术家并存：他既要苦心钻研解剖学研究，又要为提交给赞助人的项目绘制完整阴影图稿，还要用个人速记法记录构图灵感，更需为刻版师提供一丝不苟的稿件以确保毫无差错。

Lettering and writing  字体设计与书写

Perspective (视角)


After the antique world and the Middle Ages had seen objects singly and separately, the Renaissance began to embed things in a continuous matrix of space. Perhaps as early as 1424 / 25 1424 / 25 1424//251424 / 25 some Tuscan painters and mathematicians correlated the artist’s sensuous impressions with the scientist’s intellectual analysis. Disciplines so distinct could parley in Renaissance Italy, where a man might still aspire to know something about everything. Scientists needed art to clarify the world’s complexity, and artists needed science to form principles for analyzing appearances. With mathematical perspective a painter could depict objects in their “real” size within an imaginary framework stretching to the horizon. The artifice enabled a Florentine to engrave the first convincing print of a city as only a hawk could then see it. This four-foot-wide overflight was an assembly of six prints, of which a unique impression of one section [ 173 ] survived until World War II. (Big city views interested residents, who normally threw them away when dust had dimmed them after hanging on a wall.) The complete engraving of Florence was copied in a big woodcut (also unique), and was adapted in the Nuremberg Chronicle.
透视法古希腊罗马时期与中世纪将物体孤立呈现之后，文艺复兴时期开始将事物置于连续的空间矩阵中。或许早在 1424 / 25 1424 / 25 1424//251424 / 25 时期，托斯卡纳的画家与数学家便已将艺术家的感官印象与科学家的理性分析相互关联。在文艺复兴时期的意大利，这些截然不同的学科得以交融对话——当时的人们仍渴望通晓万物。 科学家需要艺术来阐释世界的复杂性，艺术家则需要科学来建立分析表象的原理。借助数学透视法，画家能在延伸至地平线的虚构框架中，以物体"真实"尺寸进行描绘。这项技艺使佛罗伦萨人得以雕刻出首幅令人信服的城市版画——其视角唯有当时的鹰隼才能企及。 这幅四英尺宽的俯瞰图由六幅版画拼合而成，其中一幅[173]的唯一印本存续至二战时期。（都市景观虽受居民青睐，但通常因悬挂墙面后蒙尘褪色而遭弃置。）完整的佛罗伦萨版画被复制为大型木刻（亦属唯一存世），并被《纽伦堡编年史》采用。
From 1483 to 99 perspective was elaborated as an end in itself in Milan by two Tuscans, Leonardo da Vinci and Fra Luca Pacioli, leading to Pacioli’s publication of the first series of perspective renderings [174]. These puzzles stimulated Germans to contrive even more outlandish fantasies [175] as perspective grew into a game for astonishment. While Pacioli was still working on his book, the
1483 至 1499 年间，两位托斯卡纳人——莱昂纳多·达·芬奇与弗拉·卢卡·帕乔利——在米兰将透视法发展为独立艺术形式，最终促成帕乔利出版了首批透视绘图集[174]。 这些谜题激发德国人构想出更离奇的幻想[175]，随着透视法逐渐演变为令人惊叹的游戏。当帕乔利仍在撰写其著作时，


Tuscan discovery somehow reached Jean Pèlerin, a canon of the cathedral of Toul, who used it for the first clear manual of perspective drawing. The French genius for discovering charm at home inspired the most personal and endearing of all perspective illustrations. These are the first prints that present rooms that we might settle into as we explore the canon’s wine cellar, his chapter house, his courtyard with an espaliered tree, and even his bedroom [ 176 ]. The very coziness of these
托斯卡纳的发现不知如何传到了图尔大教堂教士让·佩勒兰手中，他据此创作了首部清晰的透视绘画手册。 法国人发掘本土魅力的天赋，催生出最富个性且令人心生亲切的透视图集。这些早期版画首次呈现了可供我们驻足探索的空间：从教士的酒窖、议事厅、篱架树簇拥的庭院，乃至他的卧室[176]。正是这些场景的温馨质感——

This Roman’s foreshortening of façades from a mole’s-eye point of view [177] completed the lesson of Mantegna [196] by showing baroque painters how to open ceilings upward through an illusion of soaring colonnades into clouds and the toes of lolling gods.
木刻版画或许限制了它们的传播范围，不像巴洛克时期伟大建筑师维尼奥拉为更拘泥形式的时代所作的正式指导那样广为流传。 这位罗马人以鼹鼠视角呈现的建筑立面透视法[177]，通过展现如何运用高耸柱廊幻象将天花板向上延伸至云端与神祇趾尖，完善了曼特尼亚[196]的艺术启示，为巴洛克画家开辟了新的创作维度。
The last original application of perspective to art came from the scenery designer Ferdinando Bibiena, who made small opera stages seem immense by painting backdrops with buildings seen at an angle, like ships driving at you, with their walls flying backward right and left into the wings [ 178 ]. After painters and architects had monopolized perspective for over three centuries, the French mathematician Gaspard Monge took it back in the 1790 s to invent the descriptive geometry by which engineers are able to calculate spatial relations exactly enough to design the interchangeable parts of modern machinery.
透视法在艺术领域的最后一次原创应用来自布景设计师费迪南多·比比耶纳。他通过绘制倾斜视角的建筑背景——如同迎面驶来的船只，其墙壁向左右两侧延伸至舞台侧幕——使小型歌剧舞台显得恢弘壮阔[178]。 在画家与建筑师垄断透视法应用逾三个世纪后，法国数学家加斯帕尔·蒙日于 1790 年代将其重新引入，创立了描述几何学。这项理论使工程师能够精确计算空间关系，从而设计出现代机械中可互换的零部件。

Maps (地图)


About A.D. 100 in Alexandria, Claudius Ptolemy listed cities, rivers, and mountains by their latitude and longitude, and also drew maps that proved too complicated for copyists. In the 15th century his lists served Germans in Italy to found modern map-making. A German Benedictine, Master Nicolas, used these lists to construct maps that underlie the earliest engraved illustrations to Ptolemy, published in 1477 at Bologna, 1478 at Rome, and 1482 at Florence. The Bolognese and Florentine engravings were not reprinted, but the more informative Roman ones, which were the first to be started, went through four editions and were used by Columbus. They were printed in Rome by a German and were engraved, possibly by the engraver of the E E EE series of “taroc” cards [ 16 ], under the supervision of Conrad Sweynheym of Mainz, who had introduced book printing into Italy in 1465. Applying his training in making matrices for casting type, Sweynheym stamped the copperplates with steel punches for the lettering and circles to locate towns [ 179 ]. Master Nicolas’ geographical experience supplied the schemes for indicating rivers, mountains, and forests, and cleared the seas of fanciful monsters. The publication of three expensive sets of Italian engravings in five years shows the interest in geography that was soon to launch the voyages of discovery. After these first copperplates, maps were printed for 50 years in the cheaper woodcut, whose coarse detail sufficed to render the earth while it was still empty. But as surveyors added features to Europe, and as explorers doubled Ptolemy’s old world with a new one, the need for finer detail turned Flemish map-makers to copperplate even before the Antwerp book illustrators took to engraving for esthetic reasons.
公元 100 年左右，克劳狄·托勒密在亚历山大港绘制地图时，按经纬度标注了城市、河流与山脉，所绘制的地图表现得过于复杂，以致抄写者难以复刻。15 世纪时，他的地图目录为在意大利的德国人奠定了现代制图学的基础。 德国本笃会修士尼古拉斯大师据此绘制地图，成为托勒密最早的雕版插图基础。这些地图于 1477 年在博洛尼亚、1478 年在罗马、1482 年在佛罗伦萨相继出版。博洛尼亚版与佛罗伦萨版未再版，而信息更丰富的罗马版（最早启动的版本）历经四次修订，并被哥伦布所采用。 这些地图由一位德国人于罗马印刷，可能由制作 E E EE 系列"塔罗"卡牌的雕刻师[16]在美因茨人康拉德·斯温海姆监督下完成——此人早在 1465 年就将书籍印刷术引入意大利。 施韦因海姆运用其铸字模制备技术，以钢制冲头在铜版上压印文字与标注城镇的圆圈[179]。尼古拉斯大师凭借地理经验设计了河流、山脉与森林的标注方案，并清除了地图上虚构的怪兽。五年间三套昂贵的意大利版画集相继出版，彰显了即将催生发现航程的地理热潮。 在首批铜版地图问世后，五十年来地图多采用成本较低的木刻印刷，其粗犷的细节足以呈现尚未开发的地球面貌。但随着测量师不断完善欧洲地貌，探险家将托勒密所载旧世界扩展为新大陆，对精细细节的需求促使佛兰德制图师转向铜版印刷——这甚至早于安特卫普书籍插画家出于美学考量采用雕版技术。
After edifying inland scholars, maps began to go to sea. Northward explorers found it hard to calculate polar distance and direction on early maps that distorted
在启迪了内陆学者之后，地图开始走向海洋。向北探索的航海者发现，早期地图因畸变而难以计算极地距离与方向。
Figure 59: 179 Germany in the time of Caesar. Engraving in Ptolemy, Cosmografia, Rome (Buckinck), 1478
图 59：凯撒时代的德国。摘自托勒密《宇宙志》，罗马（巴金克版），1478 年铜版画
Figure 60: 179 Germany in the time of Caesar. Engraving in Ptolemy, Cosmografia, Rome (Buckinck), 1478
图 60：凯撒时代的德国。摘自托勒密《宇宙志》，罗马（巴金克版），1478 年铜版画

180 The New World. Engraving by Gerard Mercator, Netherlands, mid-16th century
180 《新世界》。杰拉德·墨卡托版画，荷兰，16 世纪中期

them by spreading apart the meridians where they actually converge. A practical solution was found by Gerard Mercator, a Fleming who combined enough skill of hand with knowledge of mathematics to be able to plot and engrave the first maps [180] whose presentation did not have to be essentially altered until our age of air travel. He founded the succession of map engravers in the seaports of Antwerp and Amsterdam who, from the 1530 until nearly 1700, expanded coastlines and lengthened rivers to keep pace with reports from explorers.
通过将实际汇合的经线向外展开来解决这个问题。弗拉芒人杰拉德·墨卡托找到了切实可行的解决方案——他兼具精湛的手工技艺与数学知识，得以绘制并雕刻出首批地图[180]，其呈现方式直至我们这个航空时代才需要进行根本性调整。 他开创了安特卫普与阿姆斯特丹海港地区制图师的传承体系。自 1530 年至近 1700 年间，这些制图师不断延伸海岸线、拉长河流，以匹配探险家们不断更新的航海报告。
In the 1660s Louis XIV made map production a government concern, as it is almost everywhere today. The French then perfected the modern self-evident symbols, and indicated altitudes by contour lines. Old wall maps, like most big prints, have mostly perished. In 1554 Mercator engraved a six-sheet wall map of Europe, of which Plantin in Antwerp sold 868 impressions from 1558 to 76. One survives.
1660 年代，路易十四将制图纳入政府管理范畴——这在当今几乎已成为普遍做法。法国人随后完善了现代制图的自明符号体系，并通过等高线标示海拔高度。古老的挂墙地图，如同多数大型印刷品，大多已消亡殆尽。 1554 年，墨卡托雕刻了一幅六幅拼接的欧洲墙地图，安特卫普的普兰丁在 1558 至 1576 年间售出 868 份复本。现存仅此一幅。

Copyright and patronage (版权与赞助)


Any Greek or Roman with pen, ink, papyrus, and patience was free to copy any text for sale. Printing introduced copyright (then called privilege), not to protect the author, but to protect the printer’s unprecedented investment in a press, type, stacks of paper, and years of training.
版权与赞助制度任何拥有笔墨、莎草纸和耐心的希腊或罗马人都可自由抄写文本用于贩售。印刷术的出现催生了版权制度（当时称为特权），其目的并非保护作者，而是保障印刷商对印刷机、活字、成堆纸张及多年技艺所作出的史无前例的投资。
The first recorded privilege conveyed absolute monopoly: in 1469, when the German John of Speyer proposed to inaugurate printing in Venice, the Senate
最早有记载的特权赋予了绝对垄断权：1469 年，德国人施派尔的约翰提议在威尼斯开创印刷业时，参议院
promised to exclude all other printers and all foreign books. Luckily, John’s prompt death cleared the way for the competition that was to make the glory of the Venetian presses. Once the Senate realized the value of printing, they encouraged it wisely. In 1486 the Senate insured a worthy format for a history of Venice by granting a monopoly for the book to the author’s chosen printer. Since few authors earned royalties until 1667, when Milton sold Paradise Lost for £ 10 £ 10 £10£ 10 with the promise of £ 5 £ 5 £_(5)£_{5} more for each of the next two printings, penniless authors existed as they always had, by sinecures or by flattering the rich for handouts, the way Horace had lauded Maecenas until the name connoted any generous patron. Renaissance authors did not dissipate their praise throughout the text but saved it for dedicatory prefaces to be detached in case the patron proved stingy or died.
承诺排除所有其他印刷商及外国书籍。幸运的是，约翰的早逝为竞争扫清了道路，这场竞争最终成就了威尼斯印刷业的辉煌。参议院意识到印刷业的价值后，便明智地予以扶持。1486 年，参议院为确保威尼斯史著作的体面出版，特授予作者指定的印刷商该书的垄断权。 直至 1667 年弥尔顿以 £ 10 £ 10 £10£ 10 的价格售出《失乐园》，并约定后续两次印刷各获 £ 5 £ 5 £_(5)£_{5} 收益前，鲜有作家能获得版税。因此穷困潦倒的作家们仍如往昔般，靠着闲职或谄媚富人换取施舍度日——正如贺拉斯曾颂扬梅塞纳斯，直至"梅塞纳斯"一词成为所有慷慨赞助者的代名词。 文艺复兴时期的作家不会在书中四处散布赞美之词，而是将其保留在献辞序言中——这些序言可被单独摘下，以防赞助者吝啬或殁世。
Long practice made a writer, not an artist, the first to dedicate a print to a patron. In 1515, when the German emperor’s astronomer and historiographer, Johannes Stabius, mapped the constellations in two woodcuts whose star figures were drawn by Dürer, he left the useful Northern Hemisphere to sell itself unsponsored, but dedicated the Southern Hemisphere to the Cardinal of Salzburg [181]. Stabius protected himself, but not Dürer, with a ten-year privilege from his imperial patron.
长期实践使作家而非艺术家成为首位将版画献给赞助人的创作者。1515 年，当德国皇帝的天文学家兼史官约翰内斯·斯塔比乌斯绘制两幅木刻星图时——其星体图案由丢勒绘制——他将实用的北半球星图作为无赞助作品自行销售，却将南半球星图献给萨尔茨堡红衣主教[181]。 斯塔比乌斯为自己争取了十年特权，却未将此特权延伸至丢勒，此举源于其与帝国赞助人的契约。
In 1569 the French autocracy armed itself against the press by forbidding any book to appear without a privilege. This restriction was extended to prints in 1685. In the mid-16th century the religious wars wasted so much money that it probably did not pay to dedicate prints. Then, in 1569, Martino Rota engraved a dedication to the Prince of Savoy in the margin of his Last Judgment after Michelangelo, a practice that engravers continued until sales to the general public paid them more than patrons.
1569 年，法国专制政权通过颁布禁令，禁止任何书籍未经特许出版，以此对抗印刷业。1685 年，这项限制被扩展至版画领域。16 世纪中叶，宗教战争耗费巨资，使得为版画题词或许已无利可图。 1569 年，马蒂诺·罗塔在模仿米开朗基罗的《最后的审判》版画边缘刻上献给萨伏伊亲王的题词，此类做法延续至版画家们发现面向大众销售比依赖赞助人更能获利之时。
Private patronage, for all its uncertainties and humiliations, may have benefited an artist more than copyright laws, which define the plagiarism of words more easily than that of images. Marcantonio bought Dürer’s prints in the Piazza at Venice to engrave some 60 copies of them [336]. When Dürer was in Venice in
私人赞助虽充满不确定性与屈辱，却可能比版权法更惠及艺术家——后者对文字剽窃的界定远比图像剽窃更容易。马尔坎托尼奥在威尼斯广场购得丢勒的版画，将其复制约六十份[336]。当丢勒造访威尼斯时——
Copyright and patronage  版权与赞助

181

The Southern Constellations. Woodcut by Dürer, 1515
《南天星座》。丢勒木刻版画，1515 年
Tomaginas axt Manidionales.
托马吉纳斯·阿克斯特·马尼多尼莱斯。
Copyright and patronage  版权与赞助
1506 he may have protested the copying of his AD, which cut into his sales of his originals, for some of Marcantonio’s plagiarisms omit it. If these two non-Venetians quarreled, the Venetian Senate ignored it, though in 1521 it granted a copyright to a native for some otherwise unknown woodcut illustrations to the Pentateuch.
1506 年，他可能曾抗议他人复制其广告，因这影响了其原作的销售——马可安东尼奥的部分剽窃作品便省略了该广告。若这两位非威尼斯人在争执，威尼斯元老院对此置若罔闻，尽管 1521 年曾为一位本国人授予版权，涉及《摩西五经》中若干未见于其他渠道的木刻插图。
The first descriptive copyright for an artist’s designs was granted in France in 1524 by Francis I to Geoffroy Tory, who had spent money to refashion the persistently Gothic Parisian books of hours by cutting metal relief blocks in imitation of Venetian woodcuts (à l’italienne) [ 251 ]. In 1527 and 29 he imitated the borders of insects and flowers (à la moderne) [ 182 ] that Flemings had been painting in prayer books since the 1480s [183]. For six years Tory’s plagiarized illustrations and borders (histoires et vignettes) were not to be copied with backgrounds in white, gray, or red, nor to be reduced or enlarged, under a fine of 25 marcs. The edict must have been flouted, for in 1526 Tory obtained a privilege for his “illustrations, vignettes, friezes, borders, headpieces, and ornaments [entrelacs]” with the fine raised to 100 marcs. But the pirating of designs went merrily on, and today it riots among designers of furniture and dresses.
1524 年，法国国王弗朗索瓦一世首次授予艺术家乔弗鲁瓦·托里设计作品的描述性版权。托里曾斥资改造巴黎那些固守哥特风格的祈祷书，仿照威尼斯木刻风格（à l’italienne）雕刻金属浮雕版块[251]。 1527 年与 1529 年间，他模仿了弗拉芒画家自 1480 年代起在祈祷书中绘制的昆虫与花卉边饰（à la moderne）[182]。 六年来，托里剽窃的插图与边饰（histoires et vignettes）被禁止以白、灰、红三色为背景复制，亦不得缩放尺寸，违者罚款 25 马克。 该法令显然遭到藐视，1526 年托里为其"插图、小插画、饰带、边框、标题装饰及花纹[entrelacs]"获得特权保护，罚金提高至 100 马克。然而设计盗版行为仍猖獗蔓延，时至今日在家具与服装设计师中尤为泛滥。

Anatomy in Florence (佛罗伦萨的解剖学)


The first grandiose Florentine design to be printed, and the only print ever to be signed by a great Florentine artist, probably represents Titus Manlius Torquatus battling a Gaul for his torque, or gold collar, which marked him as a chieftain [ 184 ]. Against the somber wall of grapes and sorghum, the figures stand out as pale as in a monumental niello [113]. Vasari says that Pollaiuolo was the first artist to flay cadavers in order to paint and model the bones and muscles in the modern-that is, Renaissance-manner. Since he was a sculptor as well as a painter, Pollaiuolo may have modeled his skinned bodies in wax manikins, which he then bent into various positions and turned front and back to engrave these five men battling their mirror images. Some of the figures raise one arm as flayed bodies were made to do when suspended from a beam by the neck and one wrist to keep them from revolving while being studied all around. Mapping every single exposed muscle, Pollaiuolo engraved figures that Leonardo ridiculed as sacks of nuts [185]. But when Pollaiuolo was not instructing, but painting
佛罗伦萨的解剖学首幅印制的宏伟佛罗伦萨设计，也是唯一由佛罗伦萨伟大艺术家亲笔署名的版画，很可能描绘了提图斯·曼利乌斯·托尔夸图斯与高卢人争夺其象征酋长身份的扭曲项圈（金项圈）的场景[184]。在葡萄与高粱构成的阴郁背景墙前，人物形象如巨型黑釉工艺品般苍白凸显[113]。 瓦萨里记载，波拉伊奥洛是首位解剖尸体以现代（即文艺复兴时期）手法描绘骨骼与肌肉的艺术家。身为雕塑家兼画家，他可能先用蜡制人体模型塑造剥皮躯体，再将其摆成各种姿势并前后翻转，从而刻画出这五位与镜像自我搏斗的战士。 部分人物单臂上举的姿态，源于剥皮尸体被悬于横梁时颈部与单腕受力的状态——此举可防止尸体旋转，便于全方位观察。波拉约罗精准刻画每块暴露肌肉，其雕刻人物却被达芬奇嘲讽为"坚果袋"[185]。但当波拉约罗不再传授技艺，转而进行绘画创作时——

185
The Battle of the Naked Men (detail)
185 《裸身男子之战》（局部）


Figure 64: 186 Hercules and the Hydra. Painting by Pollaiuolo, Florence, about 1460
图 64：186 赫拉克勒斯与九头蛇。波拉伊奥洛绘，佛罗伦萨，约 1460 年
[186], he knew well enough how to bulge the pulling muscles furiously above the inactive rest. His ten men, reaching, stooping, stretching, and twisting, compress a whole course of artistic anatomy into one picture. This print changed art more than any other print ever made in Florence, by imposing the naturalistic study of muscle and bone through dissections just when Mantegna’s engravings [187] revived the Roman sculptor’s structural logic.
[186]，他深谙如何让牵引肌肉在静止的肌群之上狂暴地隆起。画中十名男子伸展、弯腰、拉伸、扭转的身姿，将整套艺术解剖学浓缩于一幅画面之中。 这幅版画对艺术的影响超越佛罗伦萨历代所有版画——它通过解剖研究强行引入肌肉骨骼的自然主义研究，恰逢曼特尼亚的版画[187]重振罗马雕塑家的结构逻辑之际。

Mantegna (曼特尼亚)


Mantegna established the painter’s dominance over Italian printmaking with some 35 engravings in the style of his drawings. He must himself have engraved seven of them with his unique sculptural authority that develops stylistically through the Madonna of Humility [ 195 ], the two Bacchanals, the Battle of the Sea Gods, and the horizontal Entombment [ 190 ] to the Risen Christ [ 196 ]. Since part of the Sea Gods [187] was copied in a manuscript in the style of the 1460s, and other engravings of his inspired paintings and drawings of the early 705, Mantegna must have been engraving by the 60s, when he was in his 30s. If so, his bold scale and large format could have started Pollaiuolo magnifying the niello style in his Battle of the Naked Men [ 184 ].
曼特尼亚以约 35 幅仿其素描风格的铜版画，确立了画家在意大利版画领域的统治地位。其中七幅必由他亲手雕刻，其独特的雕塑感在《谦卑的圣母》[195]、《两幅酒神狂欢图》、《海神之战》及横向构图的《安葬基督》[190]至《复活的基督》[196]等作品中形成风格演进。 鉴于《海神之战》[187]部分内容曾以 1460 年代风格复制于手稿，且其 70 年代初的绘画与素描作品亦衍生出其他版画，曼特尼亚必然在六十年代——即三十余岁时——便已开始创作版画。 若果真如此，他大胆的尺度与大开本创作，或许启发了波拉伊奥洛在其《裸体男子之战》[184]中放大黑镌工艺的运用。
The two artists must have met when Mantegna visited Florence in 1466. Since both made drawings that other artists used, they may well have thought to invest their time on copperplates, whose many prints would earn them more dividends than the same effort spent on drawings. Both Pollaiuolo’s Battle and Mantegna’s engravings sold to painters who carelessly dripped paint on surviving impres-
这两位艺术家必然是在曼特尼亚 1466 年造访佛罗伦萨时相遇的。由于两人都创作过其他艺术家使用的素描稿，他们很可能认为将时间投入铜版画更为划算——相较于素描，铜版画能通过大量复刻版带来更丰厚的回报。波拉伊乌奥洛的《战役》与曼特尼亚的蚀刻版画均售予画家之手，这些画家在现存的印版上不慎滴落颜料——

sions. Mantegna further invested money by hiring at least one professional engraver to copy his drawings. The earliest document proving that a painter had commissioned engravings is an angry, disingenuous complaint from an otherwise unknown Simone di Ardizoni of Reggio, “painter and engraver,” who wrote in 1475 to Duke Lodovico Gonzaga that when he came to Mantua, Mantegna made him “good and friendly offers.” But when Simone’s friend Zoan Andrea, “a Mantuan painter,” lamented that he had been “robbed of prints, drawings, and medals,” Simone, “out of pity,” worked for him for four months “to remake the said prints.” On hearing this, “the devil [lo indemoniato] Andrea Mantegna” first threatened them and then one night had both of them beaten and left for dead. When he then accused Simone of sodomy, Simone fled to Verona “to complete the said prints.” What had angered Mantegna? Did Simone, a tramp who claimed to have “visited 40 cities,” repay the “good and friendly offers” by engraving Mantegna’s drawings for Zoan Andrea? Were the stolen prints that Simone “remade” actually unauthorized copies after Mantegna that Mantegna had seized as his rightful property? impression
曼泰尼亚还出资雇佣至少一名专业雕刻师复制其素描作品。最早证明画家曾委托制作版画的文献，是来自雷焦一位名不见经传的西莫内·迪·阿尔迪佐尼——自称"画家兼雕刻师"——于 1475 年致洛多维科·贡扎加公爵的信件。信中他愤愤不平地抱怨道，当自己造访曼图亚时，曼泰尼亚曾向他"提出慷慨友善的邀约"。 但当西蒙的朋友佐安·安德烈亚——"一位曼图亚画家"——哀叹自己"被盗走版画、素描和奖章"时，西蒙"出于怜悯"为他工作四个月"重制了那些版画"。 听闻此事后，"被恶魔附体[lo indemoniato]的安德烈亚·曼特尼亚"先是威胁二人，继而某夜命人将他们殴打至濒死。当他指控西蒙内犯有鸡奸罪时，西蒙内逃往维罗纳"以完成前述版画"。 究竟何事激怒了曼特尼亚？这位自称"游历过四十座城市"的流浪汉西蒙尼，竟以刻制曼特尼亚为佐安·安德烈亚所作的素描来回报"善意友好的邀约"？而西蒙尼"重制"的被盗版画，是否实为未经授权的曼特尼亚作品复制品——正是曼特尼亚视作正当财物而夺回的那些？

Several of Mantegna’s subjects were indeed engraved twice [ 188, 189] , one version at least undoubtedly being by Simone di Ardizoni.
曼特尼亚的若干题材确实被两次刻印[188, 189]，其中至少有一个版本无疑出自西蒙·迪·阿尔迪佐尼之手。
Mantegna forced his hired professional to unlearn his craft conventions in order to use the graver like a quill in a way that only a painter could have discovered by experimenting on his own. Where professionals worked the entire copper surface, Mantegna reserved ample blanks of air to absorb the energy that he compressed into the center. (The thrifty scrapbook collectors who later trimmed off what seemed to them waste paper left not a single impression to record the size of some of the copperplates.) By drawing with a graver to clear everything for mass and rhythm, Mantegna raised the craft of printmaking to an art as absolute as any. His rage at living too late to be an antique Roman drove him to timeless assaults on the imagination, expressed in the first prints that are not period pieces requiring historical explanation. His grandeur shows to the full in the rare early impressions that still wear the velvet of lines that granulate (how?) and mat into shadows [190]. Yet he designed so ruggedly that he kept his power even after the worn copper skinned the line [ 191 ].
曼特尼亚强迫雇佣的铜版画师摒弃技法惯例，以画家特有的实验精神，将刻刀化作鹅毛笔般运用。当专业画师填满整块铜版时，曼特尼亚刻意留白，让那些被压缩在画面中心的能量得以释放。 （后来那些节俭的剪贴簿收藏家，将他们眼中多余的纸张裁剪殆尽，导致某些铜版画的尺寸记录荡然无存。） 曼特尼亚以刻刀为画笔，为质感与韵律扫清一切障碍，将版画工艺升华为与任何艺术形式同样纯粹的艺术。他因生不逢时未能成为古罗马艺术家而愤懑，遂以超越时空的想象力发起冲击，在首批无需历史注解的版画中迸发为艺术宣言。 其恢弘气魄在罕见的早期印本中尽显无遗——那些线条仍如天鹅绒般柔润，颗粒感（如何？）与阴影交融[190]。然而他的设计如此刚劲，即便铜版磨损导致线条剥落[191]，作品仍保持着磅礴力量。
The reproductive prints after Mantegna fail to show us whether the originals were frescoes, tempera paintings, some kind of drawings, or even relief sculptures, but they surpass most black and white photographs in distinguishing between
曼泰尼亚的复刻版画未能向我们揭示原作究竟是湿壁画、蛋彩画、某种素描，抑或是浮雕，但它们在区分不同媒介方面的能力远胜于大多数黑白照片。
adjacent areas of paint of the same paleness or darkness [192,193]. The clearly articulated engravings of the Magi sets the main group of the painting in a summary of the surroundings. By consciously encasing the finished study in a suggestion of preliminary sketching, Mantegna became the inventor of the “unfinished” work of art half a century before Michelangelo.
相邻区域的颜料呈现相同的苍白或深邃色调[192,193]。三贤士清晰刻画的浮雕将画作主体置于环境概括之中。曼特尼亚通过刻意将完成的习作包裹在似初稿的暗示中，比米开朗基罗早半个世纪就开创了"未完成"艺术品的先河。
Mantegna was the only great painter who was more moved by sculpture than painting. He worked on several sculptural projects, and often painted figures as if they were carved in low relief. His interest must have started as a boy of 12 in Padua when Donatello, aged about 60, came there from Florence for a decade of sculpture. Mantegna adapted one of Donatello’s favorite themes [194] for his earliest engravings [ 195 ], which in turn conveyed the group to Rembrandt for a total transformation two centuries later [490]. The north Italian pioneering in archeology inspired Donatello and Mantegna with a passion for the antique marbles that lucky spades were then unearthing. These were not the great Greek sculptures revealed to us when the British Museum bought the Parthenon marbles in 1816, but the ancient Roman copies of Greek originals. The Romans had imported plaster molds of famous statues for reproducing in marble with a simple contriv-
曼特尼亚是唯一一位对雕塑比对绘画更着迷的伟大画家。他参与过多个雕塑项目，常以浅浮雕手法描绘人物形象。这种兴趣源于十二岁那年在帕多瓦的经历——当时六十岁的多纳泰罗从佛罗伦萨来到此地，展开为期十年的雕塑创作。 曼特尼亚将多纳泰罗最钟爱的主题[194]融入其早期版画创作[195]，而该主题又在两个世纪后经伦勃朗重新演绎，实现彻底的艺术蜕变[490]。 北意大利考古学的先驱探索，点燃了多纳泰罗与曼特尼亚对古罗马大理石雕塑的热忱——当时幸运的挖掘者正不断发掘这些珍品。这些并非 1816 年大英博物馆购得帕特农神庙雕塑时向世人展现的希腊巨作，而是古罗马人仿制的希腊原作复本。罗马人曾引进著名雕像的石膏模具，通过简单装置将其复制成大理石雕塑——

ance that located the points to which the carver cut down into the stone. Between the points, the freehand cutting tended to smooth over details and to simplify the anatomy into a grand balance as declamatory and as formal as an actor’s mask. This solid geometry of the body, deduced from the box of the torso and its junction with arms and legs, became still clearer and more teachable in Mantegna’s engravings. His prints launched the antique scheme into the mainstream of European art at about the same time that Pollaiuolo’s Battle launched the study of the body from anatomical dissections. Mantegna’s grand, ready-to-wear carapace descends through the mannerists, Veronese, Poussin, Boucher, Ingres, Canova, and Daumier, while Pollaiuolo’s deeply probed interplay of bone, muscle, and flesh became the study of Leonardo, Michelangelo, Ribera, Géricault, Rodin, and Eakins. Both approaches held their own until about 1905 when the fauves in Paris began to distort anatomy for expressiveness.
雕刻家在石头上刻出的切割点，正是通过这种方式定位的。在这些点之间，自由手绘的切割往往会抹平细节，将人体解剖结构简化为一种宏大的平衡——如同演员面具般庄重而正式。这种从躯干盒体及其与四肢连接处推导出的身体几何结构，在曼特尼亚的版画中变得更加清晰且易于传授。 他的版画将古典艺术体系引入欧洲艺术主流，恰逢波拉伊奥洛的《战役》推动解剖学研究成为人体研究的起点。 曼特尼亚宏伟的现成甲壳式构图经由风格主义者、韦罗内塞、普桑、布歇、安格尔、卡诺瓦与杜米埃传承，而波拉伊乌奥洛对骨骼、肌肉与血肉的深度探索则成为达芬奇、米开朗基罗、里贝拉、杰利科、罗丹与伊金斯的研究对象。 两种方法各执一词，直到 1905 年左右，巴黎的野兽派开始扭曲解剖结构以追求表现力。
Mantegna must have drawn antique sculptures in steep perspective as they lay on the ground or stood high in niches. An upward look at grandeur became his supreme stage effect, which he put into general circulation for baroque ceiling painters through his last engraving of the Risen Christ [ 196 ]. He had frescoed this
曼特尼亚必定曾以陡峭透视法描绘古雕塑——或横卧于地，或高立壁龛。仰视宏伟之景成为他最精妙的舞台效果，并通过其最后的版画作品《复活的基督》[196]，将此技法广泛传播给巴洛克天顶画师。他曾为这幅作品创作过湿壁画。

Christ above the door of Sant’ Andrea in Mantua, where Saint Andrew, as the city’s patron, stood at the left, and the centurion Longinus earned a place at the right for having collected Christ’s blood in a vial that was-and still is-the town’s treasure. Mantegna did not engrave the finished fresco (now weathered and repainted), but the underdrawing [ 197 ], hidden by his coloring until the plaster layers were peeled off in 1961. Being the first draftsman on copper, he chose to publish, not his colored painting, but his volumetric line.
曼托瓦圣安德烈教堂门楣上的基督像：圣安德烈作为城市守护神立于左侧，而百夫长朗基努斯因用小瓶盛接基督之血而获右侧席位——该瓶至今仍是城中至宝。 曼特尼亚并未刻录这幅已完成的壁画（现已风化并重新粉刷），而是将其底稿[197]——这幅作品被其彩色绘画层掩盖，直至 1961 年石膏层被剥离才重见天日。作为铜版画领域的先驱，他选择出版的并非彩色画作，而是其立体线稿。
While Mantegna’s paintings had only a local effect until photographs made them known, his engravings were the first commanding Italian works of art to cross the Alps since the Roman emperors had deputized their bronze and marble likenesses to overawe the provinces. Mantegna’s prints circulated widely until the 1520s, when the huge production of Marcantonio’s Roman workshop superseded them as models of Italian composition and drawing of the nude. But the explosive authority of Mantegna’s engravings has always moved and astonished great individuals like Dürer, Ribera, and Rembrandt. As late as 1892 Aubrey Beardsley died in a hotel room thumbtacked with facsimiles of all of them.
曼特尼亚的绘画作品在摄影术普及前仅具地方影响力，而其版画却是自罗马皇帝派遣青铜与大理石雕像震慑行省以来，首批跨越阿尔卑斯山脉的意大利艺术杰作。 曼特尼亚的版画广为流传直至 1520 年代，此时马尔坎托尼奥在罗马工坊的大量作品取代了它们，成为意大利构图与裸体绘画的典范。 但曼特尼亚版画的震撼力始终令杜勒、里贝拉、伦勃朗等大师动容惊叹。直至 1892 年，奥布里·比尔兹利在酒店病榻离世时，墙上仍密布着其所有版画的复制品。

Caricature (漫画)


Sir Thomas Browne wrote that “When men’s faces are drawn with resemblance to some other animals, the Italians call it, to be drawn in caricature.” Caricare means to charge selected features so as to bring out the latent animal whose nature shapes the man, according to the followers of Aristotle. For his scientific classifications, Leonardo da Vinci collected faces as impersonally as he might have collected striking butterflies. A perhaps leonine old man [ 198 ] was engraved after a lost Leonardo sketch, probably by one of the engravers trained by Mantegna to preserve the autographic individuality of a drawing. The malice that Greeks aimed at slaves and foreigners reappeared when Titian drew, not men resembling animals, but animals acting like men [ 199 ]. He was not belittling the Laocoön group [ 343 ], which he admired, but the Galenist anatomists who believed that ancient Romans and apes had had identical organs. (“If so, here is how your ancient heroes must have looked.”)
漫画家托马斯·布朗爵士曾写道："当人的面容被描绘得酷似其他动物时，意大利人称之为漫画式描绘。"根据亚里士多德学派的观点，"caricare"意指通过强化特定特征，揭示潜藏于人性的动物本质。为构建科学分类体系，达·芬奇收集面容时如同采集绚丽的蝴蝶般客观冷静。 一位或许颇具狮首特征的老人[198]，其版画取材于达·芬奇遗失的素描稿，很可能出自曼特尼亚门下某位版画家之手——他们擅长在版画中保留原作的独特个性。 当提香笔下不再是类人动物，而是类人动物时[199]，希腊人针对奴隶与异族的恶意再度显现。他并非贬低自己推崇的《拉奥孔群像》[343]，而是嘲讽那些坚信古罗马人与猿类器官相同的盖伦学派解剖学家。（"若真如此，你们的古代英雄想必是这般模样。"）
Though Sir Thomas Browne had seen caricatures (possibly by Annibale Carracci) in Italy in the 1630s, in 1665 Bernini found that no Parisian had heard of the word or the idea. Bernini was the first to caricature noblemen instead of slaves and to cajole at least his Italian victims into sharing the joke. The French drew few caricatures until the 1820s, when the triumphing bourgeoisie pursued caricature until it became almost a French art. Daumier and his editor Philipon followed English precedent by using caricature as the most dreaded political attack [ 200 ]. The supreme caricaturists have been masters of the grand manner, like some of the late Greek sculptors and moderns such as Leonardo, Michelangelo, Bernini, and Dau-mier-all artists who explored the pitfalls that they must avoid if they were to make men look noble.
尽管托马斯·布朗爵士早在 1630 年代就曾在意大利见过漫画（可能是安尼巴莱·卡拉奇的作品），但 1665 年贝尔尼尼发现巴黎人对此词汇和概念一无所知。贝尔尼尼开创性地将漫画对象从奴隶转向贵族，并至少能让意大利受害者们心领神会地分享笑料。 法国人直至 1820 年代才开始创作漫画，当时崛起的资产阶级将漫画推向巅峰，使其几乎成为法国的艺术形式。多米埃及其编辑菲利蓬效仿英国先例，将漫画作为最令人畏惧的政治攻击手段[200]。 真正的漫画大师皆是宏大风格的宗师，如古希腊晚期雕塑家及达·芬奇、米开朗基罗、贝尔尼尼、杜米埃等现代艺术家——他们皆在探索如何避免使人物显得高贵的陷阱。

Hawkers and walkers (小贩与行人)


By the mid-1400s the northern interest in daily life had started north Italians making the first pictures of street criers, who may perhaps have bawled their wares and services more often in the complex Italian cities than in the more countrified German towns. The earliest print of a street crier [ 201 ] has some of the sturdy Virgilian elegance of peasants in Ferrarese paintings. It may be all that is left of a series that could have given Annibale Carracci the idea of drawing the hawkers and walkers of his native Bologna in the 1580 s or 90 s . Annibale’s pen drawings have disappeared, but two sets of copies, etched after his death, record now forgotten aspects of city life and inspired imitations for two centuries. His picture peddler [ 202 ] is helping to dispose of the overproduction of paintings that occurred in Bologna in the late 1500 s.
小贩与行者 15 世纪中叶，北方对日常生活题材的关注促使意大利北部艺术家创作了首批街头叫卖者的画作。这些叫卖者或许在错综复杂的意大利城市中吆喝商品与服务的频率，远高于乡村气息浓厚的德国城镇。现存最早的街头叫卖者版画[201]，其质朴形象承袭了费拉拉画派农民形象中维吉尔式的刚劲优雅。 这或许是系列作品中仅存的遗作，曾启发安尼巴莱·卡拉奇在 1580 至 90 年代描绘家乡博洛尼亚的街头小贩与行者。安尼巴莱的钢笔画虽已湮没，但两套在他逝世后蚀刻的复制品，记录了如今已被遗忘的城市生活图景，并激发了长达两百年的艺术模仿。 画中这位画贩[202]正协助处理 16 世纪末博洛尼亚画作过剩的积压。

don. His trudging impresario shoulders a peepshow equipped with so-called vuesd’optique [ 203 ]. These were engraved by the hundred thousand in Paris and Augsburg with titles at the top in reverse to be read the right way around in a slanting mirror. Being of uniform size, dozens of vues-d’optique, glued end to end, made a ribbon of pictures that the peepshow operator cranked in for the customer, who peered through a large lens at city squares and palaces and celebrated battles sliding past the magic mirror to movie music from the barrel organ.
唐。这位蹒跚的经纪人扛着一个装有所谓"透镜幻灯片"的窥视表演装置[203]。这些幻灯片在巴黎和奥格斯堡以万计地雕刻印制，顶部标题采用倒置排版，需通过斜面镜才能正向阅读。 数十幅尺寸统一的透镜画首尾相接，粘合成一条画卷。窥视表演者为顾客转动画卷时，观众透过大镜头凝望城市广场、宫殿与著名战役的景象，这些画面在手摇风琴奏出的电影配乐中，从魔镜前滑过。
About 1810 Thomas Rowlandson etched a charming set of cries, one of which shows a London lass giving a letter and the glad eye to a brisk postman [ 204 ]. He serves the first postal system efficient enough to circulate illustrated periodicals to the mass of the population.
约 1810 年，托马斯·罗兰森蚀刻了一组生动的叫卖场景，其中一幅描绘了伦敦姑娘递信时对干练邮差抛媚眼的画面[204]。他所服务的邮政系统效率之高，足以将插图期刊广泛传播至大众群体。

During the centuries when street criers posed unconsciously for artists, some 300 sets of prints recorded the noisy life of Bologna, Rome, Venice, Paris, Vienna, London, Saint Petersburg, and New York. Art lost a vivid theme when modern city traffic crowded these itinerants off the pavements, and easier circulation brought customers to goods rather than goods to customers.
在街头叫卖者无意间成为艺术家画中人的几个世纪里，约 300 组版画记录了博洛尼亚、罗马、威尼斯、巴黎、维也纳、伦敦、圣彼得堡和纽约的喧嚣生活。当现代城市交通将这些流动商贩挤离人行道，便捷的物流让顾客主动寻货而非货物送上门时，艺术便失去了这个鲜活的主题。

Book covers (书封)


After Augsburg publishers industrialized book illustration in the 1470s, they started to catch the buyer’s eye with covers printed on thin paper yellowed to look like expensive fresh leather. The central panel of one of these shows the so-called pomegranate pattern [ 206 ], suggesting that the leather bindings had in turn imitated cloth book covers of perishable Italian silks. After about 1490 Ferrarese and then Venetian binders sewed small books cheaply and prettily into stiff cardboard covers printed with classical ornament [ 207 ]. A block sometimes printed three panels-for front, back, and the spine between-but without lettering, so that the cover might serve for any octavo.
书封 1470 年代奥格斯堡出版商将书籍插图工业化后，开始用薄纸印刷的封面吸引买家眼球——这些封面经特殊工艺泛黄，仿若昂贵的新鲜皮革。其中一本书的中央面板呈现所谓的石榴纹样[206]，暗示皮革装帧本身又模仿了易损的意大利丝绸布面书封。 约 1490 年后，费拉拉及威尼斯装订师开始将小册子廉价而美观地缝制进硬纸板封面，其上印有古典装饰图案[207]。单个印版有时可印制三幅面板——用于封面、封底及夹在中间的书脊——但不带文字，使封面能适用于任何八开本书籍。
Venetian publishers sometimes printed plain catch titles in bold type on the outside of the first and last leaves to identify the book whichever way it lay on the shop counter. Such cover titles must have caught Dürer’s eye on Venetian bookstalls, for he raised them to a high art in 1511 when he published his woodcut sets of the Apocalypse [ 208 ], the Great Passion, and the Life of the Virgin. No one has ever flourished Gothic letters with such illegible exultation as Dürer, who would have made the lordliest writing master of them all.
威尼斯出版商有时会在书首页和书尾页的外侧印上粗体字的简洁标题，以便无论书籍在书店柜台上如何摆放都能识别。这些封面标题必定曾吸引过丢勒在威尼斯书摊的目光，因为他于 1511 年出版《启示录》[208]、大受难记和圣母生平的木刻版画集时，将这种形式升华为高超的艺术。 无人能像丢勒这般挥洒哥特字体，以近乎狂喜的笔触书写出令人难以辨认的字迹——他本可成为最卓越的书法大师。

In the 1690 special printed covers were eclipsed for a time by papers printed in colored patterns [570] that could be cut to fit books of any size and brightened a shop counter like a flower bed. The old Venetian pasteboard covers reappeared as rococo masterpieces by the 1760 s when they dressed the souvenir pamphlets that Venetian patricians presented to their guests at a wedding, the installation of a procurator of Saint Mark [ 209 ], or the ordination of a noble nun. Grandees who could no longer afford gilded morocco could still splurge with bright printing on blue or rose cardboard.
1690 年，特制印刷封面一度被彩色图案印刷纸张取代[570]，这些纸张可裁剪成任意尺寸以适配书籍，在书店柜台上缤纷绽放，宛若花坛。 到 1760 年代，古老的威尼斯纸板封面以洛可可风格杰作之姿重现，装帧于威尼斯贵族赠予宾客的纪念册中——无论是婚礼、圣马可总督就职典礼[209]，抑或贵族修女授职仪式。那些无力购置镀金摩洛哥皮革的显贵们，仍可挥霍于蓝底或玫瑰色卡纸上绚丽的印刷工艺。
Publishers shipped books out of town in casks, unbound to fit the curve of the cask and to save weight. Over the counter, books were sold either bound or unbound, depending on the clientele. About 1640 Bosse’s bookstall [ 462 ] displays only bound volumes to elegant Parisians. In 1658 Comenius’ little woodcut [450] shows a more academic bookshop in Nuremberg. Here the public has access to books in sheets, individually wrapped and stacked flat. Each stack is identified by the book’s title on a paper inserted between the packaged sheets. Guarded by the counter, the more expensive bound books are shelved upright, seemingly presenting their fore edges, where each volume’s title would be inked. In London by the 1760s, so many books were offered folded and sewn for binding that booksellers identified them by pasting printed labels on the spine. But if a British dealer bound a set of books in leather, he wasted no money on gilt titles, but merely stamped the volume numbers to insure selling complete sets. Full information on the paper backs and paper covers was probably first printed on German almanacs in the late
出版商将书籍装入木桶运出城外，为适应桶身曲线并减轻重量，这些书均未装订。柜台售书时，根据顾客需求提供装订本或散页本。约 1640 年，博塞的书摊[462]仅向优雅的巴黎人展示装订成册的书籍。 1658 年科梅纽斯的木刻版画[450]呈现纽伦堡更具学术气息的书店。顾客可在此选购散页书籍——每册独立包装平整堆叠，每摞书间夹有标注书名的纸条。柜台后方陈列着昂贵的精装书，竖立于书架上，书脊处清晰可见墨印的卷首标题。 1760 年代的伦敦，大量折叠缝纫待装订的书稿涌现，书商们通过在书脊粘贴印刷标签来区分。但若英国商人将成套书籍装订成皮面，他们不会浪费金钱在烫金书名上，仅需盖上卷号印章以确保成套售出。纸质书脊与封面的完整信息，很可能最早出现在 18 世纪末的德国年历上。
1700 s 1700 s 1700 s1700 s and appeared by 1818 in Paris. These bright-colored paper wrappers that usually repeat the title page [662] were thrown away when the purchaser had his book bound to his personal taste, as many Frenchmen still do.
1700 s 1700 s 1700 s1700 s 并于 1818 年前后现身巴黎。这些色彩鲜艳的纸质封套通常重复着标题页的内容[662]，当购书者按个人喜好装订书籍时便会被丢弃——时至今日，许多法国人仍保留着这一习惯。
Cloth bindings began to be mass-produced about 1770, when London wholesalers experimented with canvas, which, however, tended to sweat the glue. By 1825 cotton cloth, sized to prevent its absorbing the glue, was revolutionizing trade binding from a handicraft to a machine industry, much the way the spinning jenny had revolutionized weaving in the 1780s. In 1832 an English hot press began to emboss and gild trade bindings, making them too durable and pretty to discard like the plain old canvas ones. To keep fancy trade bindings fresh on the counter, publishers protected them with printed dust jackets that purchasers immediately discarded. The earliest surviving removable dust jacket seems to be a London one of 1833. Victorian ornamental buckram bindings [210] enticed Englishmen and Americans each autumn to buy gift annuals and slim volumes of verse as Christmas presents.
布面装订约于 1770 年开始批量生产，当时伦敦批发商尝试使用帆布，但这种材料容易导致胶水渗出。到 1825 年，经过防吸胶处理的棉布彻底改变了商业装订业——从手工行业转型为机械工业，其变革意义堪比 1780 年代珍妮纺纱机对织造业的革命性影响。 1832 年，英国热压技术开始为商业装帧压花镀金，使其既坚固又美观，不再像昔日素面帆布装帧那样易被弃置。为保持精装书在书店陈列时的崭新感，出版商为其加装印刷书衣——而这些书衣往往被购买者当即丢弃。 现存最早的可拆卸护封似乎是 1833 年伦敦出品。维多利亚时期的装饰性硬布封面[210]每年秋季都吸引着英美读者购买年度礼品书和薄诗集作为圣诞礼物。

Title page and frontispiece (标题页与扉页)


Run-of-the-mill medieval manuscripts open with a solid block of writing that starts with an incipit: “Here begins the book of . . .” and continues without wasting parchment into the first words of the text. Such manuscripts end with a colophon: “Finished writing by me, John Doe, at Paris, Ash Wednesday, 1400. Praise be to God.” Until after 1500, printers followed this manuscript form with but one surviving exception in 1476. This was a title page so modern that it listed author, title, place of publication, printer-publisher, and date in Arabic numerals [211]. The surrounding frame is the first Venetian woodcut printed with metal type, and the earliest print of classical ornament [ 243 ].
标题页与扉页寻常中世纪手稿开篇即以整块文字起始，以"此处开启……之书"为开篇语，紧接着不浪费羊皮纸地直入正文首句。此类手稿以题记作结："由我，约翰·多伊，于巴黎，1400 年圣灰星期三完成抄写。愿主蒙福。" 直至 1500 年后，印刷商们仍沿袭手稿形式，仅存 1476 年一例例外。该书的标题页设计极为新颖，不仅标注了作者、书名、出版地、印刷商兼出版商，更以阿拉伯数字标明出版日期[211]。其周边装饰框采用威尼斯木刻技法，系首次以金属活字印刷，亦是古典装饰图案最早的印刷品[243]。

Woodcut frontispiece by Erhard Reuwich in Bernhard von Breydenbach, Sanctae Peregrinationes, Mainz (Reuwich), 1486
埃尔哈德·罗伊维希所作木刻扉页，刊于伯恩哈德·冯·布雷登巴赫《圣徒朝圣记》，美因茨（罗伊维希），1486 年
These unacceptable innovations began the career of three Germans from Augsburg, where books had been massively illustrated for five or six years. One of the three, Bernard Pictor (Painter), presumably drew and cut the architectural framework, despite its Italian look. (German printers left their taste at home when they took their skills abroad.) The inventive Erhard Ratdolt [ 74 ] probably selected and laid out the information even though he never afterward designed so prophetic a title page in all his subsequent 42 years of printing.
这些令人难以接受的创新，开启了三位奥格斯堡德国人的职业生涯——当时当地书籍已大规模采用插图长达五六年之久。其中一人伯纳德·皮克托（画家）据推测绘制并雕刻了建筑框架，尽管其风格颇具意大利风貌。（德国印刷商将技艺带往海外时，却将审美品味留在了故土。） 富有创造力的埃尔哈德·拉特多尔特[74]很可能负责了信息的筛选与排版，尽管在他之后长达 42 年的印刷生涯中，再未设计出如此具有预见性的标题页。
Many grand manuscripts in antiquity and the Middle Ages began with a fullpage frontispiece showing the author at his desk. The first elaborate printed frontispiece alluding to the author was designed by the Dutch artist Erhard Reuwich for Breydenbach’s Pilgrimage to the Holy Land [ 212 ]. The bejeweled lady (Jerusalem) dominates the arms of the author and his two traveling companions. Here, 20 years after the Dutch blockbooks [ 21 ] had introduced shading in parallel lines, Reuwich darkens his shadows by intersecting parallels in two directions to make a grid of crosshatching that complicated the knifework. Reuwich’s invention of the allegorical frontispiece was combined with Ratdolt’s layout for a title page in 1516 when
古代及中世纪的许多宏伟手稿皆以整页扉页开篇，描绘作者伏案书写的场景。首幅精美印刷扉页中暗喻作者形象的设计出自荷兰艺术家埃尔哈德·罗伊希之手，用于布雷登巴赫的《圣地朝圣记》[212]。佩戴珠宝的女子（象征耶路撒冷）凌驾于作者及其两位旅伴的盾徽之上。 此时距荷兰木刻本[21]引入平行线阴影技法已逾二十载，鲁维希通过双向交叉平行线形成网格状交叉阴影，使刀工更为复杂。1516 年，鲁维希发明的寓言式扉页与拉特多尔特设计的标题页版式相融合，
Holbein, aged 19, released the imagination of book designers by varying title borders for Swiss publishers. No artist ever invented so many different kinds of title pages: architectural frames with figures, storytelling landscapes, borders of running men and animals, and formal Italianate ornament. His Table of Cebes title border [ 213 ] unfolds the course of man’s life in a kind of Pilgrim’s Progress so picturesquely that he redrew it several times. His widely copied Cleopatra border [324] started a craze for perspective tricks that led to dizzy assemblages of scaffolding [ 361 ].
19 岁的霍尔拜因为瑞士出版商设计了多种书名边框，由此释放了书籍设计师的想象力。从未有艺术家创造过如此丰富的标题页样式：带人物的建筑框架、叙事性风景、奔跑人物与动物组成的边框，以及典雅的意大利式装饰。 其《塞贝斯之表》标题边框[213]以朝圣之旅般的画风展开人生历程，画面如此生动，以致他数次重绘此作。广为流传的《克娄巴特拉》边框[324]则掀起透视技巧热潮，最终催生出令人眩晕的脚手架组合[361]。
When book illustration turned from woodcut to copperplate, the great cost of engraving plus the double presswork usually constricted a book’s decoration to an author portrait that could also be sold separately, or to a frontispiece that summarized the text in one gorgeous volley of allegory. For such frontispieces, Rubens perfected the full baroque treatment with figures as heroically round as sculpture [ 429 ]. Curiously enough, Bernini, the virtuoso stone carver, made his frontispieces look like drawings [ 214 ]. The most optical of sculptors, and a magician
当书籍插图从木刻转向铜版雕刻时，高昂的雕刻成本加上双重印刷工序，通常将书籍装饰限制在可单独售卖的作者肖像，或是以华丽的寓言画面概括文本的扉页插图。 对于这类扉页，鲁本斯将巴洛克风格发挥到极致，人物造型如雕塑般浑圆雄伟[429]。耐人寻味的是，石雕大师贝尔尼尼的扉页却呈现出素描般的质感[214]。这位最具视觉效果的雕塑家，堪称一位魔术师。

with light on marble, Bernini teases the eye with his dog-eared paper that ruffles away in a mist. This witty artifice makes one regret that he condescended to design an engraving only when begged to do so by someone as important as a Jesuit general.
伯尼尼用光影在大理石上嬉戏，那张卷角的纸张在雾气中飘散，戏弄着观者的视线。这般机巧的艺术手法令人扼腕，他竟只在耶稣会总会长这般显赫人物的恳求下，才屈尊设计了一幅版画。
Every title page or frontispiece, according to the Dutch painter Gérard de Lairesse in 1707, absolutely had to include Fame blowing her trumpet. Further, “a frontispiece must 1 : please the eye, 2 : do credit to the author and the artist, 3 : help to sell the book.”
据荷兰画家热拉尔·德·莱雷斯 1707 年所述，每幅扉页或题名页都必须包含吹响号角的"声名女神"。此外，"题名页必须：1. 赏心悦目；2. 彰显作者与艺术家的声誉；3. 助力书籍销售。"
After the title page had absorbed the visual delight of the whole baroque book, it dwindled to a margin of mean moldings in the cold dawn of the Age of Reason, and it has never since regained its glory.
标题页在吸收了整部巴洛克书籍的视觉魅力之后，于理性时代的寒冷黎明中萎缩为一圈寒酸的装饰线脚，从此再未重现昔日荣光。

Milanese woodcuts (米兰木刻版画)


Today’s Italian publishing, distributed by mechanized transport, centers in Milan, but when printing began, Milan’s mule transport could not compete with Venice’s water freight. The small editions of old Milanese books were still further reduced by destroying soldiers who kept sweeping down the high-
米兰木刻版画当今意大利出版业依托机械化运输网络，以米兰为中心。但印刷术初兴之时，米兰的骡马运输难以与威尼斯的水路货运抗衡。古老米兰书籍的微量印本更因频遭蹂躏而愈发稀少——那些士兵不断沿着高地——

受难者。安德烈亚·索拉里奥木刻版画

way of Lombardy. Milanese woodcuts often copy Venetian ones. The fewer originals strike the eye with their open drawing and their knifework, which is rougher and bolder [ 215 ] than what the pressure of production developed in busier Venice and Florence. Milan’s first and greatest picture book is a Mirror of the Soul, showing the life of Christ in 76 episodes, many of which are seldom depicted elsewhere. The rare scene of Christ taking leave of his mother [ 216 ] could have suggested Dürer’s including it among the woodcuts of his Little Passion and Life of the Virgin.
伦巴第风格。米兰木刻常仿效威尼斯作品。少数原创之作以开放式线条与刀工见长，其粗粝而大胆的技法[215]，远胜于威尼斯与佛罗伦萨因生产压力催生的繁复风格。米兰首部且最伟大的图册《灵魂之镜》，以七十六幅场景展现基督生平，其中诸多情节在其他地区鲜少见于描绘。 基督与母亲告别的珍贵场景[216]，或许启发了丢勒在《小受难》与《圣母生平》木刻集中收录此题材。
These Milanese cuts are as plain and four-square as the paintings of Ambrogio Borgognone, who had come home to Milan four years earlier. If, in fact, Borgognone drew these illustrations, he may also have learned to cut them himself, for the knifework improves toward the end, instead of worsening like the work of many professional cutters in haste to be done with a long chore. The cuts show no effect from Leonardo da Vinci, who had been in Milan for 15 years, but Leonardo’s impact is clear in a large woodcut ( 15 by 11 inches) by his younger contemporary, Andrea Solario [ 217 ]. This print is known only in modern impressions from the chipped and battered block. The ruin makes one regret that big prints and drawings have always fared worse than little ones.
这些米兰式雕刻作品，其朴素方正的风格恰似安布罗焦·博尔戈尼奥的画作——这位画家四年前才重返米兰故土。倘若这些插图确系博尔戈尼奥所绘，他或许也自学了雕刻技艺，因为作品后期的刀工日趋精进，并未如许多专业雕刻师为尽快完成冗长任务而草率收尾。 这些版画未见达·芬奇的痕迹——这位大师已在米兰生活十五载。但其影响清晰可见于同时代年轻艺术家安德烈亚·索拉里的大型木刻版画（15×11 英寸）[217]。现存仅有现代复刻版，原版木板早已残缺不堪。如此损毁令人扼腕，大尺寸版画与素描向来比小幅作品更难幸存。

Full tide in Venice (威尼斯涨潮时分)


Unlike Florence, with its terse frugality, Venice-La Serenissima-flaunted her opulence on expansive pages of ornament in folios sailing forth on ships that brought back paper for printing more folios. Her bulky missals for the use of Salisbury reached England by the fleet that touched at Southampton while making for Flanders each summer until 1532. Early Venetian presses published more books than all the rest of Italy together. Her printers risked few first editions but made the best editions of books that had proved popular elsewhere. Competition reduced the price of printing to one third of that at Rome. Then, in 1596, Pope Clement VII’s Index of Prohibited Books suddenly enforced a censorship that collapsed the Venetian industry from 125 presses to 40 , reducing the annual average of publications from about 75 to about 35 , while the city’s applications for copyright slipped from 24 in 1596 to seven in 1597.
威尼斯的鼎盛时期不同于佛罗伦萨的简朴节俭，威尼斯——这座"至高无上的共和国"——在华丽的装饰页上炫耀着她的富丽堂皇。这些对开本书籍乘船远航，而归航的船只又运回纸张，用于印刷更多对开本。她为索尔兹伯里制作的厚重弥撒书，每年夏季经停南安普敦驶往法兰德斯的船队，一直运抵英格兰直至 1532 年。 早期威尼斯印刷厂的产书量远超意大利其他地区总和。当地印刷商鲜少冒险出版首版书籍，却精于制作已在别处广受欢迎的精品版本。激烈竞争使印刷成本降至罗马的三分之一。 然而 1596 年，教皇克莱门特七世颁布的《禁书目录》突然实施审查制度，导致威尼斯印刷业从 125 家印刷厂骤减至 40 家，年均出版量从约 75 种降至 35 种，该市版权申请量也从 1596 年的 24 项骤降至 1597 年的 7 项。
But until 1596, Venice created taste for all Europe by modernizing classical ornament for its first splendid use in books [ 211 ] as in architecture. The sumptuous urbanity of her Herodotus border [ 218 ] of 1497 was copied in the first full Renais-
但直至 1596 年，威尼斯才通过将古典装饰现代化，为整个欧洲开创了审美风尚——这种装饰首次在书籍[211]与建筑中璀璨呈现。其 1497 年出版的《希罗多德》卷边[218]所展现的奢华都市风情，被首部完整的文艺复兴时期著作所效仿——

218
Woodcuts in Herodotus, Historiae, Venice (Gregoriis), 1494
希罗多德《历史》木刻版画，威尼斯（格雷戈里出版社），1494 年
219
Woodcuts in Breviarium Trajectense, Gouda (Fratres Collationis), 1508
《特拉杰滕日课经》中的木刻版画，豪达（校订会修士），1508 年
sance decoration for a northern book [ 219 ]. The Venetian masterpiece, when reproduced photomechanically in the 1890s, started Englishmen and Americans designing books like it for the next 30 years. The border’s bold flow of black and white encloses a vignette at the bottom. Such tiny, yet uncluttered vignettes had been appearing independently in Venetian books for ten years to become models for Holbein [ 328 ] and to set the scale for French books.
威尼斯杰作的北欧书籍装饰[219]。当这幅作品在 1890 年代通过照相制版技术复制后，英国与美国的设计师们在随后的三十年间纷纷效仿其风格设计书籍。 边框以黑白两色大胆流动，底部环绕着一幅小插图。这类精巧而不杂乱的小插图在威尼斯书籍中已独立出现十年之久，不仅成为霍尔拜因的范本[328]，更奠定了法国书籍的版式基准。
The little Herodotus picture, which may represent Hercules choosing between ease and effort, is one of the first of the Venetian pictorial riddles that abounded from the time of Giovanni Bellini in the 1490 s until the Tiepolos of 300 years later. The compactness of the island city may have brought painters closer to poets than elsewhere, or the painters may have become more literary by illustrating so many books.
那幅小幅的希罗多德画作，或许描绘了赫拉克勒斯在安逸与艰辛间抉择的场景，堪称威尼斯绘画谜题的开端。这类谜题自 1490 年代乔瓦尼·贝利尼时期兴起，直至三百余年后的提埃波罗家族仍层出不穷。这座岛屿城市的紧凑格局，或许让画家们比其他地方的同行更接近诗人，又或许画家们因绘制大量书籍插图而愈发通晓文学。

Hypnerotomachia Poliphili (《波利菲洛的梦游》)


Francesco Colonna wrote his freakish book, The Strife of Love in a Dream, for Renaissance snobs who excluded the vulgar by reserving knowledge as the arcane perquisite of a clique. In a practically impenetrable jargon of Latin, Greek, and Italian, he adapted the form of Dante’s Divine Comedy to an allegorical dream in which Poliphilus (the lover of the antique City) wanders with Polia (the City herself) through minutely inventoried ruins and inscriptions. The author concocted “Egyptian” hieroglyphics by mixing symbols from Roman coins with actual instruments of sacrifice carved on the Temple of Vespasian in Rome [220]. The motto of the emperor Augustus, semper festina lente (always speed forward deliberately) appears as a circle for eternity, a dolphin for speed, and an anchor for deliberation [221]. The book’s publisher, Aldus Manutius, made the dolphin and anchor famous by adopting it as his printer’s mark two years later. In wider consequence, the Hypnerotomachia, Aldus’ only richly illustrated publication, started grandees symbolizing their aspirations by combining an image and a motto in an emblem to represent them like a personal
《梦中爱争》弗朗切斯科·科隆纳为文艺复兴时期的势利之徒撰写了这部怪诞之作，书名直译为《梦中爱争》。这些精英分子将知识视为小圈子的神秘特权，以此排斥平民阶层。 他以几乎令人费解的拉丁语、希腊语和意大利语混合术语，借鉴但丁《神曲》的结构，构筑出寓言式梦境：爱慕古城的波利菲洛斯与象征古城的波利亚，在精确考据的废墟与铭文中徘徊。 作者将罗马钱币符号与罗马韦斯帕芗神庙上真实的祭祀器具雕刻相融合，虚构出"埃及"象形文字[220]。奥古斯都皇帝的座右铭"semper festina lente"（永远审慎地加速前进）被演绎为象征永恒的圆环、代表速度的海豚与寓意审慎的锚[221]。 该书出版商阿尔杜斯·马努修斯两年后将海豚与锚组合为印刷商标，使之广为人知。更深远的影响在于：《梦魇战记》作为阿尔杜斯唯一精美插图的出版物，开创了贵族们通过结合图像与箴言的徽章来象征个人抱负的先例——如同专属的个人徽章。

223,224 龙。木刻版画出自《波利菲洛的梦境之战》，威尼斯（阿尔杜斯出版社），1499 年；木刻版画出自《波利菲洛之梦的论述》，巴黎（凯弗出版社），1546 年

trademark. Separately, the image or motto would only generally suggest a temperament; together, they strove to describe one individual only.
商标。单独来看，图像或标语通常仅暗示某种气质；而二者结合，则力图描绘唯一个体。
Such semisecret identifications obsessed the courts and academies of Europe until nearly 1800. Hundreds of manuals and dictionaries associated mottoes with images [ 222 ]; in 1588 emblems composed Pope Gregory XIII’s entire biography; in 1640 the Jesuits featured emblems in a huge volume commemorating their order’s centennial. The emblem became such an international expression that even the bare symbolic image without the motto (scales of justice, laurel wreath) signaled unmistakably from palace façades or the painted canvas of festival decorations. When the word spoke for the absent picture, it produced the poetry of intricate imagery that we call metaphysical if it is written in English.
这类半秘密的象征识别法令欧洲宫廷与学界痴迷不已，直至近 1800 年。数百部手册与词典将格言与图像相配[222]；1588 年，教皇格列高利十三世的完整生平由象征图案构成；1640 年，耶稣会士在纪念该教派百年诞辰的巨著中大量运用象征图案。 纹章成为如此国际化的表达方式，即便仅凭象征图像（如天平、月桂冠）而无格言，也能在宫殿外墙或节日装饰画布上传递清晰无误的信息。当文字代言缺席的图像时，便催生出精妙绝伦的意象诗学——若以英语书写，我们称之为玄学派。
The Hypnerotomachia woodcuts [ 223 ] look like a more accomplished work by the clean and elegant illustrator of the Venetian Ovid of 1497 [232], who was perhaps Benedetto Montagna. Such pure outlines were already becoming old-fashioned by 1499, when other woodcuts were being shaded. The illustrator’s felicitous invention of solid black accents recurs rarely until they formed a style in the age of Aubrey Beardsley [ 707 ]. Aldus composed his choice illustrations in formations of type that end chapters in the shape of a V or an X . Type and illustration balance with the nearly inhuman perfection of a book elaborated by the precious for the few.
《梦魇之战》的木刻版画[223]，其风格更接近 1497 年威尼斯版《奥维德》[232]那位笔触清雅的插画家——或许正是贝内代托·蒙塔尼亚——更成熟的作品。至 1499 年，当其他木刻版画开始运用阴影技法时，如此纯粹的轮廓线条已然显露过时之态。 插图师巧妙运用纯黑块面强调的技法，此后鲜有复现，直至奥布里·比尔兹利时代才形成独特风格[707]。阿尔杜斯将精选插图编排成字体阵列，以 V 形或 X 形构图收束各章。字体与插图的平衡，堪称为少数精英精心雕琢的典籍，其完美程度几近超凡脱俗。
Inevitably, the Hypnerotomachia set the taste for private presses the world over, since it was published for a public so restricted that ten years after its appearance the backer still had unsold copies on his hands. At this sad juncture, the French invaders under Francis I seem to have discovered the book, for in 1545 the Aldine press reprinted it with most of the illustrations, though without bothering to shape the type, and in 1546 a French translation came out in Paris with woodcuts exqui-
《梦魇之战》不可避免地在全球范围内掀起了私人印刷的热潮，因为它的发行对象如此有限，以至于十年后，资助者手中仍有未售出的库存。 值此困境之际，弗朗索瓦一世统领的法军似乎发现了这部著作——1545 年，阿尔迪出版社虽未重新排版，仍以原版插图为主体重印了该书；1546 年巴黎更推出法语译本，配以精美绝伦的木刻插画。
sitely adapted to the French taste [ 224 ], perhaps by Jean Goujon. The Parisian printer also harmonized picture and type, and with such care that when he made some woodcut initials too dark, he canceled them by pasting lighter ones on top, as if to demonstrate that perfection demands pains in any age.
这幅作品显然是为迎合法国人的审美而创作的[224]，或许出自让·古琼之手。这位巴黎印刷师还精心协调了插图与文字的协调性，其用心程度可见一斑：当某些木刻大写字母印得过深时，他竟将较浅的字母覆盖其上予以修正，仿佛要证明无论在哪个时代，追求完美都需付出艰辛努力。

Giorgione’s twilight (乔尔乔内的黄昏)


Just after 1500 Venetians began to dream of youths and maidens musing in the ambiguities of twilight. The painter of this idyllic dusk was Giorgione, and the printmaker was Giulio Campagnola, the only Italian between Mantegna and Marcantonio to engrave distinctively. This elaborately cultivated youth drew deceptive copies of drawings by masters, some of which are now probably hiding under grander attributions. In a signed print [ 267 ] he transposed a Mantegnesque figure and a landscape from Dürer into Giorgione’s atmosphere of reverie and Virgilian adolescence. To blur the air, he extended the powdering of dots on the bodies of Dürer’s Adam and Eve [278], stabbing the copper with swarms of specks that cluster or disperse to gather shapes out of the dusk [ 225 ]. He taught 18th-century English etchers to stipple reproductions of sentimental drawings [226], while the French marshaled the dots into lines to imitate chalk sketches [ 586 ].
乔尔乔内笔下的暮色 1500 年刚过，威尼斯画师便开始描绘少年少女在暮色朦胧中沉思的幻境。这幅田园诗般的黄昏画作出自乔尔乔内之手，而版画家朱利奥·坎帕尼奥拉——曼特尼亚与马尔坎托尼奥之间唯一风格鲜明的意大利版画家——则将其转化为版画。 这位精心培养的青年曾临摹大师素描，其作品如今或隐匿于更显赫的署名之下。在一幅署名版画[267]中，他将曼特尼亚风格的人物与丢勒的景观置入乔尔乔内梦幻般的氛围，营造出维吉尔式的青春意境。 为营造朦胧感，他在丢勒《亚当与夏娃》[278]人物躯体上延展了点状晕染技法，以密密麻麻的斑点刺刻铜版——这些斑点时而聚拢时而散开，在暮色中勾勒出形体轮廓[225]。 他教导十八世纪的英国蚀刻师用点画法复制感伤画作[226]，而法国人则将点画排列成线条，以模仿粉笔素描[586]。

霍诺拉·斯奈德。弗朗切斯科·巴托洛齐根据 T·H·本韦尔作品创作的点刻蚀版画，1784 年
However, when Campagnola’s contemporaries attempted such atmospheric ef- fects in woodcut, their equipment failed them. Woodcutters had to approximate the dots by relief lines cut so close together that the minute pits soon clogged with ink specks from the printer’s suede leather balls, and the wooden presses squeezed too feebly to force ink into the troughs between the ridges of the laid paper [227]. These drawbacks were not overcome until after 1800, when a smooth roller spread ink cleanly, and an iron press struck hard against the uniform thickness of ma-chine-made paper [636].
然而，当坎帕尼奥拉的同辈人试图在木刻中实现这种氛围效果时，他们的设备却无法胜任。木刻师只能通过密集排列的浮雕线条来模拟网点，但这些细微凹坑很快会被印刷工麂皮球上的墨点堵塞，而木质印刷机的压力又过于微弱，无法将墨水挤入有纹纸纹路间的凹槽[227]。 这些缺陷直至 1800 年后才得以克服——当时采用光滑滚筒实现均匀上墨，并以铁质压印机对厚度均匀的机械造纸施加强力压印[636]。

Etching and aquatint (蚀刻与水彩蚀刻)


When Gothic armor was decorated with oil paint, the bare steel around the paint often rusted down. Perhaps noticing this, armorers after 1400 began to decorate swords by scratching a wax coating with a design, and applying sal amoniac, vinegar, and vitriol for three or four days. Since these corrosives eroded grooves like those plowed by a graver, about 1500 Daniel Hopfer and his two sons, armor decorators in Augsburg, began to etch designs on flat iron plates for printing like engravings. Within 20 years their application of etching (from the Dutch etsen, to eat) had spread to Urs Graf in Switzerland, Altdorfer in Regensburg, Dürer in Nuremberg, and Parmigiano in Parma. About 1520 Lucas of Leiden used the modern metal, copper, for more delicate control [ 285 ]. But even the finest etched lines cannot blend into a continuous tone, for if they crowd too close together, the metal walls between the grooves break down, leaving a smoothness that catches no ink. Daniel Hopfer somehow pitted or rusted his iron plates enough to hold a light tone of ink [ 228 ], but the classic approximation of the continuous tone of watercolor wash-aquatint-was not invented until the 1650 s in Amsterdam, where mezzotint was also being invented [511]. The inventor of
蚀刻与软地蚀刻法当哥特式盔甲以油彩装饰时，油彩周围的裸露钢材常会锈蚀。 或许注意到这种现象，1400 年后的盔甲匠开始用蜡层雕刻剑身图案，再涂抹氨水、醋和绿矾浸泡三四日。这些腐蚀剂能像刻刀般蚀刻出沟槽，约 1500 年间，奥格斯堡的盔甲装饰师丹尼尔·霍普费尔及其两子开始在平板铁上蚀刻图案，如同雕版印刷般复制。 二十年内，这种源自荷兰语"etsen"（意为"腐蚀"）的蚀刻技法迅速传播：瑞士的乌尔斯·格拉夫、雷根斯堡的阿尔特多夫、纽伦堡的丢勒、帕尔马的帕尔米贾尼奥相继采用。约 1520 年，莱顿的卢卡斯开始使用现代金属铜材，以实现更精细的控制[285]。 然而即便是最精妙的蚀刻线条也无法形成连续色调——当线条过于密集时，凹槽间的金属壁会崩解，形成无法承载油墨的平滑面。 丹尼尔·霍普费尔通过某种方法使铁版表面产生足够的凹坑或锈蚀，从而承载浅色调的墨水[228]。然而，水彩渲染技法——即水彩渲染版画——这种对连续色调的经典近似表现，直至 1650 年代才在阿姆斯特丹问世，当时凹版雕刻技法也在此地诞生[511]。该技法的发明者

aquatint was a certain Jan van de Velde [229], whose process was then forgotten until Stapart’s Art de graver au pinceau (1773), and J.-B. Le Prince’s more popular Découverte du procédé de graver au lavis (1780) revolutionized etching by publishing recipes for aquatint.
水彩蚀刻技法由一位名叫扬·范德维尔德[229]的艺术家创立，其工艺随后被遗忘，直至斯塔帕特的《笔刷蚀刻艺术》（1773 年）问世，以及让-巴蒂斯特·勒普兰斯更广为人知的《水彩蚀刻工艺发现》（1780 年）出版，通过刊载水彩蚀刻的配方，彻底革新了蚀刻艺术。
Aquatint tone is etched either by dusting the bare copper with rosin, whose specks keep off the acid and become minute caps for microscopic peaks of metal, or else by coating the plate with a ground containing salt or sugar, whose grains admit acid to erode microscopic pits. Both methods roughen the copper to a sandpaper texture that catches ink in a continuous scattering [230]. Where the acid bites briefly, the tone prints light; where a deeper bite catches more ink, the area prints darker. Each separate tone prints like a hard-edged stratum of deposit, unlike
水彩蚀刻的色调可通过两种方式蚀刻：其一是在裸露的铜版上撒上松香粉末，这些微粒能阻隔酸液，形成微小的金属峰顶保护层；其二是在铜版上涂覆含盐或糖的底料，其颗粒可让酸液渗透形成微观凹坑。两种方法均使铜版表面呈现砂纸般的粗糙质感，使油墨在印刷时形成连续的散射效果[230]。 酸蚀较浅处呈现浅色调，蚀刻较深处吸附更多油墨则显深色。每种色调均如硬质沉积层般清晰分层，不同于
the hand-pricked stipple tones [ 225 ], which glide from light to dark. English etchers of views [ 376 ] elaborated aquatint to its utmost, and Goya used it more simply for dreams and drama [ 626 ]. In 1640-60, while aquatint and mezzotint [ 511 ] were being invented in Amsterdam, Castiglione in Genoa made one etching in what looks like soft ground-a technique that, like aquatint, was all but forgotten until after 1750.
手工点刻的点状色调[225]，从明到暗流畅过渡。英国风景蚀刻师[376]将软地蚀刻技法发挥到极致，而戈雅则将其简化运用于梦境与戏剧表现[626]。 1640 至 1660 年间，当阿姆斯特丹发明凹版蚀刻与凹版雕刻[511]时，热那亚的卡斯蒂廖内以类似软地蚀刻的技法创作了一幅版画——这种与凹版蚀刻同样湮没无闻的技术，直至 1750 年后才重见天日。

Gods and personifications (诸神与拟人化形象)


Though antique palace scrolls must have illustrated Ovid’s graphic anecdotes, later scribes copied only the words. The loss of antique pictures hardly mattered so long as the Middle Ages, valuing symbol above historic fact, clothed Venus and Caesar in local skirts and jerkins. From about 1460 to 75 Ovid’s Metamorphoses was rewritten to inculcate Christian morals (not always an easy conversion), with directions for dressing up burghers as gods. In the manuscript illustrations and their woodcut copies such local maskers go jolting in farm carts over the cobbles in a Flemish pageant [ 231 ].
诸神与拟人化形象尽管古宫廷卷轴曾绘有奥维德生动轶事的插图，后世抄写员却仅留文字。只要中世纪仍推崇象征胜于史实——让维纳斯与凯撒披上本土短裙与短上衣——古画的流失便无关紧要。 约 1460 至 1475 年间，《变形记》被改写为宣扬基督教道德的文本（这种转化并非易事），并附有将市民装扮成神祇的指南。在手稿插图及其木刻复本中，这些本土化角色正乘坐农用马车颠簸穿行于鹅卵石铺就的弗拉芒庆典街道[231]。
Historical correctness began to matter when the Renaissance enthusiasm for archeology demanded to see the gods as antiquity had imagined them. A new age started in 1497 when a north Italian artist (Benedetto Montagna?) invented something like antique dress to illustrate Ovid with the first long series of mythological prints [ 232 ]. These 53 woodcuts supplied immediate copy for artists and artisans. North Italian pottery decorators used the illustrations with such a specialized experience in antique subjects that they aimed the fatal arrow correctly at Achilles’
历史准确性开始受到重视，源于文艺复兴时期对考古学的热忱，人们渴望以古人想象中的形象来呈现诸神。 1497 年，一位北意大利艺术家（贝内代托·蒙塔尼亚？）开创性地设计出仿古服饰，为奥维德作品创作了首批神话题材版画长卷[232]。这 53 幅木刻版画立即成为艺术家与工匠的创作范本。北意大利陶器装饰师运用这些插图时展现出对古风题材的精湛造诣——他们精准地将致命箭矢射向了阿基里斯的
231
Cybele. Woodcut in Ovid, Methamorphose moralisie, Bruges (Mansion), 1484
西布勒。奥维德《道德变形记》中的木刻版画，布鲁日（曼森出版社），1484 年


heel [ 233 ] instead of at his back. The still rather fanciful costumes of the Venetian Ovid satisfied the early Renaissance, but as people collected more prints to compare, they judged more critically. 74 years after the Ovid, and again in Venice, the first illustrated manual of mythology specified what the well-dressed god will, or will not, wear at home [ 234 ]. Cartari compiled his social guide to Olympus from antique descriptions, mostly of the outlandish idols that late Roman superstition rummaged from all over the empire. His often conflicting quotations resulted in
脚跟[233]而非背部。威尼斯版《奥维德》中那些仍显奇幻的服饰满足了早期文艺复兴时期人们的审美，但随着人们收集更多版画进行比较，评判标准也日益严苛。在《奥维德》问世 74 年后，威尼斯再度推出首部插图版神话手册，明确规定了衣着得体的神祇在家中应穿或不应穿的服饰[234]。 卡塔里根据古代文献编纂了这本奥林匹斯社交指南，主要取材于晚期罗马迷信从帝国各地搜罗的怪诞偶像。他引用的诸多矛盾记载最终导致——

Gods and personifications
神明与拟人化形象

Fantasies so wildly hybrid proved handy for poets and indispensable for painters, who copied details the way Beaux-Arts architects were to copy historic doorways and balconies. But though Cartari took care of gods and nymphs, he neglected the personifications increasingly needed by the learned art of mannerism and the baroque. How should an artist draw Pity-like a naked, newborn babe, striding the blast? What color should he use for Fame-painted full of tongues? After 1603 he could look up such matters in the first illustrated dictionary of 150 personifications [235], compiled by Cesare Ripa of Perugia “for the use of orators, preachers, poets, painters, sculptors, draftsmen, or any educated man, and convenient for planning decorations for weddings, funerals, and triumphs.”
如此狂野的混合幻想对诗人颇为实用，对画家更是不可或缺——他们临摹细节的方式，恰似美术学院建筑师临摹历史门廊与阳台。但卡塔里虽精心描绘诸神与仙女，却忽视了矫饰主义与巴洛克艺术日益渴求的拟人化形象。艺术家该如何描绘"怜悯"？是如赤裸的新生婴儿般，在狂风中昂首阔步？ 该用何种色彩描绘满身舌头的声名女神？1603 年后，他可查阅佩鲁贾的切萨雷·里帕编纂的首部图解拟人词典[235]，该书"供演说家、传教士、诗人、画家、雕塑家、绘图师及所有有识之士使用，亦便于规划婚礼、葬礼与庆典的装饰"。
Since personifications, unlike the gods of antiquity, change as ideas change, Ripa’s Iconology evolved through successive editions to German rococo elaborations [236] that the original author would never have recognized as his. Editions of Ripa are listed in every studio inventory until the French Revolution, along with Cartari’s Images of the Gods, Vignola’s Five Orders of Architecture, some book on
由于拟人化形象不同于古代神祇，会随思想演变而改变，里帕的《图像学》历经多次修订，最终演变为德国洛可可式的繁复版本[236]——其原始作者绝不会承认这是自己的作品。直至法国大革命前，里帕著作的版本始终列于每间画室的藏书目录中，与之并列的还有卡塔里的《诸神形象集》、维尼奥拉的《建筑五式》以及某部关于...的著作。

Illustrations for architects (建筑师插图)


Vitruvius, a minor Roman architect and engineer who worked under Augustus ( 27 b.c.-a.d. 14), compiled the only surviving ancient builder’s manual by quoting from lost Greek treatises and by describing building methods out of his own practice. When the Renaissance studied his handbook and published it in 1486, it stopped the free experiments of medieval builders by imposing architectural laws that regulated the next four centuries. Italians printed his unillustrated manuscript without pictures until the fourth edition in 1511 started architectural illustrations in print. Ten years later the first translation into a modern language (Italian) drowned Vitruvius’ text in an ocean of commentary flowing out of Leonardo da Vinci’s discussions in Milan. The annotator surprisingly drew Milan Cathedral [ 237 ], on which he had worked as an architect,
建筑师维特鲁威的插图集。这位在奥古斯都统治时期（公元前 27 年-公元 14 年）任职的罗马建筑师兼工程师，通过援引失传的希腊论著并结合自身实践经验，编纂了现存唯一的古代建筑师手册。 文艺复兴时期学者研读其手册并于 1486 年出版后，通过确立规范建筑的法则，终结了中世纪建筑师的自由探索，这些法则主导了随后四个世纪的建筑实践。 意大利人最初印刷其手稿时未配插图，直至 1511 年第四版才首次引入建筑插图。十年后，首部现代语言译本（意大利语）诞生，却因莱昂纳多·达·芬奇在米兰的讨论引发的评论洪流，使维特鲁威的文本淹没其中。令人惊讶的是，这位注释者绘制了米兰大教堂[237]——他曾作为建筑师参与该教堂的建造。

These first printed renderings of an elaborate Gothic building helped to keep Gothic respectable in Italy until its revival in opera scenery shortly after 1700.
为证明古老的"Germanici architecti"（德国建筑师）在设计哥特式建筑时，同样运用了三角形、正方形和圆形这三种几何图形——这些图形被文艺复兴时期的理论家们奉为完美几何形态，他们正是基于古希腊和古罗马建筑师的理论加以阐发。这些精美哥特式建筑的首批印刷图稿，使哥特风格在意大利得以延续其尊贵地位，直至 1700 年后不久在歌剧布景中重获新生。
In 1537 Sebastiano Serlio, a Venetian architect who may have built even less than Vitruvius, started to issue the first architectural books ever illustrated by their author. He began by publishing Vitruvius’ foundation of design, the five orders of columns and entablatures, and then proceeded to original projects [ 238 ]. When Francis I employed Serlio at Fontainebleau, he re-Romanized France by replanting classicism in what was to become its second home.
1537 年，威尼斯建筑师塞巴斯蒂亚诺·塞里奥——其建筑实践可能远不及维特鲁威——开始出版史上首批由作者亲自绘图的建筑著作。他首先刊载了维特鲁威的设计基础理论，即五种柱式与檐墙体系，继而推出原创建筑方案[238]。 当弗朗索瓦一世在枫丹白露宫聘请塞里奥时，他通过将古典主义重新植入这片即将成为其第二故土的土地，实现了法国的"再罗马化"。

used, rules of thumb by the severe Vignola, whose Roman church of the Gesú became the model for many Jesuit churches in Europe and the Americas. Vignola crystallized Vitruvius’ rambling memoranda in diagrams with engraved captions [239] so terse that even unlettered workmen could assemble the classical building blocks-column, capital, entablature-in ways that could not avoid some consonance and might achieve beauty. Musicians followed a later parallel course by agreeing on sequences of keys, refrains, and recapitulations with which they could compose speedily and at the very worst coherently. The countless adaptations of Vignola’s pictorial syllabus fixed columns to all formal façades until steel construction revolutionized proportions a while after musicians had abandoned their old prearranged signals.
严苛的维尼奥拉所遵循的经验法则，其在罗马建造的耶稣会教堂成为欧洲和美洲众多耶稣会教堂的范本。 维尼奥拉将维特鲁威冗长的备忘录凝练成配有雕刻注释的图解[239]，其简洁程度甚至让目不识丁的工匠也能将古典建筑单元——柱身、柱头、檐墙——以既能保持协调又可能成就美感的方式组合起来。 音乐家们后来也遵循类似路径，通过约定音阶序列、副歌与再现段落，得以快速创作，即便最糟糕时也能保持作品连贯性。维尼奥拉图解纲要的无数变体将柱式固定于所有正式立面，直至钢结构革命重塑比例——此时音乐家们早已摒弃了那些预设的旧式信号。
Gentlemen became their own architects when Palladio offered further guidance to organize the classical units into harmonious exteriors and imaginative sequences of spaces [ 240 ]. Palladio himself designed for the Venetian patricians who were then settling newly drained marshes to enjoy the refined rustication praised by Horace, Pliny, and Varro. Wherever men-Englishmen, Russians, or Virginianshave dreamed of Horatian cultivation, they have turned to Palladio’s designs for their serene blend of beauty and use. He flanked his houses, for instance, with
当帕拉第奥进一步指导人们将古典元素组合成和谐的外观与富有想象力的空间序列时，绅士们便成为了自己的建筑师[240]。 帕拉迪奥本人曾为威尼斯贵族设计宅邸，这些贵族正迁居新开垦的沼泽地，以享受贺拉斯、普林尼和瓦罗所推崇的精致乡村生活。无论何处——英格兰、俄罗斯或弗吉尼亚——凡向往贺拉斯式田园风光之人，皆因其将美学与实用完美融合的特质而倾心于帕拉迪奥的设计。例如他在宅邸两侧设置了
