柱廊用来装饰它们，供人行走其下避开日晒雨淋，并储存根茎类蔬菜和柴火。
In 1721 Fischer von Erlach, obsessed by the Germanic ambition for comprehensiveness, collected buildings from the whole world in the first general survey of architecture, gathered, according to the English translation, “from the most approv’d Historians, Original Medals, Remarkable Ruins, and Curious Authentick Designs” [ 241 ]. His go large engravings put Chinese pavilions in every park and supplied stage designers with exotic fancies but left historians still thinking that Greeks had copied Etruscans. This Italian partiality was set right when two Englishmen published the first measured renderings of Greek temples [ 242 ], starting a Greek revival that extended Doric porticoes from Saint Petersburg to Cincinnati. By 1850 so many books had illustrated historic masterpieces that 19th-century architects could imagine beauty only as the past rearranged, thus debarring themselves from originality except in problems to which the past hardly applied, such as warehouses, factories, and railway stations.
1721 年，受日耳曼人追求全面性的执念驱使，菲舍尔·冯·埃拉赫在首部建筑通览中汇集了全球建筑，据英文译本所述，这些资料"源自最权威的历史学家、原始奖章、著名遗迹及珍贵可靠的设计图"[241]。 他那些巨幅版画让中国亭阁遍布各国公园，为舞台设计师提供异域奇想，却使历史学家仍坚信希腊人抄袭了伊特鲁里亚人。当两位英国人首次出版希腊神庙实测图时[242]，这种对意大利的偏爱才得以纠正，由此掀起的希腊复兴浪潮将多立克柱廊从圣彼得堡延伸至辛辛那提。 至 1850 年，历史杰作的图录已充斥书刊，十九世纪建筑师只能将美感视为对过往的重组，因而丧失原创力——唯有面对仓库、工厂、火车站这类与历史传统几乎无关的课题时，他们才得以突破桎梏。

Grotesque ornament (怪诞的装饰)


About the time of Christ, the old-fashioned architect Vitruvius deplored that the traditional wall paintings of realistic landscapes and factual renderings of stonework had been supplanted by “monstrosities-pediments sprouting stalks that uphold half-figures with human, or even animal heads.” This controversial modern style decorated Nero’s Golden House in Rome [ 243 ]. When Nero died (a.d. 68) his newfangled extravaganza was razed to its basement vaults, on which a terrace was laid. By the later 1400s, breaks in the vaults allowed artists to slide down the debris into chambers known as grotte, where they copied the fanciful designs on the walls and ceilings, calling them grotteschi.
怪诞装饰基督降生前后，古雅的建筑师维特鲁威曾痛惜道：传统壁画中写实的自然景观与逼真的石砌工艺，已被"怪诞之物"取代——那些顶部长出茎秆的门楣，托举着半人半兽的怪异雕像。这种备受争议的现代风格，曾装饰着尼禄在罗马的金宫[243]。 尼禄死后（公元 68 年），这座新奇奢华的建筑被夷为平地，仅剩地窖基座，其上建起露台。至 15 世纪后期，基座裂缝使艺术家得以滑入废墟中的洞穴空间，他们临摹墙壁与天花板上的奇幻图案，称之为"grotteschi"（洞穴式装饰）。
One grotesque scheme, the tall wall panels of balanced branches springing out of a central stalk, had already been adapted from other sources in a Venetian wood-
其中一幅怪诞的构图——高耸的枝干墙板由中央茎干向外延伸，呈平衡状——已从其他来源改编而来，出现在威尼斯木版画中。

244（左）怪诞装饰。佐安·安德烈亚根据《斯福尔扎祈祷书》大师作品所作的雕版画，14905

245 怪诞装饰。科内利斯·博斯雕版画，安特卫普，1540 年代246 Cleopatra. Etching by Jean Mignon after Luca Penni

cut of 1476 [211]. The example of the Golden House elaborated these vertical strips to decorate the side margins of manuscripts with panels that engravings [ 244 ] published for all to use. By 1519 the most generative version of the Golden House ceiling grotesques was frescoed under Raphael’s direction at the Vatican in the Logge, a sort of upstairs verandah. Raphael varied Nero’s reed gazebos to fit so many useful shapes that traveling artists sketched his frescoes more than the antique originals and engraved their own adaptations of them in Germany and France. There the framework of the grotesque replaced Gothic leaves as a habitat for the robust hybrid monsters that the north of Europe had been inventing during the 1000 years since the age of migrations. In Flanders the crossbred Gothic drolleries moved into cages that caught them like the stocks [ 245 ]. At Fontainebleau, the stucco modelers invented curving slabs where slim nudes exercise as in a jungle gym [ 246 ]. The slabs straightened into dizzy carpentry in French books on perspective [ 361 ]. Indeed, the French took such a liking to this mixture of structure and caprice, of logic and whim-wham, that they played with the grotesque until nearly 1900 and may still return to it some day.
1476 年版[211]。黄金宫殿的范例将这些垂直条纹加以演变，用于装饰手稿的侧边空白处，形成可供众人使用的雕版画[244]。至 1519 年，黄金宫殿天花板怪诞装饰的最富创造力版本，在拉斐尔的指导下以湿壁画形式绘制于梵蒂冈的露台——一种楼上阳台。 拉斐尔将尼禄的芦苇凉亭变形为多种实用形态，以致巡游艺术家们临摹其壁画的次数远超古迹原作，更在德法两国刻印了各自改编的版本。这些怪诞图案的框架取代了哥特式叶饰，成为欧洲北部自迁徙时代起千年来创造的强健杂交怪兽的栖身之所。 在佛兰德斯，混血的哥特式滑稽雕饰被禁锢于笼中，如同枷锁囚禁罪犯[245]。枫丹白露的灰泥雕塑师则创造出弯曲的石板，纤细的裸体雕像在其上如攀爬游乐架般运动[246]。 这些板材在法国透视学著作中化作令人眩晕的木构技艺[361]。法国人对这种结构与奇想、逻辑与任性交融的艺术形式情有独钟，直至近 1900 年仍在玩味怪诞美学，或许终有一日将重拾此道。

Books of hours (时祷书)


While Venetian folio missals were sailing to priests in faraway ports, Parisians printed handy little prayer books for families in and near France. These laymen’s books of hours contained a calendar with doggerel verses for the labors of the months, often an anatomical man to show where to bleed a sufferer under each zodiac sign [ 84 ], readings from the Gospels, the seven canonical hours of prayer to the Virgin from matins to compline, special masses for the dead, and sometimes, for humbler traditionalists, prayers to local saints.
时祷书当威尼斯对开本弥撒经书正运往远方港口的牧师手中时，巴黎人却为法国本土及周边家庭印制了便携式小祈祷书。 这些平信徒用的时祷书包含：配有诙谐诗句的月份劳作日历（常附解剖图示，标注各星座患者放血部位[84]）、福音经文选读、从晨祷至晚祷的七时圣母祷文、亡者弥撒经文，有时还为虔诚的传统信徒收录了地方圣徒祷文。
Surviving books of hours rarely agree exactly, since small dioceses often ordered only a few dozen copies, which printers made up by adding sheets of special prayers to a bulk printing of the standard parts of the book in the use of Rome. Many copies were printed on vellum to stand handling in daily reference. Carried to mass like hats and gloves that neighbors also discussed, prayer books changed fashions more sensitively than other French books. No one knows how many editions Paris printed from about 1480 to 1540, but some 1400 have survived, though often reduced to a single copy. The founder of the industry, Jean Dupré, was probably
现存的祈祷书极少完全一致，因为小教区通常只订购几十册，印刷商便通过在罗马礼仪标准部分的批量印刷中添加特殊祷文页来凑数。许多副本采用羊皮纸印刷，以耐受日常查阅的频繁翻阅。这些祈祷书如同邻里间谈论的帽子手套般被带往弥撒，其时尚变迁比其他法国书籍更为敏锐。 无人知晓 1480 至 1540 年间巴黎究竟印制了多少版本，但现存约 1400 册，尽管多数仅存孤本。该行业的开创者让·杜普雷很可能是

图 75：安特卫普（[莱斯韦尔特]）1496 年，吉蒂登（ghetyden）出土的让·杜普雷风格金属雕刻（247 件）

248 幅木刻版画，由国王的命令制作，巴黎（维拉尔），约 1490 年

printing prayer books before 1480; their existence can be inferred from blocks of copper nailed to wood that he reused in his missals of 1481, and from other cuts in his style that wandered out to Venice and Antwerp [ 247 ].
1480 年前印刷祈祷书；其存在可从他 1481 年弥撒书中重复使用的铜版木刻印版推断，亦可从流传至威尼斯和安特卫普的其他同风格版画中得到印证[247]。
Most family prayer books fit the pocket, but some were tall and thin like tiny ledgers, and some exceptionally big Grandes Heures Royales [ 248 ] were printed after 1489 at the king’s order for Antoine Vérard, the richest French publisher. His firmly outlined cuts avoided shading to facilitate printing them in the vellum presentation copies that were Vérard’s specialty. He often copied his prayer-book cuts from the most elaborate of all the books of hours, printed in the 149os by Philippe Pigouchet for Simon Vostre [ 249 ]. Horae borders agree with each text or illustration, to help slow readers find their places. Thus the Virgin’s Dormition, Funeral, and Assumption surround her moment of triumph when her newborn son is adored by shepherds, who are labeled with the names they bore in miracle plays [ 249 ].
大多数家庭祈祷书尺寸适于装入口袋，但有些却细长如袖珍账簿，还有些特别庞大的《皇家大时祷书》[248]——1489 年后奉国王之命为法国最富有的出版商安托万·韦拉尔印制。 其版画线条笔触坚实，刻意省略阴影处理，以便在羔羊皮赠阅本上印刷——这正是维拉尔的专长。他常从菲利普·皮古谢于 1490 年代为西蒙·沃斯特印刷的《时祷书》中汲取灵感，该书堪称所有时祷书中最精美之作[249]。书页边框与文字或插图相互呼应，帮助阅读缓慢者定位。 圣母安眠、葬礼与升天场景环绕着她诞下圣婴的荣耀时刻——牧羊人正膜拜着新生儿，其姓名标注源自奇迹剧中的角色设定[249]。
The few foreign imitators of such prayer books succeeded in rivaling the Parisian unity of taste only in Venice. There the printer de Sanctis, a cutter of saints’ images, transposed the French layout into Italian Renaissance ornament so exquisite [ 250 ] that it captivated a traveling French designer, grammarian, and reformer of spelling, Geoffroy Tory. When Tory returned to Paris around 1518, he found the Parisian books of hours shaded even more muddily than Strassburg woodcuts [56]. He reintroduced clarity in 1525 by adapting the 30-year-old Venetian adaptation of Parisian prayer books [251] and combining the unshaded Venetian outlines with the black accents of the Hypnerotomachia [ 223 ], both long out of fashion in Venice itself. He thus killed the Gothic book in France by launching the Italianate balance that was henceforth to formalize French official art with the chill of perfect taste. During the next 15 years, Tory also adapted Flemish manuscript borders of fruits and flowers [ 182 ]. Tory replaced the old Gothic coziness by synthesizing impersonal elegance just when the circulation of prints was internationalizing art, and Rome was imposing uniformity on the Catholic world. The last graceful personal prayer book was Queen Elizabeth I’s adaptation of the Parisian format to Anglican use in 1569 [ 252 ].
少数模仿此类祈祷书的外国作品，唯有威尼斯之作能与巴黎的统一审美相媲美。 当地印刷商德·桑克蒂斯——一位圣徒画像雕刻师——将法式版式转化为意大利文艺复兴装饰风格，其精妙程度[250]令旅居当地的法国设计师、语法学家兼拼写改革家热弗鲁瓦·托里为之倾倒。当托里约于 1518 年重返巴黎时，发现当地时祷书的阴影处理甚至比斯特拉斯堡木刻版更显浑浊[56]。 1525 年，他通过融合两股早已在威尼斯过时的元素——三十年前威尼斯对巴黎祈祷书的改编版[251]，以及《梦战》中未着阴影的威尼斯轮廓线与黑色强调技法[223]——重新引入了清晰美学。 他由此终结了法国的哥特式书籍传统，开创了意大利式均衡美学——这种完美品味的冷峻气质从此成为法国官方艺术的规范。在随后的十五年间，托里还借鉴了佛兰德手稿中水果与花卉的装饰边框[182]。当印刷品流通推动艺术国际化、罗马教廷向天主教世界推行统一规范之际，托里以合成式冷峻优雅取代了古老的哥特式温馨。 最后一部优雅的私人祷告书，是伊丽莎白一世女王于 1569 年将巴黎格式改编为英国国教使用的版本[252]。

Printing had begun to level the heterogeneous particularity of parish traditions even before the papal bull of 1571 formally purged prayer books of local idiosyncracies and stripped them to their present interchangeable austerity. The wholesale obsolescence of the old local prayer books created a sudden market that established the fortunes of the Plantin press in Antwerp through its monopoly of church books in Flanders and Spain, making it the busiest book factory before 1800.
早在 1571 年教皇诏书正式清除祈祷书中的地方特色、将其简化为如今可互换的简朴形式之前，印刷术便已开始消弭各教区传统中的异质性差异。 旧式地方祈祷书的全面淘汰催生了突发性市场，普兰丁印刷厂凭借其在佛兰德斯和西班牙的教会书籍垄断地位，在安特卫普奠定了商业根基，成为 1800 年前最繁忙的印刷工场。

Royal progresses (皇家行程)


At the end of the Middle Ages strong sovereigns centralized Burgundy, France, Spain, and England by absorbing feudal domains and provinces. While it was all very well for a supreme ruler to be crowned in some cathedral, people at large heard little about this and could be impressed only by seeing their new prince in the flesh. So each new sovereign had to tour his cities. In Flanders, the cities invested in elaborate street decorations for confronting their new ruler with pictures and inscriptions that bound him to respect their traditional rights and begged for new favors. As if to ratify such contracts by allegory, the city of Ghent in 1508 appropriated five guilders to print 300 copies of an illustrated record of the decorations that greeted the boy who would become Charles V. If this book was ever printed, it has vanished now. The first extant printed illustrations of such bluntly contractual decorations record Charles’ reception into Bruges in 1515. The local presses in Bruges were too provincial to do honor to such an occa-
王室巡行中世纪末期，强大的君主通过吞并封建领地与行省，实现了对勃艮第、法国、西班牙及英格兰的中央集权统治。尽管最高统治者在大教堂加冕的仪式庄严隆重，但普通民众对此知之甚少，唯有亲眼目睹新君亲临方能深受震撼。因此每位新君主都必须巡行诸城。 在佛兰德斯地区，各城市倾力打造华美的街道装饰，用绘画与铭文向新君主展示：既要求其尊重传统权利，又乞求新的恩惠。 仿佛要以寓言形式确认这类契约，根特城于 1508 年拨款五盾，印制三百册图文并茂的装饰记录，以纪念迎接未来查理五世的盛况。若此书真曾问世，如今亦已湮没无踪。 现存最早的印刷插图记录了 1515 年布鲁日为查理五世举行的接迎仪式——这些装饰物赤裸裸地以契约形式宣告着权利诉求。布鲁日当地印刷厂因过于乡土气息，未能为如此盛事增光添彩。

sion, and the town hated Antwerp, the nearest great printing center, so the book was printed in Paris. Charles was 15-the age of reason-when he entered Bruges to inherit the first major installment of his far-flung empire. Pushing his way through thousands of torches in the April twilight, he saw broad canvas paintings like medieval altars being opened for him. (They were probably hinged to close in case of rain.) Each one balanced a scene from the Old Testament or Roman history with an event in the history of Bruges to warn the beginning emperor to be good to his city. In one painting [ 253 ], Joshua apportions the Promised Land on the left while Bruges is founded on the right, thus requesting Charles to restore the power that the city had lost to Antwerp when its harbor silted up.
布鲁日憎恶邻近的大印刷中心安特卫普，因此该书最终在巴黎付梓。查理十五岁——这个被视为理性的年龄——踏入布鲁日继承他辽阔帝国的首块疆土。四月的暮色中，他穿行于数千盏火炬构成的灯海，目睹巨幅帆布画如中世纪祭坛画般为他展开（这些画作很可能装有铰链以便雨天收起）。 每幅巨画都将旧约圣经或罗马史的场景与布鲁日本土事件并置，警示这位新任皇帝善待故土。其中一幅画作[253]中，左侧约书亚正分配应许之地，右侧则是布鲁日建城场景——以此提醒查理：当港口淤塞导致城市衰落时，他必须重振这座曾被安特卫普取代的港口之都。
Such frank demands and Gothic diptychs gave way to servility and Renaissance ornament zo-odd years later when the Valois kings tightened their grip on France and issued the first long series of publications for ostentation. When Henry II entered Paris in 1549, the sculptor Jean Goujon was paid 45 livres to draw the woodblocks of arches and set pieces that leading artists had designed. The arch shaped like an H for Henry looks huge in the cut [ 254 ] but was actually a mere 24 feet high.
如此直率的要求与哥特式双联画，在瓦卢瓦王朝君主们加强统治并首次大规模发行炫耀性出版物后，便让位于谄媚之态与文艺复兴时期的装饰风格。1549 年亨利二世入主巴黎时，雕塑家让·古容以 45 里弗尔的酬劳，为顶尖艺术家设计的拱门与装饰构件绘制木刻版画。 这座以亨利名字首字母 H 为造型的拱门在版画中显得极为宏伟[254]，实则仅高 24 英尺。
Triumphal arches taller than their marble models in Rome could be built only by
唯有……才能建造出比罗马大理石拱门更高的凯旋门。
an exceptionally rich city like Antwerp. Here, in the spring of 1635, when the brother of Philip IV of Spain sailed up the Scheldt as governor of Flanders, he saw the river banks and all Antwerp built up with canvas arches [ 255 ] whose scale is proven by some of the earliest surviving fragments of actual festival decorations, two life-size portraits from Rubens’ studio [ 256 ]. Antwerp’s painted splendors may have been the most enormous since Roman times, in complete contrast to Amsterdam’s studied indifference when Queen Henrietta Maria came to beg for funds to finance Charles I’s losing fight with the Roundheads. Why, one wonders,

The great age of royal receptions closed with the French Revolution. In 1810, when Marie Louise traveled from Vienna to Paris to marry Napoleon, her correct and uninteresting triumphal arch was published, not in an imperial folio, but in the trade catalogue of a manufacturer of composition ornaments, where it figured as a testimonial that his decorations could stand the weather for over a year. Nowadays, when a chief of state impresses himself on the public more through radio and television than by traveling about in person, ceremonial entries mark only a few international visits of good will. The modest scale of today’s setting goes back at least to 1844 when Louis-Philippe returned a visit from Queen Victoria to patch up political differences over Egypt [ 258 ]. Less upholstered railway carriages have served for similar talks in our time.
法国大革命标志着皇家礼仪的辉煌时代落幕。1810 年，当玛丽·路易丝从维也纳前往巴黎与拿破仑成婚时，那座规整而乏味的凯旋门并未刊载于帝国典籍，却出现在某人造装饰品制造商的商业目录中——作为其装饰品经受一年多风雨考验的证明。 如今，当国家元首更多通过广播电视而非亲临现场来向公众展示自己时，隆重的入城仪式仅在少数善意的国际访问中保留。当今简朴的仪仗规模至少可追溯至 1844 年——路易·菲利普为弥合埃及问题引发的政治分歧，回访维多利亚女王[258]。而当代类似会谈中，所用的铁路车厢甚至更为简陋。

Dürer’s four horsemen (丢勒的四骑士)


After the Black Death in the mid-1300s had killed about half of Europe, the survivors and their descendants for generations dreaded the Last Things predicted in the Apocalypse. Death’s engulfment revived a very old cycle of about 50 pictures of the end of the world, which included the four terrible horsemen released by breaking the seals of pestilence, war, famine, and death. The vast Angers tapestries of the Apocalypse, woven in northern France after 1376, were designed from a manuscript tradition [ 259 ] then at least two centuries old. The Apocalypse cycle was published for everybody everywhere through many versions of a blockbook of woodcuts that centuries of experiment had refined to a serene assurance [260]. The momentum of this tradition made the Apocalypse the only book that New Testaments printed in Germanic dialects illustrated before about 1670. For pictures of the life of Christ, people looked instead at the blockbook Bible of the Poor [ 21 ], then at its typographic enlargement in the Mirror of Man’s Salvation [ 22 ], and finally at the Postils: New Testament homilies arranged as they are read in churches during the year.
丢勒的四骑士 14 世纪中叶黑死病夺走欧洲半数人口后，幸存者及其后代数代人皆对《启示录》预言的末世景象心怀恐惧。死亡的吞噬重启了约五十幅描绘世界终结的古老图景循环，其中包含四骑士——瘟疫、战争、饥荒与死亡的封印被破，四骑士随之降临。 1376 年后在法国北部编织的昂热巨型《启示录》挂毯，其设计源自至少已有两百年历史的手稿传统[259]。经过数百年实践锤炼，木刻版画的版画书以多种版本将《启示录》循环传播至世界各地，呈现出一种从容的确定性[260]。 这种传统的影响力使得《启示录》成为 1670 年前唯一在日耳曼方言印刷的新约圣经插图。 至于基督生平的图画，人们先是通过《穷人的木刻圣经》[21]获取，继而借助《人类救赎之镜》[22]的排版扩充版，最终则依靠《讲道集》——即按教会全年诵读顺序编排的新约讲道集。

Pictures for the Old and New Testaments in German translations were fixed by the 123 woodcuts of the first richly illustrated Bible, printed at Cologne about 1478, probably for the Brothers of the Common Life. These woodcuts [ 261 ] transmitted a German manuscript tradition to the boy Dürer, who was about seven when they first appeared at Cologne and 12 when they were reprinted near his house in Nuremberg. They represented the Bible itself to him as they lodged in the center of his imagination like grains of sand to produce one pearl after another. Their very
德语译本《新旧约全书》的插图源自 1478 年左右在科隆印刷的首部精美插图圣经中的 123 幅木刻版画，该版本很可能为"共同生活兄弟会"所制作。 这些木刻版画[261]将德国手抄本传统传递给了少年丢勒——当它们首次在科隆面世时他约七岁，重印于纽伦堡其家附近时他十二岁。它们如同沙粒般驻留于他想象力的核心，催生出一颗又一颗珍珠，使圣经本身在他心中具象化。它们的
Figure 82: 262  图 82：262

263
Woodcut by Hans Burgkmair in New Testament, translated by Luther, Augsburg (Otmar), 1523
汉斯·布尔克迈尔为路德译本《新约》所作木刻版画，奥格斯堡（奥特马尔），1523 年

crudity encouraged him to improve upon them, when more accomplished models might have discouraged him. On them he based the 15 woodcuts of the Apocalypse that he published when he was 27 [ 262 ]. At 19 he had finished three years of learning to draw and cut woodblocks as an apprentice in Wolgemut’s shop, Nuremberg’s center for book illustration. When he was 22 or 23 he copied Mantegna’s engravings [187] to acquire the grand manner of figure drawing, and the clear and forceful massing of forms. With the Gothic and Renaissance traditions thus funneling into him, he transfigured the hints of the crude Cologne cuts into the first pictures of violent action since the German Romanesque illustrations. His Apocalypse charges a symbol with experience. The first woodcuts initialed by a great artist, their fame made his AD the first artist’s signature to be extensively faked. For us, his four horsemen exhaust a theme in the way Raphael exhausted the theme of the Madonna and Degas the ballet dancer.
粗糙的技法反而激励他不断改进，而更成熟的范本或许会令他气馁。他以此为基础创作了 15 幅《启示录》木刻版画，于 27 岁时出版[262]。19 岁时，他在纽伦堡书籍插画中心沃尔格穆特工坊完成三年学徒生涯，期间习得绘画与木刻技艺。 22 或 23 岁时，他临摹曼特尼亚的铜版画[187]，以掌握宏伟的人物绘制技法与清晰有力的造型堆砌。当哥特与文艺复兴传统在他体内交融升华，他将科隆粗粝版画的雏形转化为德国罗马式插图以来首部展现暴力行动的画作。《启示录》赋予象征以生命体验。 作为首位在木刻上署名的大师，其作品声名远播，使"AD"成为首个被广泛伪造的艺术家签名。对他而言，四骑士主题的穷尽，恰似拉斐尔穷尽圣母主题、德加穷尽芭蕾舞者主题那般彻底。
Dürer’s followers, dodging around him, harked back to the horsemen in the Cologne Bible because it illustrates the text more literally by stringing out the riders as the seals break them out one by one. A year after Luther published his translation of the New Testament, Burgkmair’s civilized simplification of Dürer [263] cleared away clutter in an arrangement like the Cologne cut. Burgkmair had grown up in Augsburg imbibing an Italianism that Dürer, farther north, had to struggle toward all his life without ever absorbing some of its essentials. While the white heat of Dürer’s imagination fused profusion into a masterpiece, creating the taste by which the future would enjoy him, Burgkmair floated more naturally in the mainstream of art. In 1534, when Luther got around to supervising illustrations for his translation of the whole Bible, he had Lucas Cranach II modernize the first three
丢勒的追随者们绕着他转悠，却又回到了《科隆圣经》里的骑兵形象——因为这种表现方式更直白地诠释了经文：随着封印逐个开启，骑手们依次列队而出。 在路德出版《新约》译本一年后，布尔克迈尔对丢勒作品的文明化简化[263]，以类似科隆版画的构图扫除了繁杂元素。布尔克迈尔在奥格斯堡成长期间浸润于意大利艺术风气，而更北方的丢勒毕生都在努力追寻这种风气，却始终未能完全吸收其精髓。 当丢勒炽烈的想象力将繁复熔铸成传世杰作，开创后世欣赏他的审美范式时，伯克迈尔却更自然地游弋于艺术主流。1534 年路德着手为其全本圣经译本监制插图时，委托卢卡斯·克拉纳赫二世将前三个

Dürer in Italy (丢勒在意大利)


Although Dürer was not the greatest 16th-century artist, his personality lorded it over every 16th-century printmaker except Ugo da Carpi [ 347 ] and Parmigiano [ 350 ]. His restless investigations and his worldwide awareness make him enough of a puzzle without the smokescreen of incense from his German worshipers. Yet some traits stand out clear, such as his relentless economy of energy that produced so many elaborate creations in his 57 years, and his workmanlike practicality. When he was about 25 he standardized his prints in upright formats to fit economically on whole, half, or quarter sheets of paper that he marketed to all Europe. When he was 26 he dated his first print 1497, and when he was
丢勒在意大利尽管丢勒并非十六世纪最伟大的艺术家，但其人格魅力却凌驾于除乌戈·达·卡尔皮[347]和帕尔米贾尼诺[350]之外的所有十六世纪版画家之上。他永不停歇的探索精神与全球视野，即便撇开德国崇拜者们熏香弥漫的迷雾，也足以令人费解。 然而某些特质依然清晰可辨：他以惊人的精力效率在五十七载光阴里创造出无数精妙作品，更展现出匠人般的务实精神。约二十五岁时，他将版画统一为竖版格式，使作品能经济地印制于整张、半张或四分之一张纸上，销往整个欧洲。二十六岁时，他为首幅版画题上 1497 年年份，而当他

265

The Madonna with the Monkey. Engraving by Dürer, about 1498/99
《圣母与猴子》。丢勒铜版画，约 1498/99 年
33 he began regularly to combine dates with his monogram AD as a pun on Anno Domini. He is thus the first printmaker whose development we can follow continuously. He is also the first artist from whom we have letters to a friend and a diary of travel expenses.
33 他开始定期将日期与自己的缩写 AD 结合使用，以此作为对公元纪年（Anno Domini）的双关语。因此，他是首位其创作历程可被完整追溯的版画家。同时，他也是首位留有致友人书信及旅行开支日记的艺术家。
He visited Venice in his mid-20s and again in his mid-30s, taking from Italy more than any previous northern artist, and returning more. In Venice he saw Madonnas by Mantegna [193] and Giovanni Bellini, who do not hold a wizened homunuculus like northern Virgins [ 47 ] but a boy whose ampler plumpness fits better with an adult. Between his two Venetian visits, Dürer engraved such an Italianate group [265] next to a monkey that he probably also met in Venice and against a background that he had noted at home in one of his earliest watercolors [ 266 ]. This half-timbered tower in a pond looked as exotic to Renaissance Italians as Chinese pagodas were to look to 18th-century Europeans. In Venice, Giulio Campagnola copied the whole setting of this wooden storehouse [ 267 ] as though it were a rare sketch brought home by a Venetian from an expedition to mainland meadows. In Florence the German half-timbering amused the fluid and receptive Robetta [146], searching for ready-made backgrounds to combine with figures copied from Filip-
他二十五六岁时造访威尼斯，三十五六岁时再度到访，从意大利汲取的养分远超此前任何北方艺术家，归来时更带来丰硕成果。在威尼斯，他目睹了曼特尼亚[193]与乔瓦尼·贝利尼创作的圣母像——这些圣母不再像北方圣母像[47]那样怀抱干瘪的侏儒，而是抱着更符合成年人形象的丰腴男孩。 两次威尼斯之行间，丢勒曾将这组意式人物群像[265]与猴子并置——猴子想必也是他在威尼斯邂逅的——背景则取材自他早年水彩画[266]中留存的家乡景致。这座池塘中的半木结构塔楼，对文艺复兴时期的意大利人而言，如同中国宝塔之于十八世纪的欧洲人般充满异域风情。 在威尼斯，朱利奥·坎帕尼奥拉完整复制了这座木质仓库[267]的场景，仿佛是某位威尼斯商人从大陆草原探险归来时带回的珍稀素描。而在佛罗伦萨，德国半木结构建筑令灵动敏锐的罗贝塔[146]倍感新奇——他正寻觅现成的背景，以搭配从菲利普作品中临摹的人物。

pino Lippi. Italians did not copy Dürer’s Madonna and Child (Italianate though he may have thought them) the way the first Florentine engravers copied figures from ES [143]. The only great Italian to accept what Dürer had made of the Venetian figures was Giovanni Bellini, who smoothed Dürer’s fussy complexities into the larger calm of Italy [ 268 ]. He obviously shared the Italian opinion that northern figures, especially nudes, were an Italian specialty misunderstood by barbarians. However, his Gothic resourcefulness in breaking the folds of drapery recommended his prints much later to Veronese and Guido Reni.
皮诺·利皮。意大利人并未像早期佛罗伦萨雕刻师临摹 ES[143]中的形象那样，复制丢勒的《圣母与圣婴》（尽管他可能认为这些作品带有意大利风格）。唯一认可丢勒对威尼斯人物处理方式的伟大意大利艺术家是乔瓦尼·贝利尼，他将丢勒繁复的细节融入更宏大的意大利式宁静之中[268]。 他显然认同意大利人的观点：北方人物造型——尤其是裸体画——是遭蛮族误解的意大利专长。然而他运用哥特式手法处理衣褶的巧思，却使他的版画在后世深受韦罗内塞和圭多·雷尼推崇。
Dürer had more thoroughly absorbed the Italian vision in his last, and perhaps greatest Gothic dream of the Christian knight braving the Valley of the Shadow [269]. Only a supreme artist could have evoked so haunting an image out of a literary commonplace. Dürer copied the armor from his watercolor painted 15 years before of a middle-aged man loitering on a plow horse. This prosy notation took on drama in the engraving from the example of Verrocchio’s bronze statue of Colleoni [ 270 ], which was being finished when Dürer first went to Venice. Both Verrocchio and Dürer modeled their stallions on the antique bronze horses of Saint Mark’s. Dürer, who often worked at either end of his Gothic-Italian world, for
丢勒在其最后一部、或许也是最伟大的哥特式作品中，更彻底地吸收了意大利艺术的精髓——那幅描绘基督教骑士勇闯阴影谷的画作[269]。唯有至高无上的艺术家，方能从文学俗套中淬炼出如此令人魂牵梦萦的意象。丢勒将盔甲的造型，直接取自十五年前他创作的水彩画：画中中年男子正倚靠在耕作的马匹旁。 这般平淡的叙述在版画中焕发戏剧张力，其灵感源自韦罗基奥的科莱奥尼青铜雕像[270]——当丢勒初访威尼斯时，这座雕像正处于收尾阶段。韦罗基奥与丢勒皆以圣马可大教堂的古青铜马为原型塑造战马。丢勒常游走于哥特-意大利艺术世界的两端，为
269 (opposite page) The Knight, Death, and the Devil. Engraving by Dürer, 1513
269（对页）骑士、死亡与魔鬼。丢勒版画，1513 年
270 Bartolommeo Colleoni. Plaster cast of bronze statue by Andrea Verrocchio, Venice, cast 1496
270 巴托洛梅奥·科莱奥尼。安德里亚·韦罗基奥青铜雕像石膏复制品，威尼斯，1496 年铸造


once brought both unforgettably together in this engraving. He had enriched his technique in the 15 years since the Madonna with the Monkey, when he was still following Schongauer’s clear and simple structure. In the Knight, Death, and the Devil, his 70th work on copper, he elaborated strokes, flicks, and dots to distinguish steel, flesh, glass, and fur with textures as specified for specific purposes as the categories of brushstrokes in Chinese painters’ manuals. Such wizardry discouraged all subsequent serious painters from ever attempting a real mastery of the graver, which now became the exclusive tool of specialists in reproducing other men’s pictures. Dürer established and imposed the basic grammar of engraving, suffocating those close to him, but providing a guide for those lucky enough to live at some remove, like the Little Master engravers of the next generation [ 315 ].
在这幅版画中，他将两者以令人难忘的方式融合在一起。自《圣母与猴子》问世后的十五年间，他的技法日益精进——彼时他仍遵循着申高尔清晰简洁的构图风格。 在铜版画《骑士、死亡与魔鬼》——其第七十幅铜版作品中，他通过精妙的笔触、甩点与点刻技法，精准区分出钢铁、血肉、玻璃与毛皮的质感，其纹理表现之细腻，堪比中国画论中对笔触类别的专属规范。这般魔术般的技艺令后世严肃画家望而却步，无人敢再真正钻研刻刀技艺，此技艺遂沦为复制他人画作的专属工具。 丢勒确立并强加了版画的基本语法，令近身者窒息，却为那些有幸保持距离的后辈提供了指引——正如下一代的小大师版画家们[315]。

Dürer's print styles (丢勒的版画风格)


Dürer mastered the techniques of woodcut, engraving, etching, and drypoint, invented modern watercolor, and drew in every medium except red chalk. By being the only artist so versatile, he completed the transformation, begun by Mantegna and the Housebook Master (Reuwich?), of entirely freeing printmaking from its craft origins. After Dürer, printmakers were trained by drawing, not by working in wood or metal, and all the different kinds of prints fused together under the leadership of painters. Dürer used all of his print techniques except drypoint (learned from the Housebook Master) over a stretch of seven years for four versions of Christ’s Agony in the Garden, an image of isolation that must have moved a man forever struggling alone. He engraved his first dated version [ 271 ] when, at 37, he was beginning to dominate German art. His engraving style had already moved away from Schongauer’s contrasts of dark hatching and white paper to a painter’s allover tone, where shadows cling to silvery modulations emerging into the light. The contrapuntal graver constrained his hand to meditate and plot. Yet the ambiguous stance of Christ-neither quite standing nor quite kneeling-has a wild power that inspired El Greco a century later in what was possibly his last painting [ 272 ].
丢勒的版画技法丢勒精通木刻、铜版雕刻、蚀刻与干刻技法，开创了现代水彩画，除红粉笔外涉猎所有绘画媒介。作为唯一如此多才的艺术家，他完成了由曼特尼亚与《家谱集》大师（鲁维希？）开创的变革，彻底将版画艺术从工艺起源中解放出来。 杜勒之后，版画家通过素描训练而非木版或金属版制作来接受专业培养，各类版画技法在画家引领下实现融合。在长达七年的创作周期中，杜勒运用除干刻版（承袭自《手册大师》）外的所有版画技法，完成了四版《基督在园中受难》——这幅孤寂的画面，想必深深触动了这位终生独自奋斗的艺术家。 他创作首个带年份的版本[271]时，年仅 37 岁却已开始主宰德国艺术。其蚀刻风格早已超越申高尔式深浅线条与白纸的对比，转向画家式的整体色调——阴影依附于银色渐变，在光影交融中浮现。 复调式刻刀迫使他的手沉思构图。然而基督那介于站立与跪伏之间的暧昧姿态，蕴含着狂野的力量——这力量在百年后启迪了埃尔·格列柯，催生出他可能的绝笔之作[272]。
Though Dürer’s engravings traveled far and wide, his woodcuts may have gone even farther, because more of them could be printed for less money. About 1509, or perhaps earlier, he began his most popular series of woodcuts, the Little Passion. The first try of the series may have been a version of the Agony in the Garden [273] that he rejected, evidently because it was cut in the sloppy way that he condemned as “bad woodcut work.” Yet the original drawing must have charged the Christ, flat on his face, with the Gothic intensity that drove Dürer during his 205 in the Apocalypse [ 262 ]. When he published the Little Passion in 1511, he replaced this desperate image with a more tranquil one cut exactly to the personal quirks of his line [ 274 ]. This later design has the stateliness acquired by the em-
尽管丢勒的铜版画传播甚广，但他的木刻版画传播范围可能更为广泛，因为木刻版画能以更低的成本印制更多份。 约 1509 年，或更早些时候，他开始创作其最受欢迎的木刻系列《小受难》。该系列的初版可能是《客西马尼园的痛苦》[273]，但因采用他谴责为"拙劣木刻技法"的粗糙雕刻方式，最终被弃用。 然而原作素描定然赋予了面朝下倒地的基督那种哥特式张力——这种张力曾驱使丢勒在《启示录》系列中倾注毕生心血[262]。1511 年出版《小受难》时，他用更符合个人刻线风格的宁静画面取代了这幅绝望之作[274]。后期设计中，基督已获得庄严气度，这正是通过——

peror Maximilian’s official artist after he began the imperial woodcuts that still enact the Hapsburg dream of glory.
马克西米利安皇帝的御用画家，自其开启帝国木刻版画创作以来，这些作品至今仍在演绎哈布斯堡王朝的荣光梦想。
Yet all his young energy returned to him once again in his 405 when he became the first great artist to experiment with the new medium of etching. He etched only six plates, probably because the acid bit the iron too raggedly to suit his demand for exact detail. But just because etching on iron prevented him from finishing minutely, it loosened all the free fury of his swiftest sketches. When he copied his impulsive pen drawing [ 275 ] onto the etching plate [ 276 ], he did not, like most artists, sober the emotion; he intensified it.
然而，当他四十岁时，所有年轻时的活力再度涌现，成为首位尝试蚀刻这一新媒介的伟大艺术家。他仅蚀刻了六块版，或许是因为酸蚀在铁板上留下的痕迹过于参差不齐，无法满足他对精确细节的要求。 正因铁版蚀刻阻碍了他精雕细琢的追求，反而释放出他速写中最狂放不羁的激情。当他将那幅冲动的钢笔画[275]转印至蚀刻版[276]时，并未像多数艺术家那样抑制情感，反而将其升华得愈发炽烈。
Dürer suits us best today when he dares his wildest arabesques, for he was the giddiest doodler in all art. His speed in scratching the etching plate set free the ecstasy that he rightly considered his rarest gift when he wrote that “what one artist sketches with a quill in a day may outdo what another will labor over for a year.”
杜勒最适合我们今日的审美，当他挥洒最狂野的阿拉伯式卷曲纹饰时，因他堪称艺术史上最放肆的涂鸦者。他在蚀刻版上飞速刻划的动作，释放出他自认最珍贵的狂喜天赋——正如他所言："一位艺术家用鹅毛笔一日速写之作，或胜过另一人苦心雕琢整年之作。"
Dürer’s figures Dürer recalled that during his youth the Venetian painter and engraver Jacopo de’ Barbari “showed me the figures of a man and a woman which he had drawn according to a canon of proportion. I would rather have seen what he meant than see a new kingdom.” Actually Barbari confessed anatomical ignorance in the slack and mannered grace of his figures [ 277 ], but he teased Dürer into a lifelong search for a nonexistent formula. Had Dürer met Leonardo da Vinci instead of Jacopo de’ Barbari, the Florentine would have shown him that Italian nudes achieved beauty by functioning like mechanisms of pivots and levers. Mantegna would have shown him the antique sculptor’s structure of bulk that overrides details. But since copying Leonardo’s drawings and Mantegna’s engravings did not teach Dürer the logic of function and structure, and since he probably had a horror of watching the dissections that underlay most Italian figure drawing, he went to work in his own methodical way by measuring men, women, and children with calipers to plot their exact outlines [ 281 ]. In time he came to see outlines before he saw the form within, so that each separate thing explodes against its bounds, and the distinctness of details fragments the whole. His search for the ideal
丢勒的人物画丢勒回忆道，青年时期威尼斯画家兼版画家雅科波·德·巴尔巴里曾向他展示"一幅按比例法绘制的人体素描，男女各一。我宁愿亲眼见识他所说的比例法，也不愿目睹新王国的诞生。" 实际上，巴尔巴里在人物松垮做作的姿态中暴露了解剖学上的无知[277]，却诱使丢勒终生追寻一个不存在的公式。若丢勒遇见的是莱昂纳多·达·芬奇而非雅科波·德·巴尔巴里，这位佛罗伦萨大师本会向他展示：意大利裸体画的美丽源于其如枢轴与杠杆般运作的机械结构。 曼特尼亚则会向他展示古希腊雕塑家那种凌驾于细节之上的体积结构。但由于临摹达·芬奇的素描和曼特尼亚的版画未能教会丢勒功能与结构的逻辑，加之他大概对解剖学研究心存畏惧——而这正是多数意大利人体素描的根基——他便以自己的方法论投入创作：用卡尺测量男女老幼，精确勾勒其轮廓线 [281]。久而久之，他先看见轮廓而非内在形态，致使每个独立物体在边界处爆裂，细节的鲜明性将整体碎裂。他追寻理想的

277

Apollo and Diana. Engraving by Jacopo de′ Barbari
阿波罗与狄安娜。雅科波·德·巴尔巴里雕版画


nude led him to engrave Adam and Eve, God’s own personally made patterns of beauty [ 278 ]. He must have thought that here he could challenge the Italians at their own instructive specialty of figure drawing, for he signed this one print only with his full name and address, the way Pollaiuolo had signed his anatomical pattern sheet, the Battle of the Naked Men [184]. Adam’s gesture and proportions recall the Apollo Belvedere [279], unearthed in Rome a quarter century before and already the supreme model of male beauty that it continued to be until about 1800. Since Dürer probably never saw Rome, he must have known the marble through a drawing of it glimpsed in northern Italy, or shown him by Jacopo de’ Barbari. He engraved the Adam and Eve with such caution-one might say trepida-tion-that he finished the entire background before he got the courage to sneak up on the figures, around which he reserved an aura of blank to allow him to fatten them if need be [ 280 ]. He may have known the saying of Polycletus, that beauty depends on adjustments the thickness of a fingernail. Though Dürer modeled the flesh with a powdering of dots and flicks of a delicacy never seen before, however often attempted since, the engraving fails to satisfy because he was striving too tensely to achieve his masterpiece. Details steal the show, like the mouse playing by the cat’s claws in the closing instant of the world’s innocence.
裸体画促使他刻画了亚当与夏娃——上帝亲手塑造的美丽典范[278]。他想必认为，在此领域他能挑战意大利人在人物素描这一教学专长的优势，因此仅在这幅版画上署了全名与地址，效仿波拉伊乌洛在解剖图谱《裸体男子之战》[184]上的署名方式。 亚当的姿态与比例令人联想到贝尔维德雷的阿波罗雕像[279]——这尊四分之一世纪前出土于罗马的雕塑，自问世起便成为男性美的至高典范，其地位直至 1800 年左右仍未动摇。杜勒很可能从未踏足罗马，他所知的这尊大理石雕像，想必是通过在意大利北部瞥见其素描，或是雅科波·德·巴尔巴里向他展示的。 他在刻画亚当与夏娃时如此谨慎——甚至可称之为战战兢兢——先完成整个背景才鼓起勇气悄悄接近人物，并在人物周围预留空白区域，以便必要时增厚其体态[280]。 他或许知晓波利克莱托斯的名言：美在于指甲厚度的微调。尽管丢勒以空前精妙的点状粉饰与轻巧笔触塑造肌理——后世虽屡屡效仿却难企及——这幅版画终究令人遗憾，只因他为成就杰作而过度绷紧了创作神经。细节反倒成为焦点，恰似世界纯真消逝的瞬间，那只在猫爪旁嬉戏的小鼠。

Dürer's figures (丢勒的人物画)


  丢勒的人物画

281

The well-proportioned man. Woodcut by Dürer in von menschlicher Proportion, Nuremberg (Dürer), 1528. From 1532 edition
比例匀称的人体。丢勒木刻版画，选自《人体比例论》，纽伦堡（丢勒），1528 年。摘自 1532 年版
As Dürer grew older, he studied human proportions more and more. His 30 years of researches appeared just after his death in a book with woodcuts of a startling pedantry [ 281 ]. His treatise became the first study in visual statistics, as he tabulated the proportions of 200 or 300 humans by measuring them in units of 1 / 600 1 / 600 1//6001 / 600 of their height, as if to reach beauty through arithmetic. The involutions of his method gave it the authority of the arcane, and the dogmatism of his book did much to slacken the instinctive energy of the German Renaissance.
随着丢勒年岁渐长，他对人体比例的研究日益深入。他三十年的研究成果在他去世后不久便以一本木刻画册的形式问世，其中展现的严谨程度令人惊叹[281]。 这部论著开创了视觉统计学研究先河——他通过测量 200 至 300 名人体比例，将其以身高百分比为单位制成表格，仿佛要用算术推导出美学法则。其方法论的复杂性赋予了它玄奥权威，而书中教条式的论述，在很大程度上削弱了德国文艺复兴时期蓬勃的创造力。

Portrait engraving (肖像雕刻)


After Alexander the Great, rulers began to circulate their portraits on coins, where only gods had been before. The first sovereign to consider censoring printed portraits was Queen Elizabeth I, who, when she was 30, drafted an edict that she apparently never issued. Aware of her womanly presence, she decreed that copies of an official portrait by “some speciall coning payntor” should replace the “deformed” ones then being made by “paynting, graving and printing.”
肖像雕刻亚历山大大帝之后，统治者开始在钱币上铸造自己的肖像——此前钱币上仅有神祇的形象。 首位考虑审查印刷肖像的君主是伊丽莎白一世女王。三十岁那年，她起草了一道显然从未颁布的诏令。深谙自身女性魅力的她下令，应由"某位技艺精湛的画家"绘制的官方肖像取代当时通过"绘画、雕刻和印刷"制作的"变形"画像。
The first printed portrait of a living private individual was the profile of an author in a Milanese book of 1479. Italian books followed it with many portraits of artists and intellectuals. The intellectual began to be publicized in single-sheet prints when Cranach made three engravings of Luther in 1520/21 [299], and Dürer engraved Willibald Pirckheimer and the reformers Erasmus and Melanchthon [ 282 ] in 1524 to 26. Dürer had been making portraits ever since he drew
首幅活人的私人肖像画印于 1479 年米兰出版的书籍中，呈现的是某位作家的侧面像。此后意大利书籍中陆续出现了众多艺术家与知识分子的肖像。 1520/21 年，克拉纳赫为路德创作三幅版画[299]，1524 至 26 年，丢勒刻画威利巴尔德·皮尔克海默及宗教改革家伊拉斯谟与墨兰顿[282]，知识分子形象由此开始通过单幅版画传播。自丢勒绘制肖像以来，他便持续创作人物肖像。
himself in a mirror as a boy of 13, and he may have cast his very longest influence through his six engraved portraits of men, one made just before he traveled to the Netherlands, the other five soon afterward. His study of Flemish painting and his realization of his own world importance combined to invest these last engravings with a haunting authority. In the best of them his overpowering personality felt inspired to cast a spell that engulfed his sitters, making every man hanker to be thus dramatized. These prints founded a profession of portrait engraving that became one of the best paid and most dependable specialties of printmaking until about 1900.
他曾将十三岁的自己映入镜中，而他最深远的影响或许源于那六幅男性肖像版画——其中一幅创作于赴荷兰之前，其余五幅则在归国不久后完成。他对佛兰德绘画的研究，加之对自身世界级地位的觉悟，共同赋予这些晚期版画一种令人难忘的权威感。 在最杰出的作品中，他那摄人心魄的个性仿佛受到启迪，施展魔法将模特们完全笼罩，令每位男性都渴望获得如此戏剧化的呈现。这些版画开创了肖像雕刻这一职业，直至 1900 年前后，它始终是版画领域报酬最高、最稳定的专业领域之一。
Dürer drew important and impatient people quickly by looking through a fixed eyehole to trace the outline on a pane of glass [ 283 ]. But to publish portraits profitably, the printmaker had to speed up production as well as preparation. This was
丢勒通过固定的窥视孔观察，在玻璃板上勾勒轮廓，迅速完成了对重要人物和急切人物的素描[283]。但要盈利地出版肖像画，版画家不仅需要加快准备工作，还必须提高生产效率。这正是

Portrait engraving  肖像雕刻

285 Etching and engraving by Lucas of Leiden, 1520
285 莱顿的卢卡斯蚀刻与雕刻作品，1520 年
accomplished when Lucas of Leiden copied Dürer’s woodcut of Maximilian [ 284 ] to put a print [ 285 ] on sale while the emperor’s death, in 1519, was still news. Lucas rapidly etched most of the picture, reserving the slow graver for the head and hands. By introducing copper instead of the usual iron, he managed to etch lines neat enough to blend with the engraved additions. This mixed technique was to become standard for reproductive copperplates. After about 1700, almost all so-called “engravings” are really etchings touched up with the graver to smooth over transitions.
当莱顿的卢卡斯复制丢勒的马克西米利安木刻版画[284]并将其制成版画[285]出售时，皇帝于 1519 年逝世的消息仍属新鲜事。 卢卡斯迅速以蚀刻法处理画面主体，仅保留刻刀处理头部与手部。通过采用铜版替代传统铁版，他成功蚀刻出与雕刻部分完美融合的精细线条。这种混合技法后来成为复制品铜版画的标准工艺。约 1700 年后，几乎所有所谓"雕刻版画"实为蚀刻版画经刻刀修饰以平滑过渡的产物。
Lucas’ shortcut came in handy when the psychological imagination of the age of Shakespeare, Cervantes, Molière, and Racine produced perceptive portraits in quantity. The first exquisitely sensitive portrait engraver was Goltzius, who made a few big copperplates and more in locket size on silver. Although he engraved portraits only as a sideline, he attained an almost neurotic insight [ 286 ] that many artists tried to imitate but few could equal.
当莎士比亚、塞万提斯、莫里哀和拉辛时代的心理想象力大量产出敏锐的肖像时，卢卡斯的捷径便派上了用场。 首位精妙绝伦的肖像版画家是戈尔齐乌斯，他制作了几幅大型铜版画，以及更多银质的吊坠尺寸作品。尽管刻画肖像只是他的副业，却达到了近乎神经质的洞察力[286]——许多艺术家试图效仿，却鲜有能与之比肩者。
In Italy, the 76 woodcut heads in the 1568 edition of Vasari’s Lives of the Artists prepared the way for the first specialist in portrait prints, Ottavio Leoni. This Knight of Malta drew all kinds of Romans in pastels from which he engraved 40
在意大利，瓦萨里 1568 年版《艺术家传记》中的 76 幅木刻头像为首位肖像版画专家奥塔维奥·莱奥尼铺平了道路。这位马耳他骑士团骑士以粉彩绘制各类罗马人肖像，并据此雕刻了 40 幅版画。
small coppers, mostly of writers and artists. An accomplished, truthful portraitist when he began in middle age to engrave, he clustered dots like Barocci [ 436 ] to model faces, and rendered lace and breezy hair with self-taught freshness [ 287 ]. He imitated Venetian and Florentine woodcut portraits by framing many of his heads in ovals or octagons.
小型铜版画，多为文人雅士肖像。这位技艺精湛、真实传神的肖像画家，中年开始从事雕刻时，便如巴洛奇[436]般以密集的点状技法塑造面容，更以独具匠心的清新笔触[287]刻画蕾丝与随风飘扬的发丝。他效仿威尼斯与佛罗伦萨的木刻肖像风格，常将人物头像置于椭圆或八边形框中。
In Spain the example of Italy produced one portrait engraving that survives in only one impression [ 288 ] but whose unprofessional graving packs enough expression to have founded a whole school of printmaking. Who but young Velázquez could have achieved such painterly force? If he made other prints, they probably vanished in the Madrid palace fire of 1734 that seems to have destroyed all but a handful of his hundreds of drawings and oil sketches.
在西班牙，意大利的范例催生了一幅肖像版画，现仅存一版印迹[288]，但其粗粝的刻痕却蕴含着足以开创整个版画流派的艺术张力。若非年轻的委拉斯开兹，谁能成就这般绘画般的力量？倘若他创作过其他版画，它们很可能在 1734 年马德里宫殿大火中灰飞烟灭——那场大火似乎摧毁了他数百幅素描与油画速写中的绝大多数，仅存寥寥数幅。

Portrait engraving  肖像雕刻
In France the earliest school of portrait specialists appeared about 1510. Even before there was a print-collecting public, Catherine de Medicis employed portraitists to draw her courtiers for herself and for presentation to other courts. Henry IV, like Queen Elizabeth I, issued a few official engraved portraits, and Louis XIV incorporated portrait engraving into his bureaucracy after about 1650 with huge souvenir broadsides (thèses) that listed the subjects a candidate for a law degree was prepared to discuss in his examination. The thèse often displayed a large engraving of some bigwig who could further a young man’s career. The politics of patronage made the great portrait engravers of the age of Louis XIV waste their skill on faces of now forgotten lawyers and civil servants, with hardly a worthy engraving of any great French artist, musician, writer, or royal mistress.
在法国，最早的肖像画专业流派约于 1510 年出现。早在版画收藏群体形成之前，凯瑟琳·德·美第奇就雇佣肖像画家为她绘制宫廷成员画像，既供个人收藏，也用于向其他宫廷献礼。 亨利四世效仿伊丽莎白一世，曾发行数幅官方雕版肖像。路易十四则于 1650 年后将肖像雕版纳入官僚体系，通过巨幅纪念画报（thèses）列明法学学位候选人需在考试中论述的课题。 这些纪念画册常配有权贵人物的大幅版画，这些人物能助年轻人的仕途一臂之力。庇护政治的运作，使得路易十四时代杰出的肖像版画家们，将才华耗费在如今已被遗忘的律师和公务员的面容上，几乎没有为任何伟大的法国艺术家、音乐家、作家或王室情妇创作过值得称道的版画作品。
Leoni’s portrait formula came to France with Claude Mellan after Mellan had spent 12 years in Rome. There he learned to exaggerate Villamena’s manner [409] in his own unique style of curving, swelling parallels without crosshatching, all sparkling as limpidly as sunlight under the water of an aquarium [ 289 ]. The tricki-
莱奥尼的肖像技法由克劳德·梅兰带入法国，此前梅兰在罗马苦修十二载。他在那里习得维拉梅纳的夸张手法[409]，并将其转化为独特的艺术语言——以无交叉阴影的曲折膨胀平行线勾勒，所有笔触都如水族馆中阳光穿透水层般澄澈闪耀[289]。这种技巧——

The greatest French portrait engraver was Nanteuil, who mastered everybody’s technical advances and then subordinated his consummate skill to analyzing his sitters. By drawing in pastels like Leoni, he directed his eye away from line toward form and color in 216 engraved portraits that include 11 life-size heads of Louis XIV and 14 of Mazarin. Nothing could be more uniform than his plain frames, simple lighting, three-quarter poses, and fly-screen backgrounds ruled by assis-tants-and nothing short of life itself could vary more than his characters [ 290 ]. He clarified his art as unobtrusively as Racine, who was then polishing his alexandrines to a desperate delicacy.
法国最伟大的肖像版画家当属南特伊，他精通所有前人的技艺革新，继而将炉火纯青的技法服务于对人物的剖析。他效法莱奥尼以粉彩作画，在 216 幅版画肖像中将视线从线条转向形态与色彩——其中包括 11 幅路易十四等身像与 14 幅马萨林像。 其作品的统一性无可匹敌：素雅的画框、简洁的光影、三四分之三侧身姿态、由助手绘制的纱窗背景——而人物形象的丰富性却堪比生命本身[290]。他以拉辛般不着痕迹的技艺澄澈艺术境界，彼时拉辛正将亚历山大体诗句打磨至极致的精妙。
Nanteuil’s successors were not asked for psychological analysis by statesmen, who ordered full-length effigies in robes of office, treading on a baroque litter of professional paraphernalia. The psychological portrait returned when the Marquis de Marigny, Madame de Pompadour’s brother, began to direct French official art after studying in Italy with C.-N. Cochin II. There Cochin, as successful an artist as lived in all the 18th century, had absorbed the recurrent classical taste for the profiles that he admired on Greek vases and antique coins, revived in Renaissance medals and paintings. In the Salon of 1750, Cochin exhibited some pencil profiles à l’antique, which pleased so generally that over 260 of his drawings were etched in the next 20 years [ 291 ]. His friendly shrewdness evokes the very voices of his fascinating contemporaries.
南特伊的继任者们并未被政要们要求进行心理分析，后者们订购的肖像都是身着礼服的全身像，脚踩着巴洛克式的官场杂物堆。当庞巴杜夫人之弟马里尼侯爵在意大利师从小科尚二世后开始执掌法国官方艺术时，心理肖像画才得以复兴。 这位堪称十八世纪最杰出的艺术家，在意大利汲取了古典主义对侧面的偏爱——这种美学源自希腊陶器与古币的轮廓，经文艺复兴时期的奖章与绘画得以复兴。 在 1750 年的沙龙展上，科钦展出数幅仿古铅笔侧面肖像，广受好评，此后二十年间其逾 260 幅素描被制成蚀刻版画[291]。他友善而敏锐的笔触，仿佛让那些迷人的同时代人物重现声影。
Portrait engraving  肖像雕刻
292
Thomas Jefferson, aged 62. Physionotrace etching by Charles-B.-J. Févret de Saint-Mémin, 1805
托马斯·杰斐逊，62 岁。查尔斯-B.-J. 费弗雷·德·圣梅明于 1805 年创作的物理肖像蚀刻版画。
A portraitist had merely to satisfy his sitter and the next of kin until “scientific” exactitude was required of him after 1775, when J. K. Lavater began to publish a classification (based on Aristotle) of men’s characters as indicated by their facial characteristics. Lavater considered the profile to be the most revealing view. To draw profiles in machine-made facsimile, a cellist in the Versailles palace orchestra about 1784 invented the physionotrace: squinting through a surveyor’s sight of crossed hairs, he followed the sitter’s profile, thereby moving an attached pencil that traced the profile on paper. A pantograph then reduced this life-size outline mechanically to a small silhouette or copperplate etching. The physionotrace, by which even an amateur could achieve truthful likenesses, enabled refugees from the French Revolution to support themselves in the new United States [ 292 ]. This mechanized recording of profiles promoted a standard of accuracy that was not really met until photography became available in 1839. When photographic portraits began to be printed in halftone and gravure, these reproductions deprived the printmaker of the dependable specialty that Dürer had created for him three centuries before.
肖像画家只需取悦模特及其亲属，直到 1775 年后才被要求达到"科学"的精确度——当时 J·K·拉瓦特开始出版基于亚里士多德理论的分类学著作，通过面部特征解析人类性格。拉瓦特认为侧面轮廓最具揭示性。 为实现机械复制侧面肖像，凡尔赛宫乐团的一位大提琴手于 1784 年前后发明了"面容描绘仪"：通过测量仪的十字准线眯眼观察，他沿着模特侧脸轮廓移动，附着的铅笔便在纸上同步描绘出侧面轮廓。 随后通过机械缩放仪将真人尺寸轮廓缩小为小型剪影或铜版蚀刻画。这种连业余者都能绘制逼真肖像的"面相描绘仪"，使法国大革命的流亡者得以在美国谋生[292]。这种机械化侧面记录技术确立的精度标准，直至 1839 年摄影术问世才真正被超越。 当摄影肖像开始采用半色调和凹版印刷技术复制时，这些复制品剥夺了版画家赖以生存的可靠专长——而这项专长三世纪前正是由丢勒为他们开创的。

Burgkmair and the emperor (布尔克迈尔与皇帝)


Hans Burgkmair, Dürer’s junior by two years, lived in Augsburg, the international center for the Fugger Bank and imperial politics. Dürer, farther north in more Gothic Nuremberg, had to assault the Italian Renaissance as a grown man; Burgkmair grew naturally into its clarity. As a lad of 14, Burgkmair began to illustrate the church books that Ratdolt printed on his return to Augsburg, soon producing the first woodcut picture in black and three colors [ 76 ]. The relaxed grace that Burgkmair learned from Schongauer grew so Italianate that he must have followed Ratdolt’s example by going to Italy. The only proofs of such a voyage are a typical Burgkmair woodcut [ 293 ] printed (belatedly?) in a Venetian missal, and a cut of Death Killing the Lovers, with its gondola,
伯克迈尔与皇帝汉斯·伯克迈尔比丢勒小两岁，定居于奥格斯堡——这个福格银行与帝国政治的国际中心。而更北方的哥特式纽伦堡孕育的丢勒，成年后才开始冲击意大利文艺复兴；伯克迈尔却自然而然地融入了这种明晰美学。 十四岁的伯克迈尔开始为拉特多尔特返奥格斯堡后印刷的教会书籍绘制插图，很快便创作出首幅黑白三色木刻版画[76]。他从施恩高尔那里习得的从容优雅愈发呈现意大利风格，想必是效仿拉特多尔特远赴意大利取经。 此行仅存两处佐证：其一是刊于威尼斯弥撒书（或为迟印？）的典型伯克迈尔木刻版画[293]，其二是《死神夺命》版画——画中可见贡多拉船只，

After having started and developed the German method of color woodcut by printing black lines over color [ 294 ], Burgkmair in 1510 printed the first dated analysis of a picture in three intensities of one color [ 295 ], the method that Ugo da Carpi in Venice claimed as his own invention six years later [ 347 ]. Had Ugo, before 1510, made color woodcuts that Burgkmair
威尼斯式烟囱、古典装饰与波提切利式的群像奔涌，在建筑网格中获得稳定[295]。 在开创并发展德国彩色木刻技法——通过在彩色上叠印黑色线条[294]之后，布尔克迈尔于 1510 年首次印制了以单色三种浓度呈现的带日期图像分析[295]，而威尼斯的乌戈·达·卡尔皮六年后宣称此法为其独创[347]。 倘若乌戈在 1510 年前制作过与布尔克迈尔相似的彩色木刻版画

Burgkmair and the emperor
布尔克迈尔与皇帝
imitated? Or was Ugo stealing an invention that properly belongs to Burgkmair?
是模仿？还是乌戈窃取了本应属于布尔克迈尔的发明？
The three blocks of Burgkmair’s Death Strangling the Lovers were cut by the Antwerper Jost de Negker, whose Augsburg woodcutting shop was Germany’s best. Since Burgkmair also cut some of his own blocks (among them, certainly, the block that appeared in Venice with such un-Venetian cutting), he always spared the cutter the drudgery of crosshatching by shading in swelling parallels that are easy for the knife. The painterly richness of his black and white, and his urbane observation of people, made him an ideal illustrator for the various glorifications of the Hapsburgs that Emperor Maximilian dictated on his constant journeys-even while being rowed across Lake Constance. From about 1510 until Maximilian’s death in 1519, Burgkmair drew nearly 300 woodcuts for this frustrated royal author, who revised the blocks by inserting plugs with changes in a vacillation that in the end left almost all of them unpublished.
伯克迈尔的《死神扼杀恋人》三幅版画由安特卫普人约斯特·德·内格克雕刻，其位于奥格斯堡的木刻工坊堪称德国之最。 由于伯克迈尔也亲自雕刻部分版块（其中必然包括那幅在威尼斯出现的、刻法极不威尼斯风格的版画），他总会为雕刻师省去繁琐的交叉阴影处理，转而采用便于刀工处理的起伏平行阴影。 他黑白画作中蕴含的绘画丰润感，以及对人物的世故观察力，使他成为马克西米利安皇帝在频繁旅途中——即便在康斯坦茨湖划船渡湖时——所命题的各类哈布斯堡家族颂扬题材的理想插图画家。 从 1510 年左右到马克西米利安 1519 年去世，布格克迈尔为这位郁郁不得志的皇家作家绘制了近 300 幅木刻版画。这位皇帝反复修改版块，插入修改块进行调整，最终几乎所有作品都未能出版。

296 Noah, Emperor Maximilian's earliest ancestor. Woodcut by Burgkmair in Genealogy of the Emperor Maximilian, 1509-12
296 诺亚，马克西米利安皇帝的最早祖先。伯克迈尔木刻版画，见《马克西米利安皇帝世系图》，1509-12 年
Burgkmair’s first imperial assignment was the Hapsburg genealogy in over 90 cuts, starting with Noah [ 296 ]. Despite imperial nagging, he put grace and ease into the 121 illustrations to the emperor’s political autobiography, in which Maximilian, the White King, represents himself as outwitting the statesmen of Europe, and instructing armorers, musicians, dancers, painters [ 297 ], and cooks in their several professions. After printing a few proofs, Maximilian characteristically abandoned what would have become the grandest book of the northern Renaissance. Luckily, practically all of the blocks have survived for modern reprints. Maximilian, despite his intricate hesitations, was astute enough to choose Burgkmair to present his private life to posterity, while employing the less malleable, more public art of Dürer for the woodcuts of his triumphal arch and imaginary processions [ 151 ]. The dream of grandeur that this impecunious emperor committed to mere paper has outlasted what many richer princes built in marble.
布尔克迈尔的首项皇室任务是创作逾 90 幅的哈布斯堡王朝谱系图，以诺亚为开篇[296]。 尽管皇帝屡屡催促，他仍为皇帝的政治自传绘制了 121 幅优雅从容的插图。在这部自传中，"白国王"马克西米利安将自己塑造成智胜欧洲政要的形象，并指导铠甲匠、音乐家、舞者、画家[297]及厨师各自的职业技艺。印制少量样本后，马克西米利安一如既往地放弃了这部本可成为北方文艺复兴时期最宏伟著作的书稿。 所幸绝大部分木刻版坯得以保存，为现代重印提供了可能。 尽管犹豫不决，马克西米利安仍足够精明地选择伯克迈尔来向后世展现其私人生活，同时采用杜勒更具公信力却不易掌控的艺术风格，为凯旋门与幻想游行场景创作木刻版画[151]。这位穷困皇帝将宏伟梦想寄托于纸张的举动，其生命力竟超越了许多富庶君主用大理石筑就的建筑。

Cranach (克拉纳赫)


Figure 90: 298  图 90：298
The Crucifixion. Woodcut by Lucas Cranach I, 1502
《受难》卢卡斯·克拉纳赫一世木刻版画，1502 年
Cranach Lucas Cranach was born a year after Dürer, some 50 miles north of him in a village now called Kronach. In Vienna, at about 30, he drew a few woodcuts [ 298 ] in a storm of agony that calmed down when, at 32, he settled for life as painter to the Duke of Saxony at Wittenberg. In that garrison of religious revolution during the first half century of the Reformation, Cranach painted and designed woodcuts, stained glass, weapons, and wall hangings until his mid-40s, when he gradually delegated his art to two sons and more than ten assistants. He also founded a pharmacy that his descendants ran for 300 years, and became burgomaster and the duke’s political counselor and propagandist. Over 1000 paintings survive from his workshop, which perpetuated his style for 80 years until the death of Lucas II in 1586. Both father and son painted so rapidly that “before another could arrange his brushes and colors, and think what to do, they would have finished a picture.” The two Lucas Cranachs invented Protestant allegory and recorded the founders of the Reformation in incisive, neurotic likenesses. Their painting shop dominated Germany while Dürer, a slow painter, made his money and his
克拉纳赫·卢卡斯·克拉纳赫生于丢勒之后一年，其出生地位于丢勒以北约 50 英里处，现称克罗纳赫的村庄。约三十岁时，他在维也纳创作了数幅木刻版画[298]，创作过程充满痛苦挣扎。三十二岁定居维滕贝格后，他成为萨克森公爵的御用画家，此后生活渐趋平静。 在宗教改革初期半个世纪的宗教革命据点中，克拉纳赫持续创作绘画、设计木刻版画、彩绘玻璃、武器及壁挂，直至四十余岁时，才逐步将艺术事务委托给两个儿子和十余名助手。他还创办了一家药房，由后代经营长达三百余年，并担任市长、公爵的政治顾问与宣传家。 其工作室流传至今的画作逾千幅，其艺术风格延续八十载，直至 1586 年小卢卡斯·克拉纳赫逝世。父子二人作画迅捷如风，"待旁人整理画笔颜料、构思创作时，他们早已完成一幅画作"。 两位克拉纳赫开创了新教寓言画派，以犀利而神经质的笔触描绘宗教改革先驱。当杜勒这位慢工出细活的画家还在为生计奔波时，他们的画室已统治了整个德国画坛。
fame through prints. Dürer’s woodcuts furnished themes that Lucas I often em- bellished with curlicues.
通过版画成名。丢勒的木刻作品提供了主题，卢卡斯一世常以卷曲装饰加以点缀。
The elder Cranach made the only lifelike portraits of his intimate friend Martin Luther [ 299 ], who chose him to supervise the printing press that helped to drive home the Protestant attack “by preaching and talking and singing and writing and drawing.” Luther’s inclusion of drawing contributed to make his press the papacy’s most dreaded arsenal of opposition, as Cranach printed pamphlet after pamphlet in the pocket format that Savonarola had popularized for propaganda [157]. Peddlers slipped these pamphlets past Catholic censorship into towns, villages, and farms throughout Germany and beyond. Unlike the imaginative cuts on Savonarola’s paper covers, the cuts by the Cranachs decorate Luther’s tracts without illustrating their religious themes [300]. The Cranachs’ sprightly ornaments were copied all over Germany as Luther’s writings spread by piracies that imitated the original editions even to faking Wittenberg as the place of publication. Luther did not object to piracy-every printer’s way of life-for, since he earned nothing by publishing, he lost nothing by piracy. He was, however, annoyed when Nuremberg printed a stolen manuscript before he could publish it himself. To protect his printers, he persuaded the Wittenberg town council to ask the Nuremberg printers
老克拉纳赫为挚友马丁·路德创作了唯一栩栩如生的肖像画[299]，路德特意委任他监督印刷机运作——这台机器通过"布道、言谈、歌唱、书写与绘画"，助力新教攻势深入人心。 路德将绘画纳入传播手段，使他的印刷厂成为教廷最畏惧的反对派武器库——克拉纳赫接连印制了萨沃纳罗拉推广的口袋尺寸宣传册[157]。小贩们将这些册子偷运过天主教审查，散布至德国及周边地区的城镇、村庄和农场。 与萨沃纳罗拉纸封上富有想象力的雕刻不同，克拉纳赫父子的雕刻装饰着路德的传单，却未阐释其宗教主题[300]。随着路德著作通过盗版传播——这些盗版甚至伪造维滕贝格为出版地以仿冒原版——克拉纳赫父子灵动的装饰图案在德国各地被广泛复制。 路德并不反对盗版——这是印刷商的生存之道——因出版本身无利可图，盗版对他亦无损失。但当纽伦堡印刷商抢先印制他尚未出版的手稿时，他却大为恼怒。为保护合作印刷商，他游说维滕贝格市政委员会要求纽伦堡印刷商

At home his translation of the New Testament, the so-called September Bible of 1522, sold some 5000 copies in ten weeks despite the high price of two and a half guilders, and was reprinted 80 times in Germany and Switzerland during Luther’s lifetime, thus establishing a literary language for all Germany. Like all northern New Testaments, it illustrated nothing but the Apocalypse [ 264 ], a decision that must have been Cranach’s, since Luther cared little for Saint John’s vision.
请暂缓七八周直至本土版本售罄，并请仔细校对校样。在他家乡，其《新约》译本——即 1522 年所谓的《九月圣经》——尽管定价高达两块半盾，十周内仍售出约五千册，并在路德生前于德意志及瑞士重印八十次，由此确立了全德意志的文学语言体系。 与所有北方新约译本相同，该版本仅配有《启示录》插图[264]——此决定应出自克拉纳赫之手，因路德对圣约翰的异象鲜少关注。
As the only German artist who ever influenced important decisions at court, Cranach played his part in a ceremonial world, ornate and sensuous. The kept minxes that he drew and painted as Venus all emphasize their nakedness by wearing necklaces and turbans that are stylish because absurd [ 301 ]. His knights and ladies carry off their eccentric accouterments with the assurance of provincial grandees. Their courtly callousness strikes a little shudder into the dank backyard
作为唯一一位曾影响宫廷重大决策的德国艺术家，克拉纳赫在那个华美而感官的仪式世界中扮演着重要角色。 他笔下那些被宠爱的妖姬们化身维纳斯，皆以项链与头巾彰显裸露之美——这些装饰因荒诞而时髦[301]。骑士与贵妇们身披奇装异服，却带着乡绅般的笃定姿态。他们宫廷式的冷漠，在阴暗的后院里掀起一阵战栗。
where the Baptist kneels under their idle eyes to receive the formality of a beheading [ 302 ].
当施洗者在他们无动于衷的目光下跪下，接受斩首的仪式时[302]。
Cranach also pioneered in a color woodcut to imitate a German drawing in black line with white accents on tinted paper. His Saint Christopher [303] was first published as a complete black and white cut. The date, 1506, was then removed and the black block was imposed on a solid pale tint from another block in which accents were gouged to expose the white paper. Cranach thus refined the picture printing in colors that Ratdolt had started at Augsburg in 1487 [76], which differed in its whole intention from the flat areas of tone in the Italian chiaroscuros [ 492 ].
克拉纳赫还开创性地采用彩色木刻技法，在染色纸上模仿德国素描的黑色线条与白色点缀效果。他的《圣克里斯托弗》[303]最初以纯黑白版画形式出版。 随后移除 1506 年题款，将黑色版块叠加于另一块浅色底版之上——该底版经凿刻处理使白色纸面显露。克拉纳赫由此完善了拉德奥尔特 1487 年在奥格斯堡开创的彩色版画技法[76]，其整体意图有别于意大利明暗画法中平铺的色调区域[492]。

Altdorfer Albrecht Altdorfer, who was about five years younger than Dürer, came only passingly under Dürer’s influence after he had formed his own style of close engraving by copying Italian nielli [113]. In Regensburg, where shipping brought foreigners and fresh ideas to the head of navigation on the Danube, he founded a local school of art, much as Cranach did at Wittenberg. With something like Dürer’s versatility, Altdorfer painted, drew in watercolor, and designed fortifications, municipal buildings, and silverware. He was the only German printmaker of Dürer’s generation who worked more on copper than on wood, and who illustrated no books. He recorded the synagogue at Regensburg, at the time of its destruction, in an etching [ 304 ] that is the first print of an interior seen by a builder as a structure, not by a painter as a background for figures, or by a draftsman as linear perspective. It is the first print of a room that says “I was there.” When, like all men of the Reformation, Altdorfer turned to the Bible, he went to episodes of intimacy and feminine tenderness, as when the Virgin searches the temple for her 12-year-old son [ 305 ]. These appealing little engravings, in a style based partly on Dürer and partly on Marcantonio’s tranquil manner [ 339 ], domesticated the miniature format of Italian nielli to Germany and set the example for the German Little Masters [ 315 ].
阿尔布雷希特·阿尔特多夫（Altdorfer）比丢勒年轻约五岁，在通过临摹意大利黑釉工艺[113]形成自己独特的精细蚀刻风格后，仅受到丢勒的短暂影响。 在雷根斯堡——这条多瑙河航运要冲因水运而汇聚异域风情与新思想——他创立了地方艺术学派，其影响力堪比克拉纳赫在维滕贝格的成就。阿尔特多夫兼具杜勒式的多才多艺，既绘油画、水彩画，又设计城防工事、市政建筑及银器。他是杜勒同辈中唯一更偏重铜版而非木版创作的德国版画家，且从未为书籍绘制插图。 他在版画中记录了雷根斯堡犹太教堂遭毁时的景象[304]——这是首幅以建筑师视角呈现室内空间的版画，不同于画家作为人物背景的描绘，也不同于制图师的线性透视法。这是首幅宣告"我曾在此"的室内版画。 当阿尔特多夫像所有宗教改革者那样转向《圣经》题材时，他偏爱描绘亲密场景与女性柔情，例如圣母在圣殿寻觅十二岁爱子的画面[305]。 这些迷人的小型版画，其风格部分源于丢勒，部分承袭马尔坎托尼奥的静谧笔法[339]，将意大利尼埃利微型画的精致格式引入德国，并为德国小大师们树立了典范[315]。
In his slightly larger woodcuts, Altdorfer developed the delicate Venetian book illustrations of the 1480s and gos [218] by adding shading. In his cut of the Resurrection [ 306 ], the oval radiance prints lighter than the Christ inside it, showing where the block was slightly hollowed so as to press less on the paper. Dürer had already lowered the tapering needlepoints of lines that project into wide blanks, where concentrated pressure would otherwise thicken them, but Altdorfer
在稍大的木刻作品中，阿尔特多夫通过添加阴影技法，发展了 1480 年代精致的威尼斯书籍插图风格。其《复活》木刻[306]中，椭圆光晕的印痕比内部基督形象更浅，这正是因雕刻时稍作凹陷以减轻对纸张的压力所致。 丢勒早已将线条尖端收窄，使其延伸至宽阔空白处——若施加集中压力，这些线条本会变粗——但阿尔特多夫

308 枚银杯。阿尔特多夫蚀刻版画

309 银制饮杯。纽伦堡保罗·弗林特点刻工艺
seems to have been the first to lower a whole area to contrast gray with black, as Bewick was to do for wood engravings about 1800 [ 636 ].
似乎是首位将整个区域调暗以形成灰与黑对比的艺术家，正如比威克约在 1800 年为木刻版画所做的那样[636]。
Just after Giovanni Bellini and Giorgione had discovered landscape in Venice, Altdorfer became the first German landscapist. He etched the very first pure landscapes on copper [ 307 ] with the breeziness of his pen sketches and with the quill’s open flow of line. The painters of the Danube school often followed him in subordinating figures to cliffs and sunny forests, and Hercules Seghers in Holland etched Altdorfer’s moss-hung larches, which he never saw at home.
就在乔凡尼·贝利尼和乔尔乔内于威尼斯开创风景画之后，阿尔特多夫成为德国首位风景画家。他以铜版蚀刻技法创作了最早的纯粹风景画[307]，笔触如速写般轻盈，线条如鹅毛笔般流畅舒展。 多瑙河画派画家常效仿其手法，将人物置于峭壁与阳光森林之下；荷兰画家赫拉克勒斯·塞赫斯则蚀刻出阿尔特多夫笔下苔藓垂挂的落叶松——这些景致他故乡从未得见。
Altdorfer started another printmaking specialty when he etched silver-gilt goblets and spoons of Renaissance design [ 308 ]. Nuremberg silversmiths took the hint by engraving elaborate silver tableware by stabbing the copperplate with rows of dots [ 309 ]. This looks at first like Giulio Campagnola’s stipple technique [ 225 ], but it actually comes from the silversmith’s hammering with a sharp point to frost an area or to make a line twinkle. Germans and Frenchmen designed quantities of ostentatious silver platters and ewers that stored wealth for display on buffets-on which the less wealthy Italians arranged strikingly painted earthenware instead.
阿尔特多夫开创了另一项版画工艺，他以文艺复兴风格的镀银高脚杯和汤匙为素材进行蚀刻[308]。纽伦堡银匠们从中获得灵感，通过在铜版上刺戳成排的点状图案，制作出精美的银质餐具[309]。 此技法乍似朱利奥·坎帕尼奥拉的点刻技法[225]，实则源于银匠以尖锉锤击金属表面，使局部呈现霜状效果或使线条闪烁生辉。德法工匠设计了大量华丽的银盘与银壶，这些盛放财富的器皿陈列于餐柜之上；而经济条件较差的意大利人则在餐柜上陈列色彩斑斓的彩陶器皿。

Baldung and Weiditz (巴尔东与魏迪茨)


Dürer was only the most forceful and versatile member of a generation of artists more rugged than any other Germans between 1550 and 1910. In this crop of geniuses, two Strassburgers, Hans Baldung and Hans Weiditz, shared a sense of the weird that was not to reappear in Western art until Goya, although it does occur among the Japanese.
巴尔东与魏迪茨丢勒不过是 1550 至 1910 年间德国艺术家中最具力量与多才多艺的一员，而这一代艺术家比同时代任何德国人都更为粗犷。在这批天才中，两位斯特拉斯堡人——汉斯·巴尔东与汉斯·魏迪茨——共享着一种怪诞感，这种特质在西方艺术中直至戈雅时代才再度出现，尽管日本艺术中确实存在类似倾向。
Baldung achieved independence in spite of being Dürer’s apprentice in an association that was still in force in 1521 when Dürer sold Baldung’s prints on his trip to the Netherlands. In his woodcuts (but not in his paintings) Baldung was driven by the jangled agony of the German genius. More than any other Renaissance printmaker, he predicted the desperate introspection of the expressionists (like Grünewald in his paintings). It still shocks us across four centuries to see Baldung’s Christ heaved up to heaven with his heels above his head in a nightmare somersault [310] that could have been imagined only by a solitary searcher of the Bible. Baldung discharged his most brutal stabs of Christian pathos in rough little cuts as summary as mosaics [ 311 ]. His lonely turmoil found refuge in the danger of the
尽管巴尔东曾是丢勒的学徒，且两人之间的师徒关系在 1521 年丢勒赴荷兰途中代售巴尔东版画时仍具法律效力，他最终实现了艺术独立。在木刻作品中（而非油画），巴尔东被德国天才那令人心神不宁的痛苦所驱使。 他比任何文艺复兴版画家都更早预见了表现主义者（如格吕内瓦尔德在绘画中展现的）那种绝望的内省。纵使隔着四个世纪，巴尔东笔下基督被抛向天际的画面仍令我们震撼——那双脚高过头顶的噩梦般翻滚姿态[310]，唯有孤独的圣经探索者方能构想。 巴尔东以粗粝的笔触，如马赛克般简练地刺出基督教悲怆的锋芒[311]。他孤独的骚动在危险中觅得庇护——

A less lacerated but equally individual member of this great generation was Hans Weiditz, whose personal life has all but disappeared. Even his name was forgotten

314 被纠缠的老处女。魏迪茨木刻版画，见于彼特拉克《命运之书》，奥格斯堡（格里姆与维尔松出版社），1532 年

until 1904, when the mention of “Hans Weyditz of Strassburg” as the illustrator of the Brunfels Herbal [ 102 ] was connected with an Augsburg cut that is initialed twice with HW above Hbb (for H. Beitidz? Or some woodcutter?). At Augsburg, where Weiditz collaborated with Burgkmair, woodcuts in his style are dated 1518 and 1520, while more appeared later in Strassburg. Unluckily for Weiditz, the death of a translator and the bankruptcy of his Augsburg publishers delayed the printing of his two long series of woodcuts until he had left for Strassburg over ten years later, when they were printed without supervision. The original publisher had spared no expense to hire a virtuoso woodcutter (Jost de Negker?) who preserved all the crispness of Weiditz’ crinkles as they curl into half-shadows. But to find pictures for the moral platitudes of Cicero and Petrarch, never illustrated before or since, Weiditz was driven to search where Brueghel and Daumier were also to make their discoveries: in happenings too close and familiar to be noticed by anyone except a genius who can look at his home as though just arriving there. He saw that the framing of a house [ 313 ] could show how mutual help builds friendships, and an old spinster [ 314 ] can embody virtue acquired by working without thought of reward. Weiditz, life’s first gluttonous observer, poked into the marketplace, the workshops, the schools, the countinghouses, the baths, and then ventured out into the unseen fringe beyond, haunted by goblins and “those that lawless and incertain thought imagine howling.”
直到 1904 年，当《布伦费尔斯草药书》[102]的插图作者"斯特拉斯堡的汉斯·韦迪茨"与奥格斯堡的一幅木刻版画产生关联时，该版画上方两次出现 HW 字样（位于 Hbb 上方，指代 H. Beitidz？或是某位木刻师？）。 在魏迪茨与布尔克迈尔共事的奥格斯堡，其风格的木刻作品可追溯至 1518 年与 1520 年，而更多作品后来出现在斯特拉斯堡。不幸的是，译者的离世与奥格斯堡出版商的破产延误了魏迪茨两套长篇木刻系列的印刷，待他十余年后迁往斯特拉斯堡时，这些作品才在无人监督下付梓。 原出版商曾不惜重金聘请一位技艺精湛的木刻师（约斯特·德·内格克？），将魏迪茨笔下褶皱在半明半暗处卷曲的鲜明质感完整保留。 但为西塞罗与彼特拉克那些前无古人后无来者的道德箴言配图时，魏迪茨被迫踏上了布鲁盖尔与丢勒同样的探索之路：在那些近在咫尺却无人察觉的日常场景中寻觅灵感——唯有天才方能以初访者之眼凝视故土。 他洞见房屋框架[313]能展现互助如何缔结友谊，而老处女[314]的形象则诠释了不求回报的劳动所铸就的美德。 作为人生最初的贪婪观察者，魏迪茨探访了市集、作坊、学堂、账房、浴场，继而冒险踏入幽暗的边缘地带——那里盘踞着妖魔鬼怪，以及"那些被无法无天、心神恍惚的念头催生出的嚎叫者"。

The German Little Masters (德国小大师)


The German Little Masters who succeeded Dürer engraved in the tiny format that Altdorfer [ 305 ] had imported from Italian nielli. Half a dozen printmakers tastefully epitomized the allover tone of Dürer’s later engraving and Marcantonio’s tranquility. The trend away from Dürer’s exciting line toward Marcantonio’s quiet tone was probably started by the best of the Little Masters, the short-lived Bartel Beham, who is said to have worked in Marcantonio’s own studio. In Rome he evidently studied what every traveler could see without introductionsthe antique marbles in courtyards and gardens, and the house fronts that Polidoro da Caldara had frescoed with friezes inspired by Raphael and Roman sarcophagi. Before rains washed away these processional ballets of nudes, they formed a Roman art in Germany and Switzerland [ 315 ]. The only Little Master who worked in northern Germany was Aldegrever, who was also the most mannered and stylishly bizarre [ 316 ]. All the Little Masters followed Marcantonio in engraving mythological scenes, roundly drawn nudes, and the kind of erotic subjects that appear whenever a great tradition breaks up, whether in late antiquity, the end of the Renaissance, or our own time. The Little Masters also engraved ornamental motifs for craftsmen to adapt in decorative works [ 317 ]. Indeed, they might have planned their whole production to furnish ideas for other artists, who copied their diminutive engravings wholesale, especially in the enamel workshops at Limoges. Several of these contrivers of exquisite miniatures, including Bartel Beham and his more prolific but duller brother, Hans Sebald Beham, lived violently enough to get themselves jailed and banished as subversive freethinkers.
继丢勒之后的德国小大师们，沿袭了阿尔特多夫[305]从意大利镌刻工艺中引入的微型版画形式。 六位版画家以精妙手法浓缩了丢勒晚期版画的整体基调与马尔坎托尼奥的宁静气质。这种从丢勒激昂线条转向马尔坎托尼奥沉静色调的潮流，很可能由"小大师"中最杰出的巴特尔·贝哈姆开创——这位英年早逝的艺术家据传曾在马尔坎托尼奥的工坊工作。 在罗马，他显然研习了无需引荐即可观赏的艺术——庭院花园里的古希腊大理石雕塑，以及波利多罗·达·卡尔达拉以拉斐尔与罗马石棺为灵感绘制的壁画浮雕。这些裸体游行芭蕾的壁画在雨水冲刷殆尽前，曾在德国与瑞士孕育出独特的罗马艺术风格[315]。 唯一在德国北部活动的"小大师"是阿尔德格雷弗，其风格最为矫饰怪诞[316]。所有"小大师"都效仿马尔坎托尼奥，刻画神话场景、圆润的裸体人物，以及每当伟大传统瓦解时便会涌现的情色题材——无论是晚期古典时期、文艺复兴末期，还是当代。 小大师们还为工匠们雕刻装饰图案，供其在装饰作品中加以运用[317]。事实上，他们创作的初衷或许就是为其他艺术家提供灵感——尤其是利摩日的珐琅作坊，那里工匠们成批复制这些微型版画。 这些精巧微型画的创作者中，包括巴特尔·贝哈姆及其多产却平庸的兄弟汉斯·塞巴尔德·贝哈姆，其生平充满暴力冲突，最终因颠覆性自由思想家身份遭监禁与流放。

Figure-drawing books (人体素描书籍)


Barbari’s cryptic hints about human proportions badgered Dürer into muddled theorizing [ 281 ] that in turn badgered other German artists. Though they luckily could not write, they drew booklets of instructive woodcuts to raise themselves, as Dürer had done, from medieval artisans to Renaissance artists. Two of these booklets plagiarized the master’s unpublished drawings. When Dürer died just before the appearance of his big book on human proportions, Hans Sebald Beham brought out a pamphlet of the horse in profile [ 318 ], pirated from studies that Dürer must have drawn from the bronze horses of Saint Mark’s and their Renaissance adaptations. By later adding the human figure, Beham produced a self-help syllabus so practical that artists wore out edition after edition.
人体素描手册 巴巴里的隐晦人体比例提示不断萦绕于丢勒脑海，迫使他提出混乱的理论[281]，进而影响了其他德国艺术家。所幸他们不擅长文字，却绘制了教学木刻手册，效仿丢勒从中世纪工匠蜕变为文艺复兴艺术家。其中两册手册剽窃了大师未发表的素描作品。 当丢勒在人体比例巨著问世前夕离世时，汉斯·泽巴尔德·贝哈姆出版了马匹侧面图手册[318]，其内容剽窃自丢勒必曾参照圣马可广场青铜马像及其文艺复兴时期复刻版所绘制的习作。贝哈姆后来添加人体素描后，便创作出如此实用的自学教程，以致艺术家们将各版手册翻阅得破旧不堪。
Ten years after Dürer’s death another Nuremberger, Erhard Schön, adapted his drawing of elegantly disjointed manikins assembled out of stacks of boxes pivoting around a pliant axis [ 319 ]. Dürer probably took this cubist construction from lost drawings that Paolo Uccello or Piero della Francesca had made a century before. Schön’s book transmitted the box scheme to Cambiaso [ 400 ] and Poussin, but not to 2oth-century cubism, which came out of Cycladic and African sculpture and quite other theories.
杜勒逝世十年后，另一位纽伦堡人埃尔哈德·舍恩借鉴了他的绘画手法——将优雅错位的模特人偶由层叠的箱子构成，围绕柔韧的轴心旋转[319]。 丢勒的立体构图很可能源自百年前保罗·乌切洛或皮耶罗·德拉·弗朗切斯卡遗失的素描。舍恩的著作将箱体构图法传授给坎比亚索[400]与普桑，却未影响二十世纪立体主义——后者实则源自基克拉迪与非洲雕塑及截然不同的理论体系。

Figure 97: Figure-drawing books
图 97：人体素描教程
In the same year as Schön’s book in Nuremberg, Vogtherr in Strassburg published the only German drawing book that escaped Dürer’s dominance [ 320 ]. Instead of instructing systematically, Vogtherr compiled a medieval artist’s model book of usable elements, saying that “out of brotherly love for artists burdened with wife and children, I am publishing a little gathering of exotic and difficult details full of fantasy and cogitation that will spare dull heads and will cheer and inspire artists of high understanding.” His 31 pages of outlandish headdresses, hands, feet, and fantastic weapons classify spare parts to apply wherever an artist’s invention might go blank.
在施恩于纽伦堡出版著作的同年，斯特拉斯堡的沃格特尔出版了唯一一本摆脱丢勒主导地位的德语绘画手册[320]。 沃格特尔并未采用系统化教学，而是汇编了一部中世纪艺术家可供取用的元素范本集，声称"出于对背负妻儿重担的艺术家兄弟般的爱，我出版这本充满奇思妙想的异域难解细节集锦，既能让迟钝之辈免于苦思，亦能鼓舞高明艺术家的灵感泉涌"。 书中 31 页奇异头饰、手足造型与奇幻武器的图谱，如同备件库般分类收录，供艺术家在创作灵感枯竭时随时调用。
Such attachable giblets were heaped like hospitable cold platters in some Italian drawing books [ 321 ]. Vasari was probably thinking of similar assortments when he wrote that “painters delude themselves if they center on perfecting a torso, an arm, or a leg with well-studied muscles, because a part of the work is not the whole.”
这类可拆卸的内脏器官，在某些意大利素描手册中堆叠得如同盛满冷盘的丰盛宴席[321]。瓦萨里写下"画家若执着于完善躯干、手臂或腿部，精心雕琢肌肉细节，终将自欺欺人，因为局部并非整体"时，想必也联想到这般拼凑的景象。
The first wide range of models for figures draped and nude, heads, and animals, either in outline or shaded, was provided by Abraham Bloemart in 120 engravings [322]; these were still being used a century later by Boucher and his contemporaries. Dürer had included the proportions of the baby in his treatise as Leonardo da Vinci had planned to do in the book that he never pulled together. When the Counter-Reformation drafted squadrons of cupids for its campaign of blandishment, drawing books, like altars and ceilings, for years pullulated with pudgy hands, shy smiles, and tubby little rumps [ 323 ].
亚伯拉罕·布洛马特通过 120 幅版画[322]首次提供了涵盖人体衣褶与裸体、人头及动物的广泛模型，既有轮廓线稿也有阴影渲染；这些作品在百年后仍被布歇及其同时代人沿用。 丢勒在其论著中收录了婴儿比例图，这与达·芬奇未竟之作的构想不谋而合。当反宗教改革运动征召成群爱神参与其蛊惑攻势时，绘画手册如同祭坛与穹顶，在漫长岁月里充斥着胖乎乎的小手、羞涩的微笑与圆滚滚的小屁股[323]。

Holbein (霍尔拜因)


Holbein was the son and younger brother of skillful artists and grew into an inevitability of touch that looks effortless. While he was a boy in Augsburg, Burgkmair, 25 years older, was there blending Italianate harmonies into German art [ 293 ]. Holbein went to Basel at 18, fully trained, where he and his short-lived brother Ambrose drew woodcuts for the alert and learned publishers who were taking the initiative from war-torn Venice in printing for intellectual Europe. Though Holbein was anything but literary, being all eye and hand, he perfected a complete new ornamentation for books, from the title page through the decorative initials to the printer’s mark at the end.
霍尔拜因出身于技艺精湛的艺术世家，身为幼子与胞弟，他逐渐练就了浑然天成的笔触。少年时在奥格斯堡求学期间，年长他二十五岁的布尔克迈尔正将意大利式和谐美学融入德国艺术[293]。 18 岁时，霍尔拜因已完成系统训练，前往巴塞尔发展。在那里，他和早逝的兄长安布罗斯为敏锐博学的出版商创作木刻版画——这些出版商正从战火纷飞的威尼斯手中接过印刷业主导权，为欧洲知识界提供出版服务。尽管霍尔拜因并非文学才子，而是纯粹依靠视觉与手艺的匠人，他却为书籍开创了全新的装饰体系：从标题页到装饰性首字母，直至卷末的印刷商标，无不彰显其精湛技艺。
Title borders, invented in Venice [ 211 ], had appeared on many German pamphlets shortly after 1500. Holbein now made them sumptuous, humorous, or dramatic. His first, the often-copied Cleopatra border [ 324 ], is the first of many that bulk out from the page like a portico. (He drew it with the vanishing point at the left, to fit the right-hand page on which a title appears, forgetting that printing would reverse the image awkwardly.) Holbein totally reshaped the printer’s mark [28], and gave meaning to the decorative initial letter by designing alphabets around a particular theme, such as cupids playing tag and leapfrog, skeletons attacking men, or peasants dancing, working, and making love. Finally, he invented symbolic initials to challenge the reader’s learning with a guessing game. One guesses that he meant to illustrate omega with the giant Orion, though he actually drew the bard Arion [ 325 ].
标题边框始于威尼斯[211]，1500 年后不久便出现在许多德国小册子上。霍尔拜因如今将其演绎得华丽、幽默或戏剧化。 他首创的克娄巴特拉边框[324]（后被广泛模仿）堪称开山之作，其结构如门廊般从页面向外延伸。（他将消失点设于左侧以适应右页标题布局，却忽略了印刷时图像会发生笨拙的反转。） 霍尔拜因彻底革新了印刷商标[28]，并赋予装饰性首字母新意——他围绕特定主题设计字母表，如玩捉迷藏和跳马的丘比特、袭击人类的骷髅，或是载歌载舞、辛勤劳作、缠绵悱恻的农民。 最终他创造出象征性首字母，以猜谜游戏挑战读者的学识。人们推测他本欲用巨型猎户座象征欧米茄，实则画的是吟游诗人阿里翁[325]。

Such handsomeness and wit affected the professional practice of printers, but Holbein made his impact on the general public through two series of woodcuts that he drew in Basel for a German publisher in Lyons. In his Dance of Death [ 326 ], the skeletons do not mock at stock types as they do in the Gothic Danse Macabre [54]; rather, they assault people like you and me in rooms and meadows where you and I might drop.
如此英俊与机智影响了印刷工人的专业实践，但霍尔拜因通过两组木刻版画在巴塞尔为里昂的德国出版商创作的作品，对大众产生了深远影响。 在其《死亡之舞》[326]中，骷髅们并未像哥特式《死亡之舞》[54]那样嘲弄固定角色；它们直接袭击你我这样的凡人，在我们可能倒下的房间与草地上发动袭击。
Holbein’s other set, 91 scenes from the Old Testament, was as famous at the time. Here he turned for action to Baldung’s stocky, driven men, and for orderliness to the clear cuts in the first illustrated Bible in Italian [ 327 ], just as Dürer had turned to the crude but forceful cuts in the first illustrated Bible in German [ 261 ]. But whereas Dürer chose subjects from the mystical and controversial New Testament, Holbein went to the historical facts of the Old. He transformed the Venetian miniatures into monuments seen through the wrong end of an opera glass [328], for he could design in the scale of hat jewels as aptly as he frescoed house fronts.
霍尔拜因另一组作品——《旧约圣经》的 91 幅场景——在当时同样声名远扬。他借鉴巴尔东笔下敦实而充满张力的男性形象来表现动态，并从意大利首部插图圣经[327]中简洁明快的线条中汲取秩序感，正如丢勒借鉴德语首部插图圣经[261]中粗粝却富有力量的线条一般。 但不同于丢勒选取充满神秘色彩且争议颇多的新约题材，霍尔拜因则着眼于旧约的历史事实。他将威尼斯式微型画转化为透过歌剧望远镜反向端观察的纪念碑[328]——无论是设计帽饰珠宝的微观尺度，还是绘制房屋立面的宏大尺度，他皆能驾轻就熟。
No preparatory drawing is known for any Holbein woodcut. With unbelievable assurance, he apparently attacked the wood directly. Fortunately, many of his Basel illustrations were cut by a fellow Augsburger, Hans Lützelburger, who surpassed even Jost de Negker in achieving exactitude in miniature. Lützelburger’s death ended the ten-year collaboration when Holbein was about 29 . He was sorely missed during Holbein’s last 15 years in London, where some of the artist’s grandest drawings on wood were slashed by provincial botchers [ 329 ].
目前尚未发现任何霍尔拜因木刻作品的草稿。这位艺术家似乎以令人难以置信的自信直接在木板上创作。所幸他为巴塞尔创作的许多插图由同为奥格斯堡人的汉斯·吕策尔堡刻制，后者在微缩精确度上甚至超越了约斯特·德·内格克。 吕策尔堡的离世终结了长达十年的合作，当时霍尔拜因约 29 岁。在艺术家伦敦生涯的最后十五年里，这位伙伴的缺席令人痛惜——其间部分最宏伟的木版素描遭乡下粗制滥造者毁损[329]。

基督驱逐恶魔。霍尔拜因木刻版画，见于托马斯·克兰默《教理问答》，伦敦（林恩出版社），1548 年

Lucas of Leiden (卢卡斯或莱顿)


Lucas of Leiden was probably the town’s first engraver and was certainly the first engraver in the Netherlands to make an impact on the world at large. He formed his engraving style partly on that of IA of Zwolle [ 137 ] and even more on the worldwide example of Dürer, whose virtuosity he simplified, and whom he followed by signing his prints with his L and the date on a tablet. At 14 he engraved his first dated plate [330] with such mastery that the landscape was copied two years later in Rome when Marcantonio needed a background for figures from Michelangelo’s cartoon of the Battle of Pisa [ 331 ]. When Lucas blended etching with engraving in his portrait of Maximilian [ 285 ], the saving in time revolutionized copperplate technique. Lucas’ graver caressed the copper so delicately that the lighter lines wore thin before many bright impressions could be pulled. Yet this adolescent refinement of touch serves to render figures that bulk with the solid strength of old Dutch art in the Milkmaid [ 332 ], which became the model for hundreds of Dutch farm pictures and studies of cows’ hides sagging from their skeletal
莱顿的卢卡斯很可能是该镇首位铜版画家，无疑也是荷兰首位在国际上产生影响的铜版画家。他的雕刻风格部分源于兹沃勒的 IA[137]，但更多受到丢勒这一世界级典范的影响——他简化了丢勒的精湛技艺，并效仿其在版画上签名的方式：在铭牌上署名"L"并标注日期。 十四岁时他创作的首幅带年份版画[330]技艺精湛，两年后罗马的马尔坎托尼奥为米开朗基罗《比萨战役》草图人物绘制背景时，竟直接临摹了画中风景[331]。当卢卡斯在《马克西米利安肖像》[285]中融合蚀刻与雕刻技法时，这种节省工时的创新彻底革新了铜版画工艺。 卢卡斯的刻刀轻柔抚过铜版，纤细线条在多次鲜明印制前便已磨薄。然而这般青涩的精妙笔触，却在《挤奶女工》[332]中塑造出饱含荷兰古典艺术厚重力量的人物形象——这幅作品后来成为数百幅荷兰农耕画及牛皮松弛垂挂于骨架上的研究范本。

supports. Curiously, Lucas had less effect through his woodcuts [ 333 ], in which he developed the bright side lighting that had first appeared in Netherlandish block books [ 21 ]. It is a pity that his big woodcuts are the rarest of his prints, for in them he drew with his finest control and animated figures as vividly as the Master of the Lübeck Bible [ 38 ].
值得注意的是，卢卡斯通过木刻版画[333]的影响力反而较弱，尽管他在这些作品中发展了源自尼德兰木刻版画集[21]的明面光技法。遗憾的是，他那些大型木刻版画堪称其版画作品中最稀有的存在——正是在这些作品中，他展现了最精妙的控制力，人物形象的生动程度堪比吕贝克圣经画师[38]的杰作。
Although Dutch art was ultimately to base itself on Lucas’ robust welcome to everyday things, in his mid-life such endearing homeliness was banished as an embarrassing leftover from the dying Middle Ages. When all the north of Europe began drifting toward Italy, Lucas preceded the German Little Masters [315] in succumbing to the engraving style and the subject matter of Marcantonio, whose own engraving style Lucas’ early work had helped to form. Thus the publication of prints, only some 80 years old, was already interchanging enough artistic ideas to homogenize styles. Along with all his compatriots, Lucas turned so far away from medieval homely frankness to reach out for the heroic generalizations of the antique that his last engravings [334] look as though they could not possibly be by the same man, or even come from the same country, as the Milkmaid. Italian Renaissance prints made an impact on the north of Europe so violent that Netherlanders needed a century of trips to Italy before they could absorb the onslaught of Italian art and finally range themselves with Lucas’ youthful point of view. So Lucas of Leiden was Holland’s last indigenous artist until the great age of Rem-brandt-but only during his teens and early 205.
尽管荷兰艺术最终奠基于卢卡斯对日常事物的热忱拥抱，但在其中年时期，这种惹人怜爱的质朴特质却被斥为垂死中世纪的尴尬残余。当整个北欧开始向意大利靠拢时，卢卡斯早于德国小大师们[315]屈从于马尔坎托尼奥的版画风格与题材——而卢卡斯早期的作品恰恰促成了马尔坎托尼奥版画风格的形成。 由此可见，仅有八十年历史的版画出版业，已然在艺术理念的交融中促成了风格的同质化。卢卡斯与全体同胞一同，彻底背离了中世纪质朴的坦率，转而追寻古典主义的英雄式概括，以致其晚期版画[334]与《挤奶女工》相比，仿佛出自不同画师之手，甚至难以置信同属一个国度。 意大利文艺复兴版画对北欧的冲击如此猛烈，以致尼德兰艺术家需历经百年赴意游学，方能消化这股艺术洪流，最终回归卢卡斯早年的艺术立场。因此莱顿的卢卡斯成为伦勃朗时代来临前荷兰最后一位本土艺术家——但仅限于他十几岁到二十出头的岁月。
