Marcantonio (马可安东尼奥)


335 The Adoration of the Shepherds. Woodcut by Dürer in the Little Passion
335 《牧羊人的朝拜》。丢勒木刻版画，出自《小受难》
336 Engraving by Marcantonio Raimondi after Dürer
336 马尔坎托尼奥·拉伊蒙迪根据丢勒作品制作的雕刻版画
Marcantonio Printmaking changed about 1500 when painting changed from the daylit scenes of the 1400 s to Leonardo’s and Giorgione’s umber forms dissolving in twilight [ 225 ]. Dürer helped to precipitate the crisis by engraving the first prints with a broad range of shadow and a convincing distinction of textures. From then on, people wearied of Mantegna’s and Schongauer’s equivalents for various kinds of quill drawings, or the imitations of silverpoint drawings in the Florentine broad manner [ 144 ]. Young painters studied less from drawings and more from plaster casts. When they used prints, they wanted the rounding light and shade of the new paintings. They found their printmaker in Marcantonio Raimondi. A man without genius but with receptive intelligence, he absorbed and harmonized trends as smoothly as Raphael himself. A hard worker, able teacher, and efficient organizer, he became the most widely imitated of all engravers anywhere, for he was as imitable as Dürer was inimitable. If Dürer created the new doctrine of printmaking, Marcantonio was the Saint Paul who gave it currency.
马可·安东尼奥版画艺术约在 1500 年发生变革，当时绘画从 1400 年代的日光场景转向达·芬奇与乔尔乔内笔下赭色形态在暮色中消融的境界[225]。丢勒通过雕刻首批兼具宽广阴影层次与逼真质感差异的版画，加速了这场变革的到来。 自此，人们厌倦了曼特尼亚与申高尔式仿制各种钢笔画的手法，也厌倦了佛罗伦萨粗放风格中模仿银尖笔画的技法[144]。年轻画家们减少对素描的研究，转而更多地研究石膏模型。当他们使用版画时，渴望获得新绘画中圆润的光影效果。他们最终在马尔坎托尼奥·莱蒙迪身上找到了理想的版画师。 此人虽无天才之姿，却具敏锐洞察力，其融合艺术潮流之流畅堪比拉斐尔本人。作为勤勉的创作者、卓越的导师与高效的组织者，他成为全球雕版师中最广受模仿的典范——正如丢勒的独创性无法复制，马坎托尼奥的技法却可被广泛传授。若说丢勒开创了版画艺术的新教义，马坎托尼奥便是将其传播开来的圣保罗。
Young Marcantonio was apprenticed to Bologna’s leading painter and medalist, Francesco Francia, for whom he engraved belt buckles and other niello trinkets in silver. He carried the dark color of niello into his earliest copper engravings. In 1505 in Venice, he systemized his first confused scratching by copying Dürer’s engravings. He then let in still more air by the singular procedure of engraving copperplate copies after Dürer’s woodcuts of the Life of the Virgin and the Little Passion [ 335, 336]. The breadth of the woodcut lines taught his graver to indicate
年轻的马尔坎托尼奥曾拜师于博洛尼亚顶尖画家兼奖章设计师弗朗切斯科·弗朗西亚门下，为其雕刻银质腰带扣及其他银质镌刻饰物。他将镌刻工艺的深邃色调融入了最早期的铜版雕刻作品。 1505 年在威尼斯，他通过临摹丢勒的版画作品，将最初混乱的刻划技法系统化。随后他更通过独特手法——将丢勒《圣母生平》与《小受难》木刻版画转刻为铜版画复制品[335,336]——为作品注入更开阔的空间感。木刻线条的宽广度教会他的刻刀如何表现
form without particularizing textures. Marcantonio thus clarified Dürer’s discipline without corrupting his virtuosity. By then absorbing Lucas of Leiden’s limpid unity, his line became so clear and so reasonable that it had but one function-to surround a shape without calling attention to itself.
不着墨于具体质感，仅以纯粹形态见长。马尔坎托尼奥由此澄清了丢勒的严谨性，却未损其精湛技艺。继而吸收莱顿的卢卡斯那澄澈统一的风格，其线条变得如此清晰而合理，以至于仅具单一功能——环绕形体而不引人注目。
On leaving Venice, Marcantonio stopped in Florence long enough to make one of the very few records of Michelangelo’s grandest drawing, the huge cartoon of the Battle of Pisa [ 331 ], begun in 1504 and cut to pieces about 1512. In 1509/10 he established himself in Rome, where he perfected his taste by engraving after Raphael’s drawings, sometimes reproducing a composition even before Raphael had readjusted the design on the wall. Reproduction is hardly the word for an en-
离开威尼斯后，马尔坎托尼奥在佛罗伦萨停留了足够长的时间，得以制作了米开朗基罗最宏伟素描作品——巨幅《比萨战役》草图[331]的极少数记录之一。该作品始于 1504 年，约 1512 年被切割成碎片。 1509/10 年间他定居罗马，通过临刻拉斐尔素描来锤炼审美品味，有时甚至在拉斐尔尚未调整墙面设计前就已复刻出完整构图。所谓"复刻"实难形容这种——
Figure 104: 337 The Massacre of the Innocents. Quill drawing by Raphael, pricked for transfer to copperplate
图 104：337《屠婴事件》。拉斐尔钢笔画稿，经刻线处理后转印至铜版
338 Engraving by Marcantonio after Raphael
338 马尔坎托尼奥根据拉斐尔作品所作的雕刻
graver who had the ability to invent harmonious draperies for Raphael’s nudes [ 337 ] and to blend his groups into landscapes adapted from Dürer and Lucas of Leiden [ 338 ]. The French accurately call this “interpretive engraving.” For such pictorial translation, the engraver’s weeks cost more than the designer’s hours. (In 1747, for example, C.-N. Cochin II was paid 1250 livres for a drawing, and 4000 for engraving it.) All we know of Marcantonio’s business arrangements is that he is said to have worked with Raphael’s shop foreman.
这位雕刻师既能为拉斐尔的裸体画创作和谐的衣褶[337]，又能将人物群像融入借鉴丢勒与莱顿的卢卡斯[338]的景观之中。法国人精辟地称之为"诠释性雕刻"。 为实现这种绘画转化，雕刻师耗费数周的工时远超设计师的创作时间。（例如 1747 年，小夏尔-诺埃尔·科尚因一幅素描获酬 1250 里弗尔，而将其制版则获酬 4000 里弗尔。）关于马尔坎托尼奥的商业合作，我们仅知他据传曾与拉斐尔工作室的工头共事。
Marcantonio’s adaptation of northern engraving styles, and his northern backgrounds, made his prints more digestible for northern artists than Raphael’s original drawings and paintings. Painters ever since have liked Marcantonio for his sacrificing showiness to pictorial essentials. Degas found in his engravings the consolation of a consummate calm. Marcantonio’s Judgment of Paris [339], after a
马尔坎托尼奥对北方版画风格的借鉴及其北方背景的运用，使他的版画作品比拉斐尔的原作更易为北方艺术家所接受。后世画家推崇马尔坎托尼奥，因其舍弃浮华而专注于绘画本质。德加在其版画中寻得至臻宁静的慰藉。马尔坎托尼奥的《帕里斯的审判》[339]，据...

lost Raphael drawing, has been copied or adapted in 34 or more works of art, of which the most notorious is Manet’s Lunch on the Grass [ 340 ]. The French public who screamed at the girl’s indecency would not have noticed her if her gentleman friends had stripped off their morning coats and gray trousers to join her in the everyday undress of Parnassus.
失传的拉斐尔素描曾被 34 件或更多艺术作品所临摹或改编，其中最负盛名的当属马奈的《草地上的午餐》[340]。若画中绅士们脱去晨礼服与灰色长裤，以帕纳索斯山日常的裸体姿态与少女同坐，那些因少女衣着不雅而惊呼的法国公众，恐怕根本不会注意到她的存在。

Marcantonio's workshop (马尔坎托尼奥的工作室)


341-343  马尔坎托尼奥的工作室
341 Venus and Mars. Engraving by Giovanni Jacopo Caraglio after a lost drawing by Rosso Fiorentino for Pietro Aretino
341 金星与火星。乔瓦尼·雅各布·卡拉廖根据罗索·菲奥伦蒂诺为彼得罗·阿雷蒂诺创作的已失传素描所作的版画。
342 (opposite page, left) The Laocoön group as found in 1506. Engraving by Marco Dente da Ravenna
342（对页左）1506 年发现的拉奥孔群雕。拉文纳的马尔科·登特所作版画
343 The Laocoön group as restored in 1533 by G. A. da Montorsoli. Engraving by Charles-Clément Balvay Bervic, 1809
343 拉奥孔群像（1533 年由乔瓦尼·安东尼奥·达·蒙托索利修复）。查尔斯-克莱芒·巴尔维·贝尔维克版画，1809 年
Marcantonio’s workshop Marcantonio synthesized the main printmaking styles of his time with a logic so teachable that his assistants could blend their engraving indistinguishably on one copperplate. His mostly anonymous crew composed the first internationally important engraver’s shop and perfected a system of collaboration that spread uninterruptedly until about 1875, when reproductive printmaking began to give way to the cheaper and more accurate photomechanical processes [ 657 ]. In some 15 years the shop produced close on 1000 engravings after Raphael, Giulio Romano, Bandinelli, Peruzzi, and Andrea del Sarto, projecting the Italian Renaissance style into the rest of Europe by explosion. Antique sculpture also first became widely known when Marcantonio and his most prolific assistants, Agostino Veneziano and Marco Dente da Ravenna, followed the archeological enthusiasm of their native north of Italy by engraving statues fresh from the Roman earth.
马尔坎托尼奥的工坊马尔坎托尼奥以极具教学价值的逻辑体系，将同时代主要版画技法融会贯通，其助手们甚至能在同一铜版上无缝衔接各自的雕刻痕迹。这支多为无名之辈的团队组建了首个具有国际影响力的雕版工坊，并完善了一套协作体系——该体系持续发展直至 1875 年左右，随着复制版画逐渐被更廉价精确的光学机械工艺取代才告终结 [657]。约十五年间，工坊复刻了近千幅拉斐尔、朱利奥·罗曼诺、班迪内利、佩鲁齐及安德烈亚·德尔·萨尔托的作品，将意大利文艺复兴风格如爆炸般推向欧洲各地。 古雕塑艺术的广泛传播同样始于马尔坎托尼奥及其两位高产助手——阿戈斯蒂诺·维内齐亚诺与拉文纳的马尔科·丹特——他们追随意大利北部故乡的考古热潮，将刚出土于罗马大地的新雕像刻制成版画。
The shop ran until the German and Spanish sack of Rome in 1527 killed one of the engravers and scattered the rest, sending the most individual member of the group, Giovanni Jacopo Caraglio [ 341 ], as far as Poland. These fleeing engravers carried with them the system of Marcantonio’s organization to places where their style had already preceded them. The German Little Masters [ 315 ] took to Marcantonio’s own manner, while the French preferred Caraglio’s brilliant variation. All the engravings of the time, except some of Dürer’s, record basic forms under a generalized illumination [ 342 ]. But as three centuries elaborated Marcantonio’s system, reproductive engraving more and more specified exact particularities of surface and lighting [343]. The world adopted a photographic view well before photography arrived in 1839.
该工坊持续运营至 1527 年德西联军洗劫罗马期间，一名雕刻师遇害，其余成员四散奔逃，其中最具个性特质的乔瓦尼·雅各布·卡拉廖[341]远赴波兰。这些流亡的雕刻师将马尔坎托尼奥的组织体系带往各地，而他们的艺术风格早已在此前传入这些地区。 德国"小大师"[315]承袭了马尔坎托尼奥的风格，而法国人则更青睐卡拉廖的华丽变体。除杜勒部分作品外，当时所有版画都在泛光照明下记录基本形态[342]。但随着三个世纪对马尔坎托尼奥体系的精进，复制版画日益精准地呈现表面质感与光影细节[343]。 早在 1839 年摄影术问世之前，世界已然接纳了摄影般的视觉呈现方式。


Imitations of drawings (绘画的模仿)


Artists have always saved drawings that they could use, but nobody collected drawings as such until Vasari wrote about his pioneer collection in his Lives of the Artists (1550). The first extensive publication of old-master drawings was etched in the 1640s and 60s when Wenzel Hollar reproduced some of Lord Arundel’s drawings (many now in Windsor Castle), including caricature heads by Leonardo da Vinci [ 344 ]. Hollar’s fidelity to a past style gave the general public its first sight of Leonardo’s art. His etchings were probably Goya’s models for monks and witches in the Caprichos and were certainly Tenniel’s for the Ugly Duchess in Alice in Wonderland. Leonardo’s scientific drawings slept in Windsor and Milan until they took top place through photographic reproductions after 1898.
素描的仿作艺术家们向来会保存可供使用的素描稿，但直到瓦萨里在《艺术家传记》（1550 年）中提及他开创性的收藏，才有人真正开始专门收藏素描作品。 17 世纪 40 至 60 年代，温策尔·霍拉尔将阿伦德尔勋爵收藏的素描（现多存于温莎城堡）制成蚀刻版画首次大规模出版，其中包括达·芬奇的漫画头像[344]。霍拉尔对古典风格的忠实再现，使大众首次得以领略达芬奇的艺术造诣。 这些蚀刻版画很可能成为戈雅创作《奇想集》中修道士与女巫形象的范本，无疑也启发了坦尼尔在《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中丑陋公爵夫人的设计。达·芬奇的科学素描长期沉睡于温莎与米兰，直至 1898 年后通过摄影复制技术才重获瞩目。
From the 1670 s until nearly 1800 the most frequently reproduced draftsman was Guercino, who parted with few drawings during his lifetime, leaving his heirs to sell off sizable lots of them for almost a century. As soon as George III had acquired his long series, Bartolozzi started to copy them with supple skill [ 345 ] in the first publication of a single artist’s drawings in a single collection. Various etchings after Guercino’s drawings were in their turn copied in pen far and wide, to the confusion of collectors ever since.
从 1670 年代直至近 1800 年，最常被临摹的素描家当属盖尔奇诺。他生前鲜少转让画稿，致使后人近百年间持续出售其大量遗作。乔治三世购得这批系列素描后，巴托洛齐便以娴熟技艺[345]着手临摹，开创了单一艺术家画作首次成集出版的先河。 基于盖尔奇诺素描创作的各类蚀刻版画又被广泛以钢笔复刻，此后令收藏家们困惑至今。
Collectors in the 18th century began to copy their own treasures in etchings that record many lost masterpieces. The most skillful imitator of this sort was an Amsterdam amateur, Ploos van Amstel, who combined copperplate processes so deceptively that some of his prints have passed as drawings in practically every large collection. Ploos imitated the crumbling grain of chalk by coating paper with glue, powdering it when dry with metal filings, then pressing lines through the original drawing laid on top to stick the filings to the glue below. The design in filings was then pressed onto a grounded copperplate to open a stippling of dots in the ground
十八世纪的收藏家们开始通过蚀刻版画复制自己的珍藏，这些版画记录了许多已失传的杰作。其中技艺最精湛的模仿者是阿姆斯特丹的业余爱好者普洛斯·范·阿姆斯特尔，他将铜版工艺结合得如此逼真，以至于他的部分版画在几乎所有大型收藏中都被当作素描真迹。 普洛斯通过在纸张上涂胶层，待干燥后撒上金属屑，再将原稿置于其上压出线条使金属屑附着于胶层，从而完美复刻了粉笔画的斑驳质感。随后将金属屑图案压印在镀底铜版上，便在镀层表面形成点状纹理。

345
Four Putti. Etching by Francesco Bartolozzi in Eighty-two Prints … from Original Drawings of Guercino, London (Boydell), 1764-84
四位天使。弗朗切斯科·巴托洛齐蚀刻版画，选自《格雷奇诺原作素描集·八十二幅版画》……伦敦（博伊德尔出版社），1764-84 年
for etching [ 346 ]. His process was so complicated that Ploos once lost a whole year’s work by one foul biting.
用于蚀刻[346]。他的工艺极其复杂，普洛斯曾因一次糟糕的蚀刻而损失整整一年的心血。
The 18th-century imitations of drawings were the first prints that aimed at more than copying other prints or indicating the general bulk of things, for they tried to substitute printing on paper for handwork on paper. Today’s photographic processes can reproduce certain kinds of drawings and watercolors so convincingly that the beholder enjoys the full experience of the original until he is told that he is admiring a facsimile. Art museums, take note.
十八世纪的素描仿制品是首批超越单纯复制其他版画或表现事物整体形态的印刷品，它们试图以纸上印刷工艺取代手工绘制。当今的摄影工艺能如此逼真地再现某些素描与水彩画，观者在得知所赏为复制品前，竟能获得与原作完全相同的观赏体验。艺术博物馆们，请注意。

344 (opposite page)  344（对页）The King and Queen of Tunis. Etching by Wenzel Hollar after a drawing by Leonardo da Vinci in Lord Arundel's collection
突尼斯国王与王后。温策尔·霍拉根据莱昂纳多·达·芬奇素描创作的蚀刻版画，藏于阿伦德尔勋爵收藏馆。


Color printing (彩色印刷)


Color printing always costs so much time and trouble to keep one color from intruding onto another that printers originally bothered with color only to avoid even more bothersome hand painting. In 1457 the first book with a printed date imitated the red and blue initials of manuscripts [ 26 ]. In 1487 Ratdolt printed the first imitation of a hand-colored woodcut [ 76 ]. Sometime after 1506 Cranach imitated a German color drawing [ 303 ]. But when Ugo da Carpi asked the Venetian Senate in 1516 for a privilege (patent) for “a new way of printing in light and dark [a chiaro et scuro], a new thing never done before,” Germans had been elaborating color woodcuts for some ten years, and in 1510 Jost de Negker’s cut of Burgkmair’s Death Killing the Lovers [ 295 ] had already perfected the very method that Ugo da Carpi was to launch into Italy. In this method, probably invented by de Negker and claimed by Ugo da Carpi, the picture is analyzed into areas of highlights, middle tones, and darks for printing in several intensities of one color, starting with the palest. Any single tone [ 347 ] makes little sense separated from the assemblage [ 492 ]. These most Italian of prints sacrifice detail to clarify the mastering Italian passion for grandeur of design. They satisfied an Italian taste so basic that the Italians kept on making color woodcuts for centuries after the Germans had dropped them for linear black and white.
彩色印刷始终耗费大量时间精力来防止颜色相互渗染，印刷商最初涉足彩色印刷，不过是为了规避更麻烦的手工上色。1457 年，首部带有印刷日期的书籍模仿了手抄本的红蓝大写字母[26]。1487 年，拉特多尔特首次印制了仿手工彩绘木刻版画[76]。 1506 年后不久，克拉纳赫模仿了德国彩色素描[303]。但当乌戈·达·卡尔皮于 1516 年向威尼斯参议院申请"一种前所未有的明暗印刷新技法（chiaro et scuro）"的专利特权时， 此时德国人已钻研彩色木刻约十年之久。早在 1510 年，约斯特·德·内格克根据布尔克迈尔原作制作的《死神夺命》[295]，便已臻至完美——这正是乌戈·达·卡尔皮即将引入意大利的技法。 此技法可能由德·内格克首创，后被乌戈·达·卡尔皮宣称所有。其原理是将画面分解为高光区、中间调区与暗部区，以单色不同浓淡层次进行印刷，从最浅色开始渐次叠印。 任何单一色调[347]脱离整体构图[492]便失去意义。这些最具意大利特色的版画牺牲细节以彰显意大利人对宏大设计的执着追求。它们满足了意大利人最根本的审美需求——当德国人转而采用线性黑白版画时，意大利人仍持续创作彩色木刻数个世纪。
In 1633 a French painter and etcher, Francois Perrier, dimly imitated Italian chiaroscuros by printing an etched copperplate in black for the shadows and another in white for the highlights, both imposed on a medium tone of paper. Four years later Abraham Bosse obtained a patent for coloring “almanacs and wall calendars, thèses, posters, New Year’s greetings, screens, fans, and holy pictures.” After printing black outlines, he brightened them with painted watercolors, then shaded them by printing a second black plate over the watercolor. His modish nicknacks have left no trace except for the box labeled “Bosse’s fans” in his print of the fashionable shops under the law courts [ 462 ].
1633 年，法国画家兼蚀刻师弗朗索瓦·佩里埃尝试模仿意大利明暗技法，将蚀刻铜版印制成黑色阴影版与白色高光版，叠印于中色调纸张上。四年后，亚伯拉罕·博斯获得专利，可为"年历、挂历、论文、海报、贺年卡、屏风、扇面及圣像画"上色。 他先印制黑色轮廓线，再用水彩上色提亮，最后覆印第二块黑色版画形成阴影。这些时髦小玩意如今已湮没无闻，唯存其版画《法院下时尚店铺》中标注"博斯扇子"的盒子留存痕迹[462]。
In the 1770 (just when Japanese woodcuts had burst into full color) the European tone processes of mezzotint, aquatint, and stipple were printed in colors, usually after a plate had worn too much to print a brilliant black. The printer painted the plate in oil pigments with a dolly (poupée) of cloth rolled into a stump, which
1770 年（恰逢日本木版画进入全彩时代），欧洲的凹版印刷技法——凹版、水彩蚀刻版与点刻版开始采用彩色印刷，通常用于版面磨损严重无法呈现纯黑的版画。印刷师使用布料卷成的圆棒（poupée）蘸取油性颜料涂抹版面，

347

The Death of Ananias. Dark block for chiaroscuro woodcut by Ugo da Carpi after Raphael, 1518
《亚拿尼亚之死》。乌戈·达·卡尔皮根据拉斐尔原作创作的明暗对比木刻版画暗色块，1518 年

Color mezzotint by Jacob Christoph le Blon in COLORITTO; OR THE HARMONY OF COLOURING IN PAINTING Reduced to MECHANICAL PRACTICE, London (le Blon), about 1722
雅各布·克里斯托夫·勒布隆所作彩色凹版蚀刻版画，收录于《色彩艺术：绘画中色彩和谐的机械实践》，伦敦（勒布隆），约 1722 年

349 The Tuileries. Color lithograph by Thomas Shotter Boys in Picturesque Architecture in Paris, Ghent, Antwerp, Rouen, London (Hullmandel), 1839
349 凡尔赛宫。托马斯·肖特·博伊斯创作的彩色平版画，收录于《巴黎、根特、安特卫普、鲁昂、伦敦的如画建筑》（赫尔曼德尔出版社），1839 年。
cannot help blurring adjoining colors into each other. Skies in landscapes were often inked in blue, and the ground in brown for finishing in watercolors on the paper.
无法避免地将相邻的颜色相互晕染。风景画中的天空常以蓝色勾勒，地面则用棕色打底，最后在纸上以水彩完成。
In the meantime, modern color printing that approximates the density of oil paint became possible when Isaac Newton deduced from the spectrum that all colors are mixtures of red, blue, and yellow. He worked out his theory in the 16705 but did not publish it until 1704. By 1711 a wandering minor artist, J. C. Le Blon, was already superimposing the three primary colors from three mezzotint plates [ 348 ]. Though Le Blon muddied his picture by piling up ill-balanced opaque pigments, Newton’s theory proved sound for today’s four-color reproductions that scatter dots of red, blue, yellow, and black side by side for distance to blend in the eye. Faithful color reproduction demands a coordination of photographic filters and printer’s inks that did not begin to balance precisely until about 1920.
与此同时，当艾萨克·牛顿从光谱中推导出所有颜色都是红、蓝、黄三色的混合物时，现代彩色印刷技术得以实现，其色彩密度已接近油画效果。他于 1670 年代提出该理论，但直至 1704 年才发表。 至 1711 年，游历各地的二流画家 J·C·勒布隆已开始将三块凹版印刷板上的三原色叠印[348]。尽管勒布隆因堆叠失衡的遮盖性颜料导致画面混浊，但牛顿的理论为现代四色印刷奠定了基础——通过将红、蓝、黄、黑四色网点并列排列，使色点在视觉距离中自然融合。 要实现精准的色彩再现，必须协调摄影滤镜与印刷油墨，而这种精确匹配直到 1920 年左右才初见成效。
Le Blon’s premature mixture of the three primary colors soon gave way to printing any pigments that would blend like watercolors. In this more instinctive way, Viennese experiments in 1819 started lithographers building up remarkably truthful pictures by combining tints from up to 45 lithographic stones. England made the first handsome color lithographs [ 349 ], and then brightened children’s books, Christmas cards, and labels for linens by combining colors from stones, woodblocks, and etched plates, teaching these complex processes to the rest of the world. Lithographers, thus highly trained, took on the early photomechanical color printing in a technological revolution that for once threw nobody out of work.
勒布隆过早地将三原色混合的尝试很快被取代，取而代之的是能像水彩般调和的任何颜料。这种更具直觉性的方法，促使 1819 年维也纳的实验者们开始运用多达 45 块石版上的色调进行组合，从而构建出惊人逼真的图像。 英国率先制作出精美的彩色平版画[349]，随后通过结合石版、木刻版与蚀刻版色彩，为童书、圣诞贺卡及亚麻制品标签增添亮色，并将这些复杂工艺传授给世界。受过高度训练的平版印刷师们由此投身早期照相机械彩色印刷技术革命——这场技术变革罕见地未导致任何人失业。

Parmigiano (帕尔玛干酪)


While Marcantonio was perfecting reproductive engraving and Ugo da Carpi was evolving a new kind of color woodcut, the painter Parmigiano was making equally transforming discoveries. His obsession with alchemy-so strong that he finally gave up all his art for it-probably made him the first Italian to experiment with etching acid. He is certainly the first printmaker after 1500 who disregarded the complexities that Dürer imposed on engraving. Ignoring the graver, he used the etching needle like a quill skimming over paper to jot down pictorial ideas. (The engraver cannot work directly from nature as he twists and turns his plate against his burin, pushing along lines already traced.) After the first etchers had worked in line, which is easy to see on the copper, Parmigiano became the first etcher of shadows. To etch in shadows, he had to teach himself to predict his results from a negative, like a photographer, as his scratching opened lines of copper brighter than the surrounding ground. (An engraver judges shadows more readily by muscularly controlling the depth of bright grooves in equally bright metal.) Following Parmigiano, Italian painters have etched continuously to this day.
帕尔米贾尼奥当马尔坎托尼奥致力于完善复制版画技艺，乌戈·达·卡尔皮开创新型彩色木刻版画之际，画家帕尔米贾尼奥同样在艺术领域实现突破性发现。 他对炼金术的痴迷——强烈到最终为之放弃所有艺术创作——很可能使他成为首位尝试蚀刻酸液的意大利人。他无疑是 1500 年后首位摒弃丢勒为版画设定的复杂技法的版画家。他舍弃刻刀，将蚀刻针如羽毛笔般轻掠纸面，随手勾勒画面构思。 （传统雕刻师无法直接临摹自然景物，只能反复转动铜版配合刻刀，沿预先勾勒的线条推进。）当早期蚀刻师专注于铜版上清晰可见的线条刻画时，帕尔米贾尼奥开创了阴影蚀刻的先河。 要刻画阴影，他必须像摄影师般学会从负片预判效果——刮刻出的铜线会比周围钝化层更明亮。（而版画家通过肌肉控制金属表面亮沟的深度，更能直观判断阴影。）自帕尔米贾尼诺之后，意大利画家们持续运用蚀刻技法直至今日。
Parmigiano’s most famous etching was the Entombment [350], which was copied by at least nine other etchers and must have gone to Toledo with El Greco, since he painted the same cylindrical heads, extended limbs, and confluence of impassioned gestures. Parmigiano is the first painter who is known to have hired a woodcutter to reproduce his drawings [351, 352 ]. This had unhappy consequences, for Vasari reports that “one morning while Parmigiano lay in bed, his woodcutter, Antonio da Trento, who was living with him, opened a strongbox, stole all his copperplates, woodblocks, and drawings, and must have gone to the devil for all that was ever heard from him.” To reproduce the exquisite line of his draw-
帕尔米贾尼诺最著名的蚀刻版画是《安葬基督》[350]，该作品至少被九位蚀刻师临摹过，且必然随埃尔·格列柯辗转至托莱多——因为格列柯画作中同样出现了圆柱状的头颅、伸展的肢体以及激情四溢的肢体语言交汇。帕尔米贾尼诺是已知首位雇佣木刻师复制其素描的画家[351, 352]。 此事却酿成悲剧——瓦萨里记载："某日清晨帕尔米贾尼奥卧床时，同住的木刻师安东尼奥·达·特伦托打开保险箱，窃走所有铜版、木刻版与素描稿，此后杳无音讯，想必已堕入地狱。"为复刻其素描中精妙的线条——

351 Circe Giving Her Drink to the Companions of Ulysses. Quill and wash drawing by Parmigiano
351 塞西向奥德修斯的同伴们施展魔饮。帕尔米贾尼诺的钢笔水彩画

352 Color woodcut by Antonio da Trento after Parmigiano
安东尼奥·达·特伦托根据帕尔米贾尼奥作品创作的 352 色木刻版画
Figure 105: 353 Sts. Peter and Paul Healing Cripples. Etching by Parmigiano, combined with woodcut by Antonio da Trento
图 105：353 圣彼得与圣保罗治愈瘸子。帕尔米贾诺蚀刻版画，结合安东尼奥·达·特伦托木刻版画
ings, Parmigiano introduced the German kind of color woodcut into Italy [ 352 ], based on a black-line block so complete that it can satisfy with or without a color block. He also first combined copperplate with woodcut in one print, etching a sort of composition sketch in outline for printing over a woodcut like an ink wash [ 353 ]. He did not repeat this middling successful experiment, but in the 1720s the combination reappeared in England and then in France for reproducing drawings.
帕尔米贾尼奥将德国式彩色木刻引入意大利[352]，其基底采用如此完整的黑线版，无论是否搭配彩色版都能独立成章。 他还首次将铜版画与木刻结合于单幅版画中，先蚀刻出轮廓草图作为构图基础，再像水墨渲染般覆盖于木刻版上[353]。尽管他未再重复这项成效平平的尝试，但这种组合技法于 1720 年代在英国复现，随后传入法国用于复制素描作品。
Parmigiano’s etchings and woodcuts won him more admirers in France than at home. In France his lithe elegance set the fashion for the 16th century and again for the 18th. In the 17th and 19th centuries Raphael dominated in the round-faced plumpness of Rubens and Renoir. Today, in the 20th, athletics and sparser eating have brought us back to Parmigiano’s ideal, as any fashion magazine will show.
帕尔米贾尼诺的蚀刻版画与木刻版画在法国赢得的赞誉远超其祖国。 在法国，他那灵动优雅的风格引领了 16 世纪乃至 18 世纪的艺术风潮。17 至 19 世纪间，拉斐尔的审美主导着艺术界，鲁本斯与雷诺阿笔下圆润丰腴的形象便是明证。而今 20 世纪，运动风潮与节制饮食让我们重新回归帕尔米贾尼诺的理想审美——翻开任何时尚杂志便能印证这一点。

The Fontainebleau school (枫丹白露学派)


The steadiest patron of artists for a millennium, the papacy, suddenly stopped payment in 1527 when the sack of Rome forced it to fight for its life. The next year Francis I, who had raided the French Church for a huge, irresponsible income, began to transform an old hunting lodge in the forest of Fontainebleau. When he died, 19 years later, a magical palace had arisen under the direction of homeless foreign virtuosi, mostly Italian refugees in their 20 s and 30 s .
枫丹白露学派作为千年来最稳定的艺术家赞助者，教廷在 1527 年罗马遭劫后为求自保突然停止了资助。 次年，弗朗索瓦一世开始改造枫丹白露森林中一座古老的狩猎行宫——此前他已从法国教会掠夺了巨额不负责任的收入。十九年后他逝世时，这座由流离失所的外国艺术家（多为二十至三十岁的意大利难民）主导建造的魔法宫殿已拔地而起。
The chief decorators were Francesco Primaticcio from Bologna, who worked from 1532, and Rosso, the violent Florentine, who came in 1530 and drank vitriol in 1540. They celebrated their escape from the restraining eye of their elders of the High Renaissance by standardizing the human form to an ideal-the maniera-of attenuations derived from late Roman sarcophagus reliefs and from Michelangelo and Parmigiano. With outrageous cunning, the Fontainebleau sculptors and painters twisted torsos and tapered limbs of arbitrary manikins for applying like sprays of acanthus as the most exciting of ornaments [ 354 ].
首席装饰师是来自博洛尼亚的弗朗切斯科·普里马蒂乔，他自 1532 年起参与创作；还有那位暴戾的佛罗伦萨人罗索，他于 1530 年加入团队，却在 1540 年饮下硫酸自尽。 他们通过将人体形态标准化为理想形态——源自晚期罗马石棺浮雕以及米开朗基罗和帕尔米贾尼诺的纤细化手法——来庆祝自己摆脱了文艺复兴鼎盛时期前辈们的束缚。 枫丹白露的雕塑家和画家们以惊人的狡黠扭曲躯干、收束四肢，将任意人偶塑造成如卷曲叶蕨般喷涌的装饰，成就最令人心驰神往的艺术华章[354]。

354

Medea Summons Her Dragon Chariot. Engraving by René Boyvin after Leonard Thiry in Hystoria Iasonis, Paris (Mauregard), 1563
美狄亚召唤她的龙形战车。雷内·博瓦万根据莱昂纳德·蒂里在《伊阿宋史》中的作品所作的雕版画，巴黎（莫雷加尔德），1563 年。
Figure 106: 355 Sea Gods. Etching by Antonio Fantuzzi after Francesco Primaticcio, 1544
图 106：355 海神。安东尼奥·范图齐根据弗朗切斯科·普里马蒂乔作品创作的蚀刻版画，1544 年
The cold but sexy choreography of their wall paintings and stucco decorations first became known through slapdash copperplates dated 1543-47 and printed in the palace itself. The press was probably started by Antonio Fantuzzi (possibly the Antonio da Trento who stole Parmigiano’s drawings), who coarsened Parmigiano’s etching manner to a rough and ready medium for copying anything [355]. The press in the forest probably printed small editions, most of these prints being now rare. Large editions ( 250 in one instance) were then published in Paris by Pierre Millan and his almost indistinguishable successor, René Boyvin, who repeated Fontainebleau designs (especially Rosso’s) from the mid-1540s until nearly 1600 [ 356 ]. These more correct and available engravings, their neat, bright manner derived from Caraglio [ 343 ], have inspired French official art ever since, as one can see on any French banknote. At the time, the pitiless elegance of mannerism offered an emotional refuge from the catastrophe of the sack of Rome, and later from the agony of reciprocal Catholic and Protestant revenges during the Wars of Religion. The shattered world regrouped its wreckage around absolutes-the absolute dogmas of religion, the absolute prince, and the absolute standardization of the human form. Fontainebleau, as the creation of an absolute monarch, displayed the first insolently secular, one might almost say anticlerical, ostentation of Christian times. Long after work had stopped and the palace was abandoned, its vision spread in prints that enticed all Europe to emulate the libertine extravagance of its
他们壁画与灰泥装饰的冷峻而性感的编排，最初通过 1543 至 1547 年间粗制滥造的铜版画得以流传，这些版画在宫殿内直接印刷。印刷厂很可能由安东尼奥·范图齐创办（此人或许就是窃取帕尔米贾尼奥画稿的安东尼奥·达·特伦托），他将帕尔米贾尼奥的蚀刻技法粗化为一种粗犷而便捷的复制媒介[355]。 森林中的印刷厂可能只印制小批量作品，如今这些版画大多已成稀世珍品。而大部头作品（如某次印制 250 册）则由皮埃尔·米兰及其几乎难以区分的继任者勒内·博瓦万在巴黎出版，他们从 1540 年代中期直至近 1600 年持续复刻枫丹白露宫的设计（尤以罗索作品为甚）[356]。 这些更精确且易得的作品，其工整明快的风格源自卡拉焦洛[343]，自此持续启迪着法国官方艺术——法国纸币上的图案便是明证。当时，风格主义冷峻优雅的艺术形式，为人们提供了情感避难所：既可逃离罗马劫掠的灾难阴影，亦能隔绝宗教战争中天主教与新教相互报复的苦痛。 支离破碎的世界围绕绝对主义重组残骸——宗教的绝对教条、君主的绝对权威，以及人体形态的绝对标准化。枫丹白露宫作为绝对君主的杰作，首次展现了基督教时代公然世俗化、近乎反教权的奢华炫耀。当工程停滞、宫殿废弃后，其愿景通过版画传播，诱使整个欧洲效仿其放荡不羁的奢靡之风。

357 银质餐巾盒。博伊文根据罗索·菲奥伦蒂诺作品雕刻而成。
painted and stuccoed walls, its sumptuous masquerades, and its silver sculpture that had already melted into coin [ 357 ]. As an art invented by exiles-decorative, exotic, rootless-the Fontainebleau style transplanted everywhere as readily as abstract art was to do in the 1920 s.
彩绘与灰泥墙面，奢华的假面舞会，以及早已熔铸成钱币的银雕[357]。作为流亡者创造的艺术——装饰性、异域风情、无根基——枫丹白露风格的移植遍及各地，其便捷程度不亚于 1920 年代抽象艺术的传播。

Duvet


Decades after German and Italian engravers had organized their craft conventions, shops, and publishing channels, France had still produced no engraver known by name. Then, in 1520, Jean Duvet began to date prints at Dijon. Engraving started late and far from Paris, perhaps because of jealousy from Parisian guilds. Since France lacked a copperplate tradition, Duvet adapted figures from Mantegna, Dürer, Marcantonio, and others, scattering short, thick strokes so like those in Milanese engravings that some of his prints used to pass for Italian. His father had trained him to work in silver before he started to engrave, so he also, like the very first engravers, stuffed in details as thick as on embossed metal. Although he derived much from others, inspired no followers, and owes at least part of his originality to provincial ineptitude, he fascinates by his intense peculiarity. He dedi-
在德国和意大利的雕刻师们早已建立起行业协会、工坊和出版渠道数十年之后，法国仍未出现一位有名有姓的雕刻师。 直到 1520 年，让·杜维在第戎开始为版画署名。法国的雕版艺术起步较晚且远离巴黎，或许源于巴黎行会的嫉妒。由于法国缺乏铜版画传统，杜维借鉴了曼特尼亚、丢勒、马尔坎托尼奥等人的作品，采用短而粗的线条技法——其风格酷似米兰雕版画，以致部分作品曾被误认为意大利作品。 其父曾教他银器制作，故他亦如早期雕刻师般，将细节堆砌得如浮雕金属般厚重。尽管他多借鉴他人，未启发后继者，且其独创性至少部分源于地方艺术的局限，但其强烈特质仍令人着迷。他献——

图 107：358 披戴日头的妇人。让·杜维特在《启示录》中的铜版画，朗格勒，1546-56 年
Figure 108: 358 The Woman Clothed with the Sun. Engraving by Jean Duvet in Apocalypse, Langres, 1546-56
图 108：358 披戴日头的妇人。让·杜维特在《启示录》中的铜版画，朗格雷，1546-56 年
359 Henry II between France and Fame. Engraving by Duvet, about 1548
359 亨利二世在法国与名声之间。杜维特雕版画，约 1548 年
cated his 23 violent visions of the Apocalypse [ 358 ] to the king, whose coronation and love for Diane de Poitiers inspired allegories of equal strangeness [ 359 ].
他将 23 幅关于世界末日的暴力幻象[358]献给国王，后者的加冕礼与对迪安娜·德·普瓦捷的痴情，同样激发了诡谲的寓言创作[359]。
Perhaps because he worked far away from the palaces that isolated the French court from French life, Duvet did not share the noncommittal detachment of the Fontainebleau mannerists but was gripped instead by the death struggle of Catholics and Protestants. The divisions of the age seem to have divided Duvet against himself, for he joined a fanatic Catholic fraternity in France, and then (unless Dijon produced two silversmiths called Jean Duvet) defected to the enemy at Geneva, where he proceeded to design coins, stained glass, and fortifications for the Calvinists.
或许正因他远离宫廷——那些将法国宫廷与民间生活隔绝的宫殿——杜维特并未像枫丹白露的风格主义者那样保持不置可否的超然态度，反而被天主教徒与新教徒的生死搏斗所震撼。 时代的分裂似乎也撕裂了杜维特自身——他先在法国加入狂热的天主教兄弟会，随后（除非第戎真有两位名叫让·杜维特的银匠）却投奔了日内瓦的敌营，为加尔文派设计钱币、彩绘玻璃与防御工事。

Cousin


The art of Fontainebleau exhilarates partly because its componentsRoman sarcophagi, Raphael, Michelangelo, Giulio Romano, and Parmigiano-all struggle against each other. The hybrid fused into a unity permanently French in
表亲枫丹白露的艺术之所以令人振奋，部分原因在于其构成元素——罗马石棺、拉斐尔、米开朗基罗、朱利奥·罗曼诺和帕尔米贾尼诺——彼此激烈碰撞。这种混血融合最终凝结成一种恒久不朽的法式统一体。
the sculptures of Jean Goujon and in the paintings, sculptures, and prints of Jean Cousin II, both of whom were captivated by Parmigiano’s slender femininity. France adopted Parmigiano more wholeheartedly than Italy because his grace and seeming simplicity retrieved, for secular use, the smiling tenderness of French Gothic Virgins. Cousin was also the first Frenchman to etch [360] almost as fluidly as Parmigiano.
让·古琼的雕塑作品，以及让·库赞二世的绘画、雕塑与版画中，都展现着帕尔米贾尼诺笔下纤柔女性的魅力。 法国比意大利更热忱地接纳帕尔米贾尼奥，因其优雅与看似朴素的风格，为世俗艺术重现了法国哥特式圣母像中含笑的温柔。库赞亦是首位以近乎帕尔米贾尼奥般流畅技法进行蚀刻的法国艺术家。
The most original invention at Fontainebleau had been the stucco frames that surrounded the wall paintings with supple figures twining in and out of cut and curled slabs [ 354 ]. These curving cages, easier to imitate than the dancers therein entwined, preceded the Fontainebleau style as it swept across Europe. Cousin, or his father, used the scheme to decorate a treatise on perspective with naked steeplejacks scampering around a scaffolding [361]. Cousin parodied French logic by projecting his levitated acrobats from plan and elevation, as though he were drawing cubes or columns. Some years later, son or father published a treatise on drawing the figure by geometric projection. His ruler and compass failed, however, to establish coordinates for the flowing complexities of the body, just as Piero della Francesca had failed a century before.
枫丹白露宫最富原创性的发明，当属那些环绕壁画的灰泥画框——柔韧的线条在切割卷曲的石板间蜿蜒盘绕[354]。这些曲线笼罩的框架比其中缠绕的舞者更易模仿，在枫丹白露风格席卷欧洲之前便已出现。 库桑（或其父）沿用此法，在透视法论著中描绘裸体高空工人攀爬脚手架的场景[361]。 库桑以几何投影手法描绘悬浮的杂技演员，如同绘制立方体或柱体，以此戏仿法国逻辑学。数年后，其父或其子出版了关于几何投影人体绘画的论著。然而，正如皮耶罗·德拉·弗朗切斯卡一个世纪前所遭遇的困境，他的直尺与圆规终究未能为人体流动的复杂形态建立坐标体系。
360 The Annunciation. Etching by Jean Cousin II
360 《报喜》 钢版蚀刻画 作者：让·库赞二世


Pleasure gardens (游乐园)


When the French invaded Italy in 1494, they discovered country houses built for enjoyment instead of defense. Since the new cannon easily demolished any medieval fortifications, on coming home they Italianized their now useless keeps and castles, widening slit windows, opening dark courtyards, and expanding into gardens. The sudden transformation of so many great houses was recorded in the first architectural survey ever made of a whole country.
享乐花园 1494 年法国入侵意大利时，发现当地的乡间宅邸皆为享乐而非防御而建。由于新型火炮轻易摧毁了所有中世纪防御工事，归国后的法国人便将这些失去防御价值的城堡和古堡改造成意式风格：拓宽狭缝窗，开辟幽暗庭院，并向花园方向扩展。如此众多豪宅的骤然蜕变，被载入史上首次对整个国家进行的建筑普查记录之中。
The recorder was J. A. Ducerceau, the first prolific designer to adapt Italian ornament to the French taste for elegance and precision. During 20 years of travel in wartime, he neatly and exactly etched nearly 150 plans and bird’s-eye views of 30 mansions [ 362 ]. (Most of these mansions vanished after the French Revolution.) Ducerceau’s folio changed architectural illustration from woodcut to copperplate and started a series of surveys that photography continues to this day. But he had little effect on builders, despite the particularity of his detail, for the French dropped this first Italianate mode when they saw a new harmony of house and garden that the Romans invented at Frascati in the 1590s [363]. There, a pupil of Michelangelo’s sculptured the hillside, scooping out niches for cascades, slanting
记录者是 J·A·杜塞罗，这位多产的设计师率先将意大利装饰艺术融入法国人对优雅与精确的审美追求。 在战时二十年的旅行中，他精确细致地刻画了近 150 幅平面图与 30 座宅邸的鸟瞰图[362]（其中多数宅邸在法国大革命后消失）。杜塞尔索的对开本画册将建筑插图从木刻版画革新为铜版画，并开启了摄影术延续至今的系列测绘传统。 然而尽管其细节刻画独具匠心，他对建筑实践的影响甚微——当法国人目睹罗马人在 1590 年代于弗拉斯卡蒂开创的庭院与住宅新式和谐时[363]，便摒弃了这种早期意大利风格。在那里，米开朗基罗的门徒将山坡雕琢成阶梯式梯田，凿出瀑布壁龛，倾斜的

broad stairs to levels where clipped box and ilex swirled like marquetry, shapely in leaf or snow. Hilltop reservoirs shot jets of water sparkling into the sunlight in open-air galleries peopled with statues.
宽阔的台阶通向层层台地，修剪整齐的黄杨与冬青如镶嵌工艺般盘旋，无论绿叶或白雪都造就优美姿态。山顶水库在露天廊道中喷涌水柱，水花在阳光下粼粼闪耀，廊道间矗立着众多雕像。
The French enlarged the Frascati scheme in the symmetrical stairs and grand landings that once dropped from the château of Saint Germain-en-Laye to the Seine far below. In 1650 Louis XIV’s finance minister, Nicolas Fouquet, assembled 16,000 diggers for 11 years of leveling three villages at Vaux-le-Vicomte to make the grandest garden [ 364 ] since those of the Caesars. When the jealous young king imprisoned his minister and took over his group of artists in 1661, he extended the Fouquet style to the broadest decoration ever spread over the earth. Though Versailles’s immensity was inimitable, engravings of its panoramic gardens inspired German princes to surround their new baroque palaces with symmetries quite interminable enough.
法国人将弗拉斯卡蒂式设计放大，在圣日耳曼昂莱城堡至塞纳河畔的陡峭坡道上，打造出对称的阶梯与宏伟的平台。 1650 年，路易十四的财政大臣尼古拉·富凯召集 16,000 名工人，耗时 11 年将沃勒维孔特的三座村庄夷为平地，打造出自凯撒时代以来最宏伟的花园[364]。 当嫉妒心重的年轻国王于 1661 年囚禁其大臣并接管其艺术团队时，他将富凯风格延伸至人类史上最宏大的装饰工程。尽管凡尔赛宫的恢弘无可复制，但其全景式花园的版画却激励德国诸侯们在其新建的巴洛克宫殿周围打造出同样绵延不绝的对称景观。

365 和谐、奇趣与欢愉之亭，由耶稣会士楞伽·卡斯蒂廖内设计，北京颐和园，1747 年后。中国匿名铜版画

366 蛇形路，奇斯威克别墅，伦敦近郊，伯灵顿勋爵设计，约 1725 年。约翰·唐威尔雕版画
In Peking the emperor Chien Lung emulated such prints with an exotic “europerie” at his Summer Palace, which he also had engraved in the European manner [ 365 ]. Ordinarily, the Chinese and Japanese do not make gardens into outdoor drawing rooms for the meeting of men and women, but plan them as intensively as paintings or poems by contracting the wide horizon to expand the beholder’s mind.
在北京，乾隆皇帝效仿此类版画，在颐和园打造了一座异域风情的"欧式园"，园内建筑亦按欧洲风格雕刻[365]。通常而言，中日韩三国的园林并非为男女相会而设的露天客厅，而是如同绘画或诗歌般精炼凝练——通过压缩辽阔的天地，来拓展观者的心境。
France, and above all Italy, set models for a few gardens in England of a design geometric enough to extend horizontally the architecture of a house facade, but after about 1700 Englishmen began to prefer nature less methodized. While the English inventors of modern agriculture were improving the yield of their land, they also enhanced its beauty by reshaping woods and streams to make their windows frame views like Claude Lorrain paintings. A little before 1800, prints of English landscape gardens [366] furnished models for replacing many formal gardens on the Continent, as people read Rousseau on nature and could no longer pay to keep hedges clipped, gravel raked, and fountains spouting. Western man was beginning to realize that he was after all not the overlord of the universe.
法国，尤其是意大利，为英国少数几座花园树立了典范——这些花园采用几何设计，将房屋立面的建筑美学水平延伸展开。但约 1700 年后，英国人开始偏爱更自然的景观。当英国现代农业的开拓者们提升土地产量时，他们也通过重塑林木溪流，使窗外景致如克劳德·洛兰的画作般精美，从而增强了土地的美感。 1800 年前后，随着人们研读卢梭关于自然的著作，再也无力承担修剪树篱、耙平砾石、维持喷泉的开销，英式景观花园的版画[366]便成为大陆地区众多规整花园的改造范本。西方人开始意识到，自己终究并非宇宙的统治者。

Eternal Rome (永恒的罗马)


Germans in Rome printed the earliest pocket guides [ 367 ] for pilgrims, who hardly noticed works of art while touring the basilicas to pray for their souls. But when Renaissance classicism converted the north of Europe esthetically, northerners, seeking new artistic salvation at its classical source, wanted
永恒的罗马罗马的德国人印制了最早的朝圣者手册[367]，这些朝圣者在游览大教堂为灵魂祈祷时，几乎无暇顾及艺术作品。但当文艺复兴古典主义在美学上改造了欧洲北部，北方人便渴望在古典艺术的源头寻求新的艺术救赎。
367
St. Veronica’s Veil Displayed from Old St. Peter’s. Woodcut in Indulgentie & reliquie Urbis rome, Rome (Silber), about 1495
圣维罗妮卡面纱展于旧圣彼得大教堂。木刻版画出自《罗马城赦罪与圣物志》，罗马（西尔伯版），约 1495 年

pictures to take home the way pilgrims took rosaries. Near Saint Peter’s, the predictable tourist traffic supported bookshops that sold Marcantonio’s engravings after Raphael and the antique until the sack of Rome in 1527.
朝圣者带回家的圣像画，如同朝圣者带回家的念珠。在圣彼得大教堂附近，可预见的游客流量支撑着书店生意——这些书店出售马可·安东尼奥根据拉斐尔作品制作的版画，以及 1527 年罗马被洗劫前的古董。
By the 1540 s enough visitors were returning to launch the first great print publisher, Antoine Lafrery. This expatriate Burgundian assembled the first large stock of miscellaneous copperplates by buying from Marcantonio’s old stock and, beginning in 1544, commissioning new prints and copy prints from rivals. The Roman Calcografia Nazionale still prints from some of the copperplates that Lafrery included in 1573 in the earliest known catalogue of prints for sale, which lists 107 views of Rome. (The first general book catalogue grew out of the Frankfurt book fair in 1564.) So many tourists bought from Lafrery’s offerings that he engraved a special folio title page for them, The Mirror of Rome’s Magnificence. For the first time, a stay-at-home like Shakespeare could see Rome’s freshly unearthed statues [ 342 ], its half-buried ruins, even its yet unfinished civic projects [ 368 ]. Some of Lafrery’s engravings preserve all that we know of buildings that were cannibalized by baroque popes devouring everything in their haste to make modern Rome. Lafrery’s selected buildings suited the Frenchmen who also studied Roman reconstructions by Serlio and Palladio in order to adapt the classical style to France.
到 1540 年代，随着游客数量的回升，安托万·拉弗雷里创立了第一家大型版画出版社。这位勃艮第籍侨民通过收购马尔坎托尼奥的旧藏版画，并自 1544 年起委托竞争对手制作新版画及复刻版画，逐步组建起首批大型综合铜版画库存。 罗马国家铜版画厂至今仍在使用拉弗雷里 1573 年收录于已知最早版画销售目录中的部分铜版——该目录记载了 107 幅罗马风光。（首部综合图书目录诞生于 1564 年的法兰克福书展。） 拉弗雷里作品的游客购买量如此之大，他为此专门雕刻了对开标题页《罗马辉煌之镜》。莎士比亚这样的居家者首次得以窥见罗马新出土的雕像[342]、半掩于地下的遗迹，乃至尚未竣工的市政工程[368]。 拉弗雷里部分版画完整留存了那些被巴洛克教皇拆解的建筑——这些教皇为急于打造现代罗马而吞噬一切。他精选的建筑符合法国人的审美，这些法国人同时研习塞里奥与帕拉迪奥的罗马重建方案，旨在将古典风格移植到法国本土。

Temple of Antoninus and Faustina, A.D. 141. Etching by Etienne Duperac in I VESTIGI DELL' ANTICHITA DI ROMA, Rome (Rossi), 1575
安东尼努斯与福斯蒂娜神庙，公元 141 年。埃蒂安·杜佩拉克蚀刻版画，载于《罗马古迹遗迹》，罗马（罗西出版社），1575 年
The first prints of buildings in groups that walk one through a city were etched in 1575 by another Frenchman [ 369 ]. Here is Montaigne’s Rome of squalid earth engulfing the leafy ruins in a picturesque dilapidation that lured northern artists to perfect their art among broken masterpieces. A romantic young Dutchman like Breenbergh contemplated the collapse of grandeur in a twilight that dims the ruins humbled by weeds [ 370 ]. His pathos reduced Rome to less than what it really was.
1575 年，另一位法国人刻画了首批成组建筑的版画，引领观者穿行于城市之中[369]。此处是蒙田笔下的罗马——污浊的泥土吞噬着绿荫掩映的废墟，形成一幅引人入胜的破败图景，吸引北方艺术家在残破的杰作间精进技艺。 布雷恩伯格这般浪漫的荷兰青年，凝望着暮色中荒芜的废墟——杂草丛生，昔日荣光已然黯淡[370]。他的悲怆情怀，将罗马缩减至远低于其真实面貌的境地。
370

Temple of Antoninus and Faustina. Etching by Giovanni Battista Piranesi, 1758
安东尼努斯与法乌斯蒂娜神庙。乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·皮拉内西蚀刻版画，1758 年
A century later Piranesi achieved the opposite by exploiting the devices of the theatrical designer to twist the stark walls at an angle, and send them flying right, left, and aloft [ 371 ]. He etched the Eternal City in its ideal state, when the popes and their nephews had about ceased quarrying the ruins to make churches and palaces, and archeologists had not yet begun stripping the rubble to expose the misery of its minimal survival. Piranesi hypnotized the world with the spell of Rome until 1839, when the process of photography was announced, and Rome became the first city to be extensively scrutinized by the remorseless lens.
一个世纪后，皮拉内西却反其道而行之，他运用戏剧设计师的技巧，将冷峻的墙壁扭曲成倾斜角度，使其向左右及上方飞跃[371]。他刻画的永恒之城处于理想状态——那时教皇及其侄辈几乎停止了开采废墟建造教堂宫殿，考古学家也尚未开始清理瓦砾，揭露这座城市仅存残骸的凄凉。 皮拉内西用罗马的魔咒令世界沉醉，直至 1839 年摄影术问世，罗马成为首个被无情镜头彻底审视的城市。
372
Calotype by William Henry Fox Talbot, 18405
威廉·亨利·福克斯·塔尔博特拍摄的卡罗型照片，1840 年
The early photographers, who had not yet learned to make the camera lie as blandly as the brush, undid Piranesi’s magic, just as photographers of royalty undid the court painter’s flattery by exposing the tailor’s wrinkles and bunches, while the ethnographical photographer ruined the myth of the noble savage with his rogues’ gallery of paunches, knock knees, and dry dugs. Though the first photographers came to Rome with painters’ and etchers’ eyes for its impressiveness, they could not make their cameras register the awe that they themselves experienced. Yet, curiously, no one could now mistake the early Victorian photographs [372] for modern ones.
早期摄影师尚未学会让相机像画笔般平淡无奇地作假，他们破除了皮拉内西的魔力，正如王室摄影师揭露裁缝的褶皱与堆叠，打破了宫廷画家的奉承之术；而民族志摄影师则用那张张暴突的肚皮、罗圈腿和干瘪乳房组成的罪犯画廊，摧毁了高贵野蛮人的神话。 尽管首批摄影师带着画家与蚀刻师的审美眼光来到罗马，为其恢弘气势所折服，却无法让相机记录下他们亲身感受到的震撼。然而耐人寻味的是，如今无人会将早期维多利亚时期的照片[372]误认为现代作品。

373

Fantastic Ruin. Etching by Jerome Cock in PRAECIPUA ALIQUOT ROMANAE ANTIQUITATIS RUINARUM MONUMENTA, Antwerp, 1551
奇幻废墟。杰罗姆·科克蚀刻版画，选自《罗马古代遗迹精选图录》，安特卫普，1551 年

Printselling in Antwerp and London (安特卫普与伦敦版画销售)


Though print publishing began on a large scale in Rome by retailing souvenirs to pilgrims and tourists, it has usually prospered by wholesaling in centers of export. Since the print publisher had to judge foreign as well as local tastes, he was often a tourist who had stayed on, like Lafrery [ 368 ], or a traveled native.
安特卫普与伦敦的版画销售尽管版画出版业最初在罗马兴起，通过向朝圣者和游客零售纪念品实现大规模生产，但其繁荣通常依赖于出口中心的批发贸易。由于版画出版商既要判断外国市场又要把握本土品味，他们往往是旅居当地的游客——如拉弗雷里[368]——或是见多识广的本地人。
In the 1550 s the common market of the Spanish empire and the easy coinage of American silver and gold made Antwerp an ideal place for exporters of prints. Publishing centered there near the Exchange at the handsome house of the Four Winds, run by Jerome Cock, who had probably been in Rome when Lafrery was starting. Cock sold his own fantastic etchings of Roman ruins [ 373 ] for painters to copy in backgrounds, published engravings after Andrea del Sarto’s already old-fash-
1550 年代，西班牙帝国的共同市场与美洲银金的便捷铸造，使安特卫普成为版画出口商的理想之地。出版业聚集于交易所附近的"四风"宅邸，由杰罗姆·科克经营——当拉弗雷里初创事业时，科克很可能正在罗马。 科克出售自己创作的罗马废墟奇幻蚀刻版画[373]供画家临摹背景，还出版了安德烈亚·德尔·萨尔托早已过时的版画作品——
A Phaeton. Etching by Rudolph Ackermann in IMITATIONS OF DRAWINGS OF FASHIONABLE CARRIAGES, London, 1791
一辆菲亚特。鲁道夫·阿克曼蚀刻版画，选自《时髦马车图集》，伦敦，1791 年
Figure 112: 375 Kailasa Temple, Ellora, India, A.D. 725-75. Aquatint in R. M. Grindley, SCENERY, COSTUMES AND ARCHITECTURE OF INDIA, London (Ackermann), 1826
图 112：印度埃洛拉卡伊拉萨神庙，公元 725-75 年。水彩蚀刻版画，见 R. M. Grindley《印度风光、服饰与建筑》，伦敦（阿克曼出版社），1826 年。
ioned paintings, and imported an up-to-date Italian engraver. Though he published such mannerist print designers as Floris and Heemskerck [ 417 ], we thank Cock today for issuing over 60 engravings after Pieter Brueghel [ 422 ]. Cock stitched together engravings in sets of the four continents, the five senses, the seven virtues, or the nine worthies, making unbound picture books that pleased the learned with elegant Latin under the engravings, while the multitude understood the images without reading. Cock’s biblical subjects sailed as far as Mexico and Peru, where Indians enlarged them in black and white frescoes on monastery walls.
科克不仅出版了弗洛里斯和海姆斯克尔克等风格主义版画设计师的作品[417]，更引进了当时最先进的意大利雕版师。今日我们尤其要感谢他发行了六十余幅彼得·勃鲁盖尔的雕版复制品[422]。 他将版画按主题编纂成册，如四大洲、五感、七美德、九贤等系列，制作成无装订的图册。这些图册以典雅的拉丁文题注取悦学者，而大众则无需阅读文字也能理解图像。科克的圣经题材版画远销墨西哥与秘鲁，当地印第安人将其放大为黑白壁画，装饰在修道院的墙壁上。
Antwerp continued to publish important prints under Rubens [ 427 ], at which point Amsterdam and then Paris began to compete. When the French Revolution and Napoleon’s wars gave London its chance to become the world’s money market, English wealth and the wartime ban on travel turned publishers to books of views sumptuous enough to substitute for tours and cruises.
在鲁本斯执掌期间，安特卫普持续出版重要版画[427]，此时阿姆斯特丹继而巴黎开始与之竞争。法国大革命与拿破仑战争使伦敦获得成为世界金融中心的契机，英国财富的增长及战时旅行禁令促使出版商转向制作精美的风景画册，这些画册足以替代旅行与巡游的体验。
Blockade and embargo drove restless Englishmen to invent light, rugged carriages for the roads that John McAdam was experimentally paving with small broken stones. Catering to these innovations, a young German carriage designer, Rudolph Ackermann, drew, etched, and published a pamphlet of 12 “fashionable carriages” in 1791 [ 374 ]. His success encouraged him to issue carriage designs until 1825 and also to undertake over 60 folios of texts written around views of the world [ 375 ], which in time familiarized the Regency Englishman more than anyone else with the look of far places and directed his imagination to venture forth for an empire.
封锁与禁运迫使不安分的英国人发明了轻便坚固的马车，以适应约翰·麦克亚当用碎石铺设的实验性道路。为迎合这些创新，年轻的德国马车设计师鲁道夫·阿克曼于 1791 年绘制、蚀刻并出版了包含 12 款"时髦马车"的小册子[374]。 此举大获成功，促使他持续发布马车设计直至 1825 年，并着手编纂逾六十册关于世界观的论著[375]。这些著作使摄政时期的英国人比任何群体都更熟悉异域风貌，更激发他们开拓帝国疆域的想象。
Ackermann’s glamorous aquatint plates were colored in his building in the Strand by refugees from the French Revolution. They sat at long tables, passing the sheets from hand to hand as each one brushed on a color. This meant coloring 107,000 prints for Ackermann’s first big publication, the three-volume Microcosm of London in 1808-10 [ 604 ]. These prints did not have to be colored all at once, for the rolling press printed the copperplates gradually as the book sold, since the unit cost did not vary with number. Thus, worn Microcosm plates occur on paper watermarked with dates as late as the 1820s, even though bound with the original text, whose unit cost was greatly reduced by printing the 1000 copies in one press run.
阿克曼那些华丽的水彩蚀刻版画，是在他位于斯特兰德街的建筑里由法国大革命的难民们上色的。他们围坐在长桌旁，将画纸在人手间传递，每人刷上一层颜料。这意味着为阿克曼 1808 至 1810 年间出版的首部巨著——三卷本《伦敦小宇宙》[604]——上色 107,000 幅版画。 这些版画无需一次性完成上色，因滚筒印刷机可随书籍销售进度逐步印制铜版——单件成本不受印量影响。因此，即便装帧于原始文本中（该文本因千册印制一次大幅降低单价），磨损的《伦敦缩影》铜版仍可见水印日期迟至 1820 年代。
Ackermann’s salesroom [ 376 ], the first in London to be lighted with gas, looked like many printshops in England today. Here, in 1822, he imported the German vogue for gift annuals-those gracefully printed miscellanies of sugary verses and vapid pictures in stamped bindings like bonbon boxes that ladies collected until about 1840. On the new steel plates delicately etched illustrations could print perfectly to the very end of immense editions. Ackermann also invented the art magazine with the Repository of Arts (1809-28), which brought some 3000 subscribers about 1000 views of English interiors [ 376 ] and country houses, and 450 fashion plates, documented with swatches of actual fabrics.
阿克曼的展销厅[376]是伦敦首家采用煤气照明的场所，其样貌与当今英格兰众多印刷作坊别无二致。1822 年，他将德国风靡一时的礼品年刊引入此地——这些装帧如糖果盒的精美印刷品，内含甜腻诗句与空洞画作，成为女士们直至 1840 年前热衷的收藏品。 新式钢版能将精雕细刻的插图完美印制至巨量版次的最后一张。阿克曼还创办了艺术杂志《艺术宝库》（1809-1828），为约 3000 名订阅者呈现了 1000 幅英国家居[376]与乡间宅邸的图景，以及 450 幅配有真实布料样本的时尚版画。
Printselling in Antwerp and London
安特卫普与伦敦版画销售

For needle and bobbin (针与梭)


In the 1520 s publishers opened a new market by designing books for women. Their patterns for weaving, embroidery, and, eventually, lace sold so well that printers in Augsburg, Venice, and later Lyons, pirated each others’ designs in booklets that mostly wore out from the pricking of the outlines to transfer them to cloth. The men who drew almost all these designs made them more complex as their publications trained home needlewomen to greater expertness. The one surviving copy of the earliest dated book indicates even earlier ones by calling itself A New Pattern Book [ 377 ]. Its branching leaves were meant to be woven or embroidered in black on linen collars and cuffs like those in Holbein portraits.
为针线与梭子 1520 年代，出版商开辟了面向女性的新市场。他们设计的织造、刺绣乃至蕾丝图案畅销异常，以致奥格斯堡、威尼斯乃至后来的里昂的印刷商们纷纷盗版彼此的设计，印制成册——这些小册子大多因人们反复描摹轮廓以转印到布料上而磨损殆尽。 几乎所有这些图案的设计者都是男性，随着出版物培养出技艺更精湛的家庭女工，他们不断增加图案的复杂度。现存最早的带日期书籍自称《新图案集》[377]，其分枝状叶片图案本应以黑色线绣在亚麻领口和袖口上，如同霍尔拜因肖像画中的样式。
Venetians presently started to cut square openings in linen for darning patterns across the void (reticello). This pre-lace was published, as usual, only after it had been in production. The woodcuts [ 378 ], partly in negative and partly in positive, required skill to interpret. Finally, around 1560, the cobweb of darning ventured forth “into the air” (punto in aria), evolving lace of an intricacy that only copperplate could picture [ 379 ]. Engravings for lace terminate the printed designs for a technique that had at last become too complex for the amateur. Once professionals began to make lace for their living, they prevented patterns from being published for rivals to pirate.
威尼斯工匠开始在亚麻布上裁出方形孔洞，用于在空隙处编织补缀图案（reticello）。这种早期蕾丝制品一如既往，仅在投入生产后才得以公开。木刻版画[378]部分采用负片效果，部分呈现正片效果，解读时需具备专业技艺。 至 1560 年前后，这片补缀的蛛网终于"腾空而起"（punto in aria），演变出唯有铜版画方能呈现的繁复蕾丝[379]。随着蕾丝工艺日益精妙，其印刷图案终告绝版——这项技艺已超出业余爱好者的能力范畴。当专业蕾丝匠人以此为生时，他们严禁图案出版，以免被竞争对手盗版。
Amateur embroiderers have always relied on professional designers. Some of the most ingenious early embroidery designs were shaped to collars, sleeves, and gloves
业余刺绣者向来依赖专业设计师。早期最具匠心的刺绣图案多见于衣领、衣袖和手套。
Figure 116: 381 Pattern for silk caparison for a horse. Woodcut in Juan de Alcega, Libro de Geometria pratica, Madrid (Drouy), 1589

for home dressmaking [380]. In the 1500 dress patterns seem to have traveled from queen to queen by paper cutouts. Cutting patterns were first printed in Spain to help the professional tailor cut clothes for people and for horses [ 381 ] accurately and without waste. When the silk or velvet for a suit might cost a tailor’s yearly earnings, he could not afford mistakes. To help him, Alcega printed a line about three quarters of an inch long as the standard inch of Castile for converting his patterns into the inches used in other places. His publication standardized the court styles of Madrid for Spaniards stationed in Naples, Brussels, or Lima as civil servants in the first empire on which the sun never set. Conformity mattered to the
用于家庭裁缝的纸样[380]。16 世纪时，服装纸样似乎通过剪纸形式在王后之间流传。西班牙最早印刷的裁剪纸样，旨在帮助专业裁缝为人和马匹[381]精准裁剪衣物，避免浪费。 当一套丝绸或天鹅绒服装的成本可能抵得上裁缝一年的收入时，失误便难以承受。为解决此问题，阿尔塞加在版型上印制了一条约三英寸长的标尺，作为卡斯蒂利亚标准英寸的参照，便于将版型转换为其他地区使用的英寸制。他的出版物将马德里宫廷风格标准化，使驻扎在那不勒斯、布鲁塞尔或利马的西班牙公务员——在那个"日不落帝国"中——都能遵循统一规范。合规性至关重要。

The next tailors’ cutting patterns were published at Paris in 1671 to further Louis XIV’s ambition to impose French styles on the whole of the polite world. During the 1700 s 1700 s 1700 s1700 s clothes conserved their basic cut while often changing their color and woven design. Prints published styles seen at court but did not begin to initiate new styles fresh from dressmakers until fashion magazines began in Paris a decade before the French Revolution [ 382 ]. Then one of the most coveted conquests of the new bourgeoisie was the right to dress in clothes that would look silly before they could wear out. This pushed the rich to race ahead of the poor with changes that professional designers now publish almost as soon as they invent them.
1671 年，巴黎出版了下一批裁缝剪裁图样，旨在推进路易十四将法国风格强加于整个文明世界的野心。在此期间，服装虽保留基本剪裁，但色彩与织物纹样却频繁更迭。 印刷品虽刊载宫廷流行的款式，却未能开创裁缝师的新颖设计——直至法国大革命前十年巴黎时尚杂志问世[382]。此后新兴资产阶级最渴求的征服之一，便是拥有穿着新装的权利，让衣着在磨损前便显得过时。这促使富人竞相领先贫民，而专业设计师如今几乎在设计诞生之际便将新款发布。

Man's variety (人类的多样性)


Ever since about 1500 b.c., when Queen Hatshepsut in Egypt had pictures carved of the tree houses and strange beasts of the Land of Puoni (South Arabia), people have wanted to see how men live far away. This curiosity led to the voyages of discovery, whose reports sharpened an appetite for more. Even as Columbus was returning from his first expedition, a huge world history appeared at Nuremberg with woodcuts of anthropophagi and men “whose heads do grow beneath their shoulders” [ 383 ]. Pictures of real men almost as strange began to come back with explorers of uncharted shores until Central and South Americans became so familiar by 1550 that masqueraders in Rouen dressed up as Brazilians to entertain the king on a visit.
人类的多样性自公元前 1500 年左右埃及女王哈特谢普苏特命人雕刻普奥尼之地（南阿拉伯）的树屋与奇兽图景以来，人们便渴望窥见远方居民的生活图景。这份好奇催生了探索航程，而航海报告更激起了人们对未知世界的无限渴求。 就在哥伦布结束首次远征归来之际，纽伦堡出版了一部巨著《世界通史》，书中刊载着食人族与"头颅生于肩胛之下"之人的木刻版画[383]。 随着探险家们踏足未知海岸，那些真实存在却同样奇特的形象开始传回欧洲。至 1550 年，中美洲与南美洲已广为人知，鲁昂的化装舞会甚至出现巴西装扮者，为到访的国王献艺取乐。
Europeans were distracted from Americans when the Turks besieged Vienna in 1529 and kept threatening the city until the last, most frightening siege in 1683. People had already seen Turkish turbans in Schongauer’s engravings, but now the
1529 年土耳其人围攻维也纳时，欧洲人的注意力从美洲转移开来，此后土耳其人持续威胁这座城市，直至 1683 年最后一次最令人胆寒的围城战。人们早已在施恩高尔的版画中见过土耳其人的头巾，但此刻——

first detailed prints of any strangers explored the manners and customs of the Turks as they were in 1533 [ 384 ]. This strip of woodcuts 16 feet long showed more about Turkish life than many Europeans knew about the lives of their neighbors.
首批详尽的陌生人版画记录了 1533 年土耳其人的风俗习惯[384]。这幅 16 英尺长的木刻画卷展现的土耳其生活图景，远超当时许多欧洲人对邻国生活的认知。
As prints revealed the variety of the human family, neighbors from the next province, or even the next town, began to assume their place as subspecies in the great generic categories. In the 1550 the earliest series of costume prints of various peoples surveyed Europe and the Near East in some 100 Italian engravings [ 385 ]. The first of the innumerable books of the costumes of the New World as well as the Old was issued in Paris in 1562 by an otherwise unknown man whose name was probably Després, misprinted Deserpz. He copied costumes from sketches by a French navy captain and a Portuguese traveler for a modest booklet that concentrates on Europe, with a supplement on South America [ 386 ].
随着版画揭示人类家族的多样性，邻近省份乃至邻镇的居民开始在广义的分类体系中占据亚种的位置。1550 年代，最早的一系列民族服饰版画通过约百幅意大利雕版画，对欧洲及近东地区进行了考察[385]。 1562 年，巴黎出版了首部记录新旧世界服饰的著作，作者身份不详，可能名为德斯普雷（Després），但书名被误印为德塞尔普兹（Deserpz）。他根据法国海军上校与葡萄牙旅行家的素描复刻服饰，编纂成聚焦欧洲的简明手册，并附有南美洲补充内容[386]。
The first pictorial encyclopedia of all mankind was published at Venice by a nephew of Titian, at a time when foreign costumes must have been everyday sights on the canals. Vecellio included antique Roman dress and pioneered in sociology by describing local customs with each of the 420 woodcuts that covered the then known world. The woodblocks, neatly cut by a German, note even finer differences as they approach home, distinguishing the dress of each city in Italy and each class and profession in Venice itself. One of the cuts [ 387 ] shows a Venetian girl bleaching her hair by spreading it over a wicker brim while she sits in the sun on one of the flat rooftops that Venetian women appropriated as their private living and reception rooms. Nowadays the magazines and newspapers that introduce everybody to everybody else have shamed many peoples out of their local traditions, imposing skirts and trousers from icebergs to jungles.
人类首部图鉴百科全书由提香的侄子在威尼斯出版，彼时外国服饰想必已是运河沿岸的日常风景。维切利奥不仅收录古罗马服饰，更开创性地通过 420 幅木刻版画描绘各地风俗，这些版画覆盖了当时已知的整个世界。 这些由德国工匠精雕的木版画，在描绘本土风情时更显细腻：意大利各城服饰的差异，乃至威尼斯城内不同阶层与职业的装束皆被精准区分。 其中一幅版画[387]描绘威尼斯少女晒发漂白：她将发丝铺在柳编帽檐上，在平顶屋上沐浴阳光——这些屋顶已被威尼斯女性改造成私人起居室与会客厅。如今那些将所有人相互引荐的杂志报纸，正迫使许多民族摒弃本土传统，从冰原到丛林都强行推行统一的裙装与裤装。



Furniture designs (家具设计)


Furniture designs are worth printing wherever well-to-do people want to keep up with fashions created elsewhere. Nuremberg took advantage of its imperial status to issue the first printed furniture designs for less favored places. There Peter Flötner signed his cuts with his woodcutter’s chisel and mallet, and even showed himself sitting on his bed with his leather apron and another mallet in his hand [ 388 ]. He probably derived his open, unshaded lines and his classical swags and niches from the Hypnerotomachia [ 223 ]. Beds were worth embellishing in Flötner’s day when people lived among them in halls and parlors, where their curtains shut off a room within a room. In France, where Paris set fashion for the provinces, and an absolute monarch exacted more elaboration than a joiner could invent, the professional designer J. A. Ducerceau etched the most ostentatious furniture of the age. At Fontainebleau and the Louvre, the showpiece was the cabinet [ 389 ], whose doors disclosed a midget stage of mirrored niches and columns of ebony and agate. The real purpose of such doll palaces must have been to provide small talk for the intimate circle of French courtiers who scrutinized furniture so exactingly that from about 1675 to 1789 they demanded and got the most elaborately designed and intricately contrived pieces ever made. This court furniture eventually supplied ideas to be simplified in the practical designs that Paris printed in summary etchings costing a fraction of the shaded engravings after paintings.
家具设计图值得印刷，只要富裕阶层渴望追随异地风尚。纽伦堡凭借其帝国地位，率先为欠发达地区发行印刷版家具设计图。彼得·弗洛特纳用木刻凿与木锤在版画上签名，甚至展示自己身着皮围裙、手持另一把木锤坐在床上的姿态[388]。 他那开阔无阴影的线条、古典的流苏与壁龛装饰，很可能源自《梦境之战》[223]。弗洛特纳所处的时代，床具值得精心装饰——人们在厅堂起居室中与床共处，床帷将房间分隔成室内之室。 在法国，巴黎引领着各省的时尚潮流，而绝对君主对家具的奢华要求远超木匠的创造力。专业设计师 J·A·杜塞罗以蚀刻工艺打造出那个时代最炫目的家具——枫丹白露宫与卢浮宫的镇馆之宝便是那座橱柜[389]，其门扉开启时，映入眼帘的是一座微缩舞台：镜面壁龛与乌木玛瑙立柱交相辉映。 这类微缩宫殿的真正用途，想必是为法国宫廷的亲密圈子提供闲谈话题——他们审视家具时如此苛刻，以致在 1675 至 1789 年间，催生并获得了史上设计最繁复、构思最精巧的家具作品。这些宫廷家具最终为实用设计提供了灵感，巴黎印刷的简化版蚀刻图谱便将这些理念转化为平民可及的版本，其成本仅为绘画阴影版画的零头。
Prints played an odd part in the curiously individual style of the furniture designed at Antwerp in the 1580s [ 390 ]. Though Vredeman de Vries’ designs were published in the greatest seaport of the time, Antwerp’s ships spread them no farther than up the Rhine into Germany and across the Channel to England, while
在 1580 年代安特卫普设计的家具中，印花图案扮演着奇特而独特的角色[390]。尽管弗雷德曼·德·弗里斯的设计在当时最大的海港城市出版发行，但安特卫普的船只仅将这些设计传播至莱茵河上游的德国地区，以及横跨英吉利海峡抵达的英国，而

安特卫普在马德里乃至整个南美洲的统治者们，仍坚持用天鹅绒覆盖素面折叠桌。纯粹遵循弗雷德曼风格的旧家具极为罕见，直至 1882 年后，其版画作品通过照相复制技术传播，才启发了南北半球啤酒馆的装饰风格。
All the while that Italy was instructing the world through prints of architecture and figure drawing, the Italians printed no furniture designs, because each city preferred its own local style that it saw being made in open-front shops. It was almost 1700 before Rome at last brought out the only Italian furniture designs to be printed for nearly a century thereafter. Some Roman baroque sculptor such as

Furniture designs  家具设计

391 A soldier's bedroom. Etching by Filippo Passarini in NUOVE INVENTIONI D'ORNAMENTI, Rome (Rossi), 1698
391 士兵卧室。菲利波·帕萨里尼蚀刻版画，见《装饰新发明》，罗马（罗西出版社），1698 年

392 (opposite page, left) Design for mirrors. Drawing for Thomas Chippendale, THE GENTLEMAN AND CABINET-MAKER’S DIRECTOR, London (Chippendale), 1754
392（对页左）镜具设计图。为托马斯·奇彭代尔所绘，《绅士与家具匠指南》，伦敦（奇彭代尔），1754 年
Algardi must have invented this theatrical furniture of branches swirling around cupids and captives [ 391 ]. It caught on in Turin and in Austria but declaimed too operatically for France or England. Indeed, traditional English furniture excels in the exactly opposite virtues of durability, convenience, and the elegance of plainness. In 1754 England, North America, and India quickly adapted the first special publication of furniture designs, Chippendale’s Director, whose third edition in 1762 added new designs and a French text to send it still further afield. It served Chippendale as a mail-order catalogue for his busy factory by being the first publication of furniture for the drawing room, dining room, bedroom, and library. His designers intermixed Gothic window tracery, Chinese fretwork, and French chair forms with rock and shell carving from Augsburg prints. He constructed soundly for all furniture meant to be shoved about but disregarded practicality in mirror frames [ 392 ], where he let the imported fad of rococo go madder than it did anywhere in its home on the Continent. The Director summed up and ended this English hybrid. Oddly enough, the only documented furniture from Chippendale’s factory is in the classic style of Adam. Chippendale’s contemporaries varied his designs to suit themselves, but when his style ceased to be current and colloquial, the early Victorians copied his engravings literally. After about 1870, manufacturers’ trade catalogues [ 393 ], instead of books by designers, spread styles and documented their development.
阿尔加迪想必是发明了这种戏剧性的家具——枝条盘绕着爱神与俘虏[391]。这种风格在都灵和奥地利风靡一时，却因过于夸张浮华而不适合法国或英国。事实上，传统英式家具恰恰以耐久性、实用性及朴素优雅的相反特质见长。 1754 年，英格兰、北美和印度迅速采纳了首部家具设计专著《奇彭代尔指南》。该书 1762 年第三版新增设计并附法文说明，使其传播范围更广。作为首部涵盖客厅、餐厅、卧室及书房家具的出版物，它同时成为奇彭代尔繁忙工厂的邮购目录。 其设计师将哥特式窗饰、中式镂空纹样、法式椅型与奥格斯堡版画中的岩石贝壳雕刻融为一体。他为所有需移动的家具打造了稳固结构，却在镜框设计[392]中忽视实用性——任由进口的洛可可风潮在此疯狂蔓延，其畸变程度甚至超越了欧洲大陆的发源地。《指南》既总结了这种英式混搭风格，也宣告了其终结。 颇为奇特的是，现存唯一可考的奇彭代尔工厂家具竟是亚当式古典风格。其同时代人虽常根据需求改造设计，但当奇彭代尔风格不再流行时，早期维多利亚人却开始照搬其版画作品。约 1870 年后，风格传播与发展记录的载体已从设计师著作转向制造商贸易目录[393]。

Furniture designs  家具设计


Anatomy becomes a science (解剖学成为一门科学)


Before 1543 classroom lists of the parts of the body illustrated anatomy vaguely, if at all, while Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo were basing their art on the most searching studies ever drawn of dissections. But since the anatomist could not draw and the artist lacked academic system, neither alone could produce a text useful to modern science.
解剖学成为一门科学在 1543 年之前，课堂上对人体部位的罗列充其量只是模糊地描绘解剖结构，而达·芬奇与米开朗基罗的艺术创作却基于当时最深入的解剖研究成果。然而解剖学家不懂绘画，艺术家又缺乏学术体系，二者各自为政，皆无法独立创作出对现代科学有用的著作。
While Renaissance artists habitually collaborated in workshops, as architects do today, scientists did not. True scientific collaboration between artist and anatomist began in the intellectual climate of Italy when the Flemish anatomist Andreas Vesalius, a full professor at Padua University while still in his 20s, worked with John Stephen of Calcar, a Flemish painter some 15 years older, who had formed his style on Titian. The anatomist had to explain to the artist just what to clarify in a given dissection in order to fit it into a general survey of the body. Then the artist had to find the angle and lighting that best emphasized the required features. Lastly-the test of awareness-the artist had to choose among the infinite alternatives for drawing any object just those lines that unmistakably describe the stressed aspects. The resulting picture had to look “real” and yet be as selective as a diagram.
文艺复兴时期的艺术家们惯常在工作室里合作创作，如同当今的建筑师们那样，而科学家们却并非如此。当佛兰德解剖学家安德烈亚斯·维萨留斯——这位二十多岁便成为帕多瓦大学正教授的学者——与年长他约十五岁的佛兰德画家约翰·斯蒂芬·卡尔卡尔（其画风深受提香影响）在意大利的学术氛围中展开合作时，艺术家与解剖学家之间的真正科学协作才得以开启。 解剖学家需向画家阐明：在特定解剖过程中，哪些部位需要重点呈现，才能契合人体整体研究的框架。画家则需寻找最佳视角与光线，以突出所需特征。 最后——这是对艺术家认知力的考验——在无限可能的绘制方案中，必须精准选取那些能清晰呈现重点特征的线条。最终作品既要呈现"真实"感，又要像示意图般具有选择性。
In this difficult task of understanding, then of drawing so as to convey the understanding to others, John of Calcar almost attained the clarity of Leonardo da Vinci,
在这项艰巨的任务中——先是理解，继而通过绘画将理解传达给他人——卡尔卡的约翰几乎达到了达·芬奇的清晰度。
Figure 122: 394 Muscle Men. Woodcuts by John Stephen of Calcar in Andreas Vesalius, de Humani corporis fabrica, Basel (Oporinus), 1543
图 122：394 位肌肉男子。约翰·斯蒂芬·卡尔卡尔为安德烈亚斯·维萨留斯所作木刻版画，载于《人体构造论》，巴塞尔（奥波里努斯出版社），1543 年
whose drawings he evidently knew. Leonardo’s quill moves with a subtler flexibility, but is no more explicit than the bold, flowing lines of the Vesalian woodcuts. Here the muscle men [ 394 ] stand against a continuous landscape that links them in tattered ballets of eight who face you and six who turn their backs, lining up like the old frescoed Danse Macabre in Paris [ 54 ] that Vesalius certainly saw as a student. But instead of the dried cadavers of the medieval Danse Macabre, as skinny as wet cats or actual dissections, the Vesalian men flex their stripped biceps and strut like champions in a Renaissance Dance of Life that proclaims the will to keep going, come what may: the determination that distinguishes Western man from the world of Buddhism. Though none stands exactly like any antique statue, all have the robust Polyclitan proportions that Titian followed in his paintings. John of Calcar’s woodcuts used to be attributed to Titian, who indeed may have outlined the poses and proportions for the anatomical artist to fill in. Titian’s own finer line and more Olympian assurance certainly swing through the superb Adam and Eve [395] that Vesalius omitted from his biggest book, perhaps because he had had nothing to do with planning them.
他显然熟悉这些素描。达·芬奇的鹅毛笔笔触更显灵动，但其含蓄程度与维萨里木刻中粗犷奔放的线条不相上下。 这些肌肉男[394]伫立于连绵的背景中，形成八人面朝观者、六人背对的残缺芭蕾队形，如同维萨留斯求学时必定见过的巴黎壁画《死亡之舞》[54]。 但与中世纪骷髅舞中干瘪如湿猫的尸骸或真实解剖标本不同，维萨留斯笔下的男子们袒露肱二头肌，如冠军般昂首阔步，在文艺复兴的"生命之舞"中宣告无论遭遇何种困境都要继续前行的意志——正是这种决心使西方人区别于佛教世界。尽管无人完全复刻古希腊雕像姿态，所有人物都具备提香画作中遵循的波利克利坦式健壮比例。 卡尔卡的木刻曾被归于提香名下——这位大师或许确曾为解剖学家勾勒姿势与比例框架。提香那更纤细的线条与更具奥林匹斯神祇般自信的笔触，在《亚当与夏娃》[395]中尽显无遗。维萨留斯将其排除在巨著之外，或许正因他未参与创作规划。
Previous illustrators had jumbled human bones like safety pins, but Calcar was able to draw their complex perspective because Vesalius had recently invented the articulated skeleton by stringing the bones together on stiff wires for flexing into
以往的插图画家将人体骨骼像安全别针般随意堆砌，而卡尔卡尔却能精准描绘其复杂的透视关系——这得益于维萨留斯新近发明的活动骨骼模型：他将骨骼用硬质金属丝串联起来，使其能够弯曲成各种姿势。
Figure 123: 395 Adam and Eve. Woodcuts, probably by Titian, in Vesalius, Epitome, Basel (Oporinus), 1543
图 123：395 亚当与夏娃。木刻版画，可能出自提香之手，见于维萨留斯《人体纲要》，巴塞尔（奥波里努斯出版社），1543 年
Figure 124: 395 Adam and Eve. Woodcuts, probably by Titian, in Vesalius, Epitome, Basel (Oporinus), 1543
图 124：395 亚当与夏娃。木刻版画，可能出自提香之手，见于维萨留斯《医学纲要》，巴塞尔（奥波里努斯出版社），1543 年。
Anatomy becomes a science
解剖学成为一门科学

396
"The Weeping Magdalene." Woodcut by John Stephen of Calcar in de Humani corporis fabrica
396 《哭泣的抹大拉》木刻版画，出自卡尔卡尔·约翰·斯蒂芬所著《人体构造图谱》


dramatic attitudes. Calcar’s three skeletons include one wringing its hands with passionate grace [ 396 ], usually known as the Weeping Magdalene, and a skeleton contemplating a skull that could have suggested Hamlet’s “Alas, poor Yorick.” Since their backgrounds do not connect, Calcar may have drawn these skeletons before his muscle men.
戏剧化的姿态。卡尔卡的三具骷髅骨架中，有一具正以充满激情的优雅姿态搓揉双手[396]，通常被称为"哭泣的抹大拉"；另一具则凝视着骷髅头，这场景或许暗示了哈姆雷特那句"唉，可怜的约里克"。由于背景未见关联，卡尔卡可能是在绘制肌肉男之前就完成了这些骷髅骨架。
This publication, prepared in Padua and nearby Venice, should have climaxed the glorious line of Venetian scientific books. Instead, some rage, some feud, drove Vesalius to pack his manuscript and more than 200 bulky woodblocks on mules and leave Europe’s printing capital for Basel, beyond the Alps. The answer to this riddle perished when exasperation at his critics provoked Vesalius into burning his papers a year after he published his book. Yet, whatever his academic rivals had to disparage, artists at once adopted his anatomical compendium. Some still use it, absolving themselves from the messy and expensive drudgery of dissecting.
这部在帕多瓦及邻近的威尼斯编撰的著作，本应成为威尼斯科学书籍辉煌传承的巅峰之作。然而，某些愤怒与纷争迫使维萨留斯将手稿和两百余块厚重的木刻版装上骡子，离开欧洲印刷之都，远赴阿尔卑斯山彼岸的巴塞尔。 这桩谜案的答案已随手稿灰烬消散——出版一年后，韦萨留斯因对批评者的愤懑而焚毁了所有文献。然而无论学术对手如何贬低，艺术家们却立即采纳了他的解剖学手册。时至今日仍有使用者，借此免去繁琐昂贵的解剖苦役。
The publication of these woodcuts in 1543 and the unveiling of Michelangelo’s Last Judgment in 1541 established the heavy-set Roman athlete in the art of the baroque.
1543 年这些木刻版画的出版与 1541 年米开朗基罗《最后的审判》的揭幕，确立了魁梧的罗马运动员形象在巴洛克艺术中的地位。

Artists as block-cutters (艺术家作为石板雕刻师)



作为雕版师的艺术家汉斯·伯克迈尔曾坦言自己亲手雕刻过部分版块。弗朗切斯科·弗朗西亚同样精通此道——身为博洛尼亚造币厂厂长，他负责制作钱币印模；作为城中唯一技艺精湛的画家，他指导马尔坎托尼奥学习雕刻与绘画。弗朗西亚无疑设计了圣凯瑟琳·博洛尼亚的金属版块[397]，并很可能亲自完成雕刻。这位圣女逝世时，弗朗西亚年仅十三岁。 圣像面容的深邃光滑质感，与弗朗西亚绘制的祭坛画人物如出一辙，但不同于圣母像，这张面容却令人不安地酷似肖像画。而这正是圣凯瑟琳本人的肖像——五百年来，她以乌木木乃伊之姿，在宛若闺房的圣堂中接受朝拜[398]。 如今她端坐于镀金宝座之上，取代了金属浮雕中文艺复兴时期的宝座——后者装饰风格与弗朗西亚的祭坛画框如出一辙，极可能出自其手。那些终日跪拜圣凯瑟琳的信徒，最初或许购得的是印在单页纸上的弗朗西亚肖像版画，后来才将版画顶部裁剪，将其装订进圣徒文集。
397 St. Catherine de’ Vigri of Bologna. Metal cut, probably by Francesco Francia, in St. Catherine, Libro deuoto della beata Chaterina, Bologna (Benedictis), 1511
397 博洛尼亚的圣凯瑟琳·德·维格里。金属剪纸，可能出自弗朗切斯科·弗朗西亚之手，见于《圣凯瑟琳》，《圣女凯瑟琳敬礼书》，博洛尼亚（本笃会），1511 年。

Artists as block-cutters
艺术家作为石板雕刻师
Another versatile Italian artist, Domenico Beccafumi, had learned all about cutting designs into flat surfaces while he worked for nearly 30 years on the marble marquetry pictures in the cathedral pavement at Siena. Vasari says that this “uomo capriciosissimo, successful in everything, cut his own woodblocks,” and with such originality that Vasari pasted one of the prints in his famous scrapbook of drawings. In his woodcuts [ 399 ], as in his pavement, this painter of twilight devised happy, bold ways to evoke figures out of the dusk, cutting ink-blot shadows like black inlays in white marble.
另一位多才多艺的意大利艺术家多梅尼科·贝卡菲米，在锡耶纳大教堂地面上耗时近三十年创作大理石镶嵌画期间，已精通在平面上雕刻图案的技艺。瓦萨里称这位"极富天赋的奇才，凡事皆能成功，亲手雕刻木刻版"，其作品独具匠心，以致瓦萨里将其中一幅版画粘贴于其著名的素描剪贴簿中。 在这位暮色画家的木刻作品[399]中，正如他在地坪创作时那样，他巧妙运用欢快而大胆的手法，从暮色中勾勒出人物轮廓，将墨渍般的阴影如黑色镶嵌物般镌刻于白色大理石之上。
In the following generation there was one Italian draftsman whose straight, wide-apart lines seem made for easy woodcutting, somewhat the way van Gogh’s solid colors seem made for four-color process reproduction. Luca Cambiaso, a sculptor as well as a painter, could readily have cut the block [ 400 ] for this brisk seduction drawn from one of his Genoese frescoes. He certainly brushed on the wash that so skillfully heightens the effect. He might naturally have wanted to reproduce his drawings, as Mantegna had done, since he seems to have been the first artist to give a large part of his effort to making drawings specifically for sale, taking quick advantage of the mode for collecting them that Vasari’s Lives of the Artists had stimulated when Cambiaso was 23. Although his drawings were popular enough to be frequently faked, his woodcuts, oddly, are rare. His stylish block construction was imitated in Venetian book illustrations [ 401 ] by some other art-
在下一代艺术家中，有位意大利素描师笔触笔直而疏朗，其线条仿佛专为简易的木刻而生——正如梵高的纯色画作似乎天生适合四色印刷工艺。卢卡·坎比亚索既是雕塑家也是画家，他完全能亲手为这幅取材自热那亚壁画的轻快诱惑之作雕刻木板[400]。 他确实亲手刷上了那层巧妙增强效果的渍色。他自然可能像曼特尼亚那样想复制自己的素描——毕竟他似乎是首位将大量精力投入专门为销售而作的素描创作的艺术家，敏锐把握了瓦萨里《艺术家传》在坎比亚索 23 岁时掀起的素描收藏热潮。 尽管其素描作品广受欢迎以致屡遭赝造，但他的木刻版画却出奇地罕见。他在威尼斯书籍插图中[401]展现的时尚版式构图，曾被其他艺术家模仿——
399
St. Andrew or St. Philip. Woodcut by Domenico Beccafumi
圣安德鲁或圣菲利普。多梅尼科·贝卡富米木刻版画
Artists as block-cutters
艺术家作为石板雕刻师

400

Woodcut washed with ink, by or after Luca Cambiaso from his fresco of the Rape of the Sabines, in Villa Imperiali, Terralba, 15706
木刻版画，墨洗处理，据卢卡·坎比亚索所作《萨宾妇女被劫》壁画改编，该壁画原存于特拉尔巴的帝国别墅，15706 年。

401

Musical Intervals. Woodcut in Lodovico Fogliani, MUSICA THEORICA, Venice (de Sabio),1529
音乐音程。洛多维科·福利亚尼《音乐理论》中的木刻版画，威尼斯（德·萨比奥），1529 年

ist-surely a painter-who flowed lines continuously instead of sparking them with Cambiaso’s discontinuous snaps. This Venetian probably drew quite differently when not simplifying for the woodcutter, who may well have been himself.
这位画家——无疑是位画家——笔触流畅连贯，而非像坎比亚索那样以断续的笔触点出火花。这位威尼斯画家在为木刻师简化线条时，画风想必截然不同，而那位木刻师很可能就是他本人。
The airy openness of Cambiaso and his Venetian imitator is the opposite of the dark, painterly woodcuts of their contemporary Giuseppe Scolari [402], who seems to brush broad whites on solid black. Scolari drew his picture out of the dark by bundling white lines in close parallels, as though cut with the multiple tool of points like a rake that French and English wood engravers were to use in the 1920 s. Like these recent wood engravers, Scolari imagined his pictures in terms of wood, not in terms of a pen or pencil transfer onto wood. Italian artists, unlike the French, fascinate by their unpredictability, now acting like their grandfathers, now like their great-grandsons.
坎比亚索及其威尼斯模仿者的作品通透开阔，与同时代艺术家朱塞佩·斯科拉里[402]的木刻截然相反——后者作品暗沉如油画，仿佛在纯黑背景上挥洒大片纯白。 斯科拉里通过密集平行排列的白色线条将画面从黑暗中勾勒出来，仿佛使用了法国和英国木刻师在 1920 年代才开始采用的、类似耙齿状的多点刻刀。与这些现代木刻师相似，斯科拉里以木材本身为创作媒介构思画面，而非将铅笔或钢笔稿转印至木板。 意大利艺术家与法国同行不同，其不可预测性令人着迷——时而效法祖父辈的技法，时而又展现出曾孙辈的创新精神。

Titian (提香)


After the lucid outline woodcuts of the 1480 s and 90s, Venetian prints declined with the disasters that fell upon the Republic. In 1498 Vasco da Gama undercut her monopoly of Asian trade by sailing to India around the Cape of Good Hope, and in 1508 a league of her European enemies would have dismembered her had they not quarreled among themselves. Venetian discouragement shows in decades of sloppy book design and muddy little cuts in the mechanical routine imported from Strassburg [56]. But since book exports brought in money, the Senate in 1537 assured the quality of paper, at least, by decreeing that if ink were found to blot on the margins of any five leaves in any five copies taken at random from an edition, the entire edition must be burned in the Piazza.
提香继 1480 年代与 90 年代那些线条明快的木刻版画之后，威尼斯版画随着共和国遭遇的灾难而衰落。1498 年，瓦斯科·达·伽马绕过好望角航行至印度，打破了威尼斯对亚洲贸易的垄断；1508 年，欧洲诸敌本欲结盟瓜分威尼斯，却因内讧而功败垂成。 威尼斯的颓势体现在长达数十年的粗劣书籍设计与朦胧小版画上——这些机械化的制作方式源自斯特拉斯堡[56]。但因书籍出口创汇，参议院于 1537 年至少确保了纸张品质：颁布法令规定，若从任意版本中抽取五册，发现其中任意五页的页边存在墨迹晕染，则该版所有书籍必须在广场上焚毁。
While an edict might outlaw shabby materials, it took no less than Titian to raise the art of the book to its second, and perhaps greater, glory in Venice. He had begun to advertise his painting by drawing single-sheet woodcuts in 1508, when he was about 31 , and he continued to publish them along with engravings [ 408 ] until his death 68 years later. He drew his greatest woodcut [ 403 ] on 12 blocks that compose a wall decoration four feet high by seven wide. While the blocks assemble into a sweeping unity, each one by itself delights with the shapes of the blank spaces between objects [ 404 ], active voids that Titian was the first Westerner to design as sensitively as the Chinese and Japanese. The inscription boasts that this paper tapestry was “drawn by Titian’s immortal hand” and was cut by Domenico dalle Greche, of whom we know little except that he was not El Greco. Titian made the Greek woodcutter respect his reed pen line as exactly as a German cutter would have done in order to conduct the mass of energy that charges through the vast
尽管法令可能禁止使用劣质材料，但唯有提香才能将威尼斯的书籍艺术推向第二个、或许更为辉煌的鼎盛时期。1508 年，约 31 岁的他开始通过绘制单幅木刻版画宣传自己的画作，此后 68 年直至离世，他持续出版这类版画及铜版画[408]。 他最伟大的木刻作品[403]由 12 块木板组成，拼接成高四英尺、宽七英尺的壁饰。这些木板组合成气势恢宏的整体，而每块单独的木板都因物体间留白构成的形态[404]而令人惊叹——提香是西方首位能像中日韩艺术家般敏锐设计动态留白的艺术家。 题记宣称这幅纸质挂毯由"提香不朽之手绘制"，并由多梅尼科·达莱·格雷克雕刻。关于此人我们所知甚少，仅能确定他并非埃尔·格列柯。提香要求这位希腊木刻师像德国雕刻师那样精准复刻其芦苇笔线条，以承载贯穿整幅巨作的磅礴能量。
Artists as block-cutters
艺术家作为石板雕刻师
Figure 127: 403 Pharaoh's Army Drowned in the Red Sea. Woodcut by Domenico dalle Greche after Titian, 1549
图 127：403 法老军队在红海溺亡。多梅尼科·达莱·格雷切根据提香原作创作的木刻版画，1549 年
scale of this most imposing of all woodcuts. Only one book illustration is documented as Titian’s: a sensitive profile of Ariosto, vouched for years later in a letter from the poet’s nephew.
这幅最宏伟的木刻版画的规模。仅有一幅书籍插图被确认为提香所作：那是阿里奥斯托的侧面肖像，其真迹多年后由诗人的侄子在信中予以证实。
He put an even grander power into some of the most searching portrait prints made before Rembrandt’s. These were published by his friend Francesco Marcolini, who led the resurgence of the Venetian book. Titian signed Aretino’s portrait [405] all over with the descriptive lunge of his line. Only such a painter could have made a monument out of the little color-woodcut frontispiece to Aretino’s poem to his mistress Angela Sirena [ 406 ]. Titian had every reason to grant a favor to Aretino, the blackmailer of princes and Europe’s favorite bad boy, for his help in selling leftover paintings by praising them to sovereigns.
他在伦勃朗之前的某些最具穿透力的肖像版画中注入了更为宏大的力量。这些作品由他的友人弗朗切斯科·马尔科利尼出版，后者引领了威尼斯书籍的复兴。提香以富有表现力的笔触在阿雷蒂诺肖像[405]上签名。 唯有这样的画家，才能将阿雷蒂诺献给情妇安杰拉·西蕾娜的诗集[406]那幅色彩木刻扉页，升华为艺术丰碑。提香有充分理由恩赐这位勒索君主的欧洲"坏小子"——阿雷蒂诺，因他曾通过向君主们吹捧画作，帮提香售出滞销画作。
Titian’s example gave space and movement to the smallest vignettes in Venetian books, even where he himself did not draw them [ 407 ]. These illustrations graced the reading of elegant and learned Europe, for whom Venice put together the first comfortable modern books-of a lightness and compactness that fits the hand, with a title page that tells you what title pages tell today, with numbered leaves, a table of contents, and an index-all in a type that you read without noticing. It was surely these easy and urbane Venetian editions that brought Italian romances to Shakespeare and Don Quixote.
提香的范例为威尼斯书籍中最微小的插图赋予了空间感与动态美，即便这些插图并非出自他手[407]。 这些插图为优雅博学的欧洲读者增添了阅读的雅致。威尼斯为他们打造了首批舒适的现代书籍——轻巧紧凑的尺寸恰好合手，标题页承载着今日标题页的功能，配有页码、目录和索引，所有文字都采用令人不觉费力的字体。正是这些轻松雅致的威尼斯版本，将意大利浪漫故事带给了莎士比亚和堂吉诃德。

Engraving standardized (标准化雕刻)


Germans and Netherlanders invented almost all the print techniques and then elaborated them with the most determined polish. Line engraving evolved its intricate gratings through ES, Schongauer, Dürer, and Lucas of Leiden to Cornelis Cort. In Antwerp, while engraving for Jerome Cock’s international publishing house of the Four Winds [ 373 ], young Cort made pen drawings that are often mistaken for Brueghel’s. Then, in Italy during his 20s, he sent back drawings (probably his own) of Italian paintings for Cock to engrave, meanwhile teaching Italians his intelligent clarification of northern engraving. His style began to matter in 1565 when Titian lodged him in Venice to engrave paintings as advertisements for princely distribution. Titian did not hire an Italian of Marcantonio’s then stagnant school, whose close and even graver work matches the mat colors of fresco, but instead sought out this Antwerper with a flashier line that could approximate the gleam and darkness of the new Venetian painting [ 408 ]. As usual, the painter retrained the engraver to subordinate tricks of skill to the grand articulation of design, and with such effect that Cort’s later engravings were copied more often than anybody’s except Dürer’s.
德国与荷兰的版画大师们几乎开创了所有印刷技法，并以最精湛的工艺将其推向极致。线刻版画通过埃斯、施恩高尔、丢勒、莱顿的卢卡斯直至科内利斯·科特，逐步发展出精妙的网格纹理。在安特卫普为杰罗姆·科克的"四风"国际出版社刻版期间[373]，年轻的科特创作的钢笔画常被误认为是布鲁盖尔的作品。 二十余岁时旅居意大利，他将意大利画作的素描（很可能是其自创）寄回供科克雕刻，同时向意大利人传授其对北方版画技法的睿智革新。1565 年提香在威尼斯为他安排雕刻画作作为贵族分发的广告时，其风格开始崭露头角。 提香并未聘请马尔坎托尼奥学派的意大利人——该学派当时已陷入停滞，其细密甚至更显沉重的画风与壁画的哑光色调相契合——而是特意寻觅了这位安特卫普人。他的线条更富张力，能近乎完美地再现威尼斯新画派的光影变幻[408]。 一如既往，画家重新训练了这位版画家，使其将技巧的娴熟服从于宏大构图的表达，成效显著——科特后期的版画复刻率仅次于丢勒，成为当时最常被临摹的作品。
After centering in Venice for about six years, Cort spent his remaining seven years in Rome, teaching the discipline of the Antwerp workshops as redirected by Titian. Goltzius [ 419 ] learned Cort’s new style, perhaps by working directly under him. Another probable pupil, the native Roman Francesco Villamena, opened the spaces between the lines and flowed them in parallels that were later to be devel-
在威尼斯定居约六年后，科尔特余下的七年时光都在罗马度过，传授经提香重新调整的安特卫普画室技法。戈尔齐乌斯[419]或许直接师从科尔特，习得了其新风格。另一位可能的弟子——罗马本地人弗朗切斯科·维拉梅纳——开创了在线条间留白并以平行线流动的技法，这种手法后来被发展——
oped into a special style by Claude Mellan [ 289 ]. Villamena made the first heroic engravings of beggars [ 409 ], suggested perhaps by Ferrarese engravings [ 201 ] or by the studies that Annibale Carracci was then drawing of street criers [ 202 ]. Villamena thus introduced low-life subjects to Callot and the young Rembrandt.
克劳德·梅兰开创了一种特殊风格[289]。维拉梅纳率先创作了乞丐题材的英雄式版画[409]，其灵感或许源自费拉拉版画[201]，或是安尼巴莱·卡拉奇当时绘制的街头叫卖者素描[202]。维拉梅纳由此将底层生活题材引入了卡洛特和年轻伦勃朗的创作视野。
Cort’s greatest Italian follower was Agostino Carracci of Bologna, who was 21 when Cort died. Agostino’s Italian taste simplified Cort’s dependable system to make it easier to teach [410]. Agostino himself engraved so brilliantly that when he died the art world of Bologna splurged on a black and silver funeral elaborate enough to commemorate in a booklet with etchings by Guido Reni. It is noteworthy that Reni, Agostino’s young admirer, did not imitate him by engraving, but followed Parmigiano by etching, like most Italian painters. Though Agostino Carracci could not prevent engraving from declining in Italy, he finally came into his own as a model when French printmakers began to specialize either in pure engraving with Nanteuil [ 290 ] or in the etched effect of engraving with Bosse [ 456 ]. Then Agostino emerged as the consulted old master.
科尔特最杰出的意大利追随者是博洛尼亚的阿戈斯蒂诺·卡拉奇，科尔特去世时他年仅 21 岁。阿戈斯蒂诺的意大利审美将科尔特可靠的技法体系简化，使其更易于传授[410]。 阿戈斯蒂诺本人精湛的雕刻技艺令其身后博洛尼亚艺术界倾尽财力，为他举办了银黑相间的盛大的葬礼，甚至特意印制纪念册，内含圭多·雷尼的蚀刻版画。值得注意的是，这位年轻的崇拜者并未效仿阿戈斯蒂诺的雕刻技法，而是追随帕尔米贾尼诺的蚀刻路线——这恰是多数意大利画家的选择。 尽管阿戈斯蒂诺·卡拉奇未能阻止版画艺术在意大利的衰落，但当法国版画家开始专攻纯粹的铜版画（如南特伊尔[290]）或追求蚀刻效果的铜版画（如博斯[456]）时，他最终成为被奉为典范的艺术家。此时的阿戈斯蒂诺已然成为备受推崇的古典大师。
