Last woodcut books (最后的木刻版画集)


For some time after the Antwerp engraving factories had turned Flemish book illustration to copperplate, good woodcut books still hung on in Germany and Switzerland, where they had been most glorious. The final outburst of woodcut illustration escaped the commercialism of copperplate illustration because the Germans and Swiss still cut to preserve the draftsman’s individual line. The Swiss Jost Amman shows himself cutting his own design [ 411 ] in his lively little survey of 132 crafts and trades that anticipates the great French Encyclopédie [ 449 ]. In Frankfurt and Nuremberg Amman drew, and sometimes cut, thousands of woodcuts that picture the thinking and doing of his age. To ease this swarming outflow, he simplified the cutting by crosshatching sparingly and openly. The woodcutter received no such mercy from a more individual Swiss artist born the same year as Amman.
最后的木刻书籍在安特卫普雕版工厂将佛兰德书籍插图转为铜版画后，木刻书籍仍在德国和瑞士顽强存续，这些地区曾是木刻艺术最辉煌的舞台。 木版插图的最后一次爆发摆脱了铜版插图的商业化，因为德国人和瑞士人仍在雕刻时保留制图师的独特线条。瑞士人约斯特·阿曼在其生动的小型手稿中展示了自己雕刻设计的过程[411]，这幅描绘 132 种手工艺与行业的作品预见了伟大的法国《百科全书》[449]。 在法兰克福和纽伦堡，阿曼绘制并亲手雕刻了数千幅木刻版画，生动展现了那个时代的思想与实践。为应对创作洪流，他通过节制而开放的交叉线条技法简化了雕刻工艺。然而与阿曼同年出生的另一位瑞士艺术家，却未曾给予木刻匠人这般宽容。

412
St. John on Patmos. Woodcut by Tobias Stimmer in Neue Künstliche Figuren Biblischer Historien, Basel (Gwarin), 1576
帕特莫斯的圣约翰。托比亚斯·斯蒂默在《新的人造圣经历史人物》中的木刻画，巴塞尔（格瓦林），1576 年

图 129：411 伐木工。约斯特·阿曼木刻版画，载于《武器库》，法兰克福，1568 年
Tobias Stimmer drew fewer cuts than Amman because he mainly frescoed housefronts in south Germany and painted portraits in oils and decorations on glass. His painting on glass accustomed him to reserving blanks for looking through the window, and his huge outdoor frescoes (now weathered away) trained him to design even a little woodblock massively. He framed his 170 Bible woodcuts [ 412 ] with a lavishness of decoration developed from Venetian title borders. Rubens said that these pre-baroque “jewels of art” had been his principal study when young. Stimmer rivaled engraving by crosshatching tones in his woodblock with a metal point or a quill as fine as a ballpoint pen. His minuteness ruined woodcut illustration financially by increasing the cutter’s wages above copperplate illustration despite the slow, pure graver work usual in Stimmer’s time and the double presswork: screw press for the type and rolling press for the plates.
托比亚斯·施蒂默的刻痕比阿曼少，因为他主要在德国南部绘制房屋外墙湿壁画，并以油画创作肖像及玻璃装饰画。 他在玻璃上的绘画使他习惯为透视留白，而巨大的户外壁画（现已风化消失）则训练他即使设计小幅木刻版画也能气势恢宏。他以源自威尼斯标题边框的华美装饰为 170 幅《圣经》木刻版画[412]构筑框架。鲁本斯曾说这些前巴洛克时期的"艺术瑰宝"是他年轻时的主要研究对象。 施蒂默运用金属尖笔或如圆珠笔般纤细的鹅毛笔，在木版上以交叉阴影技法与雕版画相抗衡。其精微技法却令木刻插图陷入经济困境——即便在施蒂默时代普遍采用缓慢纯粹的刻刀工艺，且需双重压印（字体用螺旋压印机，版画用滚压机），其雕刻工人工资仍远超铜版画。
By 1757, when etching speeded up “engraving,” the French Encyclopédie stated that the amount of fine work done on copperplate in four or five days would require a month on wood. After about 1590 woodcut dwindled to chapbooks and to ornamental vignettes and initials that were cast in type metal and sold so generally at book fairs that commercial books looked alike everywhere.
到 1757 年，蚀刻技术加速了"雕刻"进程，法国《百科全书》指出：铜版上四五天完成的精细作品，若用木版则需耗时一个月。约 1590 年后，木刻版画逐渐萎缩为廉价小册子，以及用铸造金属字体制作的装饰性插图和首字母图案——这些作品在书展上泛滥销售，致使商业书籍在各地都千篇一律。

Jewelry designs (珠宝设计)


Jewelry designs were published after the plundering of Central America glutted Europe with sudden gold that provided the first fluid coinage, the first lavish gold thread in tapestries, the first abundance of jewelry. Since jewelers toured from court to court with their knapsacks of tools, old jewelry is better described by its style of design than by its conjectured place of manufacture.
珠宝设计图谱的问世，源于中美洲遭劫掠后欧洲突然涌入的黄金。这批黄金催生了首批流通货币，首次在挂毯中点缀奢华金线，更造就了珠宝的首次盛行。由于珠宝匠们背着工具包在宫廷间巡回作坊，旧式珠宝的风格特征往往比推测的产地更能准确描述其渊源。
The earliest book of jewelry designs [ 413 ] was engraved in Paris after Catherine de Medicis had begun the long participation of women in politics. (She did not import a fashion from home, where Florentine portraits show few and simple jewels.) Boyvin’s foursquare gold ornaments of a barbaric refinement were paid for
最早的珠宝设计图册[413]于巴黎雕刻而成，此时凯瑟琳·德·美第奇已开启女性长久参与政治的序幕。（她并未从故乡引进时尚——佛罗伦萨肖像画中可见的珠宝寥寥无几且质朴无华。）博瓦万那粗犷而精致的方形金饰，其费用由

“Aimer un Peu-Beaucoup-Passioné-ment-Pas du Tout.” Enamel brooch. Watercolor by Eugène Grasset, Paris, before 1908

by the French kings’ new privy purse that had paid for the similar stucco frames at Fontainebleau [ 246 ]. Although this assertive goldwork (all of it melted long ago) may have been exclusively French, the enamel and baroque pearl pendants of Flemish and German engravings [414] were made everywhere (and were even more eagerly faked after the 1830s). A useful pendant appeared in the 1530 s when the German invention of the fusee shrank the timepiece small enough to hang on a girdle, where the conspicuous watchcase attracted with its bright enamel on black metal [ 415 ]. Enamel freed a fantasy of design that had to be given up after about 1650 when the taste for faceted gems restricted jewelry to minerals clumped together by invisible metal. Imagination revived around 1900 when art nouveau invited the designer to fit horn and moonstone into any shape and to flow enamels as he pleased [ 416 ].
由法国国王新设立的私密金库支付，该金库曾为枫丹白露宫的类似灰泥框架买单[246]。尽管这种张扬的金饰工艺（现已全部熔毁）或许是法国独创，但弗拉芒与德国版画中描绘的珐琅及巴洛克珍珠吊坠[414]却遍布各地（1830 年代后更被疯狂仿制）。 1530 年代出现了一种实用吊坠：德国发明的发条装置使时计缩小至可悬挂于腰带，其黑色金属底座上缀满亮丽珐琅的表壳格外醒目[415]。珐琅工艺曾释放出设计想象力，但约 1650 年后因多面宝石风行，珠宝设计被迫回归以隐形金属串联矿石的传统形式。 1900 年前后，随着新艺术运动兴起，设计师得以将玳瑁与月光石塑造成任意形态，珐琅亦可随心流动，艺术想象再度焕发活力[416]。

Northern mannerists (北方风格主义者)


After about 1510, trade with the Americas and the new route to India around Africa swung commerce away from Venice toward Antwerp. To supply prints to the Old World and the New, Antwerp organized the manufacture of engravings with an efficiency learned from Marcantonio’s Roman workshop. Never before, or possibly since, did so many thousands of copperplates proliferate. The industry employed whole families of parents and children, some of whom later emigrated to Haarlem, Frankfurt, and Prague. Each dynasty of engravers shared a family style so totally that you cannot distinguish any one Galle, Wierix, Collaert, de Bry, or de Passe from another.
北方风格主义者约 1510 年后，与美洲的贸易及绕非洲的新印度航线使商业重心从威尼斯转向安特卫普。为向新旧世界供应版画，安特卫普借鉴马尔坎托尼奥罗马工坊的效率模式，系统化组织铜版画生产。如此大规模的铜版画制作盛况前所未有，后世亦难再现。 该产业吸纳了整代家族劳动力，包括父母与子女，其中部分工匠后来迁往哈勒姆、法兰克福和布拉格。每支雕版师家族都秉承着高度统一的家族风格，以至于难以区分加勒、维里克斯、科拉尔特、德·布里或德·帕斯等不同家族的具体作品。
Most did not design their own prints but worked for a new class of artists who specialized in drawing for reproduction so tidily that engravers could copy them without uncertainty. Painters developed a similar exactness of drawing to impose their personal styles on assistants who helped them with big altarpieces and wall decorations. Medieval painters had sketched out work assignments more casually because each region shared a common style.
大多数人并未亲自设计版画，而是为新兴的艺术家群体效力——这些艺术家专精于绘制可供复制的画稿，其线条工整得让雕刻师能毫无疑虑地复刻。画家们也发展出相似的精准绘画技法，以此将个人风格强加于助手身上，这些助手协助他们完成大型祭坛画和墙面装饰。中世纪画家则以更随意的方式勾勒工作任务，因为当时各地区共享着相似的艺术风格。
As Protestant Holland struggled with Catholic Belgium, Heemskerck in Haarlem dramatized every outrage in the Old Testament for Protestants who likened themselves to the Jews in bondage [417], while Spranger in Catholic Antwerp and
当新教的荷兰与天主教的比利时交锋之际，哈勒姆的赫姆斯克里克将《旧约》中每桩暴行都演绎成戏剧，供那些自比为受奴役犹太人的新教徒观赏[417]；而天主教安特卫普的斯普兰格则——
Figure 133: 417  图 133：417
Judith and Holofernes. Etching by Martin van Heemskerck
朱迪思与荷罗弗尼斯。马丁·范·海姆斯克尔克蚀刻版画
Northern mannerists  北方风格主义者
Prague proclaimed the resurgent Counter-Reformation with saints who declaim as turbulently as his gods and goddesses [ 418 ]. The prestige of a ten-year triumph in Italy, and then Hapsburg patronage, enabled Spranger to impose a sculptural swagger on the court theaters and pilgrimage churches of south Germany and Austria.
布拉格以圣徒形象宣告了复兴的反宗教改革运动，这些圣徒的宣示之声如同诸神女神般汹涌澎湃[418]。斯普兰格凭借在意大利十年凯旋的声望，加之哈布斯堡王朝的庇护，得以在南德与奥地利的宫廷剧院及朝圣教堂中，施展雕塑艺术的磅礴气势。
The virtuoso who ruled engraving was Hendrik Goltzius of Haarlem. As a baby, he had tumbled into a fire and cramped his right hand permanently shut. By being forced to draw with the large muscles of his arm and shoulder, the way the Chinese and Japanese control their brushes, he mastered a commanding swing of line. He based his engraving style on Cort [ 408 ]. His tapering curves intersect in lozenges that wrap like a fancy stocking around a wrestler’s muscles [419], studied in Rome from Michelangelo and antique marbles. This style, known as line engrav-
统治版画界的天才大师是哈勒姆的亨德里克·戈尔茨。幼年时他跌入火中，导致右手永久性痉挛无法张开。正因被迫像中日韩画家驾驭毛笔那样，运用手臂与肩部的粗大肌肉作画，他才练就了气势磅礴的线条挥洒技法。 他的版画风格奠基于科特[408]。那些渐细的曲线在菱形中交错，如同花纹长袜般缠绕在摔跤手肌肉上[419]——这种技法源自他在罗马研习米开朗基罗与古希腊大理石雕塑的成果。这种被称为线条版画的风格——

420 The Shepherd. Chiaroscuro woodcut by Goltzius
420 《牧羊人》戈尔齐乌斯创作的明暗对比木刻版画
421 Galatea. Chiaroscuro woodcut by Goltzius
421 加拉泰亚。戈尔齐乌斯创作的明暗对比法木刻版画
ing, prevailed for showpieces even after about 1875, when photographic processes began to supplant reproductive printmaking, and it survives today on dollar bills.
这种工艺在 1875 年左右摄影技术开始取代印刷复制工艺后，仍作为展示品占主导地位，如今它依然存在于美元纸币上。
Goltzius was the last professional engraver who drew with the authority of a good painter and the last who invented many pictures for others to copy. His happy vigor triumphs in a few rare woodcut landscapes [ 420 ] that had little effect on anyone except Rembrandt. While so many followed Goltzius in engraving, nobody imitated his dashing color woodcuts [ 421 ]. He often printed these in tones of a single color, like the Italians, but with a black block that carries the main design, like the Germans. His exuberance in these joyous inventions sweeps all before him.
戈尔齐乌斯是最后一位以优秀画家水准进行创作的专业雕刻师，也是最后一位为他人创作大量可供临摹画作的艺术家。他那充满活力的创作力在少数珍稀的木刻风景画[420]中得以彰显，这些作品除伦勃朗外鲜少影响他人。尽管众多雕刻师效仿戈尔齐乌斯技法，却无人能复制他那气势磅礴的彩色木刻[421]。 他常效法意大利人采用单色调印刷，却又如德国人般以黑色版块承载主体图案。这些欢快创作中奔涌的艺术激情，令一切都黯然失色。
Heemskerck, Spranger, and Goltzius supplied ideas to Rubens, Rembrandt, and countless other painters. Their northern mannerism began to look artificial when romanticism discovered a rival artifice of sentimental intensities, but today it fascinates all over again as we realize that it is not enough for an artist to feel sincere; he must convince.
海姆斯克尔克、斯普兰格和戈尔齐乌斯为鲁本斯、伦勃朗及无数画家提供了艺术灵感。当浪漫主义发现情感激荡的虚饰技法时，他们的北方风格主义开始显得做作，但如今它再度令人着迷——我们意识到，艺术家仅凭真诚感受远远不够，他必须令人信服。

Brueghel (布鲁盖尔)


Pieter Brueghel was the only designer for the Antwerp print factories who developed into a painter with a sideline of drawing for printmakers. By working his way into the complexities of painting during the last 10 or 15 years of his life, he came to design prints with ever growing amplitude. Though he went, of course, to Italy, he was the first northerner who did not see it as a panorama of ruins or as a gallery of patterns for drawing heroic nudes. Italy was simply a landscape with buildings to which he traveled through breathtaking Alpine heights. He was the first artist who saw mountains, not as distant decorations or horrid obstacles, but as slouching beasts furred with forests and drowsing above immensities of air. He etched his vision in only one plate [ 422 ], sketching too individually to please at the time, but he drew other valley views for Antwerp engravers to copy. By rejecting the Italian heroic manner and returning to the Netherlandish past of Lucas of Leiden and Hieronymus Bosch, Brueghel must have made himself look comfortably old-fashioned [ 423 ]. He was, however, up to the minute in his
彼得·勃鲁盖尔是安特卫普版画工厂中唯一一位发展成为画家，同时兼任版画师绘图工作的设计师。在他生命的最后十年或十五年里，通过深入探索绘画的复杂性，他设计的版画作品展现出日益广阔的艺术格局。 尽管他曾造访意大利，却是首位不将此地视为废墟全景或英雄裸体画素材库的北方人。对他而言，意大利不过是座座建筑点缀的景致，而通往那里的路途横亘着令人窒息的阿尔卑斯山脉。他是首位将群山视为蜷伏巨兽的艺术家——这些山峦披着森林的毛皮，在浩瀚的空气之上慵懒沉睡，既非遥远的装饰，亦非可怖的阻碍。 他仅用一块铜版[422]刻录此景，因笔触过于个性化而未获当时青睐，却为安特卫普雕刻师绘制了其他山谷景观供其临摹。布鲁盖尔摒弃意大利式英雄主义，回归莱顿的卢卡斯与耶罗尼米斯·博斯引领的尼德兰传统，此举必令他显得舒适地过时[423]。然而，他的艺术却始终与时代脉搏紧密相连。

422 Rabbit Hunters. Engraving by Pieter Brueghel the Elder
422 猎兔者。老彼得·勃鲁盖尔版画

friendships with mathematicians and cartographers, from whom, perhaps, he got his lofty view of man’s brief swarming on this little planet spread out like a map.
与数学家和制图师的友谊，或许正是从他们那里，他获得了对人类在如地图般铺展的这颗小行星上短暂纷扰的高远视角。
Probably born in a village too small for most maps, Brueghel returned to country festivals and junketings for the inspiration of some of his best pictures [ 424 ]. When he joined in a village wake or wedding, he dressed in peasant clothes, but when he sketched, he drew as aristocratically as Ingres, and even more cleanly. He did not draw figures like the Italians, as nudes inside drapery, but as though the
布鲁盖尔可能出生在一个小得连地图都找不到的村庄，他从乡村庆典和宴饮中汲取灵感，创作了部分最杰出的画作[424]。 当他参与村庄守灵或婚礼时，身着农家衣衫；但当他执笔素描时，笔触却如安格尔般贵族化，甚至更为纯粹。他笔下的人物不像意大利画派那样以布料包裹的裸体呈现，而是仿佛——

clothes and flesh had grown together through the habits of the social animal. Italian art, however, showed him how to clear a figure for its dominant lunge, and Italian heroics enabled him to draw a galleon in Antwerp’s harbor standing to the wind like an Alp in a snowstorm [ 425 ].
衣衫与血肉因社会性动物的习性而融为一体。然而意大利艺术教会他如何为人物勾勒出凌厉的动态，意大利式的英雄气概更使他得以描绘出停泊在安特卫普港的帆船——它迎风而立，宛若暴风雪中的阿尔卑斯山峰[425]。
Antwerp’s ships brought the American gold and silver that changed the basis of wealth from land to money in a revolution that is still spreading disturbance in South American haciendas. The strain of any such upheaval makes people like Brueghel ask questions, while the authorities question the right of questioning. He questioned the distribution of wealth in some of the first and acutest pictures of social protest [ 426 ]. If he also drew satires of the religious persecutions that Spanish imperialism inflicted at the end of his life, these were never engraved and must have been among the subversive drawings that he prudently directed his wife, as he lay dying, to burn. Yet Brueghel was much more than a satirist, for he was the first artist who saw people as shaped by their habits and who discovered intensity in the everyday. Both discoveries prepared the way for Rembrandt.
安特卫普的船只运来了美洲的金银，这场财富基础从土地转向货币的革命至今仍在南美庄园引发骚动。任何此类动荡都会让布鲁盖尔这样的人提出质疑，而当权者则质疑质疑的正当性。他在最早且最尖锐的社会抗议画作中，质疑着财富的分配[426]。 即便他在晚年也曾以画笔讽刺西班牙帝国主义的宗教迫害，这些作品却从未付梓，想必已随那些颠覆性素描一同被临终的布鲁盖尔谨慎地嘱咐妻子焚毁。然而布鲁盖尔远不止是讽刺画家——他是首位洞悉人类被习俗塑造的艺术家，也是首位在日常琐碎中发掘强烈情感的先驱。这两项发现为伦勃朗的艺术之路铺就了基石。

Rubens (鲁本斯)


A couple of etchings show us how grandly Rubens might have made prints if he had not chosen to economize his time by hiring engravers. In his 40 s , when he painted the ceiling for the Jesuit church in Antwerp, he recorded the oratorical grandeur of this first major commission (since burned) by etching the panel of Saint Catherine [ 427 ]. To retouch the copper, he needed an impression in the same direction as the plate. He got this by laying a fresh impression of his etching against a blank paper, and rolling both through a press to offset the damp printing onto the blank paper. He then penned alterations on the counterproof to guide his revisions on the copper. (Counterproofs, probably invented by Dürer, can also be made from drawings.)
鲁本斯几幅蚀刻版画向我们展示了，若非为节省时间而雇佣雕刻师，鲁本斯本可创作出何等恢弘的版画作品。四十岁时，他在安特卫普耶稣会教堂绘制穹顶画作，为记录这处首件重要委托作品（后遭焚毁）的雄辩气魄，他特意蚀刻了《圣凯瑟琳》画板[427]。 为修饰铜版，他需要与版面同向的印痕。他将蚀刻版的新印痕置于白纸上，通过压印机滚压使湿润的印痕转移至白纸。随后他在反印稿上勾勒修改痕迹，以此指导铜版修订工作。（反印稿技术可能由丢勒首创，亦可应用于素描稿。）
During his last 30 years Rubens imitated Titian by repeating his popular paintings and by advertising them through reproductive prints that he marketed under copyrights from Brabant, Holland, and France. When he was 30 he hired his first engraver from a local workshop, only to find that the Antwerp routine of copying neat pen drawings unfitted engravers to render the heroic flow of his oil paintings. He then imported nearly a dozen Haarlem engravers trained by Goltzius to a more athletic line and more flashing contrasts, thus diverting the consequences of Goltzius’ teaching from Holland to Belgium. By retraining the pupils of one man, Rubens united his engravers under one epoch-making style that liquified undulations from light to dark in an inspiring new splendor. He watched over their every motion, correcting their proofs in ink and opaque white, and copying some of his own paintings in tones of gray so that he, and not they, should decide on the black and white values. As he dismissed engraver after engraver, he drove the best one, Lucas Vorsterman, into a nervous breakdown, but managed by deliberate tyranny to impress his style on all of his assistants. Rubens had learned in Italy to dramatize the accepted ideas of his age with an art that is public and declamatory, and with a design so rugged that it survives execution by others.
鲁本斯在最后三十年里效仿提香，通过复刻其畅销画作并借助版画复制品进行推广——这些复制品均以布拉班特、荷兰及法国的版权形式销售。三十岁时，他首次从当地工坊聘请雕刻师，却发现安特卫普惯用的工整钢笔画复制技法，使雕刻师难以呈现其油画中磅礴的笔触韵律。 他随后引进了近十位受戈尔齐乌斯训练的哈勒姆版画家，这些艺术家擅长更富张力的线条与更耀眼的明暗对比，从而将戈尔齐乌斯技法的影响从荷兰延伸至比利时。通过改造同一位大师的门生，鲁本斯将版画家们凝聚成开创时代的统一风格——以令人惊叹的全新辉煌，将明暗交织的波浪线条化作流动的艺术。 他亲临现场监督每道工序，用墨水与不透明白色修正试印样张，甚至亲自将部分画作以灰色调复刻，确保黑白明暗的最终定夺权始终掌握在自己手中。他接连解雇多位雕刻师，最终将最优秀的卢卡斯·沃斯特曼逼至精神崩溃的边缘，却通过刻意施加的专制手段，将个人风格烙印在所有助手的作品中。 鲁本斯在意大利习得以戏剧化手法演绎时代主流观念的艺术——这种艺术具有公开宣示的张力，其粗粝的设计风格甚至能经受他人诠释的考验。
About 1608 Rubens began to design many copperplate illustrations for the Plan-tin-Moretus press in Antwerp. Balthasar Moretus complained that “Rubens takes six months to mull over a title page, and works at it only on holidays.” But no wonder. The press paid him in books worth only five to 20 guilders, as compared to the
约 1608 年起，鲁本斯开始为安特卫普的普兰丁-莫雷图斯印刷厂设计大量铜版插图。巴尔塔萨·莫雷图斯曾抱怨道："鲁本斯光琢磨一个扉页就要耗费半年光阴，而且只在节假日才动笔。"但这不足为奇——印刷厂支付给他的报酬仅是价值五至二十盾的书籍，相比之下，


428 Samson Killing the Lion that Breeds Bees. Quill drawing by Rubens
428 参孙杀死养蜂的狮子。鲁本斯钢笔画
429 Engraving after Rubens, title page for Urban VIII, Poemata, Antwerp (Plantin), 1634
429 鲁本斯作品的雕版复刻，乌尔班八世《诗集》的标题页，安特卫普（普兰坦印刷），1634 年
430 (opposite page, below) Drunken Silenus. Woodcut by Jan Christoffel Jegher after Rubens
430（对页下方）醉酒的西勒诺斯。扬·克里斯托弗·耶赫根据鲁本斯作品制作的木刻版画
100 guilders a day at which he rated his painting. Rubens’ title pages [ 428, 429] so exalted the baroque book in Antwerp that Parisians began to commission sumptuous printing there, while Flemish engravers often emigrated to Paris. Though copperplate rendered Rubens’ forms convincingly, he, like Titian, conveyed a grander amplitude through woodcut [ 430 ]. Rubens’ woodcuts are almost the last masterpieces in a medium that dwindled to ballad sheets and minor ornaments until Gauguin transformed it in 1894 [ 710 ]. Rubens sometimes drew in a cobweb of quill lines [431] that the woodcutter had to summarize in a structure simple enough for the knife to carve [ 432 ]. Since a woodcutter can remove lines, but cannot add them without drilling a hole and plugging it for new cutting, the cutter left plenty of marginal wood in proof impressions to be pared away as Rubens might direct.
鲁本斯为自己的绘画定价每日 100 盾。他的标题页作品[428,429]如此彰显安特卫普巴洛克书籍的卓越，以致巴黎人开始委托当地制作华美印刷品，而佛兰德雕刻师则常迁居巴黎。尽管铜版画能逼真呈现鲁本斯笔下的形态，但他与提香一样，通过木刻[430]传递出更宏大的气魄。 鲁本斯的木刻几乎是该媒介最后的杰作——此后木刻逐渐沦为民谣插页与次要装饰，直至高更在 1894 年革新了它[710]。 鲁本斯常以蛛网般的羽毛笔线条作画[431]，木刻师必须将其简化为便于雕刻刀处理的结构[432]。由于刻工只能削去线条而无法添加（除非钻孔填补后重新雕刻），试印时刻工会在边缘保留大量木料，以便按鲁本斯指示进行修整。

Figure 139: 434 Etching by Van Dyck, finished with engraving by Jacob Neeffs, title sheet from ICONES (the Iconography), Antwerp, 1645
图 139：434 凡·戴克蚀刻版画，由雅各布·尼夫斯完成雕刻，选自《ICONES》（图鉴）标题页，安特卫普，1645 年

Van Dyck (凡·戴克)


433 Self-portrait. Etching by Sir Anthony Van Dyck
433 自画像。安东尼·范·戴克爵士蚀刻版画
Van Dyck was 22 years younger than Rubens and was his most brilliant and independent collaborator. During his 20s he spent six years in Italy, where he must have been impressed by Italian publications of portraits of eminent men, for after returning to Antwerp in 1626 he hired Rubens’ crew of engravers to publish his own portraits of artists and writers in prints of uniform format. He himself etched over a dozen heads of his painter friends. With a painter’s promptness, he opened a ripple of lines on the copper, sprinkled them with dots for transitions in the manner of Barocci [ 438 ], and etched with a single bite of the acid [ 433 ]. His spontaneity must have jarred the Flemish taste for engravings that darken the paper out to the edges, for after pulling a few proofs of these supremely distinguished heads, probably to give to friends, he let routine engravers make them salable by finishing them-in every sense [ 434 ].
凡·戴克比鲁本斯年轻 22 岁，是他最杰出且最具独立精神的合作者。二十多岁时，他在意大利度过了六年时光，期间必定深受意大利出版的名人肖像画册所震撼——1626 年返回安特卫普后，他便雇佣了鲁本斯的雕刻团队，以统一规格的版画形式出版自己创作的艺术家与作家肖像。他亲自蚀刻了十余幅画家友人的头像。 他以画家特有的敏捷在铜版上展开线条涟漪，效法巴洛奇技法[438]以点状过渡，仅经一次蚀刻[433]便完成作品。 这种即兴创作必然与佛兰德人偏爱的版画风格相悖——后者讲究将纸张边缘都染黑。因此在印制几张极具格调的头像样本（很可能赠予友人）后，他便让常规雕刻师进行"完善"处理，使其具备商业价值——无论从何种意义而言[434]。
Van Dyck lived for success, not struggle. When he died at 42, his Iconography
凡·戴克为成功而活，而非为挣扎。42 岁逝世时，他的《圣像学》

had reached 80 plates, to which his successors added 44. In 1851 the Louvre bought all the coppers, from which it still sells passable impressions pulled from electrotypes. After Van Dyck’s etched states had been ignored by all of his contemporaries except Rembrandt, they slept until the 1850 or 60 s when they dominated portraiture in the so-called revival of etching in England [435]. Etchers have studied Van Dyck ever since, for they can hope to approximate his brilliant directness, whereas nobody can hope to approach the complexity of Rembrandt’s portraits.
版画数量已达 80 幅，其继任者又增补了 44 幅。1851 年卢浮宫购入全部铜版，至今仍出售由电镀版印制的尚可的复制品。 在伦勃朗之外，凡·戴克的蚀刻版画曾遭同时代人集体忽视，直至 1850 至 60 年代才重见天日，并在英国所谓蚀刻复兴运动中主导肖像画领域[435]。此后蚀刻艺术家们持续研究凡·戴克，因其作品中那种璀璨的直率感尚可效仿，而伦勃朗肖像画的复杂性则无人能企及。

Barocci (巴罗奇)


So long as the earth seemed but a shadow cast by heaven, the medieval artist found it simple to represent visions, but when science began to make the earth more real than heaven, the artist had to choose which world to emphasize. If a picture combined the ever more irreconcilable realms of the vision and the visionary, the artist might either demonstrate that the vision, though violating natural law, was really factual, by focusing a sharp light on every fold of cloth and
巴洛奇只要大地仍似天穹投下的阴影，中世纪艺术家便能轻松描绘幻象；但当科学使大地较之天穹更显真实时，艺术家便须抉择该着重呈现哪个世界。若画作试图融合幻象与幻觉这两个日益难以调和的领域，艺术家或可通过聚焦衣褶的每一处褶皱投射锐利光线，或可通过将幻象置于现实之上，来证明幻象虽违背自然法则却确有其事。
eyelash [ 436 ], or else he could suppress the thing seen to let the seer’s expression suggest the invisible wonder [437].
睫毛[436]，否则他便能压抑所见之物，让观者神情暗示那不可见的奇观[437]。
In both these solutions Federigo Barocci of Urbino showed the way with the last pictures that move one to fumble toward a prayer. With only four etchings, he made more effect with fewer prints than anyone except Pollaiuolo [ 184 ]. He gave currency to three of his paintings by etching them with a black and white more colorful than their pink and blue. He discovered the most personal etching style of his generation by shooting free parallels over a contour line to soften an edge and by smudging transitions with a powdering of dots [438], perhaps suggested by Giulio Campagnola [ 225 ] or by Dürer’s Adam and Eve [ 278 ]. These dotted modulations provided the basis for the style of Van Dyck [ 433 ], and then through Ottavio Leoni [ 287 ], for the French portrait engravers. Barocci in Urbino, like Cézanne in Aix, was one of the very few artists who, while isolated from the competition and criticism of art centers, beat a track for others to follow.
在这两种解决方案中，乌尔比诺的费德里戈·巴罗奇以最后几幅令人不禁虔诚祈祷的作品开辟了道路。仅凭四幅蚀刻版画，他以比波拉约洛更少的印数创造了更强烈的艺术效果[184]。他通过黑白蚀刻技法使三幅油画焕发新生——这种黑白处理反而比原作的粉蓝调更富色彩张力。 他开创了同时代最富个人特色的蚀刻技法：沿轮廓线自由延伸平行线条以柔化边缘，并用点状晕染处理过渡区域[438]——此法或许受朱利奥·坎帕尼奥拉[225]启发，或源自丢勒的《亚当与夏娃》[278]。 这种点状变调技法奠定了凡·戴克[433]的风格基础，继而经奥塔维奥·莱奥尼[287]传至法国肖像版画家。乌尔比诺的巴洛奇如同艾克斯的塞尚，是极少数在远离艺术中心竞争与批评的环境中，仍为后人开辟道路的艺术家。

Twilight’s gradual veil (暮色渐浓的帷幕)


In Rome, about 1600, Caravaggio was painting large scenes with so-called cellar lighting and Adam Elsheimer from Frankfurt was painting small night landscapes and rooms. After both died in their 305 in 1609 and 1610, their paintings directed artists toward the mystery of shadows for the next century. Both painted long-sought effects of darkness in masterpieces that they could not equal in their occasional etchings. Caravaggio may have roughed out this tiny Denial of Saint Peter [439] to try the etching needle while visiting some printmaker. This print and another might help to attribute drawings to Caravaggio, by whom none have yet been identified. His two etchings did nothing to spread his art, which became known only when painters under his influence took his lighting and his composition to other lands.
暮色渐浓的帷幕约 1600 年，罗马的卡拉瓦乔正以所谓地窖光绘制大型场景，法兰克福的亚当·埃尔斯海默则描绘小型夜景与室内画。 两人相继于 1609 年与 1610 年在三十五岁时离世，其画作却引领艺术家们在接下来一个世纪里探索光影之谜。他们在杰作中捕捉到的黑暗效果，是艺术家们长久追寻的境界——这种境界在他们偶尔创作的蚀刻版画中却难以企及。 卡拉瓦乔可能在拜访某位版画家时，粗略勾勒出这幅微型版画《圣彼得否认基督》[439]以试探蚀刻针法。此版画与另一幅作品或可佐证卡拉瓦乔的素描创作——迄今尚未有任何素描被确认为其手笔。这两幅蚀刻版画并未推广他的艺术，其声名仅在受其影响的画家们将他的光影技法与构图带往异国他乡后才得以传播。
Elsheimer approximated painting better than Caravaggio in a few rare pastorales from which Rembrandt and Claude Lorrain learned to submerge individual etched lines in a continuum of shade that blends nymphs into shrubbery [ 440 ]. The memorable darkness that recommended Elsheimer’s exquisite little paintings [ 441 ] to Rubens and Rembrandt reached the general public through seven engravings by a Dutch friend, Count Hendrik Goudt. Goudt must have produced other, now unidentified, prints to have acquired the skill for engraving the longest black to white scale then known [ 442 ]. After engraving models for a new art of somberness, Goudt himself lapsed into the shadows, for he went mad. His prints after Elsheimer started printmakers on a technical search that led to the invention of mezzotint [511] and also to Rembrandt’s dark masterpieces. Goudt’s engraving of Tobias and the Angel was of course in Rembrandt’s huge print collection, but it also reached him by a strange roundabout chain reaction. The engraving was adapted in etching by that moonstruck genius, Hercules Seghers, who was constantly absorbing other men’s pictures into his own savage singularity. As Seghers enlarged the composition, he lightened night into dusk, which his etching needle could more easily cope with, and he inflated the figures into gods tramping down the deserted hills [ 443 ]. Some eight years after Seghers’ death, when Rembrandt had acquired this copperplate along with much of Seghers’ other work, he replaced Tobias and
埃尔斯海默在少数几幅田园画中比卡拉瓦乔更接近绘画的本质，伦勃朗和克劳德·洛兰正是从这些作品中学会了将刻痕线条融入阴影的连续体，使仙女与灌木丛融为一体[440]。 埃尔斯海默那些精妙小画[441]中令人难忘的幽暗气质，经由荷兰友人亨德里克·古特伯爵的七幅版画传入大众视野。古特必然还创作过其他现已失传的版画，方能掌握当时已知最长的黑白渐变刻印技艺[442]。 在为新艺术的阴郁范式开创版画典范后，古特本人却坠入阴影——他精神崩溃了。他临摹埃尔斯海默的作品，促使版画家们展开技术探索，最终催生了凹版雕刻技法[511]，也孕育了伦勃朗的暗色杰作。 高德的《托比亚斯与天使》版画自然收录于伦勃朗庞大的版画收藏中，但其传入伦勃朗手中竟经历了奇妙的连锁反应：这幅作品先被月光痴狂的天才赫拉克勒斯·塞赫斯改制为蚀刻版画——他总将他人画作熔铸进自己狂野独特的艺术世界。 塞赫斯在放大构图时，将夜色淡化为暮色——这更便于蚀刻针处理——并将人物塑造成踏过荒凉山丘的神祇[443]。塞赫斯逝世约八年后，伦勃朗购得这块铜版及塞赫斯其他作品时，他将托比亚斯替换为

the angel with a diminished Holy Family fleeing into Egypt [ 444 ]. The furry drypoint of Rembrandt’s substitutions segregates itself from Seghers’ thorny etching, but it revives some of the shadowy mastery of Elsheimer’s original painting. Disliking the arrogance of Seghers’ conquering march, Rembrandt humbled the two around the Son of Man as they labor through the shadows of mortality. Like every artist confident of his originality, Rembrandt jumped his imagination off any handy springboard-another man’s picture, a beggar glimpsed out of a window, or one of his own sketches. He cared nothing for his point of departure, everything for his point of arrival.
天使带着缩小的圣家逃往埃及[444]。伦勃朗替换的毛茸茸干刻版画与塞赫斯的棘手蚀刻版画截然不同，却重现了埃尔斯海默原作中部分阴影处理的精妙技艺。 厌恶塞赫斯征服者般昂扬的姿态，伦勃朗将圣子周围的二人描绘得谦卑低垂，在凡俗阴影中艰难跋涉。如同所有确信自身独创性的艺术家，伦勃朗的想象力从任何现成跳板跃起——他人的画作、窗外瞥见的乞丐，或是自己的速写。他毫不介意起点，唯执着于抵达之处。

How-to-do-it manuals (操作指南)


About 1100, at Essen, a monk called Theophilus described how to make the many kinds of things used by the Church. A medieval monk could instruct his monastic brethren by sharing shop practices, but when the guilds acquired power, they kept such things secret. It was not until 600 years later that the decline of the guilds allowed Chambers and then Diderot to assemble even more comprehensive technical encyclopedias. Meanwhile, though Renaissance guilds published nothing that could help a workman, the printing of Vitruvius [237] provided a literary model for a German physician to follow in writing the first detailed description of mining [ 105 ].
操作指南约公元 1100 年，在埃森，一位名叫西奥菲勒斯的修士详述了制作教会所需各类物品的方法。中世纪的修士可通过传授工坊技艺指导同修，但当行会掌握权力后，这类知识便被严加保密。 直到六百年后，随着行会衰落，钱伯斯继而狄德罗才得以编纂出更为全面的技术百科全书。与此同时，尽管文艺复兴时期的行会未曾出版任何能帮助工匠的著作，但维特鲁威[237]著作的印刷却为德国医师提供了文学范本，使其得以撰写出首部详尽的采矿技术论著[105]。
The earliest general account of metallurgy [ 445 ] was written by a Sienese architect who worked in Italian and German foundries. Discounting prayers and magic, Biringuccio insisted on the exact weighing of ingredients and on cost accounting. In the same year as Biringuccio’s book, the most sumptuous of all Renaissance instructive manuals not only explained the use of the astrolabe (for taking the alti-
最早的冶金学通论[445]出自一位在意大利和德国铸造厂工作的锡耶纳建筑师之手。比林古乔摒弃了祈祷与魔法，坚持精确称量原料并实施成本核算。就在比林古乔著作问世的同年，文艺复兴时期最华美的教学手册不仅阐释了星盘的使用（用于测定高度——

These paper wheels (volvelles) were standardized by printing, which could not mark metal instruments with absolute accuracy until the offset process made this possible after 1904. (During the 18th century London engraved the most nearly exact calibration on metal sextants, rulers, and dials.)
星盘（用于测算恒星位置）和赤道仪（用于计算行星位置），但提供了旋转木刻版制作的实际仪器[446]。 这些纸质转盘（volvelles）通过印刷技术实现了标准化——在 1904 年平版印刷技术出现前，金属仪器无法达到绝对精确的刻度标注（18 世纪伦敦曾为金属六分仪、尺规和刻度盘制作过最精确的校准标记）。

canal water with new force into burning buildings. The brave Dutch fire crews and Amsterdam’s concentric rings of canals prevented the city from burning down as London had in 1666. London recovered so rapidly from its fire that 12 years later it saw the first serial publication for home study, Joseph Moxon’s Mechanick Exercises, intended to be Monthly continued. But the apprentice system probably discouraged young mechanics from studying on their own, for Moxon gave up after publishing the earliest instructions for smithing, woodworking, and printing [ 448 ]. (His very British promotion of self-education bore fruit long afterward in the trade schools that replaced apprenticeship during the Industrial Revolution, and his inspiration lives on in today’s correspondence courses.)
运河水以崭新力量涌入燃烧的建筑。勇敢的荷兰消防队员与阿姆斯特丹同心圆状的运河网络，使这座城市免于重蹈 1666 年伦敦大火的覆辙。伦敦从火灾中迅速复苏，仅 12 年后便诞生了首部面向家庭学习的连载出版物——约瑟夫·莫克森的《机械练习》，该书原计划每月持续更新。 但学徒制度或许阻碍了年轻技工自主学习的热情，莫克森在出版了最早的锻造、木工和印刷技艺指南后便放弃了[448]。（他极具英国特色的自学倡导，在工业革命时期取代学徒制的职业学校中结出硕果，其精神更延续至当今的函授课程。）
In Britain, where primogeniture forced younger sons of great families into trade (many making more money there than the eldest son inherited), intellectuals interested themselves in mechanical problems. Various trades were described and illustrated in Ephraim Chambers’ two-volume Cyclopaedia of Arts and Sciences (1728). When a French translation of Chambers was given to Denis Diderot for editing, the French playwright and critic enlarged the plan to include all the inventions, as well as the fresh ideas and philosophical doubts, of the age. His resulting 33-volume Encyclopédie was hounded by the censors during its 26 years of production, and with good reason, for it eroded traditions and rallied the forces that brought on the French Revolution. To prepare some 2885 engravings for the 12 volumes of plates, Diderot visited workshops [ 449 ], watched machines, had them taken apart, and even worked them himself. He was the first out-and-out man of letters not to look down his nose at mechanics. These fascinating illustrations created an interest that took concrete form in 1851 when the Crystal Palace in London assembled the arts and manufactures of all the world.
在英国，长子继承制迫使名门望族的幼子投身商业（其中许多人赚取的财富甚至超过长子继承的遗产），知识分子们则对机械问题产生了浓厚兴趣。埃弗拉姆·钱伯斯的两卷本《工艺与科学百科全书》（1728 年）详细描述并配图展示了各类手工业。 当法国剧作家兼评论家丹尼·狄德罗受托审校《钱伯斯百科全书》法译本时，他大幅扩展了编纂范围，将当时所有发明创造、新思想及哲学思辨纳入其中。最终问世的 33 卷《百科全书》在长达 26 年的编纂过程中屡遭审查机构打压——这绝非无端之举，因为它既瓦解了传统根基，又凝聚了最终引发法国大革命的力量。 为十二卷插图集准备约 2885 幅版画时，狄德罗实地考察工坊[449]，观察机械运作，要求拆解装置，甚至亲自操作。 他是首位不轻视机械的纯粹文人。这些引人入胜的插图激发了公众兴趣，最终在 1851 年伦敦水晶宫汇集全球工艺与制造业时得以具象呈现。

Children’s books (儿童读物)


Book printing started with grammars to ram Latin into boys’ heads. After about 1520 the new Protestant churches added catechisms [329] to direct the little Christian in his search for God. However, illustrations did not begin to be made especially for children until the 17th century began to explore the imagination. Then the children’s book was invented by Jan Amos Comenius, a Czech exiled for his Protestantism when he was 32 . While Comenius wandered in Protestant lands until his death nearly half a century later, his travels led him to hope that education might mitigate enough local bigotries to unite mankind. He believed, like the Jesuits, that as the twig is bent, the tree’s inclined, but while the Jesuits confined the child in splints of discipline, Comenius proposed "to allure boys’ attention with pictures that amusingly teach the chief things of the
儿童书籍的印刷始于语法书，旨在将拉丁语灌输给男孩们。约 1520 年后，新兴的新教教会增补教理问答[329]，引导幼小的基督徒寻求上帝。然而，直至 17 世纪开始探索想象力时，才出现专为儿童创作的插图。 儿童书籍的开创者是扬·阿莫斯·夸美纽斯——这位捷克学者因信奉新教在 32 岁时遭流放。此后近半个世纪，夸美纽斯辗转于新教国家直至离世，旅途见闻使他坚信：教育足以消弭地域偏见，最终实现人类团结。 他与耶稣会士同样信奉"幼苗可塑，树木可弯"的理念，但当耶稣会士用纪律的枷锁束缚孩童时，夸美纽斯却主张"以寓教于乐的图画吸引男孩注意力，传授人生要义"。

"世界。"他为稚嫩的小手制作了一本如同图鉴般精巧的书，内含 304 幅木刻版画，通过描绘那些在别处难以诠释的熟悉场景与物象，教导德国儿童学习拉丁语——后来又扩展至其他语言[450]。
His book started an educational revolution that is still spreading. Protestant publishers quickly discovered a market in children’s books. In the early 1700s the New England Primer taught the alphabet with gloomy jingles that start “In Adam’s fall we sinnéd all” and continue through “Xerxes did die and so must I.” In 1782 JeanJacques Rousseau’s Emile redirected education toward learning by doing, to develop the child’s natural goodness through example. Though little Emile’s books had no pictures, his bright response to sights and sounds started Catholics as well as Protestants illustrating books with the rewards and delights of being good [451]. These books that parents bought to quiet their children led naturally to books that children themselves might want to buy [ 452 ].
他的著作掀起了一场教育革命，至今仍在蔓延。 新教出版商迅速发现了儿童读物的市场。18 世纪初，《新英格兰读本》用阴郁的韵文教授字母表，开篇即"因亚当堕落，众生皆罪"，直至"薛西斯已逝，我亦难逃"。1782 年，让-雅克·卢梭的《爱弥儿》将教育转向实践学习，主张通过榜样激发儿童与生俱来的善良。 尽管小埃米尔的课本没有插图，但他对视觉与声音的灵动反应，促使天主教与新教出版商纷纷在书籍中描绘行善的回报与喜悦[451]。这些为安抚孩子而购入的读物，自然催生出孩子们渴望自主购买的书籍[452]。

Bellange (贝朗热)


French etching did not find its style in Paris but, through Callot and Bellange, in the border duchy of Lorraine, where a brilliant provincial court encouraged artists shortly before and after 1600 . Nancy, the capital, lies 200 to 500 miles from Paris, Antwerp, Amsterdam, and Vienna. Here travelers and soldiers from everywhere crisscrossed with ideas that converge in the exotic art of Jacques Bellange. He combined Barocci’s dotted etching and Buontalenti’s Florentine ornament with an all-out emotion that is German and an intricate feminine elegance that is French. The medley fuses in his vision of the Son sprawling between his
贝朗热的法国蚀刻版画并非在巴黎形成其风格，而是通过卡洛与贝朗热在洛林边境公国发展而成。1600 年前后，这座辉煌的省级宫廷曾大力扶持艺术家。首府南锡距巴黎、安特卫普、阿姆斯特丹及维也纳均有 200 至 500 英里之遥。 各地旅人与士兵在此交汇，思想碰撞最终凝聚成雅克·贝朗热的异域艺术。他将巴洛奇的点蚀技法与布昂塔伦蒂的佛罗伦萨装饰艺术相融合，既注入了德式奔放的情感，又糅合了法式繁复的女性优雅。这种混搭风格在他描绘圣子时展现得淋漓尽致——圣子舒展于
Figure 143: 453 Pietà. Etching by Jacques Bellange
图 143：453《圣殇》。雅克·贝朗热蚀刻版画
454 Hurdy-gurdy Player and Pilgrim from Compostela. Etching by Bellange
454 来自圣地亚哥的豎琴手与朝圣者。贝朗热蚀刻版画
Mother’s knees [ 453 ]. This frequent theme of the German late Middle Ages, which became rare in the balanced and reasonable early Renaissance, reappears in Bellange with a baroque luxury of pain. But however he refined his research in torture, this ambiguous aristocrat did not pose with Petrarch’s pleasing melancholy, nor did he display, like Byron, the wound of a titled heart; he merely stated the violent facts of a suffering age. Bellange’s blind beggars tussle with a frustrated fury that he observed with a lusciousness of disgust as one claws into a goiter as soft as an opened oyster [ 454 ]. His indolent, willowy women, with their silvery hysteria and their navels that indent through layers of silk and gauze, are the high-strung ancestors of Watteau’s well-bred, nonchalant girls. Bellange, with Parmigiano and Correggio, invented the attitudes for the 18th century.
母亲的膝盖[453]。这个在德国晚期中世纪频繁出现的主题，于均衡理性的早期文艺复兴时期日渐稀缺，却在贝朗热笔下以巴洛克式的痛苦奢华重现。但无论他如何精进酷刑研究，这位模棱两可的贵族既不摆出彼特拉克那般悦目的忧郁姿态，也不像拜伦那样展示贵族心灵的创伤；他只是陈述了一个苦难时代的暴力事实。 贝尔朗笔下的盲乞丐以挫败的狂怒扭打，他以令人作呕的颓靡凝视着其中一人撕扯甲状腺肿——那肿块柔软如刚开壳的牡蛎[454]。 他笔下慵懒纤柔的女子，带着银色的歇斯底里，脐眼透过层层丝绸薄纱若隐若现，正是瓦托笔下优雅从容的贵族少女们神经紧绷的先驱。贝尔朗热与帕尔米贾尼诺、科雷乔共同为十八世纪塑造了经典姿态。

Callot (卡洛)


Jacques Callot, the first inventive international printmaker, culled something from everywhere and imparted something to all subsequent etching and engraving. His father was master of ceremonies to the Duke of Lorraine at Nancy
雅克·卡洛，这位开创性的国际版画家，从万物中汲取灵感，并将之融入所有后世的蚀刻与雕刻艺术。其父曾任洛林公爵在南锡的礼仪主管。
while this border land was being overrun by Protestant and Catholic soldiers attacking from east and west. When Jacques was about 15 he went to Rome to study engraving under pupils of Cort [ 408 ] for some three years, after which he worked for ten years in Florence. At 28 or so he settled at home in Nancy, making a few trips to Flanders and Paris. From a life of some 43 years, more than 2000 drawings survive, studying every stroke of over 1400 prints. Such strict application never tired a vivacity so inexhaustible that he could copy his most complex etchings on second coppers with no loss of freshness.
当这片边境地区正遭受东西两路新教徒与天主教徒的军队侵袭时，年约十五岁的雅克前往罗马，在科尔特的门生门下研习雕刻技艺约三年，此后又在佛罗伦萨工作十年。 约二十八岁时，他定居家乡南锡，期间曾数次前往法兰德斯与巴黎。在他约四十三年的生命中，留存着两千余幅素描，并研究了逾一千四百幅版画的每一笔笔触。如此严谨的钻研从未消磨他那永不枯竭的活力——他甚至能在第二块铜版上复刻最复杂的蚀刻版画，却丝毫不减其鲜活神韵。
After he had learned the hack engraver’s routine in Rome, he found his path in his early 205 when he started to etch in Florence. He then made two technical innovations that were to transform printmaking on copper. Abandoning the old, hard, waxy etcher’s ground, which for a century had often flaked off and ruined work with foul biting, he adopted the lute-maker’s tough varnish of mastic and linseed oil. When this new varnish turned etching into a predictable method of picturemaking, he dared to elaborate a plate with the reasonable assurance that the acid would bite the metal only where he exposed it. Imagine his despair if foul biting had ruined his months of labor on the Fair at Impruneta [ 455 ], into which he had
在罗马习得刻版工匠的技艺后，他二十五岁初在佛罗伦萨开始蚀刻创作时找到了自己的道路。随后他实现了两项技术革新，彻底改变了铜版印刷艺术。 他摒弃了沿用百年的硬质蜡质蚀刻底料——这种材料常因剥落导致腐蚀失控而毁掉作品——转而采用制琴师使用的乳香树脂与亚麻籽油混合的强韧清漆。当这种新清漆使蚀刻成为可控的绘画技法后，他得以在合理把握酸蚀范围的前提下精心雕琢版面，确保酸液仅侵蚀暴露区域的金属。 试想当恶劣蚀刻毁掉他在《因普鲁内塔集市》[455]上耗费数月心血的作品时，他该有多绝望——那幅作品本应

455 The Fair at Impruneta. Etching by Jacques Callot, 1620
455 伊姆普鲁内塔集市。雅克·卡洛蚀刻版画，1620 年


456
The échoppe. Etching in Abraham Bosse, TRAICTE DES MANIERES DE GRAVER, Paris (Bosse), 1645
小店。亚伯拉罕·博斯版画作品，载于《蚀刻技法论》，巴黎（博斯），1645 年
packed 1138 people, 45 horses, 67 donkeys, and 137 dogs, marshaling this multitude between diagonal lanes of bare ground that avoid the older presentation of a crowd as a bumper crop of pumpkins. No one before had ever wagered so much work on the attack of the acid. Callot’s second innovation was the échoppe, a steel cylinder honed to a slant at the end [456]. By twisting this slanted oval while drawing on the grounded copper, he started a line slim and then swelled it the way an engraved line swells. He swung his echoppe as freely as a quill in turning the contours of a figure. Callot also developed, though he probably did not invent, repeated biting to etch some lines briefly and lightly, while deepening and widening others by a longer immersion in the acid.
挤满了 1138 人、45 匹马、67 头驴和 137 条狗，将这庞大队伍编列在裸露地面的斜向通道间，避免了以往将人群描绘成南瓜丰收景象的陈旧表现方式。 此前无人敢在蚀刻技法上投入如此心血。卡洛的第二项创新是"斜刻刀"——这种钢制圆筒在末端经打磨形成斜角[456]。 他将这椭圆形刻刀在铜版上扭转，先勾勒纤细线条，继而如蚀刻线条般渐次膨胀。刻刀挥舞自如，宛若鹅毛笔勾勒人物轮廓。卡洛特还发展出（虽非首创）重复蚀刻技法：短暂浸酸使线条轻盈浮现，而长时间浸泡则令其他线条加深拓宽。
When young Callot arrived in Florence, his tourist’s eye was struck by aspects of life that natives took for granted. In the public squares he looked up at comedians who pranced on platforms of loose boards and improvised ribaldries [ 457 ]. His pixilated vignettes of the commedia dell’arte-the only pictures that ever captured its wit-advertised it abroad and made it one of Italy’s most applauded exportations. He also studied beggars and cripples more methodically than Dürer, Brueghel, or Villamena, composing a natural history of mendicants [458] that was consulted by Rembrandt and all the Dutch.
年轻的卡洛特初抵佛罗伦萨时，游客的视角令他惊叹于当地人习以为常的生活景象。在公共广场上，他仰望着喜剧演员们在松散木板搭建的舞台上蹦蹦跳跳，即兴表演着粗鄙笑话[457]。 他笔下那些像素化的即兴喜剧小品——这是唯一捕捉到其机智的画作——将这种艺术形式推向海外，使其成为意大利最受赞誉的出口文化之一。他研究乞丐与残障者的方式更具系统性，远胜于丢勒、勃鲁盖尔或维拉梅纳，创作了乞丐群像的自然史[458]，连伦勃朗和所有荷兰画家都曾参考过这套画作。
In 1621 the death of his grand-ducal patron forced this would-be Florentine to leave peaceful Tuscany for his birthplace in Nancy. He returned to random de-structiveness-to the impersonal suffering of the Wars of Religion that seesawed back and forth across Lorraine, inflicting everyday lootings, beheadings, and hangings. He then etched his famous series, the Miseries of War [ 459 ], with lucidity, good manners, and the courtly indifference of one born to childhood sights of burn-
1621 年，他的大公赞助人去世，迫使这位渴望成为佛罗伦萨人的艺术家离开宁静的托斯卡纳，回到出生地南锡。 他重返战乱肆虐之地——洛林地区在宗教战争中反复沦陷，无差别地遭受着日常劫掠、斩首与绞刑。随后他以清醒的视角、得体的笔触，以及童年便目睹焚毁场景的贵族式冷漠，创作了著名的《战争的悲惨》系列版画[459]。

ing and butchering. From a loftier view of war, he etched overflights of three vast campaigns-helicopter hoverings that incorporate the reality of a panorama in the expanse of a map [460]. Callot discovered new subjects for art with new techniques for presenting them.
屠宰场。从更宏大的战争视角出发，他勾勒出三大战役的俯瞰图——如同直升机悬停般，将全景实景融入地图的广阔疆域[460]。卡洛以崭新的表现技法，为艺术开辟了全新题材。

Life in France (法国生活)


While most of Callot’s followers etched little views of France and Italy, his pupil Abraham Bosse inherited the master’s French relish for the brook water of everyday living. Otherwise they differed, for Bosse, a Parisian of Parisians, never budged from city business, while Callot risked international gypsying. After Callot gave his disciple a bottle of the new Italian varnish ground, Bosse published the formula in his manual of etchings-translated into Dutch, German, English, and Italian-that etchers used to speed the manufacture of copperplates for withstanding the wear of huge editions until they turned to etching on steel in the 1820s. Even while Rembrandt was discovering the unique magic of etching, Bosse wrote that “the etcher’s chief aim is to counterfeit engraving” and used Callot’s echoppe [ 456 ] for quickly curving swells as geometric as the more laborious
在法国的生活尽管卡洛的大多数追随者都刻画着法国和意大利的小景致，但他的学生亚伯拉罕·博斯却继承了大师对日常生活溪流般清泉的法式品味。除此之外，两人截然不同：博斯作为地道的巴黎人，始终扎根于都市事务；而卡洛则冒险踏上了国际流浪之旅。 卡洛特赠予弟子一瓶新式意大利清漆底料后，博斯将其配方刊载于版画技法手册——该书被译为荷兰语、德语、英语及意大利语——此后蚀刻师们便借此加速铜版制作，使版画经得起大量印刷的磨损，直至 1820 年代转而采用钢版蚀刻。 当伦勃朗正发掘蚀刻术的独特魔力时，博斯却宣称"蚀刻师的首要目标是仿刻版画"，并运用卡洛特发明的"回声刻刀"[456]快速勾勒出几何形态的曲线——其几何感甚至超越了耗时费力的传统技法。
Figure 146: 462 Shops under the Law Courts, Paris. Etching by Bosse
图 146：巴黎法院下方的 462 家店铺。博斯蚀刻版画
and expensive graver. Bosse’s book reduced the graver to a finishing tool for smoothing transitions in etchings, so that after about 1675 “engravings” differ from “etchings” in style, not technique. (Pure engraving did not return until the 1920 s in Paris and then only for expressive open calligraphy [ 749 ].
昂贵的刻刀。博塞的著作将刻刀降格为平滑蚀刻版画过渡处的修饰工具，因此自 1675 年左右起，“雕版画”与“蚀刻版画”的差异仅在于风格而非技法。（纯粹的雕版画直至 1920 年代才在巴黎复兴，且仅用于表现性开放式书法[749]。）
Bosse, a Huguenot who battled the orthodox academies, made the first detailed prints of artisans. In his copperplate workshop [ 461 ] the etcher, left, holds a plate coated with ground through which he is scratching lines with an echoppe. He will erode these opened lines with acid from one of the bottles on the cabinet. He has already etched most of the design on the plate that the engraver, right, is grooving with a burin while pivoting the plate on a leather cushion stuffed with sand. The central screen stops the windows from reflecting on the plates. The engraver’s window is “glazed” with oiled paper to diffuse the light on his uncovered metal. Both artisans display their work on the rear wall, where two monks and a gentleman consider purchases. The frames display paintings, or perhaps prints that are varnished rather than expensively glazed.
博斯，这位与正统学院抗争的胡格诺派信徒，创作了首批描绘工匠的精细版画。 在铜版画工坊[461]中，左侧蚀刻师手持镀有底漆的铜版，正用蚀刻刀刻划线条。他将用柜上瓶中的酸液腐蚀这些刻出的线条。右侧雕刻师正用刻刀在铜版上开槽，同时将铜版置于填满沙粒的皮垫上旋转，此时版面大部分图案已由蚀刻师完成蚀刻。 中央屏风阻隔了窗户在铜版上的倒影。雕刻师的窗户贴着油纸"玻璃"，使光线在裸露的金属上漫射。两位工匠将作品陈列在后墙，两名修士与一位绅士正驻足观赏。画框里展示的可能是油画，也可能是涂过清漆而非昂贵玻璃封装的版画。
Bosse also shows us the work and leisure of the kind of down-to-earth Parisians who talk such tart good sense in Molière’s comedies. His pictorial inventory of the
博塞还向我们展现了那些脚踏实地的巴黎人的工作与休闲生活——莫里哀喜剧中那些直言不讳的智慧之士正是如此。他用画笔记录的巴黎生活图景
463
Louis XIV Playing Billiards. Engraving by Antoine Trouvain, 1694
路易十四打台球。安托万·特鲁万雕版画，1694 年
Figure 147: Life in France
图 147：法国生活
smart shops under the law courts [462] illustrates the fashionable trifles that diarists mention, but nobody saved. Bosse recorded trivia so fascinatingly that Frenchmen have ever since made a specialty of intimate pictures that preserve more details of life in France than anywhere else. When one of Bosse’s successors etched scenes of Versailles, he avoided state ceremonies for the cozy supper parties that Louis XIV, like a prosperous citizen, gave on three evenings a week to cousinly gatherings of the innermost court circle [ 463 ].
法院底下的精品店[462]展现了日记作者们提及却无人珍藏的时髦小玩意儿。 博塞以迷人笔触记录琐事，此后法国人便专攻私密画作，其作品保存的法兰西生活细节远超其他地区。当博塞的继任者刻画凡尔赛场景时，他避开国家典礼，转而描绘路易十四如同富裕市民般每周三晚为宫廷核心圈子举办的亲密晚宴[463]。
Separated from the official Italianate art of the French palaces, the French middle class made and bought pictures of family life that reached a quiet poetry in the prints after Chardin’s paintings [ 464 ]. Prints continued to chronicle the triumph
脱离了法国宫廷中正式的意大利风格艺术，法国中产阶级创作并购买了描绘家庭生活的画作，这些作品在夏尔丹画作的版画复制品中达到了静谧的诗意境界[464]。版画持续记录着胜利的篇章。

of the sometimes rowdy bourgeoisie under the Second Empire, when they questioned values and dared misconduct [ 465 ]. Daumier found Bosse’s subject matter inexhaustible for original treatments that in turn inspired the impressionist painters. Everyday doings at home and on street corners still furnish the school of Paris with some of its happiest images [ 466 ]. The rest of us can only envy France’s pictorial history, which stretches back through the Labors of the Months painted and printed in books of hours, and sculptured on Gothic cathedrals, to its origins in the mason’s mallets and carpenter’s adzes carved on Gallo-Roman tombstones.
在第二帝国时期，有时喧闹的资产阶级质疑价值观，敢于越轨行为[465]。杜米埃发现博斯的题材源源不断地激发着新颖的创作，进而启发了印象派画家。家庭日常与街头巷尾的景象，至今仍为巴黎画派提供着最欢快的画面[466]。 我们其余人只能羡慕法国的绘画历史，它可追溯至《月份劳作》——那些绘于时祷书中、印于书籍里、雕于哥特式大教堂上的作品，其根源更可溯至高卢-罗马墓碑上石匠的槌子与木匠的斧头。

Dutch etchers before Rembrandt (伦勃朗之前的荷兰蚀刻版画家)


While regimented Antwerpers were engraving in factories, several Dutchmen in Haarlem etched with a stubborn individuality that cleared a way for Rembrandt. They gathered in Haarlem around the artistic activity centering on Heemskerck [ 417 ] and Goltzius [ 420 ]. Yet unlike these two, the others did not work for publishers but suited their own personal
伦勃朗之前的荷兰蚀刻艺术家当安特卫普工匠们在工厂里进行规整的雕刻时，哈勒姆的几位荷兰艺术家正以顽强的个性进行蚀刻创作，为伦勃朗铺平了道路。他们聚集在哈勒姆，围绕着海姆斯克尔克[417]和戈尔齐乌斯[420]为核心的艺术活动圈。然而与这两位不同的是，其余艺术家并非为出版商工作，而是顺应自身个性进行创作。
467
Figure 149: The Brindle Cat. Drypoint by Jan Vermeyen
图 149：虎斑猫。扬·弗尔梅恩的干刻版画
Dutch etchers before Rembrandt
伦勃朗之前的荷兰蚀刻版画家
tastes so much that most of their prints are now rare. Dutch etching began in earnest with Heemskerck and Vermeyen, both born at about the same time as etching itself. Both used an open manner that probably influenced etchers at Fontaine-bleau-Heemskerck for sets of Bible stories and Vermeyen for an original choice of secular subjects bluffly drawn [ 467 ]. Heemskerck stayed in Haarlem, while Vermeyen soon wandered away to Spain and north Africa, an enigmatic adventurer who founded no school. Goltzius passed his swagger on to Jacques de Gheyn II, who sketched on copper with the freedom of Parmigiano. De Gheyn preceded Rubens in learning from Titian’s followers, the Bassanos, to naturalize the heroics of Italian farmyard opulence in the Netherlands [ 468 ]. The etcher who initiated the
其作品极具艺术价值，以致如今多数版画都已极为罕见。荷兰蚀刻版画始于海姆斯克尔克与维尔梅恩，二人诞生于蚀刻技艺诞生的同期。 二人皆采用开放式技法，可能影响了枫丹白露的蚀刻师——海姆斯克尔克创作圣经故事系列，维尔梅恩则以大胆笔触开创世俗题材之选[467]。海姆斯克尔克定居哈勒姆，维尔梅恩却远赴西班牙与北非，这位神秘的冒险家未创立任何学派。 戈尔茨将这种豪放气质传给了雅克·德·盖恩二世，后者在铜版上挥洒的笔触自由如帕尔米贾尼诺。德·盖恩早于鲁本斯向提香门徒巴萨诺家族学习，将意大利农庄的富丽堂皇以自然主义手法移植到荷兰[468]。这位蚀刻艺术家开创了

Dutch etchers before Rembrandt
伦勃朗之前的荷兰蚀刻版画家

Figure 150: 469  图 150：469
Lovers. Etching by Willem Buytewech
恋人。威廉·布伊特韦赫的蚀刻版画
classic orderliness of the Dutch 17th century was Buytewech. In a life of little more than 30 years, he formed artists around him by supplying them with drawings, most of which survive only in their etched copies. He himself etched figures with a Dutch flair for eccentric elegance [ 469 ] and landscapes with an almost Chinese calligraphy in the furrows of the fields and the windbreaks of trees like pressed seaweed. For the allegories that the age demanded, he discarded the quaintly bedizened personifications that had been current since Roman times-Victory, Africa, and the rest-and invented the symbolic landscape [ 470 ].
十七世纪荷兰的古典秩序感体现在布伊特韦赫身上。在短短三十余年的人生中，他通过提供素描作品培养了周围的艺术家，这些素描大多仅存蚀刻复本。他本人以蚀刻技法创作的人物作品洋溢着荷兰特有的奇雅风韵[469]，而他的风景画中，田垄的纹理与如压制海藻般的树木防风林，竟透出近乎中国水墨的韵味。 面对时代所需的寓言题材，他摒弃了自罗马时代沿袭至今的奇装异服式拟人化表现——诸如胜利女神、非洲女神等——开创了象征性风景画的先河[470]。
The astonishing genius among early Dutch etchers was Hercules Seghers, Rembrandt’s only contemporary with force enough to make an impression on that master’s maturity. Rembrandt reworked at least one of Seghers’ plates for his own purposes [ 444 ] but does not seem to have used the technique that Seghers devised in solitary experiments. Unlike any contemporary, Seghers apparently penned lines on the bare copper with a water-soluble syrup. After coating the plate with etcher’s ground, he soaked it in water to dissolve the syrup and expose the penned lines. Since some of these lines would etch too wide to catch ink, he pitted them with a granulating process like aquatint [ 229 ]. He sometimes printed on linen, apparently making offsets by pressing the cloth against a freshly printed etching on paper. He probably invented methods as individual as these to color his prints with horizon blue, ashes of roses, and verdigris. As he beat his desperate way, Seghers copied a Baldung woodcut or a recent Dutch print by absorbing it into his own
在早期荷兰蚀刻艺术家中，赫拉克勒斯·塞赫斯堪称惊世天才，他是伦勃朗唯一能以其力量影响这位大师成熟期的同时代人。伦勃朗至少曾为自身创作目的改制过塞赫斯的一块铜版[444]，但似乎并未采用塞赫斯在孤独实验中发明的技法。与同时代任何艺术家不同，塞赫斯显然用一种水溶性糖浆在裸露的铜板上勾勒线条。 在版面上涂覆蚀刻底料后，他将铜版浸入水中溶解糖浆，使笔触线条显现。由于部分线条蚀刻过宽导致无法承载墨色，他采用类似水彩蚀刻的颗粒化工艺[229]使线条产生凹坑。他有时在亚麻布上印刷，显然通过将布料压在刚印好的纸质蚀刻版上制作复制品。 他为版画着色时，或许也发明了同样独创的方法——运用地平线蓝、玫瑰灰烬与铜绿等颜料。在绝望的探索中，塞赫斯通过吸收巴尔东木刻或荷兰新派版画的精髓，将其转化为自身艺术的养分。

intensely personal style. His hallucinatory landscapes range from views of the flats of Holland, settled like a sediment under the deep sky, to ruins and lunar gullies [ 471 ], eroded, airless, abandoned-all etched with the crabbed scraggles of a man struggling to burst out of himself.

Rembrandt’s portraits (伦勃朗的肖像画)


It is hard to describe the greatest painter of the north and the greatest printmaker of them all, because Rembrandt is so many people. Try to pigeonhole him anywhere, and he escapes. Call him a Dutchman, and he shows a deeper understanding of the essentials of the Italian High Renaissance than any northerner. Call him a master of shadows, and he draws a figure with three or four lines. Call him spiritual, and he throws grossness at you.
伦勃朗的肖像画要描述这位北方最伟大的画家、所有版画家中的翘楚实非易事，因为伦勃朗具有多重面貌。若试图将他归入任何一类，他总能挣脱束缚。 若称他为荷兰人，他展现的意大利文艺复兴精髓却比任何北方艺术家更深刻；若称他为暗影大师，他仅用三四笔便勾勒出人物轮廓；若称他为灵性画家，他却向你抛来粗粝之作。

His various selves crowd his self-portraits. In his 20s he makes mouths at the looking glass to try out pity and fear [ 472 ], while the candle agitates shadows. At 33 he has married an heiress, Amsterdam society is queuing up to be painted, and he has just seen Raphael’s portrait of Castiglione at a local auction [ 473 ]. The purchaser of the Raphael also shows him Titian’s so-called Ariosto [ 474 ] with its Venetian pose that Raphael had assimilated for his Castiglione. Imposing the Venetian layout on its Roman adaptation, Rembrandt etches himself in a Renaissance aristocrat’s wide sleeve, lounging on a parapet like the Ariosto and staring you down under a floppy beret like the author of The Courtier [ 475 ]. This is the one moment when he does not regard himself as merely his handiest model but wants to set himself on record as a pretty man. And if you were 33 and had just made a lot of money and a shrewd marriage, could you help indulging in a bit of physical vanity? Then Saskia slowly dies, Geertge goes mad. After nine years Hendrickje reestablishes order in the house and Rembrandt can again face himself in the mirror [ 476 ]. Now, at 42, what has become a potato face is mastered by those all-devouring eyes and that hand about to go exploring. Rembrandt’s obses-
他的多重自我挤满自画像。二十岁时对着镜子做鬼脸，试探怜悯与恐惧[472]，烛光搅动着阴影。 三十三岁时，他迎娶了富家千金，阿姆斯特丹上流社会争相请他作画，而他刚在本地拍卖会上目睹了拉斐尔为卡斯蒂廖内所作的肖像[473]。那位拉斐尔画作的买家还向他展示了提香的《阿里奥斯托》[474]——画中人物的威尼斯式姿态，正是拉斐尔为卡斯蒂廖内肖像所借鉴的。 伦勃朗将威尼斯式构图强加于罗马风格改编中，将自己刻画成文艺复兴贵族——身着宽大袖袍，如阿里奥斯托般倚靠在护栏上，又如《宫廷人》作者般戴着软呢贝雷帽直视观者[475]。这是他唯一不将自己视为最得手的模特，而渴望以俊美形象留名画史的时刻。 倘若你年仅三十三岁，刚发大财又娶了精明贤妻，岂能不沉溺于些许肉体虚荣？随后萨斯基亚病逝，吉尔特格精神崩溃。 九年后，亨德里克耶重整家务秩序，伦勃朗终于能再度直面镜中自我[476]。如今四十二岁的他，那张马铃薯般的脸庞被那双吞噬一切的眼睛与即将探寻的手掌控。伦勃朗的执念——
475 Self-portrait Leaning on a Ledge. Etching by Rembrandt, 1639. Reproduced in reverse
475 《倚窗自画像》伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1639 年此处为镜像复制
476 Self-portrait by a Window, Drawing. Etching by Rembrandt, 1648
476 《窗边自画像》，素描。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1648 年

Rembrandt’s portraits  伦勃朗的肖像画
sion with looking and drawing has finally fused the two acts into one reaction. He loses himself in looking until he becomes what he sees, whether he sees a gutted ox or Christ preaching, and he discharges his vision into a shorthand that instinctively nets all essentials. Becoming what he sees turns him into many things in succession and rescues him from good taste, which you demonstrate by rejections. This etching of 1648 starts the last long series of self-portraits that Rembrandt continued by painting himself in imperial loneliness.
凝视与描绘的交融终将二者熔铸为一体。他沉溺于凝视直至化作所见之物——无论是剖开的牛腹还是布道的基督——并将视觉转化为本能捕捉精髓的速写。 化身为所见之物使他接连变换多种形态，并使他摆脱了所谓"好品味"的束缚——这种品味往往通过拒绝来彰显。这幅 1648 年的蚀刻版画开启了伦勃朗最后的自画像系列，他以帝王般的孤独姿态持续描绘着自我。
We follow his etched portraits through his etchings of old friends who had helped him. He portrayed them with accessories that suggest their ways of life, quite unlike his paintings of strangers who came in off the street to sit emptyhanded in the studio chair. When he was 41 he made his only full-length etched portrait of his steadfast friend Jan Six [477]. The young patrician, dressed with rich sobriety, stands in a handsome old room and reads what might be the draft of his latest poetic tragedy. The paper glows back at the face that Rembrandt worked and reworked with microscopic touches as the focus of a figure that makes its effect by its stance and setting. Rembrandt must have regarded this as his most important etched portrait; sketches for it survive in chalk, ink, and oils. About eight years later, toward the end of the series, he made his only portrait entirely in drypoint of the bailiff of the bankruptcy court [ 478 ]—toward which Rembrandt’s business
我们通过他刻画旧友的蚀刻版画，追寻那些曾帮助过他的身影。他为他们配戴暗示生活方式的饰品，这与他描绘陌生人的画作截然不同——那些陌生人从街头走进工作室，空手坐在画室的椅子上。四十一岁那年，他为挚友扬·西克斯创作了唯一一幅全身蚀刻肖像[477]。 这位年轻贵族身着质朴华美的服饰，伫立于典雅古雅的房间中，手捧或许是他最新诗剧的草稿。纸张的光泽映照着画中人的面容——伦勃朗以显微般的笔触反复雕琢这张面孔，使其成为画面焦点，而人物姿态与环境布局共同营造出震撼效果。 伦勃朗必将此作视为最重要的蚀刻肖像——其粉笔、墨水及油画草稿均有留存。约八年前，在系列创作尾声之际，他以干刻技法完成了唯一肖像画《破产法庭执达员》[478]——伦勃朗的商业

478 (opposite page)  478（对页）

Thomas Jacobsz Haringh (Old Haringh). Drypoint by Rembrandt, 1655
托马斯·雅各布·哈林（老哈林）。伦勃朗干刻版画，1655 年

clumsiness was inevitably drawing him. The light from the thick windowpanes glows on the pale old face that has seen so many men in trouble, and now meditates on man’s misfortunes. The flesh has worn to a lucid casing for the spirit. Here Rembrandt has left the rowdy force of his adolescence so far behind that it seems to come from another man in another country. No other artist ever traveled so long a road.
笨拙的笔触不可避免地将他吸引。透过厚重的窗玻璃，微光映照着苍白的旧脸——这张面孔见证过无数人的困境，如今正沉思着人类的厄运。血肉已消磨成灵性的透明外壳。此处的伦勃朗早已将少年时期的狂放力量抛在身后，仿佛来自异国他乡的另一个男人。再没有哪位艺术家走过如此漫长的道路。

Rembrandt’s techniques (伦勃朗的技法)


About a decade after Rembrandt’s death, the Florentine critic Baldinucci marveled at “Reimbrond Vanrein’s astonishing style of etching, which he originated and which has never been practiced before or since. With scratchings and scribblings and no outline, he achieved a rich and powerful light and shade, here totally black, and there baring the paper.” This well describes the range of Rembrandt’s effects. But by subordinating his skill to an imagination that developed more subtlety than any, he makes one forget that he was also the greatest copperplate technician. While most artists perfect a single manner, Rembrandt varied to suit each subject, now dropping a tried and proven way of working to revert to an earlier one, now inventing something new. Each fresh vision dictated
伦勃朗的技法伦勃朗逝世约十年后，佛罗伦萨评论家巴尔迪努奇惊叹道："莱姆布隆德·范莱恩开创的蚀刻技法令人惊叹，此法前无古人后无来者。他以刮刻与涂写取代轮廓线，却能营造出浓郁而强烈的明暗效果——此处墨色纯粹，彼处纸底显露。" 这段描述精准概括了伦勃朗艺术效果的广度。但当他将精湛技艺服从于超凡的想象力——这种想象力比任何人都更具深邃性——人们便容易忽略他同时也是最伟大的铜版画技艺大师。多数艺术家仅精进单一风格，伦勃朗却因题材而变：时而摒弃成熟技法回归早期创作，时而开创全新手法。每种崭新视野都决定着

its own line and tone, the way each play dictated its own syntax and vocabulary to Shakespeare.
它自有其独特的行文风格与语调，正如每部戏剧都为莎士比亚规定了专属的语法与词汇。
Rembrandt and Goya found release from insistent painting commissions by making prints that they could treat as they pleased while being challenged to juggle indirect manipulations for an always surprising outcome. Rembrandt must have started to etch in his late teens, for he was no novice at 22 when he signed and dated a plate, his needle, like a quill, already weaving lively lines. During his 20s he limbered his fingers by etching mostly full-length beggars and heads of himself and his household in about 150 little exercises-half his total etchings in number but far less than half in interest. At about 28 he began to mat lines thickly to rival painting with a black and white as striking as Goudt’s engravings after Elsheimer [ 442 ]. Rembrandt’s Annunciation to the Shepherds [ 479 ] is a brilliant melodrama of fugitives and stampeding cattle. The glory in the clouds (probably suggested by a translucent stage backdrop) spotlights the night.
伦勃朗和戈雅通过制作版画摆脱了繁重的绘画委托，得以随心所欲地创作，同时又面临着通过间接手法实现惊人效果的挑战。 伦勃朗大约在十几岁晚期就开始尝试蚀刻技法，22 岁时他签名并标注日期的一块版画已显露娴熟功底——他的刻针如鹅毛笔般灵动，勾勒出鲜活的线条。二十余岁间，他通过约 150 幅练习作品磨练技艺：多为全身乞丐像及自画像与家眷肖像。这些作品虽仅占其蚀刻版画总数的一半，却承载着远超半数的艺术价值。 约二十八岁时，他开始以浓密线条构筑画面，力图以黑白对比的震撼力媲美绘画，其效果堪比古德特根据埃尔斯海默作品创作的版画[442]。伦勃朗的《向牧羊人报喜》[479]堪称一场精彩的戏剧性场景——逃亡者与惊慌奔逃的牛群交织。云层中的荣光（或许源自半透明舞台幕布的启发）将夜色照得通明。
After Rembrandt tired of making etching imitate painting and drawing, he used it to explore a third way of seeing. No brush or pencil could explode just like the single rough bite of acid (as economical as an etching by Manet) that suggests the silent shattering in the upper room [480]. Similar spontaneous jottings probably
伦勃朗厌倦了让蚀刻版画模仿油画与素描后，转而用它探索第三种视觉表达方式。任何画笔或铅笔都无法像那道粗粝的蚀刻痕迹（其精炼程度堪比马奈的蚀刻版画）那样瞬间爆发，暗示着楼上房间里无声的崩塌[480]。类似的即兴速写或许

480

underlie the intricate rework on Rembrandt’s later etchings. At one time he varied a calm open etching [ 481 ] by painting ink on the copper itself [ 482 ]. Such printings of tone could have prompted Castiglione to invent the monotype [ 527 ], in which he painted the entire subject on an unworked copperplate and then printed
支撑伦勃朗后期蚀刻版画复杂的重制工艺。他曾通过在铜版上直接涂抹墨汁[482]，对一幅平缓开放的蚀刻版画[481]进行变体创作。这种色调印刷技法或许启发了卡斯蒂廖内发明单版画[527]——他先在未经处理的铜版上绘制完整主题，再进行印刷。
Figure 151: 481 The Entombment. Etching by Rembrandt, 1645. Clean-wiped impression of first state
图 151：481《安葬》。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1645 年。初版状态，经清洁擦拭的印痕。
it as for an etching. Rembrandt usually reworked the copperplates of his late spontaneous etchings by using the graver unconventionally for medium tones and the drypoint needle for the blacks. In his early 40 s he thus combined his range from outline etching to total shading by giving equal emphasis to the light and dark
如同蚀刻版画般。伦勃朗晚年创作即兴蚀刻版时，常以非常规手法重制铜版：用刻刀处理中间色调，以干刻针刻画黑色部分。四十岁出头时，他便将轮廓蚀刻与整体阴影技法融为一体，使明暗元素获得同等强调。

halves of the Hundred Guilder Print [ 483 ], his bravura blend of etching, engrav- ing, and drypoint, one of his most complex works in any medium. Christ beats his radiance at the haunted shadows, out of which the sick and ignorant grope their way toward his illumination. Drypoint creates this furnished and inhabited darkness in one of those modulations of deep tone that must have suggested the invention of mezzotint [511] and aquatint [229] in Amsterdam at this very time. Ignoring the machine-made flatness of both these mechanisms, Rembrandt preferred to develop his individual discoveries by etching more scenes of darkness than he painted.
《百盾版画》[483]的两部分，这幅作品以蚀刻、雕刻与干刻的精妙融合展现其非凡技艺，堪称其所有媒介中最复杂的作品之一。基督以神圣光辉驱散幽暗阴影，病弱与无知者正从阴影中摸索前行，朝向他的光明。 干刻技法在深邃色调的变奏中营造出这片充盈着生活气息的幽暗空间——正是这般技法，想必启发了同时期阿姆斯特丹人发明凹版凹点法[511]与水彩蚀刻法[229]。伦勃朗无视这两种机械技法产生的平面效果，更倾向于通过蚀刻创作比油画作品更丰富的暗影场景，以此深化其个人艺术探索。
After he was about 40 , Rembrandt’s impatience led him more and more to attack the copper muscularly with drypoint, slashing with an abruptness that still startles [ 484 ]. Since drypoint wears off in a few impressions, it is unfortunate that over 75 of Rembrandt’s actual plates survive for reprintings until as late as 1906. These last, worn, reworked impressions show us less of Rembrandt’s intentions than do good photomechanical facsimiles of early impressions.
伦勃朗年近四十后，其急躁性日益促使他以干刻法猛烈攻击铜版，那凌厉的刻划至今仍令人惊叹[484]。 由于干刻版仅能印制数次便会磨损，令人遗憾的是，直至 1906 年仍有逾 75 幅伦勃朗的原始铜版被用于重印。这些最终印制的、磨损且经反复加工的复制品，远不如早期印版的优质照相机械复刻品更能展现艺术家的创作意图。

Rembrandt and the Bible (伦勃朗与圣经)


Rembrandt may never have read the entire Bible, but he meditated all his life on episodes in which the divine penetrates the everyday to surprise ordinary people in extraordinary relationships. He returned to the Bible more often than to any other subject and expressed his preoccupation most imaginatively in his etchings. Into his etchings he put as secret a part of himself as into his drawings, adding an effort for public presentation that makes them as effective as his paintings. He could throw himself into black and white, or brown and white, as wholeheartedly as into painting. Though he was not actually color blind, his paintings show that he cannot have distinguished colors as vividly as Vermeer or Monet. The comparative monochrome of his eyesight concentrated his vision on adjusting tones in a mystery of shade that his pen or needle expressed as ably as his brush.
伦勃朗与圣经伦勃朗或许从未通读整部圣经，但他毕生沉思着那些神圣力量渗透日常、以非凡关系惊动凡人的故事。他反复回归圣经的频率远超其他题材，并在蚀刻版画中以最富想象力的方式表达了这份执念。 他将如同素描般隐秘的自我倾注于蚀刻版画，并为公开展示付出的努力，使这些版画与油画同样震撼人心。他能全情投入黑白或棕白世界的创作，如同绘画般忘我。尽管并非真正的色盲，其画作却表明他无法像维米尔或莫奈那样鲜明地辨识色彩。 视觉的相对单色性使他专注于色调的微妙调整，这种阴影奥秘通过他的钢笔或刻针得以精准呈现，其造诣丝毫不逊于画笔。
Rembrandt’s most ambitious picture in any medium is the Hundred Guilder Print [ 483 ], on whose 38 figures he must have etched for as many weeks as he painted on the 29 figures in the Night Watch, plus injecting a higher voltage of emotion. The etching sums up Christ’s mission by showing him doing many things at once:
伦勃朗在任何媒介中最宏大的作品当属《百金版画》[483]。画中 38 个人物耗费的蚀刻工时，想必与他在《夜巡》中绘制 29 个人物所用的时间相当，且情感张力更为强烈。这幅蚀刻版画通过展现基督同时进行多项行动，概括了他的使命：
Figure 153: 485 Christ Presented to the People. Painting by Rembrandt, 1634
图 153：基督向民众显现。伦勃朗绘，1634 年
healing the sick, receiving little children, rebuking the Apostles, and answering the Pharisees.
医治病人，接纳孩童，责备使徒，并回答法利赛人。
Though no one but Rembrandt could have welded together such multiplicity, he achieved a more limpid fusion when he turned to single episodes. Two prints of Christ presented to the people show how 20 years of reflection deepened his insight into the Bible. When he was 28 he painted the subject in grays [ 485 ] for reproduc-
尽管唯有伦勃朗能将如此纷繁的元素熔铸为一体，但当他转向单一题材时，却实现了更为澄澈的融合。两幅《基督向民众显现》版画展现了二十载沉淀如何深化了他对圣经的洞察。二十八岁时，他以灰色调[485]创作该题材作品，旨在实现可复制性——
Figure 154: Rembrandt and the Bible

tion in a copperplate [ 486 ] that he copyrighted to emulate Rubens’ profitable advertisements during the previous 25 years. (Rembrandt, no businessman, gave up copyrighting after two tries.) He or his assistants etched most of the early Christ Presented before filling in the head and torso of Christ himself. He stands alone outdoors, as Dutch prisoners did when they were being condemned to die, while, in the darkness below, the scrimmage of his enemies cascades like a tragic car-
在铜版画[486]上，他申请了版权，以效仿鲁本斯此前 25 年间盈利丰厚的广告策略。 （雷姆布兰特并非商人，尝试两次后便放弃了版权登记。）他或其助手在完成基督头部与躯干的填充前，已蚀刻出《献耶稣于圣殿》的大部分画面。基督独自伫立于户外——正如荷兰囚犯被判处死刑时的姿态——而下方黑暗中，敌人的混战如悲剧性的车祸般层层叠叠。
Rembrandt and the Bible  伦勃朗与圣经
nival. Rembrandt later studied the Christ Presented that Lucas of Leiden had engraved over a century before [ 487 ], when medieval miracle plays were still being acted on platforms as wide as city squares. On such a platform Lucas lifted Christ and Pilate above the audience of the chief priests and the rabble, the way Greek actors were lifted above the chorus. (Saint John says that Christ was presented on the Gabbatha, actually the praetorium, which translators rendered as “the Pavement.”) When Rembrandt was 49 he made a large drypoint [ 488 ] presenting Christ on a stage even loftier than Lucas’ to separate still further the principal actors from the chorus. He interwove the rabble and the priests in a linkage more inventive than the cavalcade on the Parthenon. Their mere backs tell us how they feel toward each other and how they are reacting to the event that they and we are watching. By amalgamating intense individuals, Rembrandt perfected
伦勃朗后来研究了莱顿的卢卡斯在百余年前刻制的《基督受审图》[487]，当时中世纪的奇迹剧仍在广场般宽阔的舞台上演。卢卡斯将基督与彼拉多置于祭司长和暴民观众之上，如同古希腊演员被抬高在合唱团之上。 （圣约翰记载基督是在加巴塔被引见，实为总督府庭院，译者将其译为"石板地"。）伦勃朗四十九岁时创作了一幅大型干刻版画[488]，将基督置于比卢卡斯更高的舞台之上，进一步将主角与合唱团隔离。 他将暴民与祭司交织成比帕特农神庙浮雕更富创意的联结。仅凭背影便道尽彼此心绪，以及他们与我们共同见证这场事件时的反应。通过熔铸鲜活个体，伦勃朗臻于完美。

the tradition of drawing crowds that was first published by Schongauer in his Road to Calvary [ 132 ]. Yet because the very fascination of this front row of spectators fences us off from the drama beyond, Rembrandt proceeded to rub out all but the two ends, expunging what alone would have made the fame of anyone else. An amateur artist hesitates to erase for fear he may do worse next time, but the professional shows his mastery by the ruthlessness of his sacrifices. Rembrandt’s dele-tion-one of the boldest in all art-paid off, for it perfects the dualism of priests and rabble, Christ and Barrabas, godhead and mankind. He suddenly puts opera glasses to our eyes, pulling us into the void over the twin prison inlets to set us face to face with Christ and Pilate [ 489 ]. We now live inside the vision, oblivious to the calculations that went into its making, oblivious to the 20 years needed to get to the bottom of 200 or 300 words of reporting, oblivious even to the paper and the ink.
吸引人群的传统最早由申高尔在其《加尔瓦略之路》[132]中开创。然而正因这排观众的迷人魅力将我们隔绝于剧情的核心之外，伦勃朗遂将画面除两端人物外的所有内容抹去——他删除了任何其他画家都足以成名的部分。 业余画家因畏惧下次可能更糟而犹豫擦除，但专业人士却以无情的取舍彰显其造诣。伦勃朗的删减——艺术史上最激进的抉择之一——终获回报，它将祭司与暴民、基督与巴拉巴、神性与人性的二元对立推向极致。 他突然将歌剧望远镜置于我们眼前，将我们拉入双重监狱入口上方的虚空，使我们与基督和彼拉多面对面[489]。此刻我们置身于画面之中，全然忘却其创作背后的精妙构思，忘却耗费二十年才完成的两三百字报道，甚至忘却了纸张与墨水。

Rembrandt and Italy (伦勃朗与意大利)


Rembrandt said that he had no time to travel to Italy with the other painters, and he was right, for Italy came to him in the Amsterdam salesrooms, transforming an ambitious yokel into a world-permeating mystery. In 1639 an auction displayed Raphael’s best portrait, of Castiglione, long enough to show Rembrandt all that it had to teach him [ 473 ]. Such sales supplied him with the greatest collection of prints ever owned by any artist. Dozens of his purchases must survive in every large print collection, unidentifiable because he stored their images so completely in his eye that he never bothered to mark the paper as his property.
伦勃朗与意大利伦勃朗曾言自己无暇随其他画家赴意大利游历，此言不虚——因为意大利已通过阿姆斯特丹拍卖厅来到他面前，将这位雄心勃勃的乡下人蜕变为贯穿世界的谜题。 1639 年，一场拍卖会展出了拉斐尔最杰出的肖像画《卡斯蒂廖内》，停留时间恰好让伦勃朗领略了这幅作品所蕴含的全部艺术精髓[473]。这些拍卖会为他提供了艺术史上规模最宏大的版画收藏。如今各大版画收藏馆中，数十幅他购入的作品依然存在，却因他将图像完全铭刻于心而无法辨识来源——他从未在纸张上标注过所有权。
Mantegna’s engravings inspired him long after other artists had abandoned them for Marcantonio and still later Italians. Although it is fairly easy to adapt and improve on characterless works of art, it takes a Rembrandt to digest anything so authoritative as a Mantegna, transforming his hieratic Mother of God [195], as symbolic as a sacred monogram carved in marble, into the human mother humming to her baby snug in a window nook [ 490 ]. The upward look that Mantegna uses to awe with the eminence of grandeur here turns into the small child’s familiarity with the undersides of chairs and tables. Far from copying Mantegna’s image, Rembrandt developed unsuspected implications in its canonized theme. Most expressive discoveries are made in old familiar subject matter, for the really original artist does not try to find a substitute for boy meets girl, but creates the illusion that no boy ever met a girl before.
曼特尼亚的版画长期激励着他，即便其他艺术家早已弃之不用，转而追随马尔坎托尼奥乃至更晚期的意大利画家。 虽然对缺乏个性的艺术作品进行改编和改进相对容易，但唯有伦勃朗能消化曼特尼亚这般权威的作品——他将曼特尼亚庄严的《圣母像》[195]（如同大理石上雕刻的神圣徽章般充满象征意义）转化为窗边角落里轻哼着摇篮曲、怀抱婴儿的人间母亲[490]。 曼特尼亚用仰视视角营造的崇高威严，在此化作孩童对桌椅底部的熟悉感。伦勃朗非但未复制曼特尼亚的画面，反而在其经典主题中开辟出意想不到的深意。最具表现力的发现往往诞生于陈旧的题材——真正的原创者并非试图替代"男孩遇见女孩"的经典模式，而是创造出"世上从未有男孩遇见女孩"的幻觉。
Rembrandt also learned much from Raphael’s impeccable command of layout. He studied reproductions of some of the ten huge cartoons that Raphael drew for tapestries to decorate the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican. When these vast drawings were unrolled in Brussels, they transformed tapestry weaving for four centuries. To reproduce such large, shaded, and rounded forms [ 491 ] the Flemish weavers had to give up their traditional flat patches of bright colors for somber tones curving into shadows. (Weavers coped with the new painting’s broad volumes round-
伦勃朗还从拉斐尔无可挑剔的构图技法中获益良多。他研习了拉斐尔为梵蒂冈西斯廷教堂挂毯创作的十幅巨型草图复制品。当这些巨幅素描在布鲁塞尔展开时，彻底改变了四个世纪的挂毯编织艺术。 为再现如此宏大、富于明暗与圆润形态的画面[491]，佛兰德织工不得不摒弃传统明亮色块的平面铺陈，转而采用渐入阴影的沉郁色调。（织工们通过圆润的体量处理来应对新绘画的宽广空间——）

491 The Death of Ananias. Tapestry cartoon by Raphael, 1514-16
491 亚拿尼亚之死。拉斐尔绘制挂毯草图，1514-16 年
492 Chiaroscuro woodcut by Ugo da Carpi after Raphael
492 乌戈·达·卡尔皮根据拉斐尔原作创作的明暗对比法木刻版画
ing into depth until Jean Lurçat in 1939 revived the old, bright, flat splashes.) Raphael’s cartoons were translated more independently by Ugo da Carpi, whose color woodcuts simplified Raphael’s design into basic areas of tone [ 492 ] that conveyed the flat pattern to Rembrandt [493]. Rembrandt’s etching is reproduced
（直至 1939 年让·吕尔卡特复兴了古老而明快的平面泼彩技法。）乌戈·达·卡尔皮对拉斐尔的草图进行了更独立的演绎，其彩色木刻将拉斐尔的设计简化为基础色调区域[492]，将平面图案传递给了伦勃朗[493]。伦勃朗的蚀刻版画复制品如下：
493 Christ Preaching (La Petite Tombe). Etching by Rembrandt, about 1652. Reproduced in reverse
493 《基督布道》（小坟墓）。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，约 1652 年。反向复制

here in reverse, the way he drew it on the copper with one eye on the woodcut and a side glance at an engraving after a Raphael fresco for the attitude of Christ. Although he adapted the woodcut’s spotting, he confused Raphael’s precise placing of people on the floor, so that you cannot plot so clear a ground plan of the etching as you can of the woodcut. Rembrandt masked such ambiguities of position by blending figures in a thickness of air that makes his pictures more “real” than the Italian architectural construction. He pulls you into a circle of listeners so possessed by Christ’s utterance that nobody thinks of looking at his face. This portrait of a voice was made a few years after the supreme showpiece, the Hundred Guilder Print [483]. On this return to the theme of Christ’s ministry, Rembrandt had learned from Raphael to concentrate his drama with a simplification that looks inevitable.
在此处，他以反向手法创作：一边参照木刻版画，一边斜睨拉斐尔湿壁画的蚀刻复制品以捕捉基督的姿态。虽然他借鉴了木刻的斑点技法，却混淆了拉斐尔对人物在地面精确定位的处理，导致蚀刻版画无法像木刻那样清晰勾勒出地面平面图。 伦勃朗通过将人物融入浓厚的空气感中，掩盖了这种位置上的模糊性，使他的画作比意大利式的建筑构图更具"真实感"。他将观者引入听众的圆圈，众人如此沉醉于基督的言语，以至于无人想到要注视他的面容。这幅"声音肖像"创作于其巅峰之作《百盾版画》[483]之后的几年。 在重拾基督传道主题时，伦勃朗已从拉斐尔处领悟到：通过看似必然的简化来凝聚戏剧张力。
Figure 155: 494 Nude Man Reclining. Etching by Rembrandt, 1646
