Rembrandt’s figures (伦勃朗的人物形象)


No matter how many kinds of things Rembrandt drew, he never deserted that pivot of Western art, the human being. Unlike Michelangelo, obsessed by the muscular young man, Rembrandt, being an endless person, studied all ages and all conditions. As he developed he saw people as he saw everything else, in ever more subtle and complex relationships. He first etched small heads, then small figures in simple poses, sometimes tentatively grouped. Whereas most painters draw nudes when young, he etched almost all of his when he was 40 to 55 . His male models were certainly apprentices, who were everywhere expected to pose on warm days if they stripped passably [ 494 ]. Although Rembrandt painted two anatomical demonstrations, no drawings of dissections by him now
伦勃朗的人物形象无论伦勃朗描绘过多少种事物，他从未背离西方艺术的核心——人类。不同于痴迷于肌肉健壮的年轻人的米开朗基罗，作为一个永恒的存在者，伦勃朗研究了所有年龄段和所有境遇中的人。随着艺术造诣的提升，他看待人物的方式如同观察万物，在日益精妙复杂的关系中捕捉本质。他最初蚀刻小幅人头，继而创作简朴姿态的小型人物，偶尔尝试组合群像。 当多数画家在青年时期绘制裸体画时，他却在 40 至 55 岁间几乎完成了所有裸体蚀刻作品。他的男性模特无疑是学徒——在温暖的日子里，只要衣着得体，他们便被普遍要求担任模特[494]。尽管伦勃朗曾绘制过两幅解剖示范图，但现今已无他创作的解剖图手稿留存。
495
Bathers. Etching by Rembrandt, 1651
《沐浴者》。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1651 年

survive. The engineering of bone and muscle (Leonardo’s passion) probably interested him as little as the engineering of buildings. Provided a gesture or a vault looked convincing, it did not bother him if the arm was too short or the dome would collapse if built.
生存。骨骼与肌肉的构造（达·芬奇的挚爱）或许与建筑结构一样，都未能引起他的兴趣。只要某个姿势或拱顶看起来逼真，即便手臂过短或穹顶建成后会坍塌，他也不以为意。
The optical age of the baroque had no more optical painter than Rembrandt. While he was etching his last great landscapes, he took a copperplate to a swimming hole to sketch the bathers in the open air [ 495 ]. He saw them like Cézanne [719], as bodies fractured in dappled shade or obliterated in sunlight. No such etching occurs again until the 1880 s in France. From this noonday glimpse, Rembrandt could plunge deep into Giorgione’s twilight for the so-called Negress Lying Down [ 496 ], in a Venetian dusk compacted as thick as aspic with a skill that he
巴洛克的光学时代，再没有比伦勃朗更擅长光学绘画的画家。当他蚀刻最后一批伟大风景画时，竟带着铜版来到泳池边，在露天写生沐浴者[495]。他如塞尚[719]般凝视这些身影——或在斑驳树影中支离破碎，或在阳光下湮没无踪。 直至 1880 年代的法国，此类蚀刻技法才再度出现。从这正午的瞥见中，伦勃朗得以深入乔尔乔内笔下的暮色，创作出《卧着的黑人女子》[496]——在威尼斯黄昏的浓稠中，他以凝胶般的技艺将画面凝固得如冻肉般厚重。
496 “Negress Lying Down.” Etching by Rembrandt, 1658
496 《躺卧的黑人女子》。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1658 年

497
Abraham Sacrificing Isaac. Etching by Rembrandt, 1655
亚伯拉罕献以撒。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1655 年

498 (OPPOSITE PAGE, LEFT)
498（对页，左）

The Presentation “in the dark manner.” Detail of dark-manner etching by Rembrandt, 1654
《暗色调风格》的演示。伦勃朗 1654 年暗色调蚀刻版画细节

499

Christ Presented to the People. Detail of drypoint by Rembrandt, 1655
基督向民众显现。伦勃朗 1655 年干刻版画局部
alone commanded. It is hard enough to draw a thing to look round, but next to impossible to embed it in a shallow, yet palpable, deposit of air. To print the magic of such drypoint, Rembrandt wiped the copperplate with a touch almost as rare as the etching itself and printed it on Oriental papers that absorbed all the warm ink into their creamy softness. The woman lies in counterswings of hip and shoulder like the Venus that Velázquez was then painting in Madrid, also under Venetian influence.
独自掌控。要勾勒出环顾四周的物体已属不易，更遑论将其嵌入浅薄却可触及的空气沉积层中。为呈现这种干刻版画的魔力，伦勃朗以近乎与蚀刻技法本身同样罕见的轻触擦拭铜版，再将其印制于东方纸张上——柔滑如奶油的纸张将所有暖色墨汁尽数吸纳。 女子的臀与肩呈反向摇曳姿态，宛若委拉斯开兹当时在马德里创作的维纳斯——那幅同样受威尼斯风格影响的作品。
Italian prints showed Rembrandt how to entwine Abraham, Isaac, and the angel [ 497 ] in a human column as intricately linked as Giovanni Bologna’s marble Rape of the Sabines, published in 1584 through three woodcuts. Rembrandt’s expressive invention was to cover the boy’s face so that the shivering of his ribs makes us also suffer the gooseflesh of martyrdom. Thus a veteran actor conveys the pang of a crisis by turning his back on the audience.
意大利版画让伦勃朗学会将亚伯拉罕、以撒与天使[497]交织成人类柱体，其错综复杂的关联性堪比乔瓦尼·博洛尼亚 1584 年通过三幅木刻版画发表的《萨宾妇女被劫》大理石雕塑。 伦勃朗的艺术创新在于遮蔽男孩的面容，使他肋骨的颤动令观者亦能感受到殉道者鸡皮疙瘩般的痛苦。这恰似资深演员背对观众传递危机时刻的剧痛。
Rembrandt’s mastery of figure drawing appears most vividly in enlargements of details so tiny that he must have drawn them under a magnifying glass. This painter of wall-size dramas could also work like a gem engraver on heads that would not cover your thumbnail. On any scale it would be hard to find a face more expressive than old Simeon’s at the temple when he holds the Christ child in his arms and says: “Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace according to thy word, for mine eyes have seen thy salvation” [ 498 ]. When Rembrandt scratched
伦勃朗对人物素描的掌控力，在那些微小细节的放大图中展现得最为生动——这些细节如此细微，他必定是在放大镜下绘制的。这位擅长描绘巨幅画作的画家，也能像宝石雕刻师般精雕细琢那些连拇指甲盖都盖不住的头颅。无论在何种尺度下，都难觅比圣殿中老西缅更富表现力的面容：当他怀抱基督圣婴时，如此说道： "主啊，如今可以照你的话，释放仆人安然去世；因为我的眼睛已经看见你的救恩"[498]。当伦勃朗刻画


hairlines through the etching ground, he had to calculate just how much the ragged bite of the acid would thicken them. He shaded behind the two heads with the tapering straight lines of the graver. The next year he achieved equal character in as small a head that he incised into the hard metal itself with the jerky, slipping, stiff drypoint needle [ 499 ]. Arresting as these details are when enlarged and isolated, they project even more drama in their setting, where, unlike Dürer’s ostentatious particularities, Rembrandt’s details blend like musicians in an orchestra pulling together for an overmastering effect.
蚀刻底料上的发丝般细线，他必须精确计算酸蚀的参差咬痕会使线条增粗多少。他用刻刀尖端画出渐细的直线，在两个头颅后方勾勒出阴影。 次年，他以干刻针在坚硬金属上刻出同样精微的小型头像——针尖时而跳跃滑动，时而僵直停滞[499]。这些细节在放大孤立时已足够震撼，置于整体构图中更显戏剧张力：不同于丢勒炫技般的局部特写，伦勃朗的细节如交响乐团般浑然交融，共同营造出压倒性的艺术效果。

Rembrandt’s landscapes (伦勃朗的风景画)


In two bursts, during his late 305 and mid-40s, Rembrandt etched some 24 landscapes that influenced etchers after they were reproduced by photogravure in the 1860s and 70s. His view of Amsterdam [500] may be the earliest of the group, since it seems the most factual. Yet it is so far from
伦勃朗的风景画在 30 多岁末期和 40 多岁中期，伦勃朗分两次创作了约 24 幅风景蚀刻版画。这些作品在 1860 至 70 年代经照相凹版印刷复制后，对后世蚀刻艺术家产生了深远影响。其中《阿姆斯特丹风光》[500]或许是该系列最早的作品，因其写实风格最为鲜明。然而这幅作品却远离——
500
Amsterdam. Etching by Rembrandt, about 1640
阿姆斯特丹。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，约 1640 年
Rembrandt’s landscapes  伦勃朗的风景画
being a postcard record that Rembrandt deleted one church tower and etched the rest as he saw them on the horizon, thus making them print in reverse order. He suggested the depth that he strove for in all picture-making without resorting to the traditional framing uprights, like stage wings, to push back the center. Instead, the Dutch bogs dictated the horizontal foreground of rough sedges, the most insistent foreground in all his etched landscapes, that stretches a starting line from which the marsh river winds deep in.
这幅明信片式的版画记录了伦勃朗如何删除一座教堂塔楼，并将其余塔楼按地平线上所见原样蚀刻，从而使它们以倒序呈现。他以此展现了在所有绘画创作中追求的深度，却未借助传统框架立柱——如同舞台侧翼般——来推后画面中心。 取而代之的是荷兰沼泽地决定了粗粝莎草构成的水平前景——这是他所有蚀刻风景画中最突出的前景元素，它延伸出一条起始线，沼泽河流由此蜿蜒深入。
About five years later Rembrandt subtly varied the old stage-wing layout in the Omval, a spit of land on the Amstel [501]. With an art concealing art, he spaced milestones horizonward from the tree so close that it overruns a third of the picture, balancing the black stump to make a gate opening in to the back of the man who stares out across the rowboat to the diminishing windmills. The eye travels
约莫五年后，伦勃朗在《奥姆瓦尔》中微妙地调整了原有的舞台侧翼构图——该画作描绘了阿姆斯特尔河畔的狭长陆地[501]。 他以画中画之技法，将地标沿地平线从树木处向外延伸，使之占据画面近三分之一，与黑色树桩形成平衡，形成一道通向背景的门扉——画面中男子凝视着划向远方的独木舟，风车渐行渐远。视线由此流转
501 The Omval. Etching by Rembrandt, 1645
501 《奥姆瓦尔》。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1645 年

over lines patterned for surprise after surprise. The summer sky is clear, as Rembrandt always etched it except in visions of unstable weather.
层层叠叠的纹路，惊喜接踵而至。夏日晴空万里，正如伦勃朗笔下永恒的刻画，唯独在描绘多变天气的幻象时例外。
In the more sensitive of his two stormy landscapes [502] the coming squall generates energy on the left where gusts tousle trees, ruffling a restless surface over a stolid substructure. Rightward, the blast dissipates in lesser contrasts, dying out in a sunny, still orchard. The foreground posts and hedge drive into the oncoming wind. All these intricate and possibly instinctive calculations manage to look “real” in this glimpse of a passing turbulence that Rembrandt developed in his studio like a photographer bringing out a latent image.
在他两幅暴风雨风景画中更富表现力的一幅[502]里，即将袭来的狂风在画面左侧积聚能量，疾风肆虐的树木撩动着沉稳基底之上那片躁动的水面。 右侧，狂风在较弱的对比中消散，最终在阳光明媚的静谧果园里归于沉寂。前景的木桩与树篱迎风挺立。所有这些精妙而或许本能的构图计算，使这瞬息即逝的湍流景象显得如此"真实"——正如摄影师显影暗藏的影像般，伦勃朗在画室里精心呈现了这般景象。
Even when Rembrandt left the sky blank, he still saw it as an ocean of air cresting over the sediment of Holland, the way it appears in a view of Rhenen [503] once attributed to Seghers. This print must have inspired one of Rembrandt’s most
即便伦勃朗将天空留白，他仍视其为气流之海，翻涌于荷兰沉积地貌之上——正如塞赫斯曾被归功的《莱嫩风光》[503]所呈现的景象。这幅版画必曾启迪了伦勃朗最杰出的作品之一。
502 Trees, Farm Buildings, and Tower. Etching by Rembrandt, about 1650
502 棵树、农舍与塔楼。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，约 1650 年
original landscapes [ 504 ], known as the Goldweigher’s Field because it was formerly thought to represent the estate of a Receiver General near Amsterdam. It is the only landscape in all art that wheels under the drive of invisible wind around a pivot on the horizon, as level lands seem to wheel when watched from a fast train. Only Rembrandt could have perceived such a turning from the crawl of a horse or coach. Since the tufts of drypoint to right and left are needed to push back the horizon and to revolve the plain, this print must be seen in one of the few early impressions before the burr wore down.
原始风景画[504]，因曾被认为描绘阿姆斯特丹附近总收税官的庄园而得名"金衡师田野"。这是艺术史上唯一一幅在无形之风驱动下，围绕地平线枢轴旋转的风景画——正如从疾驰列车上眺望时，平坦的土地仿佛在旋转。 唯有伦勃朗能从马车缓行中捕捉到这般旋转感。由于左右两侧的干刻点缀需用于后退地平线并旋转平原，此版画必须观赏于早期印本——在毛刺磨平之前。
During Rembrandt’s mid-40s, human beings crowded out pure landscape as a subject for etching, forcing him to seek scenery that would merge with large fore-
伦勃朗四十多岁时，人类逐渐取代纯粹风景成为蚀刻画的主体，迫使他寻求能与前景大景融为一体的景致——
Figure 156: 503 Rhenen. Etching by Hercules Seghers or Jan Reuscher
图 156：503 雷嫩。赫拉克勒斯·塞赫斯或扬·雷乌舍尔蚀刻版画
ground figures. The Dutch flats-the only landscape that he habitually walked inebbed too fast behind a figure, abandoning it to rise solitarily into the sky. This problem led him to rework the Seghers plate of Tobias and the Angel [ 443, 444 ], where hills such as he rarely or never saw support and surround most of the bodies. He reduced Seghers’ giants to the modest Holy Family to try blending people into nature. Though his inserted drypoint segregates itself from the original etching, his experiment at least showed that sizable figures can be made to sink into a landscape if it is hilly. Feeling that steeper and more interesting hills would do even better, Rembrandt went to drawings and woodcuts that Titian and Domenico Campagnola had made when they ferried from Venice and were surprised by the abruptness of uplands. A year or so after he had reworked the Seghers plate, he dreamed a high bluff in the Venetian manner, topped it with an ominous lodge and a dumpy
地面人物。荷兰平原——他惯常漫步的唯一景致——总在人物身后迅速消退，任其孤零零地升入天空。这一问题促使他重新创作塞赫斯的《托比亚斯与天使》版画[443,444]，其中罕见或从未见过的丘陵环抱并支撑着多数人物。他将塞赫斯的巨人缩减为朴素的圣家，试图让人与自然融为一体。 尽管他插入的干刻版画与原蚀刻版画存在割裂感，但这项实验至少证明：若采用丘陵地形，大型人物形象确实能融入风景。深感陡峭而富于变化的山丘效果更佳，伦勃朗转而研究提香与多梅尼科·坎帕尼奥拉乘船从威尼斯出发时所绘的素描与木刻——他们曾被高地骤然升起的景象所震撼。 在重制《渔夫》版画约一年后，他构想出一座威尼斯风格的陡峭悬崖，崖顶矗立着阴森的守望小屋与矮胖的
504 The Goldweigher’s Field (actually Haarlem). Etching by Rembrandt, 1651
504 《黄金秤量师的田地》（实为哈勒姆）。伦勃朗蚀刻版画，1651 年

abbey [505], and linked this backdrop to old Saint Jerome in the foreground through the diagonal lion, who stares into the distance like the man in the middle of the Omval. If it is possible to guess whatever flashed an artist’s magical first glimpse, this lion provided the lucky spark that ignited the whole vision. Observing the feline S-curve, Rembrandt then crossed it with the slanting tree and the spill of rock to make a huge X X XX. He next started the procession into depth with the lion’s tail-light against dark-that pulls the wraith of a hermit backward in a diagonal prowl traveling toward the lion’s head-dark against light-where the secret eyes glare across the valley with enough of an expulsion to clear an upward blank into the far hill. Rembrandt unified these intuitions and recalls by spotting a light that is impossible yet inevitable; dream-nothing but dream-yet more deeply experienced than anything your window shows you. More than any other artist (Picasso included), Rembrandt compromised neither with verisimilitude nor with its enemy, the distortions of his imperious individuality, but grasped both together in a tension trembling with life.
修道院[505]，并通过斜卧的雄狮将这片背景与前景中的圣杰罗姆联系起来——雄狮凝视远方的姿态，恰似奥姆瓦尔中央人物的凝望。若能揣测艺术家灵光乍现的瞬间，这头雄狮便是点燃整个构图的幸运火花。 观察到猫科动物的 S 形曲线后，伦勃朗将其与倾斜的树木和倾泻的岩石交织，形成巨大的 X X XX 。 他接着以暗影中的狮子尾光为起点，引领画面向深处延伸——那尾光牵引着隐士的幽影，以斜向匍匐姿态向狮首暗影处移动。暗影与光交织之处，那双秘藏的眼睛横越山谷怒目而视，其驱逐之力足以在远山之上开辟一片向上延伸的空白。 伦勃朗将这些直觉与记忆熔铸为一体，点亮了那道不可能却又必然的光；纯粹的梦境——却比窗外所见更深刻。他超越了所有艺术家（包括毕加索），既不妥协于逼真性，也不屈从于其对立面——他凌厉个性造成的扭曲，而是将二者在颤动着生命力的张力中融为一体。

505

St. Jerome in an Italian Landscape. Etching and drypoint by Rembrandt, about 1653
圣杰罗姆在意大利风景中。伦勃朗蚀刻版画与干刻版画，约 1653 年


Rembrandt’s contemporaries (伦勃朗的同代人)


Rembrandt illuminated a whole generation of artists who fluoresced-some more, some less-in his brilliance. Many benefited from seeing how painting and printmaking quickened his vision by alternating tools and problems. Rembrandt’s youthful etchings served as models for his contemporaries, but as he grew older, he became inimitable. His early hold on his time appears in the work of Ostade, who lived all his life in Haarlem, was taught by Frans Hals, and yet etched like Rembrandt before Rembrandt began to use drypoint. Ostade etched from his mid-zos until after the master’s death without show-
伦勃朗的同代艺术家们伦勃朗照亮了整整一代艺术家，他们在他的光芒中绽放——或明或暗。许多人受益于观察到绘画与版画如何通过交替运用工具与解决问题来激发他的艺术视野。 伦勃朗早期的蚀刻版画成为同时代人的范本，但随着年岁增长，他的艺术已臻不可复制之境。他早期对时代的掌控力，在奥斯塔德的作品中可见一斑——这位终生定居哈勒姆的画家虽师从弗朗斯·哈尔斯，其蚀刻技法却早于伦勃朗运用干刻技法之前便已媲美大师。奥斯塔德从三十多岁起持续创作蚀刻版画直至大师逝世，其技艺始终不显浮夸。
507
The Bull. Etching by Paul Potter, 1650
公牛。保罗·波特蚀刻版画，1650 年
Figure 157: 508 The Traveler. Etching by Jacob Ruisdael
图 157：508《旅行者》。雅各布·鲁伊斯达尔蚀刻版画
ing that he ever saw the late Rembrandt etchings that we prize most. Avoiding religious subjects, Ostade depicted beggars, peasants, and artisans. His painter [506] glances from the plaster muscle man on the shelf to the open book of emblems or personifications beside his easel, the two sources of the baroque artist’s erudition in anatomy and allegory. Ostade’s command of the difficulties of rendering full shadow is apparent only in the early states of his etchings before his coppers, like Rembrandt’s, were reworked during two centuries of reprinting.
他从未见过我们最珍视的伦勃朗晚期蚀刻版画。奥斯塔德避开宗教题材，描绘乞丐、农民和工匠。他的画家[506]目光从架子上的石膏肌肉模型移向画架旁摊开的象征图鉴，这两者正是巴洛克艺术家解剖学与寓言知识的源泉。 奥斯塔德驾驭浓重阴影的功力，仅在其蚀刻版画的早期版本中显露无遗——如同伦勃朗的铜版画，这些作品在两个世纪的重印过程中均被反复修饰。
Paul Potter’s etchings, like Ostade’s, were prized in the 18th century. Potter and many other Dutch etchers of farm animals took their hint from Lucas of Leiden’s Milkmaid [ 332 ]. Before Potter died at 29, he had founded the Dutch animal school with his clear and determined studies of cows, sculpturally defining their hard pelts, wet snouts, and pendulousness slung under a ramshackle scaffolding of bones [ 507 ].
保罗·波特的蚀刻版画与奥斯塔德的作品一样，在 18 世纪备受推崇。 波特与众多描绘农场动物的荷兰蚀刻艺术家，都从莱顿的卢卡斯《挤奶女工》[332]中汲取灵感。这位艺术家在 29 岁离世前，已凭借其对牛的清晰而坚定的研究开创了荷兰动物画派——他以雕塑般的笔触刻画出牛只坚硬的皮毛、湿润的鼻吻，以及悬垂于摇摇欲坠的骨架下的赘肉[507]。
Potter’s followers were mostly Dutch, but Jacob Ruisdael’s dozen etchings [508] set the style for many 18th- and 19th-century artists, especially in Norwich and Barbizon. Though he etched in his later 20s, the melancholy of his old age already announces itself in the crabbed scratching that has more character than any landscape etchings except Rembrandt’s and Seghers’.
波特的大多数追随者来自荷兰，但雅各布·鲁伊斯达尔的十二幅蚀刻版画[508]为 18、19 世纪众多艺术家奠定了风格基调，尤其在诺里奇和巴比松地区影响深远。 尽管他创作蚀刻版画时年仅二十余岁，暮年的忧郁已然显露于那些蹩脚的刻痕中——这些刻痕所蕴含的个性，仅次于伦勃朗和塞赫斯的景观蚀刻版画。

509 The Resurrection of Lazarus. Etching by Jan Lievens
509 拉撒路的复活。扬·利文斯蚀刻版画510 Man in Armchair. Woodcut by Lievens
510 坐扶手椅的男子。利文斯木刻版画

While Ruisdael and Ostade knew Rembrandt’s art more than his person, Jan Lievens began by sitting beside Rembrandt to draw the same model in the same pose. Lievens, only a year younger, was not a pupil but an associate, with more taste and suavity than Rembrandt himself then possessed [ 509 ]. In his late 205 Lievens went for six years to Antwerp, where he fell in with local custom by engraving instead of etching. Christoffel Jegher, who was there cutting woodblocks for Rubens [430], may have started Lievens making the only woodcuts of the Rembrandt circle [ 510 ]. Lievens must have cut his own blocks to achieve such splintery spontaneity and the first rendering in woodcut of textures like wood and velvet. His experiment in a new medium energized a fluctuating talent with a force of personality that did not reappear in woodcutting until Blake’s Virgil illustrations of 1821 [ 610 ].
虽然鲁伊斯达尔和奥斯塔德对伦勃朗的艺术造诣了解甚深，却对其为人知之甚少，但扬·利文斯最初便是坐在伦勃朗身旁，以相同姿势描绘同一位模特。利文斯仅比伦勃朗小一岁，虽非其门生却堪称同行，其审美品味与优雅气质更胜伦勃朗当时所具[509]。 二十五岁末，利文斯赴安特卫普旅居六年，为顺应当地习俗，他转而从事雕刻而非蚀刻。当时为鲁本斯制作木刻版画的克里斯托弗·耶赫[430]，或许正是引导利文斯创作伦勃朗画派唯一木刻版画的启蒙者[510]。 为实现木刻中木纹与天鹅绒质感的首次呈现，以及那种充满木屑感的即兴效果，利文斯必然亲手雕刻了版材。这种媒介创新激发了他起伏不定的才华，赋予其鲜明个性——直至 1821 年布莱克为《维吉尔》创作插图时，木刻艺术才再度涌现这般力量[610]。

Mezzotint (半平版蚀刻法)


To print shadows as subtle as those in 17th-century painting required the wizardry of a Rembrandt. Even to approximate them, an engraver had to be as skillful as Goudt [ 442 ]. Then the discovery of mezzotint-"halftone"suddenly opened the full range from black to white to any dullard. Its fuzzy tone without line excludes personal “handwriting” but aptly matches the gradations of oil paintings, making mezzotint the one print process that takes its character exclusively from painting. The process was invented by a half-German, half-Spanish soldier, Ludwig von Siegen, who experimented in Amsterdam while Rembrandt was discovering how to etch shadows trailing behind figures. By 1642 von Siegen was rolling a spiky roulette over copper wherever he wanted a roughness to catch a tone of ink, which amounts to a localized mezzotint [ 511 ].
要印出如十七世纪绘画般细腻的阴影，需具备伦勃朗般的魔术般技艺。即便只是近似地表现，刻版师也必须拥有古特[442]那般精湛的技艺。 随后凹版雕刻术——"半色调"技术的诞生，让任何笨拙者都能轻松驾驭从纯黑到纯白的完整色谱。这种无轮廓线条的朦胧色调虽排除了个人"笔触"，却精准复刻了油画的渐变层次，使凹版雕刻成为唯一完全承袭绘画特质的版画工艺。 这项工艺由德西混血军人路德维希·冯·齐根发明。当伦勃朗探索人物背影阴影蚀刻技法时，冯·齐根正在阿姆斯特丹进行实验。到 1642 年，他已能通过在铜版特定区域滚压带刺滚轮制造粗糙纹理，从而捕捉墨色层次——这实质上是局部凹版雕刻技法[511]。
In 1657 another soldier, Prince Rupert of the Palatinate, perfected von Siegen’s invention by rocking a curved saw edge to roughen an entire plate with prickles like a file that catch ink in an allover black [512]. To make highlights, he then scraped off some of the prickles with a knife and burnished the copper smooth. If he happened to scrape any part too light, he redarkened it by roughing it again. Since the plate was roughened by an apprentice, and later by a clockwork rocker,
1657 年，另一位军人——普法尔茨的鲁珀特亲王——完善了冯·齐根的发明：他摇动弯曲的锯齿边缘，使整个铜版表面布满锉刀般的刺状凸起，这些凸起能均匀地吸附墨水形成整体黑色[512]。 为呈现高光效果，他用刀刮除部分凸起，再将铜版抛光平滑。若某处刮削过度导致过亮，则重新粗化该区域以恢复深色。由于铜版最初由学徒粗化，后由发条摇动装置完成粗化，

the mezzotinter achieved full black and white faster than any other printmaker. The speed of the scraping more than compensated for the small number of good impressions that could be printed from the fast-wearing prickles. In 1660 Prince Rupert took mezzotint to the court of his first cousin, Charles II of England, where the court painter, Godfrey Kneller, promoted it to fill the gap left by the provinciality of English engraving. English painting, often darker than Continental painting, proved ideal for the imported process.
凹版雕刻师比其他任何版画家都更快地实现了纯粹的黑白效果。刮刻速度之快，完全弥补了因刻针磨损过快而导致的优质印张数量稀少的问题。1660 年，鲁珀特亲王将凹版雕刻术带到其堂兄英格兰国王查理二世的宫廷，宫廷画家戈弗雷·克内勒大力推广此技法，填补了英国雕版画因地方性局限造成的空白。 英国绘画风格常较欧洲大陆作品更为深沉，恰与这种引进的工艺相得益彰。
The “dark manner” became famous as the “English manner” when mezzotint rose with the rise of Sir Joshua Reynolds, who, on returning from Italy in 1753, began to give it the breadth of effect that painters always give to printmaking. When English mezzotints decorated a room as effectively as small paintings, all Europe and North America bought English “fancy subjects” as well as portraits of writers, painters, and solid, handsome gentry. English portraits demonstrated that a lady could look like a lady just as she is [ 513 ], without dressing her up as Flora or Diana, and contemporary events could be portrayed in perukes as solemnly as in togas. Baroque drama was running out of imagination. The coming factual view of the world produced some of the most fascinating “fancy pieces” in mezzotints after paintings by Wright of Derby, the first important English painter who refused to move to London. His pictures of scientific experiments and mill machinery made him the pictorial prophet of the Industrial Revolution [ 514 ]. Just before the inven-
当凹版雕刻技艺随着乔舒亚·雷诺兹爵士的崛起而兴盛时，"暗调风格"便以"英式风格"之名闻名于世。1753 年，雷诺兹从意大利归来后，开始赋予这种技艺与油画相媲美的表现力。 当英国凹版蚀刻版画能像小型油画般有效装饰房间时，整个欧洲和北美都争相购买英国"奇趣题材"作品，以及作家、画家和稳重英俊的乡绅肖像。英国肖像画证明：贵妇无需扮作花神或狩猎女神，本真姿态便足以彰显淑女风范；而假发时代的当代事件，亦能如古罗马长袍时期般庄重地呈现。 巴洛克戏剧正陷入想象力枯竭。即将到来的写实世界观催生了最迷人的凹版画"奇趣题材"——这些作品源自德比郡赖特的画作。这位首位拒绝迁居伦敦的重要英国画家，其描绘科学实验与磨坊机械的画作使他成为工业革命的视觉先知[514]。就在发明——

tion of photography rivaled some of the effects of mezzotint with instant ease, David Lucas, a farmhand, learned printmaking at age 19 and became the most painterly of all mezzotinters. In his 30 s he scraped some 40 landscapes after paintings by Constable, working on the steel plates that had been introduced in 1823 to
摄影术的诞生令 mezzotint 版画技法黯然失色，其效果却能轻松即时呈现。农场工人戴维·卢卡斯 19 岁时习得版画技艺，最终成为所有 mezzotint 艺术家中最具绘画风格的代表。三十岁时，他根据康斯塔布尔的画作创作了约 40 幅风景版画，使用的是 1823 年问世的钢版进行制作。
Figure 158: 515 Noon. Mezzotint by David Lucas after John Constable, 1830

yield more impressions than copper. Lucas submitted as many as 13 trial proofs for Constable to correct with black lead and white paint until the plate finally captured the sparkle of raindrops in a sunny breeze [515]. Though Constable said that “Lucas showed me to the public without my faults,” these glimpses of fresh weather, too small for ornamenting a wall, were ignored in the excitement over photography. They cost Constable £ 700 £ 700 £700£ 700 and left Lucas to die in the poorhouse.
比铜版更能呈现生动的视觉效果。卢卡斯提交了多达 13 张试印样张，供康斯特勃用黑铅笔和白色颜料反复修改，直至印版最终捕捉到阳光微风中雨滴的闪烁[515]。 尽管康斯特布尔称"卢卡斯让我以无瑕之姿展现在公众面前"，这些清新天气的瞬间却因尺寸过小无法装饰墙面，在摄影热潮中遭人忽视。它们耗尽了康斯特布尔的 £ 700 £ 700 £700£ 700 ，更让卢卡斯最终死于济贫院。

Central Italian etchers (意大利中部蚀刻版画家)


Shortly before 1600, Italian etching-both for the connoisseur and for the folk peddler-gravitated to Bologna, where the three Car-racci-two brothers and a cousin-found time to make prints while painting with a blend of Florentine drawing and Venetian color. Agostino Carracci [ 410 ] engraved too much to belong to Parmigiano’s tradition of painter-etchers. His brother Annibale, the strongest painter of the three, was also the strongest etcher [ 516 ]. He taught his command of form and large design to Guido Reni, who joined the Carracci’s Academy and inherited their leadership in Bologna. Many of Reni’s followers also made pretty, open-line etchings of Madonnas, Holy Families, and cupids, inspired by a piety whose undoubted sincerity escapes us today. These little devotional images are saved from sentimentality by the healthy Italian love for any young mother and her child [517]. Such popular prints, rather than Bolognese paintings, carried the sweet and intimate aspect of the Italian baroque into France and Spain, prolonging its grace into the 18th century.
意大利中部蚀刻艺术家 1600 年前后，意大利蚀刻艺术——无论面向鉴赏家还是民间小贩——都汇聚于博洛尼亚。卡拉奇家族的三位成员——两兄弟与一位堂兄弟——在创作绘画时，将佛罗伦萨的素描技法与威尼斯的色彩运用相融合，同时抽身进行版画创作。 阿戈斯蒂诺·卡拉奇[410]因版画创作过多，未能归入帕尔米贾尼诺开创的画家版画家传统。其兄安尼巴莱作为三兄弟中最杰出的画家，亦是版画造诣最深者[516]。他将对形态与大构图的掌控力传授给圭多·雷尼——后者加入卡拉奇画派，继承了他们在博洛尼亚的领导地位。 雷尼的众多追随者也创作了许多优美、线条开放的圣母、圣家和丘比特蚀刻版画，其灵感源于一种虔诚——这种虔诚的真诚性，如今我们已难以体会。这些小型的宗教图像之所以免于矫揉造作，得益于意大利人对年轻母亲及其孩子的健康热爱[517]。 正是这类通俗版画，而非博洛尼亚绘画，将意大利巴洛克甜美而亲密的韵味传入法国和西班牙，使其优雅气质延续至十八世纪。
Near Bologna, Guercino sketched only twice on copper [ 518 ], but with all the flow and spirit of the quill drawings that brought him his greatest fame after his
在博洛尼亚附近，盖尔奇诺仅在铜板上素描过两次[518]，但笔触流畅灵动，尽显鹅毛笔素描的精髓——正是这种技法使他在去世后声名大噪。
death released them to the world. He luckily etched with the young, full-blown abandon that he was persuaded to repress for conformity to academic taste. The most violent Italian painter-etcher was Pietro Testa. Like many Tuscans, Testa settled in Rome-not, however, for papal money but for his interest in archeology. He reconstructed paroxysms of antique brutality [519] with details as exactly documented as Mantegna’s or Piranesi’s. But poor Testa, lacking Piranesi’s productive drive to live, drowned himself in the Tiber.
死亡将他们释放到世间。他幸运地刻画出年轻时那种饱满奔放的放纵，这种特质曾被劝说压抑以迎合学院派的审美。 最狂暴的意大利画家兼蚀刻师当属彼得罗·泰斯塔。与许多托斯卡纳人相似，泰斯塔定居罗马——但并非为教廷金钱，而是出于对考古学的热忱。他以媲美曼特尼亚或皮拉内西的考据精度，复原了古罗马暴虐时代的痉挛性场景[519]。可悲的泰斯塔却缺乏皮拉内西那般以创作维生的生命驱动力，最终在台伯河中溺亡。

Meanwhile, Florence produced the most exported Italian etcher of the age in Stefano della Bella, who was 11 when Callot left there to go home to Nancy. Della Bella learned from Callot’s pupils to etch with French precision and mordancy [520] and to be a specialist etcher instead of a painter who etched on the side, like many Italians. He was also the first influential printmaker who did not cater to piety; of his over 1000 plates, only 28 were made on religious themes for the French market. Della Bella’s etching took on a richer tone from Rembrandt when he spent the decade of his zos in Paris. There, where he had more followers than at home, he passed on his picturesque command of ornament [ 521 ] to Lepautre [ 538 ]. Callot and della Bella were the first to etch their personal fantasies as offerings for collectors’ portfolios. (A decade or so later, Poussin became the first painter to work less on specific commissions than on his own for possible sale.) The print, traditionally a recipient of prayers and a go-between of information, thus also became an esthetic commodity, as it now is exclusively. Della Bella was the last artistic creator in Florence until Giovanni Fattori [ 682 ] in the 1860s. In fact, after the death of Caravaggio in 1609, Italian painters and printmakers innovated less than Bernini and Borromini did in their sculpture and architecture. Italy had by then trained Netherlanders, Frenchmen, and Spaniards to explore fresh ways in drawing, painting, and printmaking.
与此同时，佛罗伦萨孕育了当时最负盛名的意大利蚀刻版画家斯特凡诺·德拉·贝拉——卡洛特离开该城返回纳西时，他年仅十一岁。德拉·贝拉师承卡洛特的门徒，以法式精准与犀利笔触精研蚀刻技艺[520]，成为专职蚀刻版画家，而非像多数意大利同行那样兼作绘画。 他还是首位不迎合宗教题材的有影响力的版画家：其千余幅版画中，仅有 28 幅为法国市场创作的宗教题材。三十岁那年旅居巴黎期间，德拉贝拉的蚀刻技法从伦勃朗处汲取了更丰富的色调。在巴黎——那里追随者远多于故乡——他将自己对装饰性画面[521]的掌控力传授给勒普特尔 [538]。卡洛与德拉贝拉率先将个人幻想蚀刻成版画，作为收藏家作品集的献礼。（约十年后，普桑成为首位更专注创作可售作品而非特定委托的画家。）版画由此从传统祈祷载体与信息媒介，蜕变为纯粹的美学商品——这正是其当代定位。 在 1860 年代乔瓦尼·法托里[682]出现之前，德拉·贝拉是佛罗伦萨最后一位艺术创作者。事实上，自 1609 年卡拉瓦乔逝世后，意大利画家与版画家在创新上的突破，远不及贝尔尼尼和博罗米尼在雕塑与建筑领域的成就。彼时意大利已培养出众多荷兰、法国及西班牙艺术家，引领着素描、绘画与版画艺术的革新之路。

Italy and Rembrandt (意大利与伦勃朗)


In the 1600s Italy’s traditional centers of painting turned to innovating in other fields-Venice creating dramatic music, Padua and Bologna exploring physiology, and Florence, through Galileo, founding modern physics. But in Naples and Genoa, weaker artistic traditions left natives open to foreign influences. Caravaggio’s months in Naples in 1607/08 helped to darken Neapolitan painting in a dramatic manner that a Spanish follower brought to Valencia, there forming José Ribera as a Caravaggist even before he settled in Naples at the age of 28 .
意大利与伦勃朗 17 世纪时，意大利传统绘画中心纷纷转向其他领域的创新——威尼斯开创了戏剧性音乐，帕多瓦与博洛尼亚探索人体生理学，佛罗伦萨则通过伽利略奠定了现代物理学基础。但在那不勒斯和热那亚，较弱的艺术传统使当地人更易接受外来影响。 卡拉瓦乔 1607 至 1608 年间在那不勒斯的数月驻留，以戏剧性手法深化了当地绘画的暗色基调。其西班牙追随者将此风格带至瓦伦西亚，使何塞·里贝拉在 28 岁定居那不勒斯前，便已成长为卡拉瓦乔画派的代表人物。
In Naples, Spain had dominated so long that Ribera continued to live among Spaniards who satirized each other and cut Olympus down to their own size. His irreverent Silenus [ 522 ] appeared the year when Rembrandt’s first dated etching began his experiments toward the dramatic contrasts of black and white that Ribera had already achieved. With a control of form that harks back to Mantegna, Ribera modeled shadows around a glare of light as though he wielded a brush instead of a needle. Although he etched as powerfully as any of Rembrandt’s contemporaries, his etchings have remained unpopular because of the harsh particularity of his satyrs-all bone and tendon-his blown-up drunkards, and his dried-out old men. As his legacy to students, Ribera etched studies of heads in one of the few vigorously drawn manuals of drawing [ 523 ].
在西班牙长期统治下的那不勒斯，里贝拉始终生活在西班牙人中间——他们互相讽刺，将神圣的奥林匹斯山贬低到与自己平起平坐的程度。他那部不敬的《西勒诺斯》[522]问世之年，伦勃朗首幅标注年份的蚀刻版画正开启其黑白对比的戏剧性探索，而里贝拉早已驾驭了这种技法。 里贝拉对光影的掌控令人联想到曼特尼亚，他以光影交织塑造阴影，仿佛执笔而非刻针。 尽管其蚀刻技法与伦勃朗同时代人同样精湛，但因作品中刻画的酒神舞者——骨骼与筋腱清晰可见——以及膨胀的醉汉与干瘪老人等刻薄特质，其蚀刻作品始终不受欢迎。作为留给学生的遗产，里贝拉在少数几部笔触强劲的绘画教程[523]中刻画了人头素描研究。
522 Silenus. Etching by José Ribera, 1628
522 西勒诺斯。何塞·里贝拉蚀刻版画，1628 年
523 Drawing exercise. Etching by Ribera
523 素描练习。里贝拉的蚀刻版画

Ribera’s most independent pupil was a native Neapolitan, Salvator Rosa. As the last Italian artist who aspired to the Renaissance ideal of the universal man, Rosa painted, etched, wrote poems and plays, acted, and made scenery in his private theater. He invented the romantic landscape of crags and gullies as stage sets for hermits, brigands, and violent heroes [ 524 ]. He set attitudes for French and English romantics in 1775 to 1825 through his most imitated works in any medium-a drawing book in 62 etchings of volatile soldiers who brag, strut with spears, and plunge their heads into their desperate hands [ 525 ].
里贝拉最独立的弟子是土生土长的那不勒斯人萨尔瓦托·罗萨。作为最后一位追求文艺复兴时期"通才"理想的意大利艺术家，罗萨既绘画又刻版，既写诗又写剧本，既演戏又为私人剧院制作布景。他创造了由嶙峋岩壁与蜿蜒沟壑构成的浪漫风景，作为隐士、强盗和暴力英雄的舞台背景[524]。 1775 至 1825 年间，他通过其最广为模仿的跨媒介作品——一本收录 62 幅蚀刻画的素描集——确立了法英浪漫主义者的艺术风范。画中狂放不羁的士兵们或夸夸其谈，或持矛昂首阔步，或将头埋入绝望的双手[525]。
After Rembrandt absorbed Ribera’s demonstration of painterly etching, the results returned to Italy through Benedetto Castiglione [526], Rembrandt’s junior by ten years, who grew up in Genoa while Van Dyck was there painting the first vast portraits with palatial backgrounds. Castiglione’s asps, skulls, broken columns, and toppled urns assembled the paraphernalia of evanescence for G. B. Tiepolo and the whole 18th century. He may never have seen a painting by Rembrandt,
伦勃朗吸收了里贝拉的绘画蚀刻技法后，这些成果通过比他小十岁的贝内代托·卡斯蒂廖内[526]传回意大利。卡斯蒂廖内在热那亚成长期间，范戴克正在当地创作首批以宫殿为背景的巨幅肖像画。 卡斯蒂廖内的毒蛇、骷髅、断柱与倾覆的瓮，为乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗乃至整个十八世纪绘制了虚无的道具库。他或许从未见过伦勃朗的画作，

Italy and Rembrandt  意大利与伦勃朗

527
A Tomb Discovered. Monotype by Castiglione  A Tomb Discovered.   Monotype by Castiglione  {:[" A Tomb Discovered. "],[" Monotype by Castiglione "]:}\begin{aligned} & \text { A Tomb Discovered. } \\ & \text { Monotype by Castiglione } \end{aligned}
but he was the first artist outside the Netherlands to adopt Rembrandt’s early etching manner of scribbled shadows. The heavy film of ink that Rembrandt partly wiped off some of his plates [ 482 ] may have given Castiglione the idea of doing the same thing on an unscratched surface, thus discovering Italy’s only technical invention in printmaking, the monotype, made by painting a picture in printer’s ink or painter’s colors on a nonabsorbent surface such as copper or varnished cardboard, then printing it in a rolling press like an etching. Since one printing licks most of the ink off the smooth surface, leaving too thin a film for a good second printing, this offset painting is called a monotype [ 527 ]. Although it sacrifices duplicability, the printmaker’s most profitable asset, the monotype (like the mezzotint) is easy to work in either direction, from white to black by painting with ink or from black to white by wiping some off again. The informality of the monotype’s dab-and-wipe disgusted specialist printmakers, and even the convenience of its directness failed to attract painters after Castiglione until Degas made over 400 monotypes [ 685 ], many of which, like some of Castiglione’s, served as bases to be worked over in colors.
但他却是荷兰以外首位采用伦勃朗早期蚀刻技法——即涂鸦式阴影处理的艺术家。 伦勃朗在某些版面上擦除部分厚重墨层的做法[482]，或许启发了卡斯蒂廖内尝试在未经刮刻的表面进行同样操作，从而开创了意大利版画史上唯一的技法发明——单色版画。该技法是在铜版或上漆纸板等不吸水表面涂抹印刷油墨或颜料作画，再通过滚压印刷机如蚀刻版画般印制而成。 由于单次印刷会刮除光滑表面上大部分油墨，导致残留薄膜无法进行优质二次印刷，这种转印绘画被称为单色版画[527]。尽管牺牲了可复制性——这是版画家最有利可图的资产——但单色版画（如同凹版雕刻）操作灵活：既可从白到黑（用墨绘制），亦可从黑到白（刮除部分墨层）。 单版画随意涂抹擦拭的创作方式令专业版画家不屑，即便其直接便捷的特性，在卡斯蒂廖内之后也未能吸引画家青睐——直至德加创作逾 400 幅单版画[685]，其中许多作品如同卡斯蒂廖内的部分创作，成为后续彩色绘制的底稿。

Landscape (风景)


In China and Japan men have long seen themselves as the companions of the carp, the deer, the pine, the snow. Ten centuries ago the Chinese were already painting landscapes in which man appeared, if at all, as a momentary speck to witness time flowing with the river and life melting in the mists. But Western man, heir to the egocentric Greeks and Hebrews, at first relegated landscape to decoration on Roman walls and then to backgrounds in medieval paintings.
山水在中国和日本，人们自古便视自己为鲤鱼、鹿、松树、雪的伴侣。 千百年前，中国山水画中若现人影，不过是瞬息的微尘，见证着时间随江河奔流，生命在朦胧中消融。而西方人承袭希腊与希伯来人的自我中心传统，起初将山水降格为罗马墙壁的装饰，继而沦为中世纪绘画的背景。
Landscape was humanized into importance as Arcadia by Claude Lorrain, born Claude Gelée in Lorraine, some 15 miles from Nancy. There, in his late 20s, Callot started him etching, putting tools in his hands without imposing a point of view. Yet something of Callot’s zest for everyday doings carried over to Claude when he arrived in Rome and etched the Spanish ambassador with a corporal’s guard rambling past a plaster statue of the newly elected German emperor [528]. Once Claude had settled in Rome he found it to be his spiritual home, as so many have done. Neglecting the ruins that puzzled more educated visitors, Claude followed his village boy’s instinct by dwelling from dawn to dusk in the hills and pastures of the Campagna, sketching them with sepia washes as exactly graded as a Chinese
克劳德·洛兰将风景画升华为"阿卡迪亚"般的人文境界。这位出生于洛林地区（距南锡约 15 英里）的艺术家原名克劳德·热莱。 二十余岁时，卡洛特启蒙他学习蚀刻技艺，将工具交予他却不强加艺术理念。然而当克劳德抵达罗马后，卡洛特对日常生活的热忱仍影响着他——他蚀刻的西班牙大使与列队军士，漫步于新当选的德意志皇帝石膏雕像旁[528]。 定居罗马后，克劳德如众多艺术家般将此地视为精神家园。他无视令学识渊博的访客困惑的古迹，凭着乡间少年本能，从黎明到黄昏徜徉于坎帕尼亚的丘陵牧场，以棕褐色水彩勾勒景致——其色调层次之精妙，堪比中国水墨画的渐变技法。

He hardly varied this manner in the etchings that he dated from his zoth to his 63 rd year. Claude was also the first etcher and painter to look square into the eye of the sunset, past dissolving spars and columns [ 530 ]. Though French painters neglected Claude’s native woodnotes for Poussin’s reasoned coherence, he made posterity see the Campagna through his
画家们，将羊群、牧羊人与灌木丛[529]刻画在错综复杂的线条中——这些技法源自埃尔斯海默的小版画[440]。在他从 30 岁至 63 岁期间创作的蚀刻版画中，这种风格几乎未曾改变。 克劳德更是首位直面落日余晖的蚀刻师与画家，穿透消融的桅杆与柱影[530]。尽管法国画家们偏爱普桑的理性统一性而忽视克劳德本土的林间音符，他却让后世透过他的作品看见坎帕尼亚的田园风光。
eyes until nearly 1900. He inspired a school of pastoral etchers in Holland, and 18th-century England expressed its veneration for him in manuals for drawing landscape.
直到近 1900 年才被世人瞩目。他启发了荷兰的一批田园版画家，而 18 世纪的英国则通过风景画教程表达了对他的崇敬之情。
Such printed manuals taught British naval officers to record harbor mouths and landfalls, and soldiers to sketch fields and hills clearly enough to help a commander plan a battle. England’s good roads encouraged travel in coaches, from which the passengers studied the scenery or even sketched it on pocketable pads while changing horses. The local dampness kept watercolors moist long enough for a painter to finish his landscape at leisure, and after the 1750 s a watercolorist could lay a perfectly even wash of sky on the new English wove paper instead of contending with the old laid paper that streaked color in parallel troughs. These circumstances encouraged the publication of more landscape drawing books in England than elsewhere. The most original was that by Alexander Cozens, who roughed out the masses of an imaginary scene by brushing “with swiftest hand” on crumpled paper. His random “blots” remind us today of Chinese brush paintings, which Cozens probably never saw. He aquatinted these “blots” [ 531 ] for students to place under translucent paper as suggestions for drawing finished pictures.
这类印刷手册教会英国海军军官记录海港入口与登陆点，指导士兵清晰勾勒田野山丘，以便指挥官规划战役。英格兰完善的道路网络促进了马车旅行，乘客们在换马途中观赏风景，甚至能在便携画板上速写。 当地的湿润气候使水彩颜料保持足够湿润，画家得以从容完成风景画创作。1750 年代后，水彩画家能在新型英式平纹纸上均匀铺展天空色调，无需再为传统有纹纸上颜料形成平行沟槽的色带而烦恼。这些条件促使英国出版的风景写生书籍远超其他地区。 最具原创性的是亚历山大·科赞斯的作品，他以"迅捷之手"在皱纸上挥洒，勾勒出虚构场景的整体轮廓。他那些随性的"墨渍"，在今日看来颇似中国水墨画——尽管科赞斯可能从未见过中国画。他将这些"墨渍"印制成版画，供学生置于半透明纸下作为绘制完整画作的参照。
Highly practical imaginary landscapes were published by the landscape gardener Humphrey Repton, who would sketch the view from a house as it was and then hinge on a flap to show how he could make it look if supplied with funds [ 532 ]. Funds that were massive even by English standards enabled the Duke of Devonshire to transform a landscape on the grandest scale in the 1830 s when he sodded over the village that had clustered by his doors at Chatsworth in order to surround his Italianized palace with a solitude as sweeping as Claude Lorrain’s Campagna. As far as the duke could look, he thereafter saw nothing to disturb the mood of Claude’s drawings, of which he owned the largest collection.
景观设计师汉弗莱·雷普顿曾出版过极具实用性的想象景观图册。他先勾勒房屋原有的视野景观，再通过活动翻页展示若获得资金支持后可实现的改造效果[532]。 即便以英国标准衡量也堪称巨额的资金，使德文郡公爵得以在 1830 年代进行规模空前的景观改造——他将查茨沃思庄园门前聚居的村落全部掩埋，只为让这座意大利风格的宫殿被如克劳德·洛兰笔下罗马平原般辽阔的寂静所环抱。 此后公爵视野所及之处，再无任何事物能扰乱克劳德画作的意境——而他恰是克劳德作品的最大收藏家。

Art exhibitions (艺术展览)


In 1483 the first exhibition catalogue listed and illustrated the relics displayed annually at Bamberg Cathedral. In 1495 the printer used some of the Bamberg cuts to represent quite different reliquaries at Würzburg. This economy really did not matter, since early catalogue illustrations always modernized the reliquaries so as not to embarrass the priesthood by advertising Romanesque hand-me-downs. In 1502 Vienna printed an exhibition catalogue that showed how relics were displayed to pilgrims outside the great shrine of Saint Stephen [ 533 ]. A row of priests, each one bearing a reliquary, halted in unison from window to window in the treasure tower. At such displays pilgrims held out little convex mirrors to soak up the saintly emanations for use at home. (In 1438 Gutenberg had contracted to cast such mirrors for pilgrims to Aix-la-Chapelle.)
艺术展览 1483 年，首部展览目录首次系统记载并配图展示了班贝格大教堂每年陈列的圣物。1495 年，印刷商挪用部分班贝格版画来呈现维尔茨堡截然不同的圣物匣。这种挪用实则无关紧要——早期目录插图向来会对圣物匣进行现代化改造，以免因展示罗马式旧物而令神职人员难堪。 1502 年维也纳印刷的展览目录展示了圣斯蒂芬大教堂[533]圣龛外向朝圣者陈列圣物的场景：一列神职人员每人手持圣龛，在宝藏塔的窗前整齐列队驻足。朝圣者们举着小巧的凸面镜，汲取圣徒的灵光以供居家使用。 （1438 年古腾堡曾承接为前往亚琛朝圣者铸造此类镜子的合约。）
The first prints of a private collection were made after Lord Arundel (1585-1646)
私人收藏的首批印刷品是在阿伦德尔勋爵（1585-1646）之后制作的。

had assembled the first great English connoisseur’s cabinet during his travels as a diplomat. He commissioned his household artist, Wenzel Hollar, to etch over 100 of his antique marbles, pieces of silver, paintings, and Leonardo drawings [ 344 ]. If he planned to publish these as a catalogue of his collection, he was thwarted by his political misfortunes. The first great catalogue of a secular collection was issued instead by the Hapsburg archduke Leopold William while he was governing the Netherlands in 1646-56. 246 of his paintings were engraved individually, with their dimensions and a description in French, German, Spanish, and Latin, to proclaim the archduke’s princeliness throughout the multilingual Hapsburg domains. The book also shows how the paintings crowded the old palace at Brussels from
在担任外交官期间的旅途中，他已组建了英国首个伟大的鉴赏家藏品室。他委托宫廷画家温策尔·霍拉尔为其逾百件古董大理石雕、银器、绘画及达·芬奇素描制作蚀刻版画[344]。若他曾计划将这些作品编纂成藏品目录，其政治厄运却使计划落空。 世俗收藏的首部伟大目录实则由哈布斯堡大公利奥波德·威廉于 1646-1656 年统治荷兰期间发行。书中 246 幅画作均单独蚀刻，附有尺寸及法、德、西、拉丁四语说明，旨在向多语种的哈布斯堡领地彰显大公的王公气度。该书亦展现了布鲁塞尔旧宫殿内画作如何密布其间——

floor to ceiling [ 534 ], the way they hung in every gallery until after 1900, when they began to be strung in a single line to thin out the growing museum crowds.
从地板到天花板[534]，这些作品曾以这种方式悬挂在每个展厅，直至 1900 年后，为疏散日益拥挤的博物馆人流，才开始被单排悬挂。
The first representations of an artist’s collection fill six wide engravings with the sculptures that François Girardon, Louis XIV’s busiest sculptor, bought out of his large earnings and installed beside models of his own works [ 535 ]. The juxtaposition shows us which Roman statues and Michelangelo marbles influenced French official art and how they were adapted. (The imaginary arrangement was invented by Gilles Oppenord, the most baroque of French decorators.)
首批艺术家收藏的呈现占据了六幅宽幅版画，其中收录了路易十四最繁忙的雕塑家弗朗索瓦·吉拉东用丰厚收入购入的雕塑，这些作品陈列在他自己作品的模型旁[535]。 这种并置展示了哪些罗马雕像和米开朗基罗的大理石作品影响了法国官方艺术，以及它们是如何被改编的。（这种想象中的陈列方式是由法国装饰艺术家中最巴洛克风格的吉勒·奥彭诺德构思的。）
When painters began to work more on their own initiative than on order, they organized exhibitions to sell their offerings. In 18th-century Venice they hung or stood their unframed, turpentine-smelling canvases outdoors in the square of San Rocco. In Paris and London the rains forced canvases indoors for formal showings at the Louvre and Somerset House. Prints provide pictorial inventories of some of these exhibitions from the first Paris Salon in 1699 until newspaper reports substituted inadequately after 1800. The camera began to record exhibitions when the Ingres-Delacroix show was photographed in place in 1855. On the unusually lofty walls of Somerset House [ 536 ], Reynolds and Lawrence commandeered the midheight for full-length portraits that they calculated to look their best when seen from below, using the formula that Rubens discovered at Genoa in 1606. In 1851 the first worldwide exhibition of contemporary art was made known through many illustrated publications and gorgeous color prints [ 537 ]. The Crystal Palace directly inspired the scope, arrangement, and catalogues of the Victoria and Albert Museum, all of which in turn guided many museums in the United States.
当画家们开始更多地凭自主意愿而非受委托作画时，他们便组织展览来售卖作品。18 世纪的威尼斯，艺术家们将未装裱、散发松节油气息的画布悬挂或竖立在圣罗科广场的露天场地上。在巴黎和伦敦，雨水迫使画布移入室内，于卢浮宫和萨默塞特宫举行正式展览。 版画为这些展览提供了图像记录，从 1699 年首届巴黎沙龙展直至 1800 年后被报纸报道所取代。1855 年，当安格尔-德拉克罗瓦联展现场被摄影记录时，相机首次开始为展览留影。 在萨默塞特宫[536]那异常高耸的墙面上，雷诺兹与劳伦斯占据中段位置悬挂全身肖像画——他们运用鲁本斯 1606 年在热那亚发现的构图法则，精心计算出从下方仰视时效果最佳的悬挂高度。1851 年，首届全球当代艺术展通过大量图文刊物与华丽彩色版画广为人知[537]。 水晶宫的展览模式直接启发了维多利亚与阿尔伯特博物馆的规模规划、展陈布局及图录编纂体系，而这些经验又反过来影响了美国众多博物馆的发展方向。

Interior decoration (室内装饰)


Medieval and early Renaissance rooms would have looked bare to us. So long as courts shifted from palace to palace, they packed up tapestries to clothe cold stone or brick quickly and a little sturdy furniture that often folded or knocked apart to load on mules. The more local and sedentary Italian princes at least unified the bare uncurtained rooms by getting the best painters to fresco the walls. But when Louis XIV decided to keep his nobles under his eye by making Versailles the only place worth getting invited to, he elaborated a harmony of decoration down to the last curtain tassel and flower bed. Charles Lebrun invented the required sumptuousness out of antique Roman architectural sculpture with a splendor that Jean Lepautre published to the world through 2350 etchings [ 538 ]. Lepautre etched the first corpus of interior decoration with a swift,
室内装饰中世纪及文艺复兴早期的居室在我们看来会显得空荡。只要宫廷在各座宫殿间迁徙，人们便会打包挂毯以迅速装点冰冷的石墙或砖墙，再带上些许简易家具——这些家具往往可折叠或拆卸以便驮上骡背。定居于本土的意大利诸侯们至少通过聘请顶尖画家在墙壁绘制湿壁画，使这些未设窗帘的空房间显得统一协调。 但当路易十四决定将凡尔赛宫打造成贵族们梦寐以求的社交圣地，以此掌控贵族动向时，他将装饰的和谐性推向极致——从窗帘流苏到花坛布置都精雕细琢。 夏尔·勒布伦从古罗马建筑雕塑中汲取灵感，创造出华丽的装饰体系，其辉煌程度由让·勒波特通过 2350 幅蚀刻版画向世界展示[538]。勒波特以迅捷的笔触刻画出首部室内装饰全集，

In France itself, the style broke abruptly in 1715 when the gloomy old king’s death released the court. The younger courtiers fled to Paris to build themselves snug houses in the cosier Regency manner. The new, intimate rooms doubled their apparent depth through mirrors over the focus of talk, the fireplace. For a witty unity, Oudry’s illustrations to Lafontaine [ 98 ] might be carved on the paneling or
在法国本土，这种风格于 1715 年戛然而止——当阴郁的老国王驾崩，宫廷重获自由。年轻的宫廷人士纷纷逃往巴黎，以更温馨的摄政风格为自己建造舒适宅邸。新式亲密居室通过在交谈焦点——壁炉上方悬挂镜子，使视觉深度倍增。为营造机智统一的氛围，奥德里为拉封丹作品绘制的插图[98]可镌刻于壁板之上，或

Then, in the 1760s, Englishmen returning from the Grand Tour began to satisfy their nostalgia for Hadrian’s Villa and Nero’s Golden House by commissioning Robert Adam to resurface their Tudor halls with painted plaster lozenges and hexagons mirrored in the design of the carpet. Since Adam had little antique furniture to imitate, he matched the authentic Roman wall treatments by inventing furniture with square, tapered legs and a revival of marquetry. His scheme of classical quotations restricted everything except the old-master paintings to one decade and one taste. Adam’s huge folio on interior decoration-the first in England-also influenced the Continent. In France in the 1770 s his engravings [ 541 ] and the fashion for English simplicity went to make the Louis XVI style (then called antique) an alternative to the continuing rococo (then called pittoresque or moderne).
1760 年代，从欧洲大旅行归来的英国人开始委托罗伯特·亚当为都铎式大厅重新粉刷，用彩绘灰泥菱形与六边形图案与地毯设计相呼应，以此满足他们对哈德良别墅和尼禄黄金宫殿的向往。 由于亚当缺乏可供仿制的古董家具，他通过设计方形锥形腿家具并复兴镶嵌工艺，使室内装饰与古罗马墙面处理相呼应。其古典引用的设计方案将除老大师油画外的所有元素限定于同一时代与品味。亚当那部英国首创的室内装饰巨著亦影响了欧洲大陆。 1770 年代，他的版画作品[541]与英式简约风潮传入法国，促使路易十六风格（当时被称为古董风格）成为持续盛行的洛可可风格（当时被称为风景画风格或现代风格）的替代选择。

The emperor’s official designers presented this grandeur as though it were engraved on ice [ 542 ]. Such mastery of decoration exhausts the collaborating imagination with perfection that no work of expressive art can ever attain. The revolutions that followed Napoleon’s downfall frightened the surviving aristocrats into Gothic Revival retreats [ 543 ] where they could imagine themselves back in the safety of their supposed origins during the Crusades.

As historical ages began to evoke emotional attitudes, the 19th century revived different styles to express different functions-Gothic for churches, Medicean Renaissance for clubs and banks, Louis XIV for municipal buildings, and Roman for law courts. An architect varied styles the way a character actor varies dialects. A shared architectural idiom suitable for all occasions appeared only in the 19205 when the Bauhaus in Weimar invented an international style.
当历史时期开始唤起情感态度时，19 世纪复兴了不同风格以表达不同功能——哥特式用于教堂，美第奇文艺复兴风格用于俱乐部和银行，路易十四风格用于市政建筑，罗马风格用于法院。建筑师变换风格的方式，如同性格演员变换方言。直到 1920 年代，魏玛包豪斯创立国际风格时，才出现适用于所有场合的通用建筑语汇。

Stage scenery (舞台布景)


An Italian in France published the first illustrated treatise on stage scenery, showing an indoor platform set with lath and canvas"houses" [544] like those previously built on outdoor platforms for miracle plays. The action volleyed like a tennis ball, between opposite “houses” close to the audience, as it must have done in the original production of Romeo and Juliet. In Serlio’s curtainless

A century later the Medici staged spectacles in the first outdoor secular theater of modern times, shaped like a Greek theater. The uphill slope of the Boboli Gardens was scooped out into an arena where educated horses paced in wide pavanes surrounded by the court, under cover at the rear of the Pitti Palace, and the rainresistant populace in the bleachers [ 545 ]. The action advanced and withdrew as it was to do in the illusory depth of perspective scenery. Della Bella’s etching appeared in one of those prestige publications that a prince sent to other princes to
一个世纪后，美第奇家族在现代首个露天世俗剧场——一座仿照古希腊剧场建造的场馆——上演了盛大的表演。博博利花园的坡地被开凿成竞技场，训练有素的骏马在宫廷成员环绕下以宽阔的帕凡舞步行进，背景是皮蒂宫后方的遮蔽区域，而防雨的观众则坐在看台之上[545]。 表演随着透视景深的虚幻效果推进或后撤。德拉贝拉的蚀刻版画刊载于某本显赫刊物中——诸侯们常将此类刊物互赠以彰显威仪。

In Vienna one Italian opera, The Golden Apple [546], required 22 total trans- formations operated by gigantic wooden machines that dispelled a temple into clouds and sea, then gathered these into a Roman triumph complete with a lion chariot and captive kings.
在维也纳上演的意大利歌剧《金苹果》[546]中，需要通过巨型木制机械装置完成 22 次场景转换：先将神庙化作云海，继而凝聚成罗马凯旋场景，其中既有狮驹战车，亦有俘虏国王。
In Munich (the other great home of northern opera) illusions like the fish-eye view of men rowing behind a scrim [ 547 ] required that the auditorium be darkened by snuffing candles or by hoisting the chandelier through a hole in the ceiling. But, as in the old, bright palace hall, the side walls of the auditorium still continued onto the stage in a wide corridor or mall until about 1700, when the Bibiena family of theater designers began to distinguish the stage from the baroque house by scenery of a contrasting style, such as Gothic, and by painting the backdrop with buildings that either point at you like an oncoming ship, or narrow back into a corner, or else combine both schemes in an X X XX of intersecting colonnades [ 548 ]. This imaginative geometry opened even the tiniest stage to a vastness of dreams for the prince (who paid the bill) seated in the central box where the perspective lines converged. The eight busy Bibienas advertised their skill from 1690 to 1790 by publishing many of the sumptuous theatrical books that imposed Italian opera scenery on all Europe. With a deftness now lost, they could paint a balustrade plunging outward by diminishing the balusters as evenly as beads. Other stage designers might vary effects with more poetry and freedom, but none could draw so exactly for reproduction in striking engravings.
在慕尼黑（北方歌剧的另一大摇篮），诸如在纱幕后呈现划船者鱼眼视角[547]这类幻象效果，需要通过熄灭蜡烛或将吊灯吊入天花板孔洞来使观众席陷入黑暗。 然而直至 1700 年前，观众厅的侧墙仍如古老明亮的宫殿大厅般延伸至舞台，形成宽阔的走廊或长廊。此时剧场设计师比比耶纳家族开始通过对比风格的布景——如哥特式——将舞台与巴洛克式建筑区分开来，他们在背景幕布上绘制建筑群：或如迎面驶来的船只般朝观众延伸，或向角落收窄， 或将两种手法融合，以交错的柱廊形成 X X XX 的空间结构[548]。这种富有想象力的几何构图，使最狭小的舞台也能为坐在中央包厢（视线收敛点）的王子（即买单者）展开浩瀚的梦幻空间。 1690 至 1790 年间，八位忙碌的比比埃纳家族成员通过出版众多华美戏剧书籍宣传技艺，将意大利歌剧布景风潮席卷全欧。他们以如今已失传的娴熟技法绘制栏杆——通过将栏杆柱均匀缩小如串珠般排列，营造出向外倾斜的视觉效果。其他舞台设计师或许能以更富诗意与自由的方式变化效果，但无人能如此精准作画，以利于制作震撼的版画复制品。

like the roasting of rancid mutton.) An audience could begin to see bright colors after Paris in the 1780s introduced the six-candle-power smokeless lamp with a glass chimney, and especially after 1817 when clean gaslight began to brighten and dim London stages. The first great designer to use full color was Schinkel [ 549 ], who worked in Berlin when Napoleon’s wars had beggared Germany. Like his forerunners on the baroque stage, he painted on canvas the dream palaces that he could not construct in stone. Unhampered by the need for permanence, the cost of marble, the delays of masons, and the whims or deaths of patrons, Schinkel and all the old stage designers evoked visions of exotic styles and daring designs that sometimes shaped real buildings. Yet it is a pity that the great stage sets mostly decorated dramas of mythological twaddle. The masters of modern drama who wrote from 1575 to 1675 wished no visual intervention to distract their audiences from sharing a passion. Molière asked for nothing but some actors and three chairs.
（如同烤焦的羊肉散发着酸败气味。）自 1780 年代巴黎引入六烛光功率的无烟灯（配有玻璃灯罩）后，观众开始能看见鲜艳色彩；尤其在 1817 年洁净的煤气灯开始照亮并调暗伦敦舞台之后。 首位运用全彩设计的伟大设计师是申克尔[549]，他在拿破仑战争使德国倾家荡产时于柏林执业。如同巴洛克舞台上的先驱者们，他将无法用石材建造的梦幻宫殿绘于画布之上。 摆脱了永久性需求、大理石成本、石匠工期以及赞助人喜怒无常或殒命的束缚，申克尔与所有古典舞台设计师共同唤醒了异域风格与大胆设计的幻象，这些构想有时甚至影响了现实建筑。可惜的是，这些宏伟的舞台布景大多装饰着神话故事的无稽之谈。 1575 至 1675 年间的现代戏剧大师们，不愿任何视觉干扰破坏观众共情激情。莫里哀仅需演员与三把椅子——别无他求。

The copyrighted picture story (受版权保护的图画故事)


Before the 1730s England produced illustrations for books and crude broadsides but no single-sheet prints other than maps, views, and a few portraits. To protect this weak effort imported prints had to pay a varying customs duty that for a time levied sixpence per print-often thrice
在 1730 年代之前，英国仅能制作书籍插图和粗制海报，除地图、风景画及少量肖像外，尚无单张印刷品。为保护这微弱的本土产业，进口印刷品须缴纳浮动关税——当时每张印刷品需缴六便士，有时甚至高达三倍。
the price at home-while France, confident of a superior production, admitted prints for a mere 100 sous per hundredweight. Britain, having reduced court patronage by being the first modern country to tame its kings, had left engravers at the mercy of unscrupulous publishers. If an engraver ventured to publish on his own, anybody could legally undersell him with cut-rate copies.
国内价格——而法国凭借生产优势，仅以每百磅 100 苏的价格准入印刷品市场。英国作为首个驯服君主的现代国家，削弱了宫廷庇护，致使雕版师沦为无良出版商的玩物。若雕版师敢于自行出版，任何人都可合法地以低价复制品压价竞争。
The British writer, at least, had protected himself from piracy by the very first general copyright act in 1709, when William Hogarth, who was to protect the engraver, was still a 12-year-old apprentice learning to engrave flourishes and coats of arms on silver tankards and salvers. He, like Daumier, was the son of a thwarted author. Both Hogarth and Daumier more or less taught themselves to draw and paint the dramas that their fathers had tried to write. Hogarth said, “I treat my subject as a dramatic writer; my picture is my stage, and men and women my players” [ 550-555]. When he was 34 he painted the first of his "modern moral subjects"The Harlot’s Progress. He regarded the paintings as mere preliminaries, for he said that he planned to live “by small sums from many by means of prints which I could Engrave from my Picture myself.” He cannily did not bother with "great correct-
至少英国作家在 1709 年通过首部《版权法》获得了版权保护，当时威廉·霍加斯——这位未来将保护雕刻师权益的艺术家——还只是个 12 岁的学徒，在银制酒杯和托盘上刻画花饰与纹章。他与杜米埃一样，都是怀才不遇作家的儿子。 霍加斯与杜米埃都通过自学掌握了绘画技艺，将父亲们未竟的文学剧作转化为视觉叙事。霍加斯曾言："我以戏剧作家的视角处理题材；画布即舞台，人物皆为演员"[550-555]。 34 岁那年，他创作了首幅"现代道德题材"作品《妓女生涯》。他视这些画作仅为铺垫，因他计划"通过自行雕刻画作制版印刷，从众人处获取微薄收益维生"。他精明地避开了"宏大正确"的创作道路——
Figure 168: 550-555 Marriage à la Mode. Engravings after William Hogarth, London, 1745
图 168：550-555《时髦婚姻》。威廉·霍加斯版画集，伦敦，1745 年
The copyrighted picture story
受版权保护的图画故事

The copyrighted picture story
受版权保护的图画故事

ness in drawing or fine Engraving, which would set the price out of reach of those for whome they were cheifly intended." He at least delayed copyists by soliciting subscriptions for The Harlot’s Progress while he was still engraving it, taking in 1240 guineas for as many sets of the prints, whereas he realized only 84 guineas when he auctioned the six original oil paintings. His print sales after publication must have suffered from the eight pirated copies of the series. This first original story told in pictures for “reading” succeeded because it pictured Defoe’s middleclass moralizing with rooms, clothes, and gestures as exactly observed as in Bosse’s sets of prints of the Parisian middle class [ 462 ]. The Harlot was soon staged as a pantomime and as a ballad opera, and it inspired English novelists to describe telling details of manners, dress, and settings. But if Hogarth’s prints were to continue to earn him dividends, he had to stop the piracies, so he-a fighter in every inch of his five foot three-persuaded Parliament to enact the first copyright for “Designers, Engravers, Etchers, &c.” The first prints so protected for 14 years were Hogarth’s series of The Rake’s Progress, inscribed “Publish’d ye. 25 June, 1735. According to Act of Parliament.” Until 1911 commercially published English prints continued to bear their exact date of publication, as American prints (but no others) did after 1831. The pictorial copyright act did for Hogarth what the writer’s act had done for Defoe and Dr. Johnson: it enabled him to work independently. Not only did Hogarth not need to slave for a publisher or flatter a patron, he was free to
"若采用素描或精美雕版印刷，其价格将远超主要受众的承受范围。"他在雕刻《娼妓的历程》期间通过预售订阅至少延缓了抄袭者的行动，以 1240 几尼的价格售出同等数量的版画套装，而当他拍卖六幅原作油画时，仅获得 84 几尼的收益。 该系列出版后，其印刷品销量必然因八种盗版复制品而受损。这部首创的"可阅读"绘本之所以成功，在于它通过房间、服饰和姿态等细节，精准呈现了笛福所倡导的中产阶级道德观——其观察之细腻堪比博斯描绘巴黎中产阶级的版画集[462]。 《荡妇》很快被改编为哑剧和叙事歌剧，并激发英国小说家们描绘风俗、服饰和场景的生动细节。 但若想让版画持续带来收益，霍加斯必须遏制盗版——这位身高仅五英尺三英寸的斗士说服议会颁布了首部保护"设计师、雕刻师、蚀刻师等"的版权法案。首批受此保护（有效期 14 年）的作品正是霍加斯的《浪子历程》系列，其扉页题写着"根据 1735 年 6 月 25 日议会法案出版"。 1735 年 6 月 25 日。依据议会法案"。 直至 1911 年，英国商业版画仍沿袭精确标注出版日期的传统——这与 1831 年后美国版画的做法相同（其他国家则不然）。图像版权法案对霍加斯的作用，恰似作家法案之于丹尼尔·笛福与萨缪尔·约翰逊：它赋予了艺术家独立创作的自由。霍加斯不仅无需为出版商卖命或讨好赞助人，更得以自由地
express himself about any class of people without fear of censorship-England having been the first country to abolish most kinds of censorship shortly before Hogarth was born. France, on the contrary, would not trust an engraver to own a press, even for proving his copperplates, from 1586 to 1734, and required prints to be marked A.P.D.R. (Avec Privilège du Roy) from 1685 to 1790, to certify that the printmaker had deposited a stipulated number of impressions and secured authorization to publish. British liberties developed Hogarth into the first British artist to make an impression on the Continent, where his picture stories set the style for some French engravings and furnished themes for writers in French and German. The British freedom of the press was the envy, or the dread, of outsiders for a century before it spread to other peoples.
在任何阶层的人群面前畅所欲言而无需担心审查——英国早在霍加斯出生前不久就率先废除了绝大多数审查制度。 相反，法国从 1586 年到 1734 年间，甚至不允许雕刻师拥有印刷机来校对铜版，更在 1685 至 1790 年间强制要求版画标注"A.P.D.R."（Avec Privilège du Roy）字样，以证明印刷商已按规定存放指定数量的印品并获得出版许可。 英国的自由发展使霍加斯成为首位在欧洲大陆留下印记的英国艺术家——他的连环画故事不仅为法国版画确立了风格范式，更向法德作家提供了创作题材。在英国的新闻自由向其他民族传播之前，这一百年间它始终是外界羡慕或畏惧的对象。

Trade catalogues (贸易目录)


While advertising must be as old as walls, its great extension began with printing. The first dated typography advertised indulgences for sale at Mainz in 1453. Printers soon pushed their own product with little handbills and then with book catalogues. No one knows when or where advertisements were first illustrated, but by about 1650 a wrapper for pins or playing cards commonly displayed the swinging sign that identified a shop before houses were numbered. After about 1700 smart London shops gave out trade cards (as matchbooks are given today) that were often engraved with some of the merchandise to make a one-page catalogue [556]. In Paris the royally subsidized porcelain and tapestry
贸易目录广告虽与墙壁同龄，其蓬勃发展始于印刷术诞生。最早可考的印刷品是 1453 年美因茨出售赎罪券的广告。印刷商很快开始用小传单推广自家产品，继而推出书籍目录。广告何时何地首次配图尚无定论，但约 1650 年间，在房屋尚未编号的时代，别针或扑克牌的包装纸上已常见悬挂招牌的图案——这正是店铺的标识。 约 1700 年后，伦敦时髦商铺开始分发商业卡片（如同今日的火柴盒），卡片常以雕版印刷展示部分商品，形成单页商品目录[556]。在巴黎，由皇家资助的瓷器与挂毯

factories issued no trade cards, while lesser firms needed only a few for the intimate cliques of courtiers and financiers. Italy advertised even less, since local craftsmen worked for neighbors. But by the mid-1700s the Sheffield and Birmingham metal factories and the Staffordshire potteries began to manufacture so much more than they could sell locally that they started to advertise through the first illustrated trade catalogues in book form. These were not given to customers but to middlemen. The middlemen erased the manufacturer’s name, lest their clients order direct from the factory, and wrote in prices in pounds, pesetas, livres, dollars, and rupees, as British trade followed the British flag.
大型工厂从不发行贸易卡片，而中小型企业只需为宫廷贵族和金融家的核心圈子准备少量卡片。意大利的广告宣传更为稀少，因为当地工匠多为邻里制作商品。但到 18 世纪中叶，谢菲尔德和伯明翰的金属工厂以及斯塔福德郡的陶器作坊开始生产远超本地销量的产品，于是通过首批图册形式的贸易目录进行广告宣传。这些目录并非分发给客户，而是提供给中间商。 中间商们会抹去制造商名称——唯恐客户直接向工厂下单——并在目录中标注以英镑、比塞塔、法郎、美元和卢比计价的商品价格，因为英国贸易始终追随英国国旗所到之处。
Illustrations show the plated silverware [ 557 ] that Sheffield began to manufacture in the 1740 s and perfected in the 1760s by fusing two thin plates of silver to a thick core of copper and then rolling this sandwich in a thin sheet to be shaped with classic simplicity. The illustrations look as though they had been engraved by the factory hands who engraved decorations on the actual silver pieces. Birmingham specialized in brassware as well as saws, sextants, and tin shower baths. Its catalogue [ 558 ] sold brass drawer pulls and furniture mounts to France, where they were chased, gilded, and applied to French furniture.
插图展示了谢菲尔德于 1740 年代开始制造、并在 1760 年代臻于完美的镀银器皿[557]——通过将两片薄银片熔合于厚实的铜芯之上，再将这种三明治结构轧制成薄片，最终以经典简约的造型呈现。 这些插图仿佛由工厂工匠亲手雕刻而成——他们正是为实物银器镌刻装饰纹样的匠人。伯明翰则专精黄铜器皿，同时生产锯具、六分仪及锡制淋浴盆。其产品目录[558]记载的黄铜抽屉拉手与家具镶件远销法国，经当地工匠浮雕镀金后，被镶嵌于法式家具之上。
In Germany the long-established iron foundries began about 1800 to advertise stoves and neoclassic decorative castings. The Nuremberg cottage industry of toy-
在德国，历史悠久的铸铁厂约于 1800 年开始宣传炉具和新古典主义装饰铸件。纽伦堡的玩具家庭作坊产业——
making varied its 18th-century line of dolls and dollhouses with toy carpenter shops, microscopes, magic cabinets, and electric machines [ 559 ] for children of up-to-date parents who had read Rousseau on learning by doing. German toy catalogues captured and held the export trade until 1914.
为迎合那些研读卢梭"做中学"理论的现代父母，该公司将 18 世纪的娃娃屋系列产品进行了多样化升级，新增了玩具木工坊、显微镜、魔法柜和电动玩具[559]。德国玩具目录由此垄断出口贸易直至 1914 年。
Furniture was hard to advertise in catalogues so long as the mass-produced pieces were as universally standardized as Windsor chairs, and the better pieces were made to individual order. But in the 1830 s the bandsaw, based on a British patent of 1808, was developed in the United States for the mass production of furniture composed of ponderous softwood scrolls veneered with mahogany. Factories could keep busy only by the pictorial advertising of their latest designs [ 560 ].
只要大批量生产的家具像温莎椅那样普遍标准化，而精品家具仍按个人订单定制，家具就很难在目录中做广告。但在 1830 年代，基于 1808 年英国专利的带锯在美国得到发展，用于批量生产由沉重的软木卷曲木料制成、表面贴有桃花心木贴面的家具。 工厂唯有通过图文广告展示最新设计才能维持生产运转[560]。
The United States, as the first large custom-free territory with a not quite impossible postal system, encouraged factories to sell directly to customers through innumerable mail-order catalogues. A Yankee specialty-the light carriage, springy
美国作为首个免关税的大型地区，拥有并非完全不可行的邮政系统，通过数不胜数的邮购目录鼓励工厂直接向顾客销售产品。一种扬基特色产品——轻便马车，弹簧悬挂

The success of mail orders produced a middleman who stocked hundreds and then thousands of articles when Montgomery Ward in Chicago in 1872 sent out the first general list of the various things that a family might need in a village or on a farm. Montgomery Ward and Sears Roebuck unintentionally developed their catalogues into illustrated encyclopedias of social history.

18th-century books (十八世纪书籍)


The 18th century perfected a fresh, seductive format for books subsidized by wealthy patrons for wealthy bibliophiles. These books were not meant to be read but rather to be admired two facing pages at a time. In 1719 Claude Gillot, Watteau’s teacher, diminished Louis XIV’s royal folio format into a neat block of type and picture [ 562 ]. Gillot was the next French printmaker after Callot to see wit and grace in the everyday and to keep pace with comedians. In Venice the invention of the rococo book completed four centuries of collaboration between Venetian artists and publishers. Borders as elaborate as those in old Parisian prayer books [ 249 ] surrounded gratulatory odes in the souvenir pamphlets that Venetian grandees gave to guests at family ceremonies [ 563 ]. The last of many Venetian books to be imitated outside Venice was a massive folio of Tasso that took years to prepare. Though each canto begins with the old baroque fullpage copperplate, it ends with a new kind of vignette of figures sporting on an airy island [ 564 ]. But since Piazzetta’s witty vignettes were dwarfed by the monumental page, the French, about 15 years later, scaled down the Venetian scheme to
十八世纪书籍十八世纪为书籍开创了一种精致迷人的新形式，这些书籍由富有的赞助人资助，专为富裕的藏书家打造。它们并非供人阅读，而是让人逐页欣赏。 1719 年，瓦托的老师克劳德·吉洛特将路易十四的皇家对开本缩减为精巧的图文组合[562]。继卡洛之后，吉洛特成为又一位在日常生活中捕捉机智与优雅、紧跟喜剧演员步伐的法国版画家。在威尼斯，洛可可书籍的诞生标志着威尼斯艺术家与出版商四百年合作的巅峰。 威尼斯贵族在家族庆典赠予宾客的纪念册中[563]，贺词诗篇被镶嵌在精美边饰中——其繁复程度堪比古巴黎祈祷书[249]。最后一部在威尼斯境外被广泛仿效的威尼斯书籍，是耗时数年制作的塔索巨著对开本。 尽管每卷诗篇仍以巴洛克式整版铜版画开篇，结尾却采用了全新风格的插图——人物在轻盈岛屿上嬉戏[564]。但由于皮亚泽塔的俏皮插图在宏伟版面中显得渺小，约十五年后法国人便将威尼斯的版式方案缩小为

The paper, “singing” through the ink, sets the brilliant key. C.-N. Cochin noted that “vignettes must be etched, not engraved, to keep the spontaneity of a sketch, which engraved finishing destroys.” Though some Parisian book illustrators specialized in designing and others in etching, each could do the other’s work well enough for any number to collaborate as one. This unity of effort so impressed alert amateurs that they began to bind preliminary drawings with the engravings to make de luxe copies.
爱神们慵懒地倚在随心消散的云絮上[565]，画面、字体与纸张的精妙协调，恰能取悦这个时代挑剔的闲人。纸张透过墨色"吟唱"，奠定了璀璨的基调。 C.-N.科钦曾指出："小插图必须采用蚀刻而非雕刻工艺，方能保留素描的即兴神韵——雕刻的修饰会扼杀这种灵动。"尽管巴黎部分书籍插画家专攻设计，另一些则精于蚀刻，但双方皆能胜任对方的工作，使团队协作如一人般流畅。这种完美配合令敏锐的收藏家们深受震撼，他们开始将草图与蚀刻版画装帧成册，制作成精装典藏版。

Rococo and classicism in Germany (德国的洛可可与古典主义)


After the Thirty Years’ War ended in 1648, half a century of silence settled on the ruins of Germany. When initiative finally returned, a new kind of pilgrimage church arose in south Germany and Austria at ancient abbeys and on the sites of peasant visions in the fields. The new builders explored the rococo with a rapture of release from the Vitruvian regulations imposed ever since the end of the flamboyant Gothic. From about 1730 to 1750 churches rivaled heaven with the seraphic intoxication of white light sliding
德国的洛可可与古典主义 1648 年三十年战争结束后，半个世纪的沉寂笼罩着德国的废墟。当创造力终于复苏，一种新型朝圣教堂在德国南部与奥地利涌现——它们矗立于古老修道院遗址，或坐落于田野间农民圣灵显现之地。 这些新建筑师以狂喜之姿探索洛可可风格，挣脱了自华丽哥特式建筑消亡后便束缚他们的维特鲁威式规制。约 1730 至 1750 年间，教堂以滑落的白色光晕营造出天使般的醉意，与天国相抗衡。

from unseen sources across plaster sculpture tinted in shrimp pink, salad green, gilt, and silver.
从看不见的源头流淌，穿过粉虾色、沙拉绿、镀金与银色的石膏雕塑。
Architecture’s new mystery of brilliance surpassed the efforts of all Germanic painters except one-Maulpertsch of Vienna, who also used his experience of the Tiepolos’ etching to make a few bold and subtle prints as bonuses issued yearly by a mutual benefit society [ 566 ]. Germany did not invent the rococo-indeed, where and by whom was it invented?-but Augsburg took the lead in disseminating the style through sets of four or six etched designs stitched together with a loop of linen thread [567]. Augsburg motifs spread south into Italian ceilings, west to Portuguese choir stalls, and north to Chippendale mirrors, for the Augsburg publishers marketed their ornament prints as efficiently as their ancestors had marketed the first mass production of woodcut books in 1470 to 90 [ 33 ].
建筑艺术的新奇光彩超越了所有日耳曼画家的创作，唯独维也纳的毛尔佩尔茨例外——他同样借鉴提埃波罗家族的蚀刻技法，为互助协会每年发行的赠品制作了几幅大胆而精妙的版画[566]。 德国并非洛可可风格的发源地——事实上，这种风格究竟诞生于何处、由谁开创？——但奥格斯堡率先通过四幅或六幅蚀刻设计组成的套件，以亚麻线环扣装帧的方式传播此风格[567]。 奥格斯堡的装饰图案向南渗透至意大利天花板，向西延伸至葡萄牙唱诗席，向北影响到奇彭代尔风格的镜子。这些出版商推广装饰版画的效率，堪比其先辈在 1470 至 1490 年间推广首批量产木刻书籍时的盛况[33]。
In contrast to these south German factories, Prussia had but one printmaker of note, Daniel Chodowiecki, who painted French gallantries on enamel nicknacks
与这些南德工厂相比，普鲁士仅有一位值得注意的版画家——丹尼尔·霍多维茨基，他将法国风流韵事绘制在珐琅小饰品上。
Rococo and classicism in Germany
德国的洛可可与古典主义

The Drawing Lesson. Etching by Daniel Chodowiecki in ALMANACH GENEALOGIQUE, Berlin, 1781
素描课。丹尼尔·霍多维茨基的蚀刻版画，见于《家谱年鉴》，柏林，1781 年
until he was about 30, when he taught himself to etch, perhaps by studying prints after Chardin [ 464 ]. He then etched over 2000 tiny, truthful glimpses of burghers in placid little Berlin during the Age of Reason. He was also the German specialist for illustrating pocket almanacs on subjects like men’s hobbies, women’s occupations [ 568 ], or the life of Frederick the Great.
直到约三十岁时，他自学了蚀刻技艺，或许是通过研习夏尔丹的版画作品[464]。此后，他创作了逾两千幅微型蚀刻版画，真实地捕捉了启蒙时代宁静小城柏林中市民生活的点滴。 他同时也是德国插画界的专家，为袖珍年鉴绘制插图，题材涵盖男性爱好、女性职业[568]，以及腓特烈大帝的生平。

Wallpaper (壁纸)


The earliest wallpaper found on a wall shows a silk-weave pattern of pomegranates, printed in black on the back of a London proclamation 1509. This was discovered in England, where most wallpapers printed before 1750 have survived. The prevalence of middling wealth allowed Englishmen to cheer their rooms with paper, while Continentals had either tapestries or nothing. Early English black and white wallpapers [569] imitated woven designs and the blackwork then being embroidered in every household. From about 1690 to 1800 papers with miniature designs for covering walls, lining drawers, or binding pamphlets became a specialty of Augsburg, Germany’s busiest producer of all decorative arts. To imitate the gleam of the embossed and gilded leather wall coverings that Germany and the Netherlands imported from Spain, the Augsburgers cut thick relief plates of copper and heated them to emboss brass foil on single sheets of colored paper [570].
壁纸迄今发现的最早壁纸出现在一堵墙上，其丝绸织纹图案为石榴，以黑色印于 1509 年伦敦公告的背面。该发现位于英格兰，当地保存着 1750 年前印刷的大部分壁纸。中等财富的普遍存在使英国人得以用壁纸装点居室，而欧洲大陆居民则要么悬挂挂毯，要么空墙无饰。 早期英式黑白壁纸[569]仿效织物纹样及当时家家户户流行的黑线绣工艺。约 1690 至 1800 年间，德国奥格斯堡作为装饰艺术品最繁忙的产地，将用于墙面装饰、抽屉衬里或册页装帧的微型图案壁纸发展为特色产品。 为模仿德荷两国从西班牙进口的压花镀金皮革壁饰光泽，奥格斯堡工匠切割厚铜浮雕板，经加热后将黄铜箔压印于彩色单张纸上[570]。
By 1700 England was gluing together 12 squares of blank paper, each about 22 by 35 inches, for printing in rolls that were easier to paste on a wall than the German single sheets. The British rolls received the main color from a woodblock smacked with a mallet, other colors then being added to the basic design from stencils that cheap child labor could center on the woodcut basis. In 1748 a British ambassador to Louis XV changed the style and production of French wallpaper by
到 1700 年，英国人已开始将 12 张空白纸张（每张约 22×35 英寸）粘合为卷筒状印刷品，这种形式比德国的单张纸更便于墙面粘贴。英国卷筒壁纸的主色调由木刻版经槌击印制而成，其他色彩则通过模板添加至基础图案——廉价童工便能将这些模板对准木刻版中心进行印刷。 1748 年，英国驻路易十五大使通过
decorating his Paris salon with British blue flock paper. Although the French gov- ernment levied 20 livres import duty per hundredweight on British flock paper (as against a mere 100 sous for British engravings), the French imported it until stopped in 1755 by the Seven Years’ War. In the 1760s a Parisian manufacturer, Jean-Baptiste Réveillon, hired court designers of tapestries and silks to adapt their inventions to the most subtle and vivid wallpaper that had yet been produced [ 571 ]. His
用英国蓝绒纹壁纸装饰他的巴黎沙龙。尽管法国政府对英国绒纹壁纸征收每百磅 20 里弗尔的进口关税（而英国版画仅需 100 苏），法国仍持续进口此类壁纸，直至 1755 年因七年战争而中断。 1760 年代，巴黎制造商让-巴蒂斯特·雷维永聘请宫廷挂毯与丝绸设计师，将他们的创新成果应用于当时最精妙鲜活的壁纸创作[571]。他的
