571 风味。蓝白壁纸，由巴黎的 J.-B. Réveillon 设计，1789 年前

572
Gardens of Bagatelle. Wallpaper, Paris, about 1800
巴加泰尔花园。壁纸，巴黎，约 1800 年
573
Captain Cook’s Voyages. Wallpaper by Joseph Dufour, Macon, 1806, in Ham House, Peabody, Massachusetts
库克船长的航海之旅。约瑟夫·杜弗尔绘制壁纸，梅肯，1806 年，现藏于马萨诸塞州皮博迪市汉姆府。
papers invaded England, and their success gave him such grand airs as a deputy to the Etats Généraux that the French Revolution began by sacking and burning his factory 11 weeks before it stormed the Bastille.
法国军队入侵英格兰，其胜利使他作为法国三级会议代表时气焰嚣张，以致法国大革命爆发前十一周，人们便洗劫焚毁了他的工厂——而就在十一周后，革命者攻占了巴士底狱。
But in Edinburgh an event had already occurred that was to change French wallpapers even more than Réveillon’s designs. There, in 1788, the first panorama was exhibited in a kind of silo 25 feet across, painted with a view of Edinburgh itself. This started a craze for building panoramas 100 or more feet in diameter that wrapped the beholder in a painting of a famous town or a recent battle. After war in 1793 prevented Englishmen from introducing panoramas into France, the American Robert Fulton obtained a license to build one in Paris. When lack of funds forced him to cede his license, other impresarios built two in what is still called the Passage des Panoramas, showing the 1793 siege of Toulon and the monuments of Paris. Immediately an enterprising factory produced a sort of home version in a scenic wallpaper of the Gardens of Bagatelle [ 572 ].
但在爱丁堡，一场比雷维永的设计更深刻地改变法国壁纸行业的事件早已发生。1788 年，首幅全景画在当地展出——那是一座直径 25 英尺的筒仓状建筑，内壁绘有爱丁堡全景。此举引发了建造百英尺乃至更大直径全景画的热潮，观者仿佛置身于名城风光或战役场景的巨幅画卷之中。 1793 年战争阻断了英国人将全景画引入法国的计划，美国人罗伯特·富尔顿随即获得在巴黎建造全景画的许可。当资金短缺迫使他转让许可权后，其他经营者在至今仍被称为"全景画廊"的场所建造了两幅作品，分别展现了 1793 年土伦围城战与巴黎的纪念碑群。 随即一家创新工厂推出家用版产品——以巴加泰尔花园[572]为题材的景观壁纸。
Scenic papers came into their own in 1804 with a panorama 20 strips wide of Captain Cook’s voyages in the Pacific [573]. Families bought the paper with a printed description “so that, without leaving his home, a man can transport himself into the presence of the strange peoples he has read about, and a mother can instruct her bright little girl in history, geography, and botany.” The foreground of exotic trees pushed back the distance, as in the painted panoramas, and also served to frame doors and windows. These largest of all woodcuts required thousands of enormous blocks for the many tints and colors and a constant humidity to print correct register on the long stretches of paper. Most of the scenic wallpapers produced in Paris and Alsace from 1800 to 1835 have survived in the United States where wooden houses kept them dry, and conservative taste cherished them long after they bored Europe. They were priced out of existence after 1829 when endless strips of the new machine-made paper fed the first steam-driven presses for printing repeat designs at the rate of 18,000 yards a day. In 1933 England alone printed enough wallpaper to girdle the earth some 30 times.
风景画报于 1804 年凭借库克船长太平洋航行全景图（由 20 幅画幅组成）大放异彩[573]。家庭购买这类画报时会附带印刷说明："让男人足不出户便能置身于书中描述的异域民族之中，母亲也能借此教导聪慧的女儿学习历史、地理与植物学。" 异域树木构成的前景如同绘制全景画般延伸至远方，同时框起门窗。这些史上最大的木刻版画需使用数千块巨型木板呈现丰富色调，且必须保持恒定湿度才能在长卷纸上精准套印。 1800 至 1835 年间巴黎与阿尔萨斯制作的风景壁纸，多数在美国得以保存——木结构房屋保持其干燥，保守审美使其在欧洲遭弃后仍被珍视。1829 年后，当新型机器制造的无尽纸卷驱动首台蒸汽印刷机，以日产 18000 码的速度印制重复图案时，传统壁纸便因价格失衡而消亡。 1933 年，仅英国一国生产的壁纸总长度就足以环绕地球约 30 圈。

On cloth, china, and enamel (在布料、瓷器和搪瓷上)


In 1751/52 Irishmen invented, and Englishmen developed, picture printing to revolutionize the decoration of cloth, chinaware, and enameled copper. For centuries Europeans had block-printed cloth with oil stains that washed out. These became particularly unsatisfactory when they had to compete with Indian cottons hand painted in washable dyes.
在布料、瓷器和搪瓷器上 1751/52 年间，爱尔兰人发明、英国人发展了图案印刷技术，彻底革新了布料、瓷器和搪瓷铜器的装饰工艺。数百年来，欧洲人采用油渍木版印刷布料，但油渍易被洗掉。当这些布料不得不与印度手工绘制的棉布（采用可水洗染料）竞争时，这种印刷工艺尤其令人不满。
From 1676 to 78 in London and Amsterdam various mordants were thickened into pastes for block-printing to produce fast reds, browns, and purples at one dip into a brew of madder roots. Additional fast colors might then be hand painted on the cloth with fluid dyes. At about this time some engravings of maps and thèses
1676 至 1678 年间，伦敦与阿姆斯特丹的工匠们将各类媒染剂浓缩成糊状，用于木版印刷。只需将布料浸入茜草根熬制的染液中，便能获得持久的红、棕、紫色调。随后可再以液态染料手工描绘其他耐光色泽。大约同期，部分地图与论文的铜版画亦采用此法制作。
On cloth, china, and enamel
在布料、瓷器和搪瓷上
were printed on satin in printer’s ink. Attempts to print fast colors from engravings failed because the metal grooves did not retain the fluid dyes. Then, in 1752, Francis Nixon, a Dublin engraver, made dyes viscous enough to print engravings on linen and cotton. This led to a production of washable pictures on cloth, three to six feet tall and as intricate as the most laborious embroidery [ 574 ]. Moving to London, Nixon made a sensation with a public accustomed to cloth blockprinted in simple repeats about one foot tall. A Scot, Thomas Bell, speeded up the decoration of cloth by printing it from relief rollers in 1783 and from engraved rollers in 1790.
这些图案是用印刷油墨印在缎面上的。尝试用铜版画印刷艳丽色彩的努力均告失败，因为金属凹槽无法保留液态染料。直到 1752 年，都柏林雕刻师弗朗西斯·尼克松研制出粘稠度足够的染料，才得以在亚麻布和棉布上印刷铜版画。 由此催生出可水洗的布面画作，尺寸三至六英尺高，其精妙程度堪比最繁复的刺绣[574]。移居伦敦后，尼克松以突破性的工艺震撼了习惯于简易重复图案（约一英尺高）的公众。1783 年，苏格兰人托马斯·贝尔运用凸版滚筒印刷技术，1790 年则采用雕刻滚筒印刷技术，大幅提升了布料装饰的效率。
The most productive of the early printers on cloth was a German, Christoph Phillip Oberkampf, who started block-printing in 1760 at Jouy near the gates of Versailles and in 1770 added a copperplate press. His cloth was not cheap, for the eight yards then needed for a dress could cost up to 240 livres, while the same length of black satin cost only 40 livres in 1787. Nevertheless, by 1805 he was employing three full-time designers, five copperplate engravers, 40 woodblock cutters, and
早期布料印刷业中最高产的印刷商是德国人克里斯托夫·菲利普·奥伯坎普夫，他于 1760 年在凡尔赛城门附近的茹伊开始木版印刷，1770 年又添置了铜版印刷机。 其织物价格不菲——当时制作一件裙装所需的八码布料最高可达 240 里弗尔，而 1787 年同等长度的黑色缎料仅需 40 里弗尔。尽管如此，到 1805 年他已雇佣三名专职设计师、五名铜版雕刻师、四十名木版雕刻师，以及
Figure 176: 574  图 176：574
Shepherds among Ruins. Engraving printed on cotton by Robert Jones, Old Ford, London, 1761
废墟中的牧羊人。罗伯特·琼斯于伦敦老福德制作的棉版雕刻版画，1761 年
On cloth, china, and enamel
在布料、瓷器和搪瓷上
575
The Constitution. Engraving printed on glazed earthenware, Liverpool, after 1797
《宪法》。刻印于釉面陶器上，利物浦，1797 年后
175 printers in a total staff of 1322 employees. His factory flourished until soldiers of the Allies plundered it in 1805 and Oberkampf died.
在总计 1322 名员工中，有 175 名印刷工。他的工厂兴旺发达，直至 1805 年盟军士兵洗劫工厂，奥伯坎夫也因此去世。
Intricate and inexpensive decoration began on chinaware and enameled copper at about the same time it began on cloth. In 1751 John Brooks, an Irish mezzotinter, applied in Birmingham for a patent on “an art entirely new, and of his own invention” for “printing upon enamel and china from engraved, etched, and mezzotinto plates, and from cuttings in wood and mettle, impressions of History, Portraits, Landskips, Foliages, Coats of Arms, Cyphers, Letters, and other Devices.” In 1754/55 Brooks reapplied for his patent from Battersea. His invention was brilliantly simple. A woodblock, copperplate, or in time a lithographic stone was printed in pure oil on thin paper or a flexible gelatin sheet, from which the oiled design was offset onto enamel or glazed china. When finely powdered enamel color was dusted on, it stuck to the oiled areas and slid off the bare glaze. A brief firing melted the enamel dust into the glaze. Suddenly anybody could afford snuffboxes, teacups, and dishes ornamented with the fine detail previously reserved for rich men’s porcelains. The demand for the new transfer-printed wares was such that Commons was told in 1759 that " 30 or 40 Frenchmen and Germans are constantly employed in drawing and designing" at Birmingham alone. Even greater production began at Liverpool when the kilns loaded directly onto ships to export cream-colored earthenware with black-printed American patriotic designs for the new United States [ 575 ]. (The ships returned with copper ore from Cuba.)
约在同一时期，瓷器和搪瓷铜器上开始出现精美且廉价的装饰，这与织物上的装饰发展同步。 1751 年，爱尔兰凹版雕刻师约翰·布鲁克斯在伯明翰申请专利，称其发明了"一种全新技艺"，可"通过雕刻、蚀刻及凹版雕刻的铜版，以及木刻与金属刻版，在珐琅与瓷器上印制历史场景、肖像、风景、植物纹样、纹章、徽记、字母及其他图案"。 1754/55 年间，布鲁克斯从巴特西重新提交专利申请。其发明原理精妙而简明：先将木刻版、铜版（后期亦可使用平版石）印制的纯油墨图案转移至薄纸或柔性明胶片上，再将油墨图案转印至珐琅或釉面瓷器。当细粉状珐琅颜料撒布其上时，颜料会附着于油墨区域，从裸露釉面滑落。 经短暂烧制，珐琅粉便熔入釉面。从此，任何人都能拥有饰有精美纹饰的鼻烟壶、茶杯和餐盘——这些细节曾是富人瓷器的专属。新型转印瓷器需求旺盛，1759 年科蒙斯被告知仅伯明翰一地"就有三十至四十名法国人与德国人持续从事绘图设计工作"。 当窑炉直接装船出口奶油色陶器时，利物浦的生产规模更上一层楼——这些陶器印有黑色美国爱国图案，专供新成立的合众国市场[575]。（返航时船只满载古巴铜矿。）
The English Industrial Revolution thus extended picture printing to household things as well as to newspaper illustration [ 638 ] and color lithographs [ 641 ]. These applications all presupposed the factory system, which differs from cottage industries not by numbers of hands but by the need for expensive machines and expert supervision.
英国工业革命由此将图片印刷技术推广至家居用品领域，同时应用于报纸插图[638]与彩色平版印刷[641]。这些应用均以工厂制为前提——其与家庭作坊的区别不在于劳动力规模，而在于需要昂贵机器与专业监督。

Venetian and Roman printmakers (威尼斯与罗马版画家)


In Venice a century of pictorial stagnation ended in the early 1700s with the emergence of her last great painters, who also schooled Europe in etching. Since Venetian etchers either worked with painters, or were painters themselves, they experimented without regard for copperplate craft conventions.
威尼斯与罗马版画家 18 世纪初，威尼斯画坛结束了长达一个世纪的停滞期，涌现出最后一批伟大画家，他们同时将蚀刻技艺传授给整个欧洲。由于威尼斯蚀刻师或与画家合作，或本身就是画家，他们在创作中大胆尝试，完全不受铜版工艺传统束缚。
The most radical innovator was Antonio Canal, better known as Canaletto. After his father had taught him to paint the perspective of stage scenery with rapid accuracy in his early 20s, Canaletto went to Rome and learned picturesque composition from Pannini’s arrangements of ruins. Somewhere he studied Dutch street scenes in which burghers saunter, gossip, and cheapen fish. He was 44 when he dated one of his 30 etchings, published by the British consul at Venice. British tourists brought this set of prints to England before Canaletto traveled there when he was about 50 for the first of two visits. He etched in long, clean, trembling lines that twinkle like moist sunlight on water, and he shaped his leisurely figures as if he had exactly dripped them with treacle [ 576 ]. No detail disturbs the gentlemanly composure of a simplicity too difficult, too personal, to found a school.
最具革新精神的艺术家当属安东尼奥·卡纳尔，人称卡纳莱托。二十岁出头时，他跟随父亲习得快速精准绘制舞台景深技法，随后远赴罗马，从潘尼尼的废墟构图中领悟了风景画的精髓。 在某处，他研习了荷兰街景画——市民们悠闲漫步、闲谈八卦、讨价还价购买鱼货。当他在威尼斯英国领事馆出版的三十幅蚀刻版画中标注创作年份时，年方四十四。 这组版画由英国游客带回本土，此时卡纳莱托约五十岁，正开启其两次访英之旅中的首次。他以纤长清亮的颤动线条刻画画面，宛若水面闪烁的湿润阳光；人物姿态悠然舒展，仿佛被糖浆精准滴落塑形[576]。所有细节皆不扰其绅士般的从容气质——这种极致简约的风格既难以复制，又极具个人特色，终究未能开创画派。
576 Tower near Mestre. Etching by Canaletto
梅斯特雷附近的 576 号塔楼。卡纳莱托蚀刻版画
The most imitated Venetian etcher, especially in France, was Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, Giovanni Battista’s eldest son, who used his father’s sparkling, idiosyncratic scribbles [ 581 ] to freshen standard crosshatching into something new, yet adaptable. Domenico’s Venetian painter’s training in atmospheric landscape and the grouping of figures served him to etch 27 episodes of the Holy Family’s Flight into Egypt [ 577 ]. So many variations would not have been possible with a hieratic subject like the Nativity or the Crucifixion. Domenico also developed variations on other themes in witty, modish albums of ink drawings for Venetians cooped up in houses too constricted by canals for hanging big pictures. Photographic reproductions have made these series of drawings into today’s high fashion, but Domenico Tiepolo impressed his contemporaries during his late teens to his early zos when he advertised the family fresco team by etching 116 of his father’s decorations, reanimating all the sunny grandeur of this last recklessly aristocratic art [ 578 ].
在威尼斯蚀刻艺术家中，最受模仿者当属乔瓦尼·多梅尼科·提埃波罗——乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔的长子。他运用父亲那璀璨而独特的笔触[581]，将传统交叉线条技法焕新为既具创新性又富于适应性的表现形式。 多梅尼科在威尼斯画家训练中习得的氛围化风景与人物群像技法，助其完成了《圣家逃往埃及》系列的 27 幅蚀刻作品[577]。 若以圣婴诞生或耶稣受难这类庄严题材，绝不可能呈现如此丰富的变奏。多梅尼科还为受困于运河环绕的狭窄住宅、无处悬挂巨幅画作的威尼斯市民，创作了机智新潮的水墨画册，在其他主题上也发展出丰富变体。 摄影复制品使这些系列素描成为当今时尚宠儿，但多梅尼科·提埃波罗真正令同时代人惊叹的，是他十几岁到二十出头时为家族壁画团队宣传所作的 116 幅父亲装饰画蚀刻复制品——这些作品重现了这种最后的、放纵不羁的贵族艺术所蕴含的阳光般壮丽[578]。
Venetian etching could also adapt itself to darkness to match the bloom of Piazzetta’s charcoal smudges, for which Pitteri etched in parallels like Mellan’s engraved sweeps [ 289 ], but blended his etched lines into broad tones by knotting
威尼斯蚀刻技法亦能顺应暗调，以匹配皮亚泽塔炭笔晕染的绽放效果——彼特里为此采用平行蚀刻手法，如梅兰雕刻的扫掠线条[289]，却将蚀刻线条交织成广阔色调，形成结状效果。
Venetian and Roman printmakers
威尼斯与罗马版画家
577 The Flight into Egypt. Etching by Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, 1750-52
577 《逃往埃及》。乔瓦尼·多梅尼科·提埃波罗蚀刻版画，1750-52 年

578

Glory and Honor. Etching by G. D. Tiepolo after a ceiling painted by Giovanni Battista Tiepolo
荣耀与尊荣。G·D·提埃波罗根据乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗绘制的穹顶壁画创作的蚀刻版画

579 St. John the Evangelist. Etching by Giovanni Marco Pitteri after Giovanni Battista Piazzetta
579 圣约翰福音书。由乔瓦尼·马尔科·皮特里根据乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·皮亚泽塔的版画作品蚀刻而成。
580 The Madonna of the Grand Duke. Engraving by Raphael Morghen after Raphael, 1823-26
580 大公爵的圣母像。拉斐尔·莫尔根根据拉斐尔原作制作的铜版画，1823-26 年
them with threaded specks in some secret of technique [ 579 ]. These ragged lines deepened into even more dramatic shadows when enlarged by Piranesi.
那些带有螺纹斑点的线条，蕴藏着某种技艺的奥秘[579]。当皮拉内西将其放大时，这些参差的线条便化作更具戏剧性的阴影。
Venice’s living collaboration of painters and etchers made for a sparkle that was rare in Rome, where tourists demanded prints of old paintings, old statues, and old buildings. With no painters on hand to prod them, Roman reproductive printmakers unthinkingly elaborated their technique into the ponderous, engine-turned engravings of Victorian parlors. After an engraver had copied a Raphael painting in a laborious wash drawing, and then had studied his tired transcription during months of pushing his graver, he had long forgotten Raphael’s poetic essence [ 580 ]. The empty competence and expensive drudgery of most later reproductive engravings made the world yawn at Raphael until good photographic reproductions revealed his reasoned and sensuous nobility.
威尼斯画家与蚀刻师的鲜活协作，孕育出罗马罕见的艺术光芒。在罗马，游客们追捧着古画、古雕像与古建筑的复制品。缺乏画家现场指导的罗马复刻版画家们，不假思索地将技艺发展成维多利亚时代客厅里那些沉闷的机械蚀刻版画。 当雕刻师耗费数月苦力，先以水彩素描临摹拉斐尔画作，再反复推敲刻刀下的疲惫复制品时，早已遗忘了拉斐尔诗意的精髓[580]。后来多数复制品空有技艺却沉闷乏味，令世人对拉斐尔作品兴致索然——直至精良的摄影复制品揭示出他理性与感性交融的崇高境界。


G. B. Tiepolo and Piranesi (G·B·提埃波罗与皮拉内西)


In his happy, busy 75 years, Giovanni Battista Tiepolo revived the glory of Italian fresco painting, brushed thousands of sketches, and still found moments to etch some 25 coppers with a magical dash that stimulated Piranesi, Fragonard, and Goya. Tiepolo in turn had formed his unvarying etching style on Castiglione’s Rembrandtesque, chopped-straw scribbles [526], also taking over the romantic stage properties of broken urns, goatish satyrs, asps, and skulls. But while Castiglione submerged time’s trash heap in twilight, Tiepolo turned necromancy into wit with sunlight from his airy brushwork [ 581 ].
乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗在其幸福而忙碌的七十五年间，重振了意大利壁画的辉煌，创作了数千幅素描，仍抽空以神奇的笔触蚀刻了约二十五幅铜版画，其艺术魅力启发了皮拉内西、弗拉戈纳尔和戈雅。 提埃波罗的蚀刻风格则源自卡斯蒂廖内的伦勃朗式碎草笔触[526]，同时继承了破碎花瓶、山羊般的萨提尔、毒蛇与骷髅等浪漫主义舞台元素。 但卡斯蒂廖内将时间的废墟淹没在暮色中，提埃波罗却用他轻盈的笔触[581]将巫术转化为智慧。
Tiepolo’s and Castiglione’s etchings were mainly what started Piranesi on his career. As youngsters both Canaletto and Piranesi had learned to render architecture promptly and convincingly by painting scenery for Venetian opera houses.
提埃波罗和卡斯蒂廖内的蚀刻版画主要启发了皮拉内西的艺术生涯。卡纳莱托和皮拉内西年轻时都曾为威尼斯歌剧院绘制布景，由此学会了迅速而逼真地描绘建筑。

582 A Prison. Etching by Giovanni Battista Piranesi from INVENZIONI CAPRIC DI CARCERI
582 监狱。乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·皮拉内西的蚀刻版画，选自《监狱奇想录》

583

Tomb of Cecilia Metella under construction. Etching by Piranesi in ANTICHITA ROMANE, Rome, 1756
塞西莉亚·梅泰拉陵墓施工图。皮拉内西蚀刻版画，载于《罗马古迹》，罗马，1756 年
Figure 177: G. B. Tiepolo and Piranesi
图 177：乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗与皮拉内西
While working for the theater, Piranesi etched 14 dream prisons [ 582 ] in free sweeps of shadow as translucent as sepia wash. Dramatist though he was, the theater was not to be his world, for he had absorbed from his engineering father and uncle a north Italian passion for archeology that drove him to discover his true home in Rome. From his settling there in his late 205 until his death 50 years later, he raised the old Roman craft of view-making to such fame that he came to embody Rome itself for the world at large more than any other individual except the pope. In nearly 1000 etchings he enlarged Pitteri’s ragged parallel lines [ 579 ] for biting his copperplates in metal troughs so rugged that he could calculate his profits on printing 4000 impressions from each plate. To simplify sales, he etched his address and his modest early price of 21 / 2 21 / 2 21//221 / 2 paoli under the title of each view. He used his stage painter’s skill with the scena per angolo [ 548 ] of buildings twisted askew to push Roman structures to the top and sides of the picture in a hallucinating grandeur of action [371]. The walls tower above a modern infestation of human degenerates who flutter like moths strayed into the daylight. When Rome’s weedshrouded remains began to fascinate him the way cadavers fascinate an anatomist, he presented them with all the apparatus of anatomical exposition. His atlases of sections and reconstructions cut down to the foundations, probed joints for building methods and postulated how Romans might have hoisted their magnified stone blocks [ 583 ].
在剧院工作期间，皮拉内西以自由挥洒的阴影勾勒出十四座梦幻监狱[582]，其通透质感宛若棕褐色水洗效果。 虽是戏剧家，剧院却非他的归宿。他从工程师父亲和叔父那里继承了北意大利人对考古学的热忱，这股热情驱使他最终在罗马找到了真正的归宿。自二十五岁定居罗马直至五十年后离世，他将古罗马的透视画技艺推向巅峰，以至于在世人眼中，他几乎成为罗马的化身——其影响力仅次于教皇。 在近千幅蚀刻版画中，他将皮特里粗犷的平行线条[579]放大，在金属槽中刻蚀铜版时手法如此粗粝，竟能精确计算每版印刷 4000 张的利润。为简化销售，他将地址与早期低廉的 21 / 2 21 / 2 21//221 / 2 帕奥利定价刻在每幅风景画标题下方。 他运用舞台画师的技艺，以扭曲倾斜的建筑"scena per angolo"[548]手法，将罗马建筑推至画面顶端与侧边，营造出幻觉般的宏大动势[371]。高耸的城墙俯视着现代堕落人群的侵扰，他们如误入白昼的飞蛾般翩跹。 当罗马被杂草覆盖的遗迹开始像尸体吸引解剖学家那样吸引他时，他便用解剖学展示的全套工具来呈现这些遗迹。他的剖面图集与重建图集将建筑剖至地基，探查接合处以探究建造方法，并推测古罗马人如何吊起那些巨大的石块[583]。
As he studied and collected ancient marbles, he began to adapt their carved orna-
当他研究并收藏古代大理石雕塑时，他开始借鉴其雕刻的装饰——
Figure 178: G. B. Tiepolo and Piranesi
图 178：乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗与皮拉内西
584
A mantelpiece. Etching by Piranesi in DIVERSE MANIERE D’ADORNARE I CAMMINI, Rome (Salomoni), 1769
壁炉架。皮拉内西蚀刻版画，选自《壁炉装饰的多种方式》，罗马（萨洛莫尼出版社），1769 年
ment to designing mantelpieces, clocks, and sedan chairs in etchings that prepared the climate for the Empire style. He was also the first designer to use Egyptian details, standing Pharaohs on their heads [584] as high-handedly as Borromini, a century before, had upended obelisks onto their points to flank Roman doorways.
他致力于设计壁炉架、钟表和轿子，其蚀刻版画为帝国风格的兴起奠定了基础。他还是首位运用埃及元素的设计师，将法老像倒置于顶端[584]，其气魄之大堪比百年前博罗米尼将方尖碑倒置于尖端，矗立于罗马门廊两侧的壮举。
Piranesi’s passion for a Rome that never was saved him from getting lost in the nit-picking of print techniques and made him one of the rare print specialists who achieved drama and grandeur without the clarifying discipline of painting. He was actually so far from being a painter that he drew his on-the-spot notes in precise proportion, but purposely bare and dry enough to reserve for his etching needle the painter’s excitement of inventing shadows on crumbling brick and ravaged marble. Etchings so obsessive imposed a super-Roman scale on the architectural imagination that was to create our law courts, museums, and railroad terminals.
皮拉内西对一个不曾存在的罗马的痴迷，使他免于沉溺于版画技法的吹毛求疵，成为罕见的版画大师——在缺乏绘画的澄明训练下，他依然成就了戏剧性的宏伟。 他与画家身份的距离之远，体现在他现场速写时虽保持精准比例，却刻意保持简洁干涩的笔触——只为将刻刀留给画家那般在斑驳砖墙与残缺大理石上创造阴影的激情。这些近乎痴迷的蚀刻版画，为建筑想象赋予了超罗马式的宏大尺度，最终塑造了我们的法院、博物馆与火车站。

Watteau and Boucher (瓦托与布歇)


inspired 18th-century Europe through more prints than any other painters of their time. Watteau drew and painted so compulsively during his 37 consumptive years that he had time to etch only ten coppers [ 585 ]. His dash and lightness, which delighted when he sketched, so flouted the craft conventions of reproductive printmaking when he etched that, after printing a few trial proofs, his etchings, like Van Dyck’s, were “finished” by professional engravers. He saw few of his works engraved by others, but after he died, the most avid collector of his works, Jean de Julienne, had 622 of his drawings and paintings reproduced on copper. This pioneer attempt to illustrate an artist’s complete work led in the long run to today’s comprehensive monographs on individual artists, and in its immediate effect it started all Europe imitating Watteau’s poetic scenes of lovers in neglected gardens. However, Watteau cast his most haunting spell with the anything but poetic subject of a shop sign showing half a dozen rich people haggling for luxuries [ 586 ]. Here he outdid his great Dutch model, Terborch, in the tension between a commonplace deal and its lyrical presentation.
瓦托和布歇通过比同时代任何画家都多的版画作品，启发了 18 世纪的欧洲。 瓦托在 37 年肺结核缠身的岁月里执笔作画如痴如醉，却仅有十幅铜版蚀刻作品问世[585]。他速写时令人惊叹的灵动笔触，在蚀刻版画中却因打破复制版画的技艺规范而遭质疑——试印数张后，其蚀刻作品便如凡·戴克的作品般，最终由专业雕刻师"完成"。 生前他鲜少目睹作品被他人蚀刻，但身后其最狂热的藏家让·德·朱利安将 622 幅素描与油画转刻铜版。这项开创性尝试旨在完整呈现艺术家作品，最终催生了当今针对个别艺术家的综合性专著，而其即时效应则是整个欧洲纷纷效仿瓦托笔下恋人流连荒园的诗意场景。 然而瓦托最令人心醉神迷的魔力，竟来自一幅全然不诗意的题材——描绘六位富人讨价还价购买奢侈品的店招画[586]。在这幅作品中，他超越了荷兰大师特伯赫，将寻常交易与抒情呈现的张力发挥得淋漓尽致。

图 180：587 弗朗索瓦·布歇根据瓦托素描创作的蚀刻版画，1727-31 年 588 吉尔·德马托根据布歇作品创作的点蚀版画
To finance the publication for over 15 years out of his own pocket, Julienne had to sell subjects as they were finished. This glutting of the market forced him finally to remainder most of the 100 sets and shortened the vogue for Watteau. The 40 artists in his employ, nearly all the printmakers of France, speeded the work by blending the tried copperplate formulas for reproducing paintings: Bosse’s for architecture, Cort’s for clouds, Barocci’s for faces, and the new Venetian school’s for general swiftness of attack. By developing quick etching at the expense of slow engraving, they introduced painters to etching as a sideline, and started professional printmakers etching forcibly enough to sparkle through the finishing with the graver.
为维持刊物长达十五年的出版经费，朱利安不得不将完成的作品逐批售出。这种市场饱和最终迫使他将百套作品中的大部分降价处理，也缩短了瓦托作品的风靡期。 他雇佣的 40 位艺术家几乎囊括了法国所有版画家，他们通过融合经实践验证的铜版画复制技法加速了创作进程：建筑部分采用博斯的技法，云朵部分采用科尔特的技法，人脸部分采用巴洛奇的技法，而新威尼斯学派则以整体的快速处理见长。 通过发展快速蚀刻而牺牲慢速雕刻，他们让画家们将蚀刻作为副业，并促使专业版画家们以足够强烈的力度进行蚀刻，以致在刻刀的修饰下仍能闪耀光芒。
Julienne began his publication with the comparatively straightforward problem of reproducing 351 of the magically deft figure drawings that Watteau stored up to group and regroup in his paintings. 103 of these drawings were etched by François Boucher as he turned 20 [ 587 ]. Watteau’s red chalk strokes, impeccably accented with black, limbered Boucher’s etching needle as it crisply imitated them, and the
朱利安的出版工作始于相对简单的问题：复刻瓦托为绘画创作而积累的 351 幅精妙绝伦的人物素描。其中 103 幅由弗朗索瓦·布歇在二十岁时以蚀刻版画形式呈现[587]。瓦托那灵动自如的红粉笔线条，经布歇蚀刻针的灵动演绎，在清晰复刻时更添韵律。 瓦托以红粉笔勾勒的线条，辅以精妙的黑色点缀，令布歇的蚀刻针灵活地模仿其笔触，呈现出鲜明的效果。

590 Venus Asking Vulcan to Forge Arms for Aeneas. Etching after Boucher's painting of 1747
590 金星请伏尔甘为埃涅阿斯锻造武器。据布歇 1747 年油画蚀刻版画



exercise brilliantly liberated his drawing pencil. With over twice Watteau’s working time, Boucher etched some 180 original copperplates, while his paintings and drawings were copied for 50 years in nearly 1300 prints that permeated European art from the day when he became known by winning a prize at the age of 20 . His etchings after Watteau helped to propagate such a taste for reproductions of drawings that when his own drawings began to sell, 266 of them were etched in stipple substitutes by Gilles Demarteau [ 588 ]. These were printed in red ink to look like red chalk drawings for framing as little pictures to hang in the small blank spaces of elaborately decorated paneling.
布歇的创作才华令他的画笔焕发光彩。他耗费的时间是瓦托的两倍有余，蚀刻了约 180 幅原创铜版画，而他的绘画与素描作品在 50 年间被复制成近 1300 幅版画，自他 20 岁获奖成名之日起便渗透进欧洲艺术界。 他临摹瓦托的蚀刻版画助长了对素描复制品的追捧，当其原作开始售出时，吉勒·德马尔托[588]便以点刻法复刻了 266 幅作品。这些作品以红墨水印制，仿若红粉笔素描，专为装裱成小幅画作而设计，可悬挂于精雕细琢的镶板间隙处。
Boucher’s most original inventions were decorative, especially in the fashionable style of chinoiserie, to which he was introduced by having etched 12 Figures Chinoises by Watteau. The 18th century was fascinated by a mostly imaginary Cathay, with a court etiquette more ancient and elaborate than its own, and a practical morality unembittered by the wrangling of priests. Chinoiserie decorations tended to be finicky and improbable, except when Boucher drew Celestials with a generous scale and a dreamlike humanity [ 589 ]. His French common sense and the drive of his sensuality also made him the last painter to present the gods of Olympus in pulsing flesh and blood [ 590 ].
布歇最具原创性的创作体现在装饰艺术领域，尤其擅长时髦的西式中国风。他因蚀刻瓦托的《十二幅中国风人物》而接触此风格。十八世纪沉醉于一个多半虚构的 Cathay（中国），那里宫廷礼仪比本国更古老繁复，实用道德未被神职人员的争吵所玷污。 中式装饰往往繁琐而离奇，唯独布歇笔下的天朝子民例外——他以宽厚的尺度勾勒出如梦似幻的人性光辉[589]。其法式常识与感官冲动的驱使，更使他成为最后一位以鲜活血肉呈现奥林匹斯众神的画家[590]。

Etching in France and Switzerland (法国与瑞士的蚀刻工艺)


French 18th-century printmakers deferred to copperplate conventions when they etched the groundwork for formal official prints that imitated engraving, but when they did not have to finish with the graver, they etched almost as spontaneously as the Venetians. One of the most intelligent French etchers was the younger C.-N. Cochin, who was appointed Louis XV’s illustrator of festivities when he was 20 and became the darling portraitist of the intellectuals [ 291 ]. Like most 18th-century Frenchmen, he freezes in the togas of Roman tableaux but is witty and acute when at home with his friends in the royal drawing school on the one day a year when a woman posed for three hours [591]. The silent intensity of such student competitions trained 18th-century French artists to their almost interchangeable command of hand.
法国与瑞士的蚀刻艺术 18 世纪法国版画家在为仿刻版画的正式官方印刷品制作底稿时，仍遵循铜版画的传统规范；但当无需使用刻刀完成作品时，他们的蚀刻技法几乎与威尼斯画派同样自由奔放。 法国最聪慧的蚀刻艺术家之一是小 C.-N.科钦，他二十岁时被任命为路易十五的庆典插画家，后来成为知识分子圈中备受宠爱的肖像画家[291]。 与多数十八世纪法国人相似，他在描绘罗马题材时拘泥于古装画的框架，但在皇家绘画学院与友人共度的时光里却展现出机敏锋芒——每年仅此一日，有位女性模特会为他们摆出三小时的姿态[591]。这类学生竞赛中无声的专注氛围，使十八世纪法国艺术家们练就了近乎千篇一律的娴熟技法。
Cochin was born in a dynasty of artists as interrelated as the old nobility, whose
科钦生于一个艺术世家，其家族关系错综复杂，如同古老的贵族世系，其
591 Mlle Clairon posing for the first tête d’expression competition at the Académie, Paris, 1759. Etching by Charles-Nicolas Cochin II
591 克莱隆小姐为巴黎学院首届表情肖像比赛摆姿势，1759 年。查尔斯-尼古拉·科尚二世蚀刻版画

inbreeding also characterizes a family like the Saint-Aubins. A Saint-Aubin who designed embroidery was himself the son of another embroiderer, and in turn became the father of four artists. His eldest son, Charles-Germain de Saint-Aubin, styled himself “embroiderer of the King’s coats, waistcoats, and breeches,” and said, “I have drawn 40,000 designs for embroiderers, weavers, and lacemakers, all of which have vanished, as I myself will vanish.” A dozen of his decorative inventions survive today in a set of etched monograms concocted out of flowers, stalactites, and stars [ 592 ]. His ravishing etchings of the daily life of butterflies [ 593 ] are trifles that achieve the aim of the age by taking to the air as they made light of the needed effort. The most successful son, Augustin, was received into the Académie, designed skillful vignettes for countless books, and etched over 500 profiles in the style introduced by Cochin. But perhaps just because Augustin swam com-
近亲繁殖同样是圣奥班家族的特征。一位设计刺绣的圣奥班，其父亦是刺绣师，而他自己又成为四位艺术家的父亲。其长子夏尔-热尔曼·德·圣奥班自称"国王外套、马甲和马裤的刺绣师"，并言道： "我为刺绣师、织布工和蕾丝匠绘制过四万幅图案，如今都已消逝，正如我终将消逝。"他设计的十几件装饰作品至今尚存，是一组由花朵、钟乳石和星辰构成的蚀刻字母组合[592]。 他描绘蝴蝶日常生活的迷人蚀刻版画[593]虽属小品，却以轻盈姿态飞向天空，恰如其分地实现了那个时代的艺术追求。最成功的儿子奥古斯丁入选法兰西学院，为无数书籍设计精巧的插图，并以科钦开创的技法蚀刻了 500 余幅肖像轮廓。但或许正因奥古斯丁游刃有余——

pliantly with the current of his time, he seems to us to have less personality than his embroiderer brother and much less than the fascinating Gabriel, the elder brother who shamed the family with lifelong failure. After poor Gabriel thrice missed a scholarship for Rome in his late 20s, he lived alone in horrifying disorder while he mooned around town sketching anything and everything. On the wide margins of catalogues for auctions and the biennial Salons he drew thumbnail notations that document the exhibited works of art for us today. In occasional little etchings that then seemed as amateurish as Watteau’s, Gabriel preserved the freshest and gauziest visions of old Paris: its theaters, its public gardens, its art exhibitions, and its coffeehouses [ 594 ]. The city’s jostle inspired him with a verve that nevertheless deserted even him when he strained after the high style of allegory.
他随波逐流，在我们看来，他的人格魅力远不及刺绣的弟弟，更不及那位迷人的长兄加布里埃尔——这位终生失败的兄长令家族蒙羞。当穷困潦倒的加布里埃尔在二十多岁时三度错失罗马奖学金后，他独自生活在骇人的混乱中，整天在城里闲逛，随手勾勒着任何事物。 在拍卖目录与双年沙龙的宽阔页边，他随手绘制的简略标注，为后世留存了这些展出艺术品的珍贵记录。 在那些偶尔创作的小版画里——当时它们看起来和瓦托的作品一样业余——加布里埃尔保留了老巴黎最清新、最朦胧的景象：剧院、公共花园、艺术展览和咖啡馆[594]。城市的喧嚣激发了他蓬勃的创作力，然而当他勉强追求高深的寓言风格时，这份灵感连他也抛弃了。
The Parisian punishment of deviations from “good taste” did not frighten Switzerland. There the pastellist Liotard, after five years in Istanbul and elsewhere, dared put a major effort into big etched family portraits in which he explored the mysterious tone made by pressing cloth into a soft etching ground [ 595 ]. These works from beyond the range of Parisian dictates have still not been properly valued for their large vision and delicate adjustment of light.
巴黎对偏离"雅致品味"的惩罚并未令瑞士却步。在那儿，粉彩画家利奥塔尔历经伊斯坦布尔等地的五年游历后，大胆投入精力创作大型蚀刻家族肖像，探索将布料压入柔软蚀刻底料所产生的神秘色调[595]。这些超越巴黎教条范畴的作品，其宏大的视野与精妙的明暗调度至今仍未获得应有的评价。

The estampe galante (《雅致版画》)


Under Louis XIV official engravings ceremonially glorified the king’s buildings, his battles, his courtiers, and his person. The next century shifted to the pleasures of the individual, and especially to the ruses and obstacles that could complicate love sufficiently to fill life’s vacancy. While rooms in England were hung with mezzotints of prominent English people and of dairymaids and lusty stable lads, French salons were decorated with engravings of galanterie, meaning urbane pleasures. French printmakers elaborated the estampe galante with that harmony of skills which made the 18th century unique. One man drew the picture, a second etched most of the copper [596], a third smoothed the transitions with a graver [ 597 ], a fourth designed the decorative border, and a fifth engrossed the lettering-all collaborating toward what looks like one man’s inspiration. Admiration for the teamwork is tempered only by a slight disappointment at the leveling of personalities. Contemporary collectors preferred the state after the graver had refined the details but before the lettering had been added (avant la lettre.) The preliminary etched state, whose raggedness catches some personal brilliance, learned from the Venetians, was not put on sale because, as the
路易十四统治时期的宫廷版画，通过官方雕版画庄严颂扬着国王的建筑、战役、朝臣及其本人。 下个世纪则转向个人享乐，尤其着迷于那些足以填补生命空虚的爱情诡计与障碍。当英国的房间挂满英国名流、奶娘和健壮马厩小伙的凹版画时，法国沙龙却装饰着象征雅致享乐的"风流画"。 法国版画家以精妙技艺协作创作"雅致版画"，这种工匠协作模式成就了十八世纪的独特艺术生态：一人绘制画面，二人刻制铜版[596]，三人以刻刀[597]修饰过渡，四人设计装饰边框，五人书写题字——众人协作呈现出宛如单人创作的灵感之作。 对这种团队合作的赞叹，仅因个性被抹平而稍显遗憾。当代收藏家更青睐刻刀精炼细节后、题字添注前的版本（称作"题字前版"）。这种承袭威尼斯技法、以粗粝质感闪现个人才华的初版蚀刻，因"题字前版"的特殊价值而未被公开发售。

Académie Royale said in 1761, its “lack of finish might damage the artist’s reputation.” At this time the woodcutter Papillon dismissed etching as “a sketcher’s amusement.”
皇家美术学院在 1761 年指出，其"未完成的状态可能损害艺术家的声誉"。此时木刻艺术家帕皮永则将蚀刻技法贬为"素描者的消遣"。
The briskest contriver of gallant escapades was Fragonard, the Frenchman who also came closest to the Tiepolos’ happy largeness of design. During his 205 and early 305 in Venice and elsewhere in Italy, he miniaturized G. B. Tiepolo’s etching style to record Italian paintings, at the same time training his hand through penciling swift copies of baroque ceiling decorations. The great Italians energized his art with a dash that substitutes adequately for passion [ 598 ].
最擅长构思绅士冒险故事的当属法国画家弗拉戈纳尔，他亦最接近提埃波罗家族那种欢快而宏大的设计风格。在威尼斯及意大利各地度过的二十五岁至三十五岁期间，他将乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗的蚀刻画风格微缩化，用于记录意大利绘画，同时通过速写巴洛克天花板装饰来磨练技艺。 伟大的意大利艺术家们为他的创作注入了活力，这种灵动之笔足以替代激情[598]。
The circumstantial observer of aristocratic manners, Moreau le jeune, fitted the theme of gallantry into two series of engravings, later called Le Monument du Costume, designed, as if in anticipation of the guillotine, “to document the manners and dress of the French in the 18th century.” The first series matures a young married
贵族礼仪的旁观者莫罗·勒·让，将骑士精神主题融入两组版画系列，后被称为《服饰纪念碑》。这些作品仿佛预见了断头台的降临，旨在"记录十八世纪法国人的礼仪与服饰"。首组作品描绘了一对新婚夫妇的成熟风采。

The second series follows the day of a young aristocrat from his being dressed and frizzed to his midnight supper party, and then contrasts these vanities with the “true happiness” of a farmer’s family on the 12th plate. Though Moreau was the son of a wigmaker, he showed himself as conversant with the rooms and the bearing of the aristocracy as if he had been born one of the wealthy, curled darlings that he depicted.
从初次怀孕时的琐碎消遣与风流韵事[599]，到羽饰与钻石交相辉映的宫廷盛宴中登峰造极，这位女性的华丽变迁尽数呈现。 第二组作品则聚焦年轻贵族的一日：从梳妆打扮到深夜宴会的辗转，最终在第十二幅版画中将这些虚荣与农家"真实的幸福"形成鲜明对照。莫罗虽出身假发匠之家，却对贵族阶层的居室布局与仪态举止了如指掌，仿佛他生来便是画中那些卷发富家子弟中的一员。
At the end of the century, when Rousseau was piqueing surfeited appetites with the surprise of simplicity, Greuze brought love into family life [600] with the young mother nursing her baby, the erring daughter coming home for paternal pardon, or a family music lesson.
世纪末，当卢梭以质朴的惊奇唤醒人们被过度满足的感官时，格勒兹将爱注入家庭生活[600]——年轻母亲哺育婴儿，迷途女儿归家求父宽恕，或是全家共奏乐章的温馨场景。
The carefree estampe galante perished in the French Revolution, along with the sweetness of life that Talleyrand regretted losing. Only one artist, Prud’hon, was
那无忧无虑的雅致版画在法国大革命中消亡，连同塔列朗扼腕痛惜的那些生活中的甜蜜。唯独一位艺术家——普鲁东——
able to carry the seductiveness of the old monarchy across to the hard heroics of the Empire. But love had suffered a sea change. Fashionable people were now seen at church, and sunlight filtered into drawing rooms through stained glass. To tingle agreeably, sensuality now had to spice itself with sacrilege in the mutual swooning of meaty monks and depilated nudes [601]. The blurring of the romantic penumbra taxed the last formal refinement of sophisticated engraving, just when the new invention of lithography was being perfected to get such effects more spontaneously.
能够将旧君主制的魅惑气息，传递到帝国的刚烈英雄主义之中。但爱情已然经历了翻天覆地的变化。时髦人士如今出现在教堂，阳光透过彩色玻璃洒进客厅。感官刺激要令人愉悦地战栗，如今必须在肥硕的僧侣与剃光体毛的裸体者相互晕眩的交融中，掺入亵渎的辛辣滋味[601]。 浪漫主义的阴翳渐趋模糊，恰在此时，新发明的平版印刷术正臻完善，能更自然地呈现此类效果，却也耗尽了精致雕版印刷最后的正式修饰。

Rowlandson and Debucourt (罗兰森与德布库尔)


Rowlandson was William Blake’s exact contemporary but in life and character so exactly Blake’s opposite that the antithesis discredits the “spirit of an age” as a convenient fiction. While Blake’s fame grew slowly inside the English-speaking world, Rowlandson quickly affected the Continent almost as decisively as Hogarth had. When Rowlandson’s father lost his money in the silk trade, the boy was brought up by a French aunt, who sent him to the Royal Academy drawing school at 15. The British neglect of figure drawing may have been remedied by a visit to Paris, for somehow he became the only English-
罗兰森与德布库尔罗兰森与威廉·布莱克恰是同时代人，但其生平与品性与布莱克截然相反，这种对立关系使"时代精神"沦为便利的虚构。当布莱克在英语世界声名渐起之际，罗兰森却如霍加斯般迅速而深刻地影响了欧洲大陆。 当罗兰森的父亲在丝绸贸易中破产后，少年由法国姑母抚养长大，15 岁时被送入皇家美术学院绘画学校。英国人对人体素描的忽视或许因他赴巴黎求学而得到弥补——不知何故，他竟成为唯一一位——
man of his time to draw the figure with the accurate ease of the French. He wrote little except his signature on thousands of watercolors, which show that he traveled in Great Britain, France, and the Netherlands. He exhibited watercolors only when he was 18 to 30 , after which his work began to coarsen, probably because he played cards with other sporting bloods instead of looking at the work of other artists. His art shows absolutely no effect from the innovations of Turner, who astonished England with his first big painting 27 years before Rowlandson died. During his 50
作为当代人，他能以法国画家的精准从容描绘人物。除在数千幅水彩画上签名外，他鲜少落笔，这些作品显示他曾游历英国、法国和荷兰。他仅在 18 至 30 岁间展出水彩画，此后作品渐趋粗粝，或许因他沉迷与其他纨绔子弟打牌，无暇研习他人画作。 他的艺术创作完全未受透纳革新风格的影响——透纳以首幅巨作震撼英伦时，距罗兰森逝世尚有二十七年之遥。在其五十载艺术生涯中，

working years Rowlandson often multiplied watercolors in replicas made by counterproofing [427] the preliminary drawing, and it was said that he “etched as much copper as would sheathe the British navy.” His dashing evocations of hunting [602] and boxing revealed the classic style for the great British specialty of sporting prints, into which he put more spirit than any specialist who followed him because he played with them for diversion instead of turning them out as a daily chore. Many of his etchings (but not his watercolors) satirize politicians [603] with a license that Philipon fought to introduce into France in the 1830s [659].
罗兰森创作生涯中常通过反向蚀刻[427]将草图复制为水彩复制品，据说他"蚀刻的铜版足以装甲英国整个海军舰队"。 他笔下充满活力的狩猎[602]与拳击场景，奠定了英国运动版画这一伟大领域的经典风格。相较于后来者，他赋予作品更鲜活的灵魂——因为他创作这些题材是出于兴趣而非日常功课。 他的许多蚀刻版画（但非水彩画）以肆无忌惮的笔触讽刺政客[603]——这种艺术自由正是菲利蓬在 1830 年代为法国争取的[659]。

604

Copying Old Masters at the British Institution. Aquatint by Pugin and Rowlandson in THE MICROCOSM OF LONDON, London (Ackermann), 1808-10
在英国机构临摹古典大师。普金与罗兰森的凹版蚀刻画，收录于《伦敦小宇宙》，伦敦（阿克曼出版社），1808-10 年
605 (OPPOSITE PAGE, ABOVE) Vauxhall Gardens. Aquatint after Rowlandson, 1785
605（对页上方）沃克斯豪尔花园。罗兰森原画的软刻版画，1785 年
To publish his caricatures while they still would sell as news, Rowlandson etched in rapid open lines for one deep bite of the acid. He then watercolored the first proof as a model to send upstairs in the publishing house of Rudolph Ackermann in the Strand, where French refugees copied the colors on the whole edition of prints. When he did not have to rush, he clothed his elegant, lively lines with the tone of aquatint [229] to supplement the finishing watercolor. The price, usually a shilling, often appears on the plate itself, and there is sometimes the notice that prints may be “lent out for the evening.” Thus Rowlandson snuggled into the heart of the country jollity that Englishmen lost after the “dark Satanic mills” began to dirty the air. Even London retained some village greenery and leisure when he etched it in one of the most human surveys of a great city. For the 104 views of the Microcosm of London, he fitted figures into architectural backgrounds drawn by a French refugee, Augustus Pugin [ 604 ].
为使漫画在仍具新闻价值时及时出版，罗兰森采用快速开放线条进行蚀刻，仅经一次深蚀处理。随后他将首版水彩样稿作为范本送往斯特兰德街鲁道夫·阿克曼出版社的楼上工坊，由法国难民工匠为整版印刷品复制色彩。 当无需赶工时，他便为优雅灵动的线条披上凹版水彩的色调[229]，以此补充最终的水彩润色。版画价格通常为一先令，常直接标注于版面之上，偶尔还附有"可借阅至晚间"的提示。 罗兰森就这样蜷缩在乡村欢愉的中心地带——当"黑暗的撒旦式工厂"开始污染空气后，这种欢愉便从英国人生活中消失了。 即便在伦敦，当他以最人性化的视角描绘这座大都市时，仍保留着乡村的绿意与闲适。在《伦敦小宇宙》的 104 幅景观中，他将人物置于法国流亡者奥古斯都·普金[604]绘制的建筑背景中。
Rowlandson’s French experience probably fitted him to collaborate with Pugin as smoothly as any artistic team in Paris. Before France and England stopped trading (1793 to 1812), Rowlandson repaid his debt to French art by setting a model for French prints of the Directoire in his breezy familiar etchings of the highjinks of fishmongers and countesses, bullyboys and tarts. Only seven years after the motley line-up of his Vauxhall Gardens [ 605 ], a similar carnival of impertinent fashion plates appeared in Paris in the masterpiece of Debucourt [ 606 ], who elaborated the Parisian technique of color printing until it needed no additional hand painting to complete the effect.
罗兰森在法国的经历，或许使他与普金的合作堪比巴黎任何艺术团队般默契。在英法贸易中断前（1793 至 1812 年），罗兰森以轻松写意的蚀刻版画为法国艺术报了恩——他笔下鱼贩与伯爵夫人、恶霸与风尘女子的嬉闹场景，为督政府时期的法国版画树立了典范。 在他创作《沃克斯豪尔花园》[605]那幅五花八门的画作仅七年后，巴黎便出现了德布库尔[606]的杰作——同样充满无礼时髦人士的狂欢盛宴。这位艺术家将巴黎彩色印刷技法推向极致，使作品无需额外手绘便能呈现完整效果。


English romantics (英国浪漫主义者)


In England, as in Germany [632], romantic artists retreated from the beginnings of modern industry into solitudes where they invoked a religious spirit outside the established churches. Romantic art was everywhere literary, but particularly so in England, where many artists wrote. These authorartists, with slight art schooling, rebelled against the increasing 18th-century dominance of dexterity over personality.
英国浪漫主义者在英国，正如在德国[632]那样，浪漫主义艺术家们从现代工业的萌芽中退隐至僻静之地，在那里他们唤起了一种超越传统教会的宗教精神。浪漫主义艺术无处不在地体现为文学形式，而在英国尤为显著——许多艺术家同时也是作家。这些作家兼艺术家虽受过有限的艺术训练，却反抗着 18 世纪日益盛行的以技巧凌驾于个性之上的风气。
Henry Fuseli preached the gospel in Zürich until he came to London at the age of 22 . Here, supporting himself by writing about art, he began seriously to draw and paint. He made a few soft-ground etchings by coating a copperplate with fat, laying a drawing face up on it, and pressing the drawn lines with a stylus to stick the fat to the back of the paper. Acid then bit the copper in charcoal-like lines that cannot be retouched unobtrusively [ 607 ]. Coarse cloth pressed onto the fatty coating makes a continuous tone [ 595 ]. Soft-ground etching, Castiglione’s forgotten invention, disappeared when lithography reached similar effects more directly.
亨利·富塞利在苏黎世传道，直至 22 岁来到伦敦。在此地，他靠撰写艺术评论谋生，并开始认真从事绘画创作。他曾制作过几幅软地蚀刻版画：先在铜版上涂抹油脂，将素描稿正面朝下覆盖其上，再用刻刀压出线条使油脂附着于纸张背面。 酸蚀铜版后形成的炭笔状线条无法自然修饰[607]。粗布压印于油脂涂层可形成连续色调[595]。这种卡斯蒂廖内发明的软地蚀刻技法，在平版印刷能更直接实现类似效果后便逐渐失传。
The renegade clergyman’s satanic satires affected his deeply religious, but anticlerical contemporary, William Blake. When Blake, at 14, began a seven-year apprenticeship with an engraver, he was set to copying medieval tombs in Westminster Abbey until he drew clothed figures so willowy that they can hardly lift the liquid weight of their draperies. He studied anatomy from engravings that must have included plunging muscle men from Michelangelo’s Last Judgment. During his remaining 50 years, he wrote lyrics that everybody remembers and then impenetrable cosmic twaddle. As his writing worsened, his drawing improved, so that the best of the writer rarely collaborated with the best of the painter. While poverty
这位叛逆神职人员的魔鬼式讽刺作品，深深影响了其同时代那位虔诚却反教会的诗人威廉·布莱克。十四岁起，布莱克开始跟随一位雕刻师进行为期七年的学徒生涯，最初任务是临摹威斯敏斯特教堂的中世纪墓碑。然而当他绘制衣着人物时，笔下人物纤细得几乎无法撑起衣料的流体重量。 他通过版画研习解剖学，其中必然包含米开朗基罗《最后的审判》里肌肉贲张的男子。此后五十年间，他创作了家喻户晓的诗歌，却也写下晦涩难懂的宇宙絮语。当文字日趋拙劣时，画技却日益精进，致使这位作家的巅峰之作鲜少与画家巅峰之作相得益彰。而贫困——
607
Witch and Mandrake. Softground etching by Henry Fuseli
女巫与曼德拉草。亨利·富塞利软地蚀刻版画
Figure 186: 608 "Pity, like a naked, newborn babe, striding the blast." "Illuminated fresco" by William Blake, 1795
图 186：608 "怜悯，如赤裸的新生婴儿，在狂风中昂首阔步。" 威廉·布莱克《光照壁画》，1795 年
forced him to engrave potboilers as drably as the next hack, he privately devised highly personal methods for his imaginative prints. He made “illuminated frescoes” by painting outlines on varnished cardboard, offsetting them onto paper through a rolling press, and finishing the picture with watercolor [ 608 ]. Rowlandson had already started this technique with red chalk, which may have reached Blake by roundabout report. He had a more unusual instructor for the books of illustrated poems-his “illuminated printing”-that he published from his early zos to his mid-60s, so unsuccessfully that he found few purchasers for the Songs of Innocence at five shillings and America at 10/6. For these he followed instructions received in a dream from his dead brother, who probably told him to write and draw with etching ground on varnished paper, press these lines onto a metal plate, and let acid erode the metal around them. Lines etched in such low relief would be hard to ink without the barely lowered background. Blake could have avoided this by pressing his relief plates against ink spread on a smooth sheet of metal. Like the Chinese and Japanese, who paint as they write and write as they paint, Blake in his own way charged his line with energy enough to flow from word to picture and
迫使他像其他庸才一样刻画乏味的应景之作时，他私下里为自己的创意版画设计了极具个人特色的技法。他通过在涂漆硬纸板上勾勒轮廓，经滚压机转印至纸张，再用水彩完成画面，制作出"彩绘湿壁画"[608]。罗兰森早已用红粉笔开创此技法，布莱克或许是通过间接传闻得知了这种手法。 在他二十多岁至六十多岁期间出版的插图诗集——即其"彩绘印刷"作品——背后，还有一位更为奇特的导师。这些作品市场反响极差，以致《天真之歌》定价五先令、《美国》定价十先令六便士仍鲜有买家问津。 为此他遵循已故兄长梦中传授的技法：在涂漆纸上以蚀刻底料书写绘图，将线条压印于金属板，再以酸蚀刻周围金属。 如此浅浮雕的线条若无微凹背景便难以上墨。布莱克本可将浮雕版直接压印在涂墨的平滑金属板上。如同中日韩艺术家将书写与绘画融为一体，布莱克以独特方式赋予线条充沛能量，使其能自文字流淌至画面——
English romantics  英国浪漫主义者

609

Hand-colored relief etching by Blake, 1794, title page for The Book of Urizen
布莱克手绘浮雕蚀刻版画，1794 年，《乌里森之书》题页

610

An Eclogue. Wood engraving by Blake in R. J. Thornton, VIRGIL ADAPTED FOR SCHOOLS, London (M’Gowan), 1821
牧歌。布莱克木刻版画，见于 R·J·桑顿编《学校用维吉尔诗选》，伦敦（麦高恩出版社），1821 年

611

Sleeping Shepherd. Etching by Samuel Palmer, 1857
沉睡的牧羊人。塞缪尔·帕尔默蚀刻版画，1857 年
back again [ 609 ]. Since copybooks taught him to draw as well as to write, he flourished figures like seaweed into any pattern imagined with his impeccable instinct for layout. Although Blake’s relief etchings are the oldest now known, a perhaps more workable recipe for relief etching was described about 1504 by Leonardo da Vinci. While Blake was working on his last illuminated book, he engraved 17 boxwood blocks for a classroom edition of Virgil’s Eclogues [610]. These dusky evocations of dream so shocked the schoolmaster-editor that he allowed them to appear (somewhat cut down) only at the insistence of Sir Thomas Lawrence and other painters.
再度归来[609]。由于练习本教会了他绘画与书写，他凭借无可挑剔的版式直觉，将人物形象如海藻般舒展成任何想象中的图案。尽管布莱克的凸版蚀刻是现存最古老的同类作品，但莱昂纳多·达·芬奇约在 1504 年描述的凸版蚀刻技法或许更为实用。 当布莱克创作最后一部彩绘本时，他为维吉尔《牧歌》的课堂版雕刻了 17 块黄杨木版[610]。这些暗色调的梦幻意象令担任校长的编辑震惊不已，最终在托马斯·劳伦斯爵士等画家的坚持下，才允许这些作品（经部分删减）得以出版。
Blake’s art had to wait for a wide public until his whirlpool swirling resurfaced in art nouveau. Being more the poet’s painter than the artist’s, this supreme painterpoet is revered only as far as English is spoken. Though he taught no pupils, he fascinated a band of disciples. In his last years he hypnotized a boy of 19, Samuel Palmer, who was starting to paint some of the most poetic of English watercolors. When Palmer translated Virgil’s Eclogues, he etched 17 coppers [611] in whose haunted shadows, he said “a thousand little luminous eyes peer through.”
布莱克的艺术直到新艺术运动中漩涡般的风格重现时，才获得广泛的公众认可。这位至高无上的画家诗人，与其说是艺术家的画家，不如说是诗人的画家，其声望仅限于英语世界。尽管他从未收徒，却吸引了一群追随者。 晚年时，他令 19 岁的少年塞缪尔·帕尔默如痴如醉，后者正着手创作最具诗意的英国水彩画。当帕尔默翻译维吉尔《牧歌》时，他蚀刻了 17 幅铜版画[611]，在那些幽灵般的阴影中，他宣称"千百双微光闪烁的眼睛正窥视着"。

Early lithography (早期平版印刷术)


Lithography-from the Greek for stone drawing or writ-ing-is the only major art-print process whose invention was described by its inventor. It could have been invented as long ago as woodcut, for it requires nothing but grease, water, paper, and fine limestone. While it should ideally have arrived in time to multiply the drawings of Michelangelo’s contemporaries, it actually coincided aptly with the romantic cult of genius that preferred a master’s autograph sketch, no matter how slight, to a formal work carried out by assistants. In the 1790s, in Munich, young Alois Senefelder was too poor to pay for publishing his amateurish plays and songs, or even to buy copper for etching them himself. Instead, he wrote in grease on paper, pressed the greasy lines onto limestone, soaked it with water, and applied greasy printer’s ink that stuck to the stone only where the first grease had marked, being rejected where the stone had absorbed water. A sheet of paper pressed against the stone accepted the inked markings. To write in liquid grease, Senefelder filed a piece of steel clock spring into a pen, thus ultimately initiating the British steel pen industry. He patented his “chemical printing” at Munich in 1799. In 1800 he sought a patent in London, where the process was introduced through an album of lithographs by prominent artists. The Philadelphian president of the Royal Academy, Benjamin West, started the series in 1801 with the earliest dated lithograph by any artist who is still remembered [612].
早期平版印刷术平版印刷术——源自希腊语，意为石上绘画或书写——是唯一由发明者亲自描述其发明过程的主要艺术印刷工艺。它可能早在木刻术出现时就已诞生，因为它仅需油脂、水、纸张和优质石灰岩。 虽然它本应在米开朗基罗同时代人的作品问世时出现，以便复制这些画作，但实际上它恰好与浪漫主义的天才崇拜相契合——这种崇拜更青睐大师的亲笔草图，无论多么简略，都胜过助手完成的正式作品。1790 年代，在慕尼黑，年轻的阿洛伊斯·塞内费尔德穷得连出版自己业余戏剧和歌曲的钱都没有，甚至买不起铜版来自己蚀刻。 于是他改用油脂在纸上书写，将油痕压印于石灰石上，浸湿石板后涂抹油性印刷油墨——油墨仅附着于原始油脂痕迹处，而被石板吸水的区域则排斥油墨。将纸张压在石板上即可转印油墨图案。为书写液态油脂，塞内费尔德将钟表钢簧磨制成笔尖，此举最终催生了英国钢笔工业。 1799 年他在慕尼黑为"化学印刷术"申请专利。1800 年赴伦敦申请专利时，通过知名艺术家石版画集向当地推广该工艺。皇家艺术学院费城籍主席本杰明·韦斯特于 1801 年启动该系列，其作品成为现存最早可考的石版画[612]。
Lithography immediately succeeded as a parlor game. In an age when persons of quality learned drawing as inevitably as they learned writing, an alert hostess provided stones for her dinner guests to sketch lithographs as souvenirs. By 1805 the Orléans family was enlivening its exile at Twickenham by drawing family pro-
平版印刷很快成为一种客厅游戏。在那个贵族学习绘画如同学习书写般理所当然的时代，机敏的女主人会为晚宴宾客提供石板，让他们绘制平版画作为纪念品。到 1805 年，奥尔良家族在特威克纳姆的流亡生活中，通过绘制家族肖像画增添了生机——

612 "He is not here, for he is risen." Pen lithograph by Benjamin West in Specimens of Polyautography, London (Vollweiler), 1801-07
612 "他不在这里，因为他已经复活了。" 本杰明·韦斯特创作的石版画，收录于《多版画样本集》，伦敦（沃尔韦勒出版社），1801-07 年

613 Adelaïde de Orléans. Lithograph by her brother, Duc de Montpensier, 1806
613 阿德莱德·德·奥尔良。其兄蒙潘西埃公爵所作石版画，1806 年
files [613]. Commercially, however, lithography failed during the 20 years of Napoleon’s wars and their aftermath. Then, in 1819, expert Parisian painters attracted enough vigorous draftsmen to put lithography on a par with engraving, while a Philadelphia magazine published the first lithographic illustration outside Europe. The Orient started about 1837 when a British press in Delhi made possible the wide publication of writings in the swinging Indian and Persian scripts. Then all the world began to draw on stone.
石版印刷术在拿破仑战争及其余波的二十年间未能实现商业化。直至 1819 年，巴黎的绘画大师们吸引到足够多才华横溢的素描师，使石版印刷术与雕版印刷平起平坐；而费城的一本杂志则刊载了欧洲以外的首幅石版印刷插图。 东方版画始于 1837 年左右，当时德里一家英国印刷厂实现了用印度和波斯文字广泛出版著作的可能性。自此，全世界都开始在石版上作画。
When lithography achieved its first artistic success in England, British aquatinters, who had recently perfected their skill, tried to quash the upstart process with a heavy import duty on the uniquely apt Munich stones. But British (and American) lithography was more seriously hurt when it was snubbed as a cheap makeshift for reproductive aquatint and engraving. Ruskin spoke for the English-speaking world in 1857 when he said “Let no lithographic work come into your house if you can help it.” The leading landscapists-Girtin, Turner, and Constable-never worked on stone, though they occasionally etched; and Lawrence waited until his last weeks before beginning his only lithograph.
当平版印刷术在英国初获艺术成功时，刚刚精进技艺的英国水彩蚀刻师们试图通过对慕尼黑石材征收高额进口关税来打压这项新兴工艺。但更致命的是，当平版印刷被轻蔑地视为水彩蚀刻与铜版画复制的廉价替代品时，英国（及美国）的平版印刷业遭受了沉重打击。 1857 年，罗斯金代表英语世界发出警告："若能避免，切勿让石版画作品进入你的家门。"顶尖风景画家——吉尔廷、透纳和康斯特布尔——虽偶尔进行蚀刻创作，却从未涉足石版画；而劳伦斯直至生命最后数周才着手创作其唯一石版画作品。
The professional lithographers and aquatinters both specialized in illustrating books of views, where aquatint gave way to the less expensive lithograph in the 1840s, and the lithograph gave way to the still cheaper wood engraving and photograph in the 1860s. In Paris, English lithographs with the romantic trappings of Walter Scott and Byron inspired the hugest view publication of them all-Baron Taylor’s 20-volume Voyages Pittoresques dans l’ancienne France [ 614 ]. In England about half of the views explored foreign lands, while the many series of French views mostly confined themselves to France. English lithographs followed aquatints by being kept thin for possible watercoloring, while French lithographs were drawn with the density and vigor of oil paintings.
专业石版画家和凹版蚀刻画家都专攻风景画册的插图创作。1840 年代，昂贵的凹版蚀刻技术逐渐被成本较低的石版画取代；而到了 1860 年代，石版画又让位于更为廉价的木刻版画和摄影技术。 在巴黎，带有沃尔特·斯科特与拜伦浪漫色彩的英国石版画，催生了规模最宏大的风景画集——泰勒男爵的 20 卷本《古法国风光游记》[614]。在英国，约半数风景画描绘异域风光，而众多法国风景画系列则多局限于本土题材。 英国石版画承袭凹版蚀刻技法，刻意保持画面薄透以便水彩润色；法国石版画则以油画般的浓墨重彩与蓬勃气势绘制。
In 1839 the first completely successful color lithographs in Boys’ Picturesque Architecture [ 349 ] entailed an exact registering of areas and a complex blending of tones that frightened painters away from color work until 1889, when Bonnard’s colored lines allowed free overlappings [ 720 ]. British specialists developed color lithography for linen labels, children’s books, and posters. Similarly, the United States used lithography for billheads, cigar-box lids, and popular prints. In New York even Currier & Ives felt that they had to advertise their lithographs as “engravings.” Germans also used lithography for copying, but with unexpected results
1839 年，《少年绘本建筑集》[349]首次成功实现全彩平版印刷，其精确的区域套印与复杂的色调融合令画家们望而却步，直至 1889 年博纳尔的彩色线条技法开创自由叠印之先河[720]。 英国专家将彩色平版印刷应用于亚麻布标签、童书和海报。美国同样采用平版印刷制作账单抬头、雪茄盒盖及通俗画作。在纽约，连柯里尔与艾夫斯公司都不得不将平版画标榜为"雕版画"。德国人也用平版印刷进行复制，却意外收获了新成果。
614
Rue de Gros-Horloge, Evreux. Lithograph by Richard Parkes Bonington in Baron Taylor, VOYAGES PITTORESQUES DANS L’ANCIENNE FRANCE, Paris (Didot and others), 1820-78
埃夫勒市大钟街。理查德·帕克斯·博宁顿石版画，收录于泰勒男爵《古法国风光游记》，巴黎（迪多等出版社），1820-78 年

when they reproduced Maximilian’s unfinished prayer book. The emperor had adapted the layout of Parisian prayer books [ 249 ] by surrounding a text printed in 1513 with fanciful quill drawings by Dürer, Cranach, Baldung, and others. This half-finished book slept until some of Dürer’s borders were traced on thin transfer paper and lithographed in 1808 [615]. The delayed publication detonated a threecentury time bomb. It gave Goethe his first sight of the “divine hilarity” that danced in Dürer when he went exploring with a quill, and it set a style for German book illustration for the next half century [ 616 ].
当他们复刻马克西米利安未完成的祈祷书时。这位皇帝借鉴了巴黎祈祷书的版式设计[249]，在 1513 年印刷的文本周围环绕着丢勒、克拉纳赫、巴尔东等人创作的奇幻羽毛笔画。这本半成品沉寂多年，直至 1808 年有人将丢勒的部分边框图案描摹在薄转印纸上进行平版印刷 [615]。这场延迟的出版引爆了沉睡三百年的时空炸弹。它让歌德初次领略到丢勒执笔探索时迸发的"神圣欢愉"，并为德国书籍插画确立了未来半个世纪的风格基调[616]。

Géricault and Delacroix (热里科与德拉克罗瓦)


By taking on all the technical cookery, the lithographic printer frees the artist to concentrate on his simple, exasperatingly difficult specialty-drawing. Unlike other printmakers, the lithographer, like the woodcut designer, draws directly in black what will print in black. Since lithographs are drawings, they vary as spontaneously as drawings and more than any other kind of print. Realizing all this, French painters used lithography rather than etching for their immediate reactions to life and events, and they created more great lithographs than everybody else put together.
热里科与德拉克罗瓦通过承担所有技术性烹饪工作，平版印刷师使艺术家得以专注于其简单却令人沮丧的艰深专长——绘画。与其他版画家不同，平版画家如同木刻设计师，直接用黑色勾勒出将以黑色呈现的画面。正因平版画本质是绘画，它们的变幻如素描般自然，远胜于其他任何版画形式。 深谙此道的法国画家们，选择石版画而非蚀刻版画来即时记录生活与事件的瞬间，由此创造的杰作数量远超其他所有版画流派的总和。
Figure 188: 617 Boxers. Lithograph by Théodore Géricault, 1818
图 188：617 名拳击手。石版画，作者：泰奥多尔·杰利科，1818 年
The first major artist to work consistently in the new medium was Géricault, who produced about 80 lithographs in the last six years of his short, angry life. He was the first French artist to be fascinated by England, then recently discovered by refugees from the French Revolution. An anonymous English etching of a boxing match between an Englishman and a Negro in 1811 must have inspired his lithograph of 1818 [617], drawn before Frenchmen began to box. At the left a spectator reclines
首位在新媒介中持续创作的重要艺术家是热里科，他在短暂而愤懑的生命的最后六年里创作了约八十幅石版画。他是首位被英国吸引的法国艺术家——当时英国刚被法国大革命的流亡者们发现。 1811 年一幅匿名英国蚀刻版画描绘了英国人与黑人之间的拳击比赛，这必然启发了他 1818 年的石版画[617]——该作品创作于法国人开始拳击运动之前。画面左侧，一名观众斜倚着
618
Entrance to the Adelphi Wharf, London. Lithograph by Géricault, 1821
伦敦阿德尔菲码头入口。热拉尔·德·热里科石版画，1821 年
like an antique river god as if to mark the modern revival of the Greek ideal of sport as a test of naked agility and courage, supplanting the medieval ideal of a chivalric pageant in armor. Géricault, Rowlandson, and Goya celebrated the boxer or the bullfighter as these former village rowdies were becoming national heroes.
如同一位古老的河神，仿佛在昭示着希腊体育理想的现代复兴——它以赤裸的敏捷与勇气为试金石，取代了中世纪盔甲骑士游行的理想。当这些昔日的乡村捣蛋鬼逐渐成为民族英雄时，热里科、罗兰森和戈雅便将拳击手或斗牛士奉为艺术的主题。
During the two years that Géricault starved in London, he wrote “I have abandoned the buskin and Holy Writ to dwell in the stable.” England so impressed him with the only serious school of horse portraiture that he adapted its allover density to stone [618] in the first powerful lithographs of contemporary life. But these darkest and most rebellious of Géricault’s prints did not sell in England and were not exported to France, so that when he died at 33, he had hardly affected lithographic practice.
在杰利科于伦敦忍饥挨饿的两年间，他写道："我已弃绝戏剧与圣经，栖身于马厩之中。"英国独有的严肃马匹肖像画派令他深受震撼，他将这种遍布画面的浓密笔触移植到石版上[618]，创作出首批展现当代生活的震撼石版画。 然而杰利科这些最阴郁叛逆的石版画在英国未能售出，也未出口法国，以致他 33 岁离世时，几乎未对石版画实践产生影响。
It was Delacroix who gave lithography his prestige as the heroic visionary who single-handedly stormed-and sometimes captured-the passionate grandeur of Titian and Tintoretto. He was 25, and drawing pale, dry caricatures on stone, when Goya’s bullfight lithographs [631] appeared in Bordeaux to provide the flashing shadows of his maturity. Three years later Delacroix started the great French production of luxurious books with lithographs by painters when he illustrated Goethe’s Faust [ 619 ]. He was not so much inspired by Goethe’s “uninteresting” poem as by a stage production that he saw in London in 1825. Goethe, however, thought that “M. Delacroix’s quick sketches-somewhat rough, but spirited . . . outdid my own imagining.” Like many pioneer publications, the Faust lost moneyso much money that Delacroix could never again induce a publisher to sponsor his
正是德拉克罗瓦赋予了平版印刷艺术崇高地位——这位英雄般的先驱者单枪匹马地冲击并捕捉了提香与丁托列托作品中那炽热的宏伟气魄。当戈雅的斗牛石版画[631]在波尔多问世，为他成熟期的作品注入闪烁的阴影时，年仅 25 岁的他正用苍白干涩的笔触在石板上勾勒着漫画。 三年后，他为歌德《浮士德》[619]创作石版画插图，由此开启法国奢华绘本的黄金时代。真正激发他灵感的并非歌德"乏味"的诗作，而是 1825 年在伦敦目睹的舞台剧。 然而歌德认为"德拉克罗瓦先生的速写——略显粗粝却充满灵性……超越了我自身的想象"。如同许多开创性出版物，《浮士德》蒙受巨额亏损，以致德拉克罗瓦再也无法说服出版商资助他的作品。


lithographs on literary themes. Thus no text accompanies his longest series, the 16 lithographs for Hamlet, on which he worked for 15 years. He studied Hamlet’s hands from a woman’s to feminize him in the moonstruck hysteria of the romantic theater [620]. France, with Delacroix’s Hamlet and young Théodore Chassériau’s contemporary, and rival, etchings of Othello [ 621 ], succeeded better than England in illustrating Shakespeare. Is this because artists feel they can supply something to a translation that has cut away Shakespeare’s poetry to expose his action,
以文学主题为题材的石版画。因此，在他耗时十五年创作的最长系列——为《哈姆雷特》绘制的 16 幅石版画中，并未配有任何文字。他研究女性的手部特征来塑造哈姆雷特，使其在浪漫主义戏剧的月光迷醉中呈现女性特质[620]。 法国在莎士比亚插图创作上比英国更为成功，德拉克罗瓦的《哈姆雷特》与年轻的泰奥多尔·沙塞里奥同时代的《奥赛罗》蚀刻版画[621]便是明证。这是否因为艺术家们认为，当译本割舍莎士比亚的诗意以凸显其戏剧冲突时，他们能为作品注入新的生命力？

whereas in English his imagery makes scenery impertinent and overwhelms illustration? Both these Shakespeare illustrations sold as badly as the Faust, being ignored like most truly original book illustrations, all the way from the Hypnerotomachia [ 223 ] to Vollard’s publications.
然而在英语中，他的意象却使风景显得不着边际，更淹没了插图本身？这两幅莎士比亚插图的销量与《浮士德》同样惨淡，如同从《梦境战争》[223]到沃拉德出版物间所有真正原创的书籍插图那样，始终遭人冷落。
When Delacroix starts from a source more visual than verbal, as in his heroic grappling of animals fighting to the death [622], he does indeed tap the energy that he admired in the baroque and the High Renaissance. His technical scrutiny of Goya’s Caprichos, acquired by copying some of them in pen and then in aquatint, bore fruit when he used the same format and the same dramatic division of light and shade for his own magnificent aquatint of a torso glimmering above embers and hot iron [ 623 ].
当德拉克罗瓦从视觉而非语言的源泉出发时——正如他在描绘动物殊死搏斗的英雄画面[622]中所展现的那样——他确实汲取了巴洛克与文艺复兴鼎盛时期令他倾慕的能量。 他通过钢笔临摹再以凹版蚀刻复制戈雅《奇想集》的技法研究，最终结出硕果——当他运用相同版式与戏剧性的明暗对比，创作那幅炽热铁烙与余烬间闪烁的躯干凹版蚀刻杰作时[623]。

Goya


After the 18th century had refined a few themes to the point of exhaustion, the old way of art collapsed with the old way of life-in downfalls that cleared a road for new starts. At this moment for the unexpected the first tremendous personality of the coming age arose in Spain, where no great artist had appeared during more than a century of French and Italian importations.
戈雅十八世纪将若干主题推至精炼殆尽的境地后，旧有的艺术形态便随旧有的生活方式一同崩塌——这些衰亡为新生开辟了道路。就在这个充满意外的时刻，西班牙涌现出新纪元首位伟大的艺术家。此前一个多世纪里，当法国与意大利艺术风潮席卷欧洲时，西班牙本土竟未曾孕育出任何杰出艺术家。
Francisco Goya was born in the tough, barren Spanish northeast. After some provincial art lessons, he looked at baroque paintings in Italy, then settled in Madrid
弗朗西斯科·戈雅出生于西班牙东北部贫瘠艰苦的地区。在接受过一些地方艺术教育后，他前往意大利观摩巴洛克绘画，随后定居马德里。
in his late 205 shortly after Giovanni Battista Tiepolo had died there in 1770. The etchings of both Tiepolos inspired Goya to advertise his own work by etching one of his tapestry cartoons in the elder Tiepolo’s translucent blend of parallel scribbles. Goya maintained this manner for the rest of his life, gradually enriching it through the study of Rembrandt. In the pure Venetian style he etched 16 of the king’s Velázquez paintings [ 624 ] in the first publication of the then little known Spanish royal collection. Having the run of the palace started the young painter on his lifelong study of Velázquez, whose greatest (though posthumous) pupil he became.
戈雅在二十五岁末期，于 1770 年乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·提埃波罗逝世后不久，便开始创作。提埃波罗父子的蚀刻版画启发了戈雅，促使他以长辈提埃波罗那种半透明的平行线条交织技法，蚀刻自己的一幅挂毯草图来宣传作品。 此后戈雅终生沿袭此法，并通过研习伦勃朗逐步深化技法。他以纯正威尼斯风格蚀刻了国王收藏的 16 幅委拉斯开兹画作[624]，首次向世人展示了当时鲜为人知的西班牙皇家画库。宫廷的自由创作空间开启了这位青年画家毕生研究委拉斯开兹的历程，最终使他成为这位大师最杰出的（虽属身后）传人。
He painted tapestry cartoons and then portraits until an illness deafened him and shocked his very Spanish communicativeness into his only year of apathy. Had he died then-at 46 (nine years older than Raphael at his death)-Goya would now be forgotten by all except specialists in decadent Spanish painting. A sudden buzzing silence locked him into his boyhood, haunted by village ghosts and goblins. When he recovered enough to work again, he learned the newly popularized technique of aquatint [ 229 ] to overlay his 18th-century line with the lights and shadows of romanticism. Out of this emotional crisis and technical exploration there emerged a new individual who burst on the world in 1799 when, at 53 , he published the first long set of prints ever made in Spain, the 80 Caprichos.
他先是绘制挂毯草图，继而创作肖像画，直至疾病夺去他的听力，将他那极具西班牙特色的健谈天性震入唯一一年的麻木状态。倘若他当时离世——时年四十六岁（比拉斐尔去世时年长九岁）——如今除了西班牙颓废画派的研究者，世人早已遗忘戈雅。突如其来的嗡鸣般寂静将他囚禁在童年记忆中，村落幽灵与妖魔的幻影萦绕不去。 当他恢复得足以重拾画笔时，他掌握了新近流行的软版蚀刻技法[229]，用浪漫主义的光影效果覆盖其十八世纪的线条风格。这场情感危机与技法探索孕育出崭新的艺术家，他于 1799 年以五十三岁之龄震撼世界——出版了西班牙史上首套长篇版画集《八十奇想》。
Since Madrid had no printshop (Paris had 30), he put his bound etchings on sale
由于马德里没有印刷店（巴黎有 30 家），他便将装订好的蚀刻版画拿出来出售。

624
Aesop. Etching by Francisco de Goya, 1778, after painting by Velázquez
624 伊索寓言。弗朗西斯科·戈雅蚀刻版画，1778 年，据委拉斯开兹油画创作


in the perfume and liquor shop under the rooms where he lived. After four years only 27 sets had sold for an ounce of gold each. As an old man Goya recalled that foreigners had bought more than Spaniards, but the only sales record is of four sets bought by a Spanish patron. In 1803 he obtained a pension for his son by ceding the 80 coppers and 240 sets of impressions to the royal printing office. Their 1850 catalogue was remaindering the leftovers with such poor success that it omitted Goya from its list of Spain’s six great printmakers. The word capricho refers to the goat (cabra) who scorns the huddle of sheep on the valley floor to browse dangerously on the cliffs. Goya’s Caprichos comment outwardly on the hobbles of ignorance in Spain’s medievalism, then being revealed by new ideas from France and England, but they really disturb because they confront us with whatever it is that visits you and me in our sleep [ 625 ].
在他居住的房间下方的香水与酒铺里。四年间仅售出 27 套，每套售价一盎司黄金。年迈的戈雅回忆道，外国买家比西班牙人更热衷购买，但唯一留存的销售记录显示，有四套被一位西班牙赞助人购得。 1803 年，他将 80 枚铜版与 240 套印版转让给皇家印刷所，以此为儿子换取养老金。该印刷所 1850 年的目录仍在清仓处理剩余作品，但反响甚微，甚至将戈雅从西班牙六大版画家名单中剔除。 "奇想"（Capricho）一词源于山崖上的山羊（cabra）——它蔑视谷底羊群的蜷缩，执意在险崖上啃食。戈雅的《奇想集》表面批判西班牙中世纪思想桎梏，当时法国与英国的新思想正揭露这些桎梏；但其真正令人不安之处，在于直面那些潜入你我梦境的未知存在[625]。
These etchings were the first Spanish works of art to strike the world outside Spain. Delacroix copied some and French lithographers reproduced others, while Goya’s paintings stayed put except for a few lent to the Louvre during the 1840 s . The Caprichos have always been Goya’s most popular works in any medium, though they are as miniatures to murals compared with the incomplete second set of fantasies that he etched 15 or 20 years later. He called these biggest of his aqua-
这些蚀刻版画是首批在西班牙境外引发轰动的西班牙艺术作品。德拉克罗瓦曾临摹其中部分作品，法国石版画家也复制了其他作品，而戈雅的油画则始终留在西班牙本土，仅有少数于 1840 年代借展卢浮宫。 《奇想集》始终是戈雅所有媒介中最受欢迎的作品，尽管相较于他十五或二十年后蚀刻的第二套未完成幻想系列，这些作品如同微缩版壁画。他称这些最大尺幅的软水蚀刻版画为——

鬼怪将至。戈雅《奇想集》中的水彩蚀刻版画
tints Disparates, for which the nearest English word might be Incongruities. This time he explored to the outer boundaries of dream, discovering sights that haunt like Rembrandt’s [ 626 ].
斑驳的异质，其最贴切的英文对应词或许是"不协调"。此刻他探寻至梦境的边界，发现的景象如伦勃朗画作般令人魂牵梦萦[626]。
War upset Goya’s life as profoundly as deafness had done, when on the night of May 2/3, 1808, Madrid rebelled against Napoleon’s easy invasion. By early summer Spaniards everywhere had thrown themselves into a resistance that grew ever more desperate for six years, until they drove the last Frenchman back across the Pyrenees. The face-to-face killings around rocks and in doorways, the dismembering reprisals, the famine that sank on thousands-all these excitements and agonies came into focus in Goya’s eye. Since he must have heard accounts of more than he actually saw, vision overpowered fact, freeing him to transmute experience into art with the erudition of the Italian baroque.
战争对戈雅生活的冲击，如同当年失聪般深刻。1808 年 5 月 2 至 3 日夜，马德里起义反抗拿破仑的轻而易举的入侵。初夏时节，西班牙各地民众已投身于抵抗运动，这场持续六年的抗争日益绝望，直至将最后一名法军驱逐回比利牛斯山脉彼岸。 岩石间与门廊里的近身厮杀，肢解式的报复，吞噬万千生灵的饥荒——所有这些惊心动魄的惨剧都聚焦于戈雅的镜头之下。由于他听闻的惨状远超亲眼所见，视觉冲击超越了现实本身，使他得以运用意大利巴洛克式的深邃学识，将亲历的创伤升华为艺术。
Hostilities meant few painting commissions to distract him from etching the 80 Disasters of War, so named in analogy with Callot’s Miseries of War when they were first published 35 years after Goya died. Obsessed by the fighting, by the 20,000 who starved to death all around him in Madrid, Goya reworked these etchings more persistently than any others. War shortages forced him to make do with ill-beaten coppers and to cut up two of his own etchings to use the backs. Poor
战火纷飞，绘画委托寥寥无几，使他得以全身心投入《战争的 80 种灾难》的蚀刻创作。该系列以卡洛的《战争的悲惨》为蓝本命名，在戈雅逝世 35 年后首次面世。战争的残酷令他魂牵梦萦——马德里城内两万民众饥饿而亡的景象萦绕心头，促使他比任何其他作品都更执着地反复修改这些蚀刻版画。 战争物资短缺迫使他使用打制粗糙的铜版，甚至裁切两幅自己的蚀刻版画取用背面。可怜的
Figure 191: 627 Forebodings of Doom. Aquatint by Goya from Los Desastres de la Guerra
图 191：627 厄运的预兆。戈雅《战争的灾难》系列中的水彩蚀刻版画
628 Not Even for Women. Aquatint by Goya from Los Desastres . . .
628 妇女亦难逃厄运。戈雅《灾难》系列中的水彩蚀刻版画……

varnish ground admitted acid for spots of foul biting. Though few prints sold as people scrounged for crusts, Goya let nothing stop him from imagining pictures that stab, because he was above making propaganda for Spain or against France, and because he faced war with the individualist passion of a Spanish Christian. The series opens with a man flinging out his arms [627] in a supplication that Goya repeated in a painting of Christ’s Agony in the Garden. The impression shown here was printed after some 50 years in storage had tarnished the copper, muddying the shadows and graying the highlights. The Disasters grip the heart in any state, but the rare wartime impressions, pulled while the coppers were still bright [628], reveal a grace, a seductiveness of the flesh, that Goya retained from his 18th-century youth. His good manners drive home war’s final horror-its uselessness.
油漆底料吸收了腐蚀斑点的酸液。尽管人们为填饱肚子四处搜寻残羹冷炙，版画销量寥寥，但戈雅仍毫不犹豫地构思那些刺痛人心的画面——因为他超越了为西班牙造势或反法宣传的层面，更以西班牙基督徒特有的个人主义激情直面战争。 本系列以一名张开双臂[627]的男子开篇，戈雅在《基督在花园中的痛苦》画作中重复了这一祈求姿态。此处展示的版画因铜版存放五十余年而氧化，阴影变得浑浊，高光处泛灰。 《灾难》系列无论何时都令人心悸，但那些战时印制的珍贵版画——铜版尚存光泽时印制[628]——却流露出一种优雅，一种肉体本身的诱惑力，这是戈雅自十八世纪青年时期便保留的品质。他优雅的笔触将战争的终极恐怖——其徒劳无益——刻入人心。
After the six years of anguish ended in 1814, Goya relaxed with a fanciful historical sequence of bullfights in 33 aquatints. Although now, by 1816, Madrid had a printshop, these first great sporting prints seem to have sold almost as badly as the Caprichos. Goya persistently spent on printmaking what he earned by portrait painting, even going to the expense of importing English copperplates for his bullfights. Few artists since Tintoretto have been able to launch figures securely into the air [629]; here Goya made good his claim that a painter should observe a man falling off a roof exactly enough to go home and draw him. In some of his bullfights he deployed figures against blank paper as decoratively as Utamaro [ 697 ], his contemporary, as though a global tide of taste carried entirely disconnected artists to the same point at the same time.
1814 年，历经六年的苦难岁月终告结束，戈雅以 33 幅水彩蚀刻版画创作的奇幻斗牛历史系列作品放松身心。尽管 1816 年马德里已设有印刷作坊，但这些首批杰出的体育题材版画似乎与《奇想集》一样滞销。 戈雅将肖像画所得收入持续投入版画创作，甚至不惜进口英国铜版制作斗牛画。自丁托列托以来鲜有艺术家能如此精准地将人物抛向空中[629]；此处他印证了自己的主张：画家应精确观察从屋顶坠落之人，返家后便能精准描摹。 在某些斗牛作品中，他将人物置于空白纸张上，其装饰性手法堪比同时代的喜多丸[697]——仿佛全球审美浪潮将素无交集的艺术家们同时推向了相同境地。
Figure 192: 629 The Lightness and Dexterity of Juanito Apiñani. Aquatint by Goya from Arte de lidiar los Toros
图 192：629 胡安尼托·阿皮尼亚尼的轻盈与灵巧。戈雅创作的软版蚀刻画，选自《斗牛艺术》
With experience gained from the tragedy of the Disasters and the exquisite de- liberation of the Bullfights, Goya shaped his simplest and grandest print, the Giant [630], in the attitude of the bruised Greek bronze boxer that he remembered from his youth in Rome. Relying on consummate skill, he dared to aquatint an allover black on a copperplate and then scrape out the highlights as though it were a mezzotint. He needed a surer hand than a mezzotinter’s, since, if he scraped a part too light, he could not darken it again. The Giant is the last work of art from a civilized country that projects an unreason, a bone-marrow terror, like an African mask, or any other sacred object shaped by the dread of God.
从"双重灾难"的悲剧中汲取经验，在斗牛场景的精妙构思中淬炼技艺，戈雅以青年时期在罗马记忆中那尊伤痕累累的希腊青铜拳击手为灵感，创作了其最简洁而恢弘的版画《巨人》[630]。凭借炉火纯青的技艺，他大胆地在铜版上采用凹版蚀刻法施以全面黑色，继而刮出高光部分，宛若 mezzotint 凹版雕刻技法。 他需要比凹版雕刻师更稳健的手法——一旦刮刻过浅，便无法再加深。这幅《巨人》是文明世界最后一件艺术品，它投射出非理性的骨髓之惧，犹如非洲面具，抑或任何因对上帝的敬畏而诞生的神圣器物。
When the Inquisition returned to Spain with the Bourbon kings, Goya, aged 78, joined distinguished political exiles in Bordeaux. There, late in 1825, he drew four big lithographs of bullfights [ 631 ]. He propped his stone on an easel like a canvas, grayed it all over, then crayoned the darks and scraped out the lights. Half blind, he used a magnifying glass but really relied, like a pianist, on the experience stored in his muscles. He, who was about 75 when he first tried his hand at casual transfer lithographs in Madrid, was 79 when he achieved the first great works of art on stone-the first that combine the freedom of a sketch with a black and white as rich, as rounded as the impasto of a painting. The artist formed in the age of Boucher had explored until he had made himself the contemporary of his grandchildren. Like Dürer, he began in one world and ended in another. But while Dürer refashioned himself in the likeness of an art that already existed, Goya groped his way into the central drift to come.
当宗教裁判所随波旁王朝重返西班牙时，78 岁的戈雅加入了在波尔多流亡的政界名流行列。1825 年末，他在那里创作了四幅斗牛题材的大型石版画[631]。他将石版像画布般架在画架上，整体涂上灰色底色，再用蜡笔勾勒暗部，刮出亮部。 半失明状态下，他虽借助放大镜，却如钢琴家般主要依靠肌肉记忆中的经验。这位约 75 岁时在马德里初试水印石版画的艺术家，79 岁时在石板上创作出首批伟大艺术作品——首次将素描的自由与绘画般厚重圆润的黑白质感完美融合。 这位在布歇时代成长的艺术家不断探索，直至与孙辈成为同时代人。如同丢勒，他始于一个时代，终于另一个时代。但当丢勒以既有的艺术形态重塑自我时，戈雅却在黑暗中摸索着走向未来的艺术主流。
