outward only as far as it interested him [703]. Such wispy scribbles would have looked scrubbed without the atmospheric film of ink that he left on his plates. He authenticated each impression that he so deftly printed on paper torn out of an old book by penciling his butterfly (developed from a W ) on a marginal tab left when he trimmed the print.
仅在涉及自身兴趣时才向外延伸[703]。若非他在印版上留下的墨气薄膜，这些纤细的涂鸦本该显得被擦拭过。他将从旧书撕下的纸张灵巧地印上图案后，便在裁切时留下的页边标签上用铅笔勾勒出自己的蝴蝶标记（源自字母 W 的变形），以此为每幅印品背书。
Just before going to Venice, Whistler returned to lithography with mature experience, drawing conveniently on transfer paper from which the crayon strokes were pressed onto the stone. These papers were translucent enough to place upon previous tries for tracing with improvements. He thus repeated attempts, which he considered failures, at the portrait of his equally delicate and equally waspish contemporary, the Comte de Montesquiou [ 704 ]. When he published his first set of lithographs in 1887, he started a new practice by charging £ 4 / 4 / o £ 4 / 4 / o £_(4)//4//o£_{4} / 4 / \mathrm{o} for sets signed in pencil, and half as much for unsigned impressions, even though all were printed alike in a lithographic shop. Arbitrary restrictions to raise prices had been institutionalized in 1847 when the Printsellers’ Association was formed to limit the number of proofs that might be printed, thus obtruding rarity into a kind of picture that had traditionally been everybody’s. Such snobbery appealed to Whistler, whose dandyism in dress, art, and sarcasm generated more publicity than any other Eng-lish-speaking artist ever achieved. Yet the esthetic fragility that he imposed on England and North America lacked the vitality to spread further.
在前往威尼斯之前，惠斯勒带着成熟的技艺重拾平版画创作，他巧妙地利用转印纸将蜡笔线条压印在石板上。这些纸张足够透明，可置于先前试印的石板上进行改进性描摹。他如此反复尝试，将那些被视为失败的画作——即为他那位同样纤弱又同样尖刻的同代人蒙特斯基厄伯爵[704]所作的肖像——重新演绎。 1887 年出版首套石版画时，他开创性地对铅笔签名版收取 £ 4 / 4 / o £ 4 / 4 / o £_(4)//4//o£_{4} / 4 / \mathrm{o} 费用，而无签名版仅收半价——尽管所有作品均出自同一印刷作坊。 1847 年版画商协会成立时，便通过限制试印数量将人为抬价制度化，将稀缺性强加于传统上人人可得的画作。这种势利行径正合惠斯勒心意——其在服饰、艺术与讽刺中的纨绔作风，为他赢得了英语世界艺术家前所未有的声名。 然而他强加于英美两国的审美脆弱性，终究缺乏向更广阔领域蔓延的生命力。

The line block (线块)


Shortly before photography was announced in 1839, printers devised ways for turning line drawings into relief blocks mechanically. In 1834 Daumier, always eager to experiment, tried out one such invention, scratching a drawing through a plaster coating on a steel plate, after which molten type metal cast the incised lines as relief for printing with type like a woodcut [ 705 ]. In Paris in the 18705 photography was applied to the principle of the gillotype [665] to make today’s line block. Firmin Gillot’s son placed a photographic negative of a line drawing on a metal plate coated with albumin and sensitized with bichromate. Wherever light struck through the negative it waterproofed the albumin, sticking it to the metal. After water washed off the rest, acid ate down the bared metal, leaving the protected lines in relief. Since the special photographic negative regis-
线条版块在 1839 年摄影术问世前夕，印刷工人们已开发出将线条画机械化转化为凸版的技术。1834 年，向来热衷尝试新技法的杜米埃便试用了其中一项发明：先在钢板上刮除石膏涂层露出底层，再用熔融的铅字金属铸出刻痕形成的凸起线条，最终像木刻版画那样进行印刷[705]。 1870 年代的巴黎，摄影术被应用于吉洛版印刷原理[665]，由此诞生了现代线条版。 吉洛之子将线稿的照相底片置于涂覆蛋白质并经重铬酸盐感光的金属板上。底片透光处使蛋白质防水固化于金属表面。经水洗去未感光部分后，酸蚀刻出裸露金属，形成凸起的保护线条。由于特殊照相底片能记录——

丹尼尔·维尔热绘制的线框图，载于帕布罗·德·塞戈维亚·奎韦多所著《奎韦多》，巴黎（邦胡尔出版社），1882 年

This premeditated spontaneity revolutionized illustrations for books and especially for magazines of humor. For the first line-block illustrations of artistic importance, Daniel Vierge drew with skinny lines to allow for their thickening slightly in reproduction [706] and also revived the black blot of the Hypnerotomachia [ 223 ].
素描师在黑白稿上作画时刻意忽略浅蓝色调，先用蓝色蜡笔研究画面构图，再在这张静态草稿上快速勾勒出可摄影的黑色素描。这种预先设计的即兴创作方式彻底革新了书籍插图，尤其为幽默杂志开辟了新天地。 丹尼尔·维尔热创作的首批具艺术价值的线刻版画，采用纤细线条绘制以便在复制时略微加粗[706]，同时复活了《梦境战争》中标志性的黑色墨渍[223]。
The black blot and the flat pattern of Japanese prints distinguished the incredible outpouring of line-block illustrations drawn by Aubrey Beardsley during the last half dozen of his 25 tubercular years [ 707 ]. The young invalid’s flippancy stung like death. As an amateur actor, he characterized with grotesque pungency. As an instinctive decorator, he originated a style that was directly imitated in Vienna and Saint Petersburg and that cleared out representational clutter for the drawings of Matisse and Picasso.
日本版画的墨色渲染与平面构图，使奥布里·比尔兹利在肺结核缠身的二十五载人生后半段[707]所创作的线刻版画作品脱颖而出。这位年轻病人的轻佻笔触如死神般刺痛人心。 作为业余演员，他以怪诞犀利的笔触塑造角色；作为天生的装饰艺术家，他开创的风格直接被维也纳与圣彼得堡效仿，为马蒂斯和毕加索的素描作品扫清了具象艺术的杂乱障碍。

Yvette Guilbert Singing in the Divan Japonais, Jane Avril in the Audience. Color lithograph poster by ToulouseLautrec, 1892
伊薇特·吉尔伯特在"日本沙龙"演唱，简·艾芙莉在观众席。图卢兹-洛特雷克彩色平版印刷海报，1892 年

Toulouse-Lautrec (图卢兹-洛特雷克)


The great Chinese ink painters came from a bureaucratic aristocracy trained to a semipictorial writing. Although European gentlefolk used to be taught to draw as they were taught to write, the aristocracy of Europe, so rich in remarkable authors and investigators, has produced only one remarkable artist: Count Henri-Marie-Raymond de Toulouse-Lautrec Monfa. Lautrec would probably have painted no better than his father if the breaking of both his legs in his teens had not saved him from wasting his life hunting with his cousins. Casehardened with an aristocrat’s contempt for middle-class circumspection, he threw himself into the Paris of prostitutes and hoofers, who also had to put on a show and shrug off suffering with a jest. His fever for living burned out his life when he was 36 . He had drawn since he was a baby. After the sketchiest instruction in painting, he found in Degas and in Japanese prints the sifting of appearances that he needed for summing up a person or an animal in a few tingling lines. This pictorial shorthand looked like caricature-the distortion of a physical feature-but actually expressed an insight as innocent, and therefore as alarming, as a child’s. Looking upward from his child’s height, he caught people at startling angles in pictures to be hung high [708]. He exercised his command of line and his joy in color through printers trained in color lithography by Chéret [641]. Lautrec drew his first color lithograph for a poster when he was 26 . In the ten years that he yet had to live, his oils, vibrant though they often are, changed the course of art less than his lithographs, and especially his posters [709], which still startle by their strategy of attack. When their yellow and orange and black first flared in the gaslight of the boulevards, no one could miss the fact that art had taken a new turn.
图卢兹-洛特雷克中国杰出的水墨画家皆出自官僚贵族阶层，他们受过半绘画式的书法训练。尽管欧洲绅士们也曾像习字那样学习绘画，但欧洲贵族阶层——这个孕育了众多杰出作家与学者的群体——却仅诞生了一位卓越的艺术家：亨利-玛丽-雷蒙·德·图卢兹-洛特雷克·蒙法伯爵。 若非少年时双腿骨折，使他免于随表亲们虚度狩猎光阴，劳特累克的画技恐怕难超其父。他带着贵族对中产阶级的蔑视，将自己投身于巴黎的妓女与舞女之中——这些生灵同样需要表演，用玩笑掩盖痛苦。他燃烧生命的热忱，在他 36 岁时耗尽了生命。 他自幼便执笔作画。在接受过最粗浅的绘画指导后，他从德加与日本版画中领悟到提炼表象的艺术——只需寥寥数笔便能勾勒人物或动物的精髓。这种绘画速记看似漫画式的肢体变形，实则传递着孩童般纯粹而惊人的洞察力。 他以孩童的视角仰望世界，将人物定格在惊人的角度，创作出一系列需高悬墙壁的作品[708]。他通过受谢雷特训练的彩色平版印刷师，施展对线条的掌控力与对色彩的热忱[641]。 劳特累 26 岁时为海报创作了首幅彩色石版画。在他余下的十年生命里，那些虽常显生动的油画，对艺术进程的影响远不及他的石版画——尤其是海报作品[709]，其震撼人心的视觉冲击策略至今仍令人惊叹。 当他们的黄、橙、黑三色首次在大道煤气灯下闪现时，没有人会忽略艺术已迎来新转折的事实。

Gauguin and Munch (高更与蒙克)


By 1757 woodcut had declined to the point where Papillon, the first historian of woodcutting, complained that printers bothered to ink blocks only once for every five impressions. Woodcut suddenly returned as a spectacular modern medium when Gauguin, coming home in 1893 from Tahiti, prepared to publish his prose poem Noa Noa (Fragrance, Fragrance) with woodblocks almost as large as the largest lithographs that Manet had drawn for Poe’s Raven eight years before [ 681 ]. Gauguin, his hand trained after five years of carving doors and furniture, gouged ten big end-grain boxwood blocks that set the mood for his reveries by recombining figures that he had painted in the South Seas. Where other artists would have counterfeited themselves, Gauguin profited from the restrictions of woodcut to create his most original, most widely imitated works in any medium. The brutal idols that he had long been painting he now dematerialized on the wood by spinning around them a cocoon of luminous filaments
高更与蒙克到 1757 年，木刻艺术已衰落至此，以致首位木刻史学家帕皮永抱怨道：印刷工每印五张版画，仅给木板上墨一次。 1893 年，高更从塔希提岛归国，准备以木刻版画出版其散文诗《诺亚诺亚》（香气，香气）。这些木刻版几乎与马奈八年前为爱伦·坡《乌鸦》绘制的最大石版画尺寸相当[681]。 高更历经五年雕刻门扇与家具的锤炼，在十块横切面黄杨木大板上凿刻出南太平洋画作中的人物重组，以此营造梦幻意境。当其他艺术家沉溺于自我复制时，高更却从木刻的技法限制中获益，创作出其所有媒介中最独具匠心、最广为模仿的杰作。 他长期描绘的野蛮偶像，此刻在木板上消解为虚无——他以发光的丝线为这些偶像编织出茧状的氛围。
scratched on the end grain with the needles and coarse sandpaper that he must have seen lithographers using to shape soft forms out of a solid black coating on stone. Blocks cut as no other end grain had ever been attacked before, with the broadest gouges and the finest scratchers, became decorative reliefs that might incidentally serve for printing. Gauguin continued to experiment, sometimes printing the same block in black over burnt orange, smudging the register to enrich the tone, and sometimes fogging the design by pressing the inked block against paper under a mattress on which he sat or stood. The resulting visions of night in the tropics blur and glimmer, dim with vapors, dreaming of love and danger [710]. He had invented the most original woodcuts since Blake’s little Virgil illustrations of 1821 [610].
他用针和粗砂纸在木料的端面上刻划，想必是目睹了石版画家如何用这些工具在石板上厚重的黑色涂层中雕琢出柔和的形态。 这些木板被前所未有地切割——用最宽的凿子和最细的刮刀处理横截面，最终成为可兼作印刷用的装饰浮雕。高更持续实验：有时在焦橙色底上覆印黑色同版，通过错位晕染来丰富色调；有时则将沾墨的木板压在纸张上，坐在或站立于床垫之下，使图案朦胧模糊。 由此诞生的热带夜色幻象朦胧闪烁，雾气氤氲中弥漫着爱与危险的梦境[710]。他创造了自布莱克 1821 年《维吉尔》插画以来最富原创性的木刻艺术[610]。
But Gauguin’s innovations, unlike Blake’s unnoticed experiments, quickly energized artists in Germany and elsewhere, even though his dream book never came into being as a whole. Gauguin’s woodcuts, rather than his paintings, prepared artists for African sculpture and conveyed his mastery of decoration to art nouveau.
但高更的创新不同于布莱克那些无人问津的尝试，迅速激发了德国及其他地区艺术家的创作热情——尽管他的《梦之书》始终未能完整问世。正是高更的木刻版画（而非油画）为艺术家们接触非洲雕塑铺平了道路，并将他精湛的装饰技艺传承给了新艺术运动。
Art nouveau, the only original decoration since rococo, writhed and whipped across walls and posters in France and exploded into neurosis in Norway when Edvard Munch became obsessed with the sick adolescent girl and the vampire woman. Although Munch was financed by government grants until rich patrons began to care for him, his cyclone of self-pursuit tormented him as poverty never tormented Gauguin. Munch’s woodcuts, more than his etchings, his lithographs or even his paintings, created the language of style for the German expressionists [ 744 ]. Like Hiroshige [ 699 ], he printed the grain of the plank [ 711 ], and like Gauguin, he excited the voids with the debris from the accidental splintering of the gouge [ 712 ].
新艺术运动作为洛可可之后唯一的原创装饰艺术，在法国的墙壁与海报上蜿蜒翻腾，当爱德华·蒙克痴迷于病弱少女与吸血鬼般的女性形象时，它在挪威迸发为神经质的爆发。尽管蒙克曾靠政府补助度日，直至富有的赞助者开始关照他，但自我追寻的旋风折磨着他——这种折磨远胜于贫困对高更的煎熬。 与蚀刻版画、石版画乃至油画相比，蒙克的木刻作品为德国表现主义者开创了风格语言[744]。 他像广重[699]那样印出木板的纹理[711]，又像高更般用凿子意外碎屑的残痕点燃空白[712]。

1898

International virtuosos (国际演奏大师)


The interlude of peace from 1812 to 1914 allowed more people in the Western world to accumulate wealth than ever before in history. The new millionaires summoned portraitists to wide and constant travels. As these painters from varied origins visited the great galleries and studied the universally admired old masters-Velázquez, Hals, Tiepolo, Boucher, Fragonard, Reynolds, and Gainsborough-their styles converged in an international virtuosity that summarized appearances with a flashing ease obviously worth serious financial investment. Some of these painters, such as Sorolla and Sargent, made few prints. Another, Zorn, made many as reductions of his oil portraits for the sitters to give to relatives and friends. He also etched nudes indoors and outdoors (often from snapshots) with a declared sensuality that rescues them from photographic banality. He laid his deeply bitten lines in a slanting rain of brilliance that simply and boldly moves bulk in depth [ 713 ]. When a first try disappointed him, he threw the plate aside, repeated the subject until he got a promising start, and then continued to retouch throughout the printing. However intricate his decisions, he resolved them to an effect of promptness.
国际艺术大师 1812 至 1914 年的和平间歇期，使西方世界积累财富的人数达到历史之最。 新晋百万富翁们召唤肖像画家们踏上漫长而频繁的旅程。这些出身各异的画家们遍访各大美术馆，研习备受推崇的古典大师——委拉斯开兹、哈尔斯、提埃波罗、布歇、弗拉戈纳尔、雷诺兹和庚斯博罗——他们的画风逐渐融合成一种国际化的精湛技艺，以令人惊叹的轻松姿态概括外在形象，显然值得投入巨额资金。其中索罗拉和萨金特等画家制作的版画寥寥无几。 而佐恩则大量制作油画肖像的缩小版，供委托人赠予亲友。他更以蚀刻技法创作室内外裸体画（常取材于快照），其宣示的感官美学令作品摆脱了摄影的平庸。他以倾泻而下的斜向线条刻画出深邃的明暗层次，简洁而大胆地塑造出立体的体积感[713]。 初试未果时，他便弃版重来，反复刻画直至获得理想开端，继而在整个印刷过程中持续修饰。纵使决策过程错综复杂，他总能化繁为简，呈现出行云流水般的艺术效果。

Watteau Drawings. Drypoint by Paul Helleu, about 1900
瓦托素描。保罗·埃勒干刻版画，约 1900 年
An even more direct sketching in drypoint served Paul Helleu for perhaps 2000 interchangeable heads of pretty ladies in identical hats and hairdos, interrupted by occasional inspirations of femininity as seductive as anything out of the 18th century [ 714 ].
干刻法赋予保罗·埃勒更直接的素描表现力，他创作了约两千幅可互换的美女头像——她们戴着相同的帽子，梳着相同的发型，偶尔迸发的女性魅力灵感却如十八世纪画作般魅惑人心[714]。
A more vivid energy went into the few drypoints that were casually thrown out by Giovanni Boldini, the last of the traveling Italian virtuosos. He had practiced art in his father’s Ferrarese studio even while learning to talk. His lifelong sport of all-day drawing and painting developed an intoxicating illusion of spontaneity in arresting the movement of horses, musician’s fingers, and serpentine women. The opalescence that he deduced from a white satin gown or a black fur cape also gave “color” to the drypoints [ 715 ] that he never bothered to publish.
乔瓦尼·博尔迪尼——这位最后的意大利游历大师——随手创作的几幅干刻版画却蕴含着更鲜活的能量。他自幼在父亲位于费拉拉的工作室习艺，甚至在学说话时便已开始艺术训练。终生不辍的全天候绘画创作，使他捕捉奔马、乐师指尖与蜿蜒女性身姿时，总能营造出令人沉醉的即兴幻觉。 他从白色缎裙或黑色毛皮斗篷中提炼出的乳光质感，也为那些从未付梓的干刻版画[715]增添了"色彩"。

Prints by French sculptors and painters (法国雕塑家与画家的版画作品)


In 1755 the Parisian Académie de Peinture admitted engravers only if they promised not to paint. The jealous guilds imposed specialization until they were destroyed by the French Revolution, thereafter leaving artists as free as their Italian Renaissance predecessors to take up new media in mid-life. Thus Daumier, Degas, and Renoir discovered fresh possibilities in sculpture because they ignored the professional sculptor’s don’ts, and Renoir, Cézanne, and Rodin did the same for printmaking. Kneading clay and chiseling marble strengthened Rodin’s hand to pull a drypoint needle through copper as flowingly as another hand might move a pencil over paper. He made his few drypoint heads sparkle like bronze [716], giving them more personality than any copperplate portraits since Rembrandt and Van Dyck. When he sketched from the nude, he fixedly scrutinized the model to release his pencil from the censorship of his eye, relying on his sculptor’s grip on form to waft bodies in and out of space as lyrically as Michelangelo. Rodin made five such elusive drawings on lithographic transfer paper, while many more were sensitively transposed to stone by the printer Auguste Clot, who convincingly copied even the sopping of Rodin’s watercolor washes [ 717 ].
法国雕塑家与画家的版画作品 1755 年，巴黎绘画学院规定版画家入学会时必须承诺不从事绘画创作。这些嫉妒心强的行会强制推行专业分工，直至法国大革命将其摧毁。此后艺术家们重获自由，如同意大利文艺复兴时期的前辈们那样，得以在中年时期探索全新媒介。 正因如此，杜米埃、德加与雷诺阿得以在雕塑中开辟新境——他们无视职业雕塑家的禁忌；雷诺阿、塞尚与罗丹则在版画领域重现了同样的突破。揉捏黏土与凿刻大理石的训练，使罗丹的手掌能如执笔般自如地将干刻针穿梭于铜版之上。 他仅有的几幅干刻版画头像如青铜般闪耀[716]，赋予人物的个性远超伦勃朗与凡·戴克之后的任何铜版肖像。当他写生裸体时，凝视模特时目光如炬，让铅笔挣脱视觉的桎梏，凭借雕塑家对形态的掌控力，使人体在空间中飘动，其诗意之境堪比米开朗基罗。 罗丹在石版转印纸上创作了五幅如此难以捉摸的素描，而印刷师奥古斯特·克洛特则将更多作品敏感地转印到石版上，他甚至精确复刻了罗丹水彩渍的渗流效果[717]。
This virtuoso craftsman, Clot, implemented the great conquest of French printmaking in the 1890s-color. In old European prints color had amounted to little
这位技艺精湛的工匠克洛特，在 1890 年代实现了法国版画艺术的伟大突破——色彩运用。在欧洲古老的版画中，色彩曾微不足道。

718 Pinning the Hat. Color lithograph by Auguste Renoir, 1898
718 《别上帽子》。奥古斯特·雷诺阿彩色平版画，1898 年
more than a childish brightness in hand-painted Gothic woodcuts, a harmonious monochrome in Italian chiaroscuros, and candy-box tints in 18th-century copperplates. No singing subtlety could appear until Chéret [ 641 ] had brought the English skill in color lithography into France. Clot then put this refined technique at the service of the best painters, helping Renoir the way he had helped Rodin. Renoir in his 50 s 50 s 50 s50 s made a few prints in techniques handy for a pencil draftsman and water-colorist-soft-ground etching and transfer lithography. He would watercolor a black and white lithographic proof for Clot to imitate in color lithography. The masterpiece of this collaboration, showing Berthe Morisot’s daughter pinning a cousin’s hat, took five years to mature through versions in pastel, oils, three etchings, and two lithographs. The final version [ 718 ], printed from 11 stones in black, gray, and nine colors, achieves a sensuous grandeur rarely seen since Titian and Rubens, and a design, like theirs, bold enough to survive execution by an assistant.
手绘哥特式木刻中不仅有稚气未脱的明快，意大利明暗对比技法中蕴含着和谐的单色美学，十八世纪铜版画里更闪耀着糖果盒般的缤纷色调。直到谢雷特[641]将英国彩色平版印刷的精湛技艺引入法国，才得以呈现出如歌般的细腻韵味。 克洛特将这门精湛技艺奉献给顶尖画家，如同昔日扶持罗丹般扶持雷诺阿。雷诺阿在其《 50 s 50 s 50 s50 s 》中运用铅笔素描家与水彩画家熟悉的技法——软地蚀刻与转印平版——创作了数幅版画。他先为黑白平版试印稿绘制水彩，再由克洛特以彩色平版复刻。 两人合作的巅峰之作——描绘贝尔特·莫里索之女为表亲别帽的画面——历经粉彩稿、油画稿、三版蚀刻版画及两版石版画的反复推敲，历时五年方臻成熟。 最终版本[718]采用十一块石版印制，运用黑色、灰色及九种色彩，成就了自提香与鲁本斯以来罕见的感性壮丽，其构图之大胆足以经受助手执行的考验，堪与两位大师比肩。

图 221：721（对页左）庭院。爱德华·维亚尔彩色平版画，选自《风景与室内》，巴黎（沃拉德画廊），1899 年
The same lithographic printer added the colors to Cézanne’s nudes that bulk like cliffs under the chalky sunlight of Provence [ 719 ].
同一位平版印刷师为塞尚的裸体画添上了色彩，那些裸体如悬崖般在普罗旺斯白垩般的阳光下巍然耸立[719]。
Printed color became even more inventive in 1895 when Clot helped artists to work directly on the stones, starting with Bonnard’s Aspects of Life in Paris. This set of prints was sponsored by a newcomer from the West Indies, Ambroise Vollard. Vollard sold paintings for a canny fortune that he threw away by spendthrift plunges into publications on which he lavished a frantic care, even though most found few buyers for the next 20 years. To break away from routine manufacture, he commissioned prints from artists who were not professional printmakers. When he organized his stable of adventurous painters, Vollard, Bonnard, and Vuillard were all 28, and Lautrec was 31 . Vollard encouraged Bonnard and Vuillard to suppress line in lithography for a riddle of tangles meeting, overlapping, or scrambling into each other to shape sunlight into a nursemaid or to sink an aunt into the wallpaper. It took repeated trials to soften colors into Bonnard’s dust grays and brick pinks, and Vuillard’s spotlights of surprise. Opalescent wit transformed the street corner, bridge traffic, kitchen [ 720 ], even the middle-class parlor, while the design of a courtyard [721] anticipated abstract paintings like Mondrian’s. Vollard followed these portfolios with over 20 illustrated books in which the text sometimes overlays the picture [ 722 ], as it does on Japanese fans. He left many books unfinished when a motor car killed him in 1939. As that rare animal, an unliterary Frenchman, his example made the typical 20th-century de luxe book into a set of prints boxed with any old text.
1895 年，克洛特协助艺术家直接在石版上创作，开创了更富创意的彩色印刷技术，首部作品便是博纳尔的《巴黎生活图景》。这组版画由来自西印度群岛的新锐收藏家安布罗瓦兹·沃拉尔赞助出版。 沃拉尔以精明的眼光购入画作赚得盆满钵满，却因挥霍无度投入出版事业而挥霍殆尽——尽管他倾注狂热心血的出版物在随后的二十年里鲜有买家问津。为打破常规制作模式，他特邀非专业版画家创作版画。 当沃拉德组建这支先锋画家团队时，沃拉德、博纳尔和维亚尔皆为 28 岁，劳特累克 31 岁。沃拉德鼓励博纳尔与维亚尔在石版画中摒弃线条，以错综交织的谜题般色块相互碰撞、重叠或交融，将阳光塑造成保姆的轮廓，或让姨妈隐没于壁纸纹样。 反复试验才将色彩淬炼成博纳尔的灰尘灰与砖粉红，以及维亚尔的惊奇聚光灯。乳白色的机智改造了街角、桥上车流、厨房[720]乃至中产客厅，而庭院设计[721]则预见了蒙德里安式的抽象画。 沃拉尔继这些画册后又创作了二十余部图文并茂的书籍，文字时而如日本扇面般覆盖画面[722]。1939 年他因车祸殒命时，诸多著作尚未完成。作为罕见的非文学派法国人，他的创作范式将二十世纪典型的豪华书籍塑造成装帧精美的版画集，配以任意旧文。

Villon (维永)


Figure 222: 723 La Parisienne. Color aquatint by Jacques Villon, 1902
图 222：723《巴黎女郎》。雅克·维永彩色水彩蚀刻版画，1902 年
724 The poet J.-P. Dubray. Etching by Villon, 1933
724 诗人让-保罗·杜布雷。维永蚀刻版画，1933 年
Villon Ways of seeing changed totally during Jacques Villon’s half century of etching. Born near Rouen and christened Gaston Duchamp, he was the elder brother of the cubist sculptor Raymond Duchamp-Villon, and of Marcel Duchamp, who painted the Nude Descending a Staircase when he was 25 and then mocked at all art with Dada. Their notary father gave his three sons a passion to analyze and formulate, while their grandfather, an etcher, accustomed them “to smell etching acid and to listen to an aquatint ground whispering as it melts.” When he went to Paris, aged 20, Gaston changed his name to Jacques Villon because, like the poet François Villon, he “loved the freedom of an ardent life [une vie chaude].” Also like Villon the poet, the painter Villon proceeded to grasp at life as hard as he hammered at artistic form. For 15 years of drawing for comic magazines he pursued people walking and talking, instead of studying posed models. He had etched since he was 16, but he now began in earnest with color aquatints [ 723 ], whose elegant spotting and Parisian smartness recall Lautrec. In 1906 Villon retired permanently
维永雅克·维永半个世纪的蚀刻生涯彻底改变了人们的观感。这位出生于鲁昂附近的艺术家原名加斯东·杜尚，是立体派雕塑家雷蒙·杜尚-维永的兄长，也是马塞尔·杜尚的兄长——后者 25 岁时创作了《下楼的裸体》，继而以达达主义嘲弄所有艺术。 他们的公证人父亲赋予三个儿子分析与表达的热忱，而身为蚀刻师的祖父则让他们"闻惯蚀刻酸的气息，听惯软地版在熔化时低语的声响"。 二十岁赴巴黎时，加斯东改名为雅克·维永，因他如诗人弗朗索瓦·维永般"热爱炽热人生[une vie chaude]的自由"。与诗人维永相似，画家维永以锤击艺术形式的力度，同样全力攫取生命。 十五年间为漫画杂志作画时，他追逐行走交谈的人群，而非研究摆姿势的模特。十六岁起便开始蚀刻，此时他正式投身彩色凹版蚀刻[723]创作，其优雅的斑点技法与巴黎风尚令人联想到劳特累克。1906 年，维永永久退出画坛。
to the suburbs, where he and his brothers discussed cubism, helping to crystallize it during those magical farewell years of peace. Villon’s cubism rationalized the open window of the impressionists by screening it with a fishnet of crisscross lines that catches objects on contact [ 724 ]. This scheme particularly suited his needle because, as he remarked, while a pencil left him free to explore and retreat," Etching grips like a lasso, exacting precision." In his color etchings and his paintings planes began to intersect like sheets of fire, for his cubism did not renounce the excitement of color. His years of drawing people instead of models kept his intellectual logic alert to a sitter’s particularity. He said, “When a sitter reveals something, grab it. A portrait is a holdup.”
在郊区，他和兄弟们讨论立体主义，在那些和平的告别岁月里，帮助它逐渐成形。 维永的立体主义通过交错线网的筛选，为印象派敞开的窗户赋予了理性——这张网在接触瞬间便捕捉物体[724]。这种技法尤其契合他的刻刀，正如他所言："铅笔让我自由探索与退却，而蚀刻如套索般紧抓，要求绝对精准。" 在他彩色蚀刻版画与油画中，平面开始如火焰薄片般交错——他的立体主义从未摒弃色彩的激情。多年以人物而非模特为对象的素描训练，使他敏锐捕捉肖像对象的独特性。他宣称："当模特流露真情时，务必抓住瞬间。肖像画就是一场劫持。"

Matisse (马蒂斯)


In the 1890s the beginning deluge of photographic halftone illustrations made verisimilitude so cheap it also cheapened the paintings that competed with photographs in naturalistic detail. Alert painters realized that they could recapture expressiveness only by unloading the clutter of literalness. But to divest oneself of a skill is as hard as to acquire one, and the renunciation is blamed instead of praised. Matisse, who did not begin to paint until he was 20, soon started to fight his way out of the representation that he had learned in the Louvre by copying Poussin, Boucher, and Chardin. By his mid-zos this “apostle of the ugly” was shocking Paris with the violence of his fauve (wild beast) paintings, and by his even more distorted sculptures and linoleum cuts. Linoleum-the stuff that hobbyists botch-is cut with knives and gouges like wood, but coarsens all detail. Brutality of effect suited Matisse’s new course as he followed Cézanne for a figure’s unity of structure and action, van Gogh for the strokes of air that encase her, and African idols for the clash of scales giant head and tall torso on dwarf legs [ 725 ].
马蒂斯 19 世纪 90 年代，摄影半色调插图的汹涌浪潮使逼真效果变得廉价，也贬低了那些在自然主义细节上与照片竞争的绘画作品。敏锐的画家们意识到，唯有摆脱写实主义的繁琐束缚，才能重获表现力。但舍弃一项技艺与习得它同样艰难，这种舍弃反而招致非议而非赞誉。 马蒂斯二十岁才开始绘画，却很快挣脱了在卢浮宫临摹普桑、布歇和夏尔丹时习得的写实桎梏。三十岁出头，这位"丑陋的使徒"便以野兽派画作的暴力美学震撼巴黎，其扭曲变形的雕塑与油画布版画更令人瞠目。 油毡——业余爱好者常搞砸的材料——像木材一样用刀具和凿子切割，却使所有细节粗糙化。 这种粗粝效果恰与马蒂斯的新方向契合：他追随塞尚追求人物结构与动作的统一性，借鉴梵高笔下包裹人物的空气笔触，并从非洲偶像中汲取灵感——巨型头颅与修长躯干在矮小腿部上的尺度碰撞[725]。
Figure 223: 725  图 223：725
Nude in Chair. Linoleum cut by Henri Matisse, 1906
《椅子上的裸体》。亨利·马蒂斯创作的油毡版画，1906 年
Throughout his life, Matisse made prints by fits and starts. Even though the First World War did not grip him, it still interrupted his painting enough to turn him back to printmaking. By then he had learned to hide the drudgery that he always underwent to batter his way to an appearance of serenity “as comfortable as an armchair.” No one will ever know how many lithographic transfer papers he filled with drawings of a woman’s back before finally flowing the fewest lines into living thrusts and counterthrusts that equal the great Chinese and Japanese in selectiveness and surpass them in suggesting the body’s construction [ 726 ]. “Once my line, inspired by a life of its own, has shaped the light of the empty paper without spoiling its bloom of white, I stop.” In the 1920s Matisse surprised by returning to academic representation [ 727 ], though with a shorthand gained by his long efforts to simplify. Wealth and fame now freed him to concentrate on the closed world of his sensuousness, on the odalisques endlessly lolling among embroideries, and on the still lifes grouped around his own sculptures and paintings.
马蒂斯毕生断断续续地创作版画。尽管第一次世界大战并未将他卷入战火，却仍足以打断他的绘画创作，迫使他重拾版画技艺。彼时他已学会掩饰创作过程中的艰辛——他总要历经磨砺才能抵达"如扶手椅般舒适"的宁静境界。 无人知晓他究竟在多少张石版转印纸上描绘过女性背影，直至最终以最精炼的线条化作鲜活的推与反推，其取舍之精妙堪比中日韩大师，在暗示人体构造方面更胜一筹[726]。"当我的线条获得生命灵感，在不破坏纸张纯白光泽的前提下勾勒出空白纸张的光影时，我便停笔。" 1920 年代，马蒂斯令人意外地回归学院派写实风格[727]，却以经年简化技艺淬炼出的速写手法呈现。财富与声望使他得以专注于感官世界的封闭王国——那些在绣缎间慵懒徘徊的奥达丽斯克，以及围绕着他自己的雕塑与画作排列的静物群像。
He broke out of this autointoxication in his early 6os by illustrating books that forced fresh subjects on him. His first, and perhaps greatest, illustrations were his 29 etchings for Mallarmé’s poems. He always etched with his eye on the model, often brushing a rhythm of lines on the grounded copper to guide his needle. The Mallarmé contains his portrait of Baudelaire, who died two years before Matisse
他六十岁出头时，通过为书籍绘制插图摆脱了这种自我沉溺的状态，这些插图迫使他接触全新的题材。他最早也是最杰出的插画作品，当属为马拉美诗集创作的 29 幅蚀刻版画。他创作时始终注视着模型，常在打磨过的铜版上刷出线条韵律来引导刻针。马拉美诗集里收录了他为波德莱尔创作的肖像——这位诗人比马蒂斯早逝两年。



Charles Baudelaire. Photograph by Etienne Carjat, 1863
夏尔·波德莱尔。埃蒂安·卡尔贾摄，1863 年

729 Etching by Matisse in Poésies de Stéphane Mallarmé, 1932
729 马蒂斯蚀刻版画，收录于《斯蒂芬·马拉美诗集》，1932 年

was born. The artist’s adaptation of a photograph [ 728 ] reveals what he habitually extrapolated from his model, and why. By raising the eyebrows, and opening and slanting the eyes, as Raymond Duchamp-Villon had done in his cubist bust, Matisse deformed fact to disengage the truth of the poet’s vision [729]. The calculated distortion does not destroy the likeness, but interprets it. Other distortions might vary the emphasis while still preserving the central personality. For his last and most joyous book, Jazz, Matisse cut and pasted colored papers to be reproduced by stencils. His impression of lagoons [ 730 ] recalls a glimpse from an airplane into the wonders of the airscape, which he here introduced into art. Whatever may become of Matisse’s reputation, he will always be able to say with Poussin, “I neglected nothing.”
艺术家对照片的改编[728]揭示了他惯常从模特身上提炼的元素及其缘由。通过扬起眉毛、睁大并斜视双眼——正如雷蒙·杜尚-维永在立体主义半身像中所做的那样——马蒂斯扭曲了现实，从而解构了诗人视觉中的真实[729]。 这种精心设计的变形并未破坏肖像的相似性，而是对其进行了解读。其他变形手法或许能改变强调重点，同时仍保留人物的核心个性。在创作其最后一部也是最欢快的作品《爵士乐》时，马蒂斯剪贴彩色纸张，通过模板进行复制。他描绘的泻湖[730]令人联想到从飞机上俯瞰空中奇景的瞬间，而这种视角正是他引入艺术领域的创新。 无论马蒂斯的名声将如何流转，他始终能如普桑所言："我未曾遗漏任何事物。"

Picasso (毕加索)


dominates the 20th century as Dürer dominated the 16th, and for similar reasons. With technical mastery and electrifying inventiveness, each developed the styles of his time in a mass of inescapable images. Picasso has lived as long as Hokusai, moved about as restlessly, and left as staggering a multitude of works by molding life into every canvas, gutter finding, paper napkin. He has made the civilized world react through love or shock and express itself in more critical writing than any other artist has ever inspired during his lifetime. Over half of this writing is in French and English, but only a fraction is in Spanish or Catalan, Picasso’s native tongues.
毕加索主宰二十世纪，正如丢勒主宰十六世纪，其原因亦如出一辙。凭借精湛技艺与震撼人心的创造力，二人皆以层出不穷的视觉符号，塑造了各自时代的艺术风貌。 毕加索的寿命与葛饰北斋相当，足迹同样遍布四方，更将生命熔铸于每幅画布、每片街头拾得之物、每张餐巾纸上，留下令人目眩的作品群。他令文明世界或倾心或震惊，激发了比任何在世艺术家都更庞大的批判性论述。其中逾半数论述以法语和英语书写，而毕加索的母语西班牙语或加泰罗尼亚语的论述却仅占极小部分。
By mastering traditional drawing and painting while still a child, Picasso freed himself all his long life to enjoy the reckless delight of a child who builds a tower of blocks to kick it down. He summed up his skirmishes with boredom by saying “I play many instruments.” By the time he was 14 vagrancy had been built into him by his having been shifted from the poetry of his native south of Spain to the business drive of the northwest and then to the bizarre crosscurrents of the northeast. At 20 Barcelona had matured him into a Catalan, with the Catalan’s stinging language, his drastic originality, and his view out across the Pyrenees. The momentum of change next swept him northward into France, where for over 60 years he camped out at a succession of addresses as willful as the succession of his styles. When he had acquired several manners, he began to date his prints and drawings even before signing them, as though he were publishing a diary, the diary of an expatriate whose adopted country has never possessed his eye, while his native country has dissolved into a tourist vaudeville of toreros and castanets.
毕加索自幼精通传统绘画技艺，此生便得以摆脱束缚，尽享孩童般的恣意欢愉——如同搭建积木塔再将其踢倒那般纯粹。他将与无聊的较量概括为"我擅长演奏多种乐器"。 十四岁时，流浪的基因已在他体内扎根——他从故乡西班牙南部的诗意天地，被抛入西北部的商业洪流，又被卷入东北部的怪诞漩涡。 二十岁时，巴塞罗那将他淬炼成加泰罗尼亚人——拥有加泰罗尼亚人尖锐的语言、激进的原创精神，以及纵览比利牛斯山脉的视野。变革的浪潮随后将他推向北方的法国，六十余载间，他辗转栖居于诸多居所，其住所更迭之随意，恰如其艺术风格的层层迭变。 当他掌握了多种艺术手法后，竟在签名之前便为版画与素描标注日期，仿佛在出版一部日记——一部流亡者的日记。在他眼中，这片他选择的土地从未真正属于自己，而故土早已消融成斗牛士与响板交织的旅游杂耍。
At 26 he broke irrevocably with the past when he and Braque, “like two mountain climbers roped together,” explored beyond Cézanne’s reduction of forms to the cube, cylinder, and cone to assemble these shapes as though they were partly transparent and partly turned upward, downward, or sideways. Only Picasso had the power and the humanity to join irreconcilables by juggling this solid geometry into recognizable portraits of individuals [ 731 ]. He and Braque analyzed banal objects familiar enough to recognize in fragments: bottle, pipe, newspaper, guitar, cigar, with lettering indicating planes and identifying objects. They enjoyed the play of wit engendered by turning their subtlest distorting glasses onto the stuffiest mid-dle-class trumpery.
26 岁那年，他与布拉克"如同两名用绳索相连的登山者"，在塞尚将形式简化为立方体、圆柱体和圆锥体的基础上继续探索，将这些形状组合得仿佛部分透明，部分向上、向下或向侧面倾斜，从此与过去彻底决裂。 唯有毕加索兼具力量与人文关怀，能将不可调和的元素融合——他将这种立体几何变幻为可辨识的人物肖像[731]。他和布拉克剖析着寻常物件的碎片：酒瓶、烟斗、报纸、吉他、雪茄，用标注平面与物体的字母进行分析。他们乐于将最微妙的变形透镜对准最陈腐的中产阶级小玩意儿，从中榨取机智的戏谑。
After Picasso had discovered in cubism a world that no one had suspected, he derived his later transformations of actuality from past styles such as Romanesque painting, Pompeian frescoes, and African, Iberian, or Cycladic sculpture. He developed their implications into manners that delight and surprise but should not disconcert any museum-goer who has really looked. Even more than Cézanne, Picasso could call his works “reminiscences of museums.” As he explored new manners he did not drop old ones, any more than a musician would abandon the piano just because he later mastered the violin. As his work stretched into decades, his com-
毕加索在立体主义中发现了一个无人知晓的世界后，他从罗马式绘画、庞贝壁画以及非洲、伊比利亚或基克拉泽斯群岛的雕塑等过往艺术形式中汲取养分，进而对现实进行再造。他将这些艺术形式的内涵转化为令人惊喜的艺术手法，但对真正懂得观赏的博物馆访客而言，这些作品并不令人困惑。比起塞尚，毕加索更可称其作品为"博物馆的回忆"。 探索新技法时，他并未舍弃旧技法，正如音乐家不会因精通小提琴就放弃钢琴。随着创作跨越数十年，他的——
pulsion to change became a pattern of return that alternated manners in the same week, ultimately in the same morning. Rembrandt also varied his attack from etching to etching, and Shakespeare modified his syntax and vocabulary to suit the theme of each play. But while Rembrandt deduced his different treatments from the nature of his various subjects, Picasso would draw a bull or a bowl of fruit in such an arbitrary variety of ways that it looked as though he had few subjects to choose from. Actually, he lived in a whole gallery of obsessions-the mountebank’s family and the blind beggar, the littered table, jazz musicians, massive girls and husky boys, the bull and the man-bull, the artist and his work, his own children and their assorted mothers, or himself as an imp quizzing Rembrandt and Velázquez. One theme ran through from beginning to end-woman, either as man’s submissive
改变的冲动最终演变成一种循环模式，在同一周内、甚至同一个早晨里交替呈现不同的风格。伦勃朗也会在不同蚀刻版画中变换技法，莎士比亚则根据每部戏剧的主题调整句法与词汇。但伦勃朗的变换源于不同主题的本质需求，毕加索却以如此随意多变的方式描绘公牛或水果碗，仿佛他可供选择的主题寥寥无几。 实际上，他栖身于整座痴迷的画廊——江湖术士家族与盲乞丐、杂乱的餐桌、爵士乐手、丰腴的女孩与粗壮的男孩、公牛与人牛、艺术家与作品、自己的孩子与她们各异的母亲，或是化身小恶魔质问伦勃朗与委拉斯开兹的自己。贯穿始终的主题唯有女性，或作为顺从的妻子，或作为叛逆的情人。

comforter, or, if demanding, as a biting, clawing monster. When he was 23 and poor, she was a tender El Greco Madonna and his refuge should he suffer the worst that a painter can suffer-blindness [732]. She becomes the enigma of elegance when he has captured the world’s attention [733]. In his middle age she is the dream of desire to the rough faun-the Minotaur’s cousin-who unveils her in the
当他 23 岁穷困潦倒时，她如温柔的埃尔·格列柯圣母，是他避难所——倘若遭遇画家最惨痛的厄运：失明[732]。当他赢得世人瞩目时[733]，她化作优雅的谜题。 中年时，她化作粗犷牧神——那牛头怪的表亲——渴求的梦境，在

troubled moonlight of a Goyesque aquatint [ 734 ]. Drawn in lines as pure as those engraved on Etruscan bronze [109], she lies in antique nudity beside Jove-Picasso turned sculptor [ 735 ]. In a division of light like an Italian chiaroscuro woodcut [ 492 ], some Andean girl’s doll inflates into a pinheaded dinosaur that could pluck stars as easily as flowers [ 736 ].
忧郁的月光如戈雅式水彩蚀刻版画[734]。她以纯粹如伊特鲁里亚青铜雕刻的线条[109]被勾勒，赤裸身躯横卧于化身雕塑家的宙斯-毕加索身旁[735]。 在如意大利明暗对比木刻般的光影分割中[492]，某安第斯少女的玩偶膨胀成头如针尖的恐龙，摘星如采花般轻而易举[736]。

So adventurous a lover as Picasso naturally liked printmaking for the gamble of the outcome and for its leaving a record of each state or transformation as a possible start for a new work on another stone or copper-or perhaps a new canvas or sculpture. Instead of the usual modifying to perfect a print toward a preconceived ideal, Picasso replaced one image with another that was not necessarily better, but was at least different [ 737, 738]. Though he upset the grand manner of Delacroix or Velázquez as cavalierly as anything of his own, Picasso could not help admiring their construction, elaborated by a slugging patience that he could not stomach for himself. (He attacked his Guernica in such eager disorder that he finished it while basic inspirations were still coming in, too late to incorporate.)
毕加索这般冒险的艺术家，自然钟情于版画创作——既因其结果充满未知变数，又因它能记录每个阶段或形态的转变，这些记录可能成为在另一块石版或铜版上创作新作品的起点，抑或催生新的画布或雕塑。他并未像常人那样通过反复修改使版画趋近预设的理想状态，而是用另一幅画面取代原有画面，新画面未必更优，但至少与众不同[737,738]。 尽管毕加索颠覆德拉克罗瓦或委拉斯开兹的宏大风格时，其肆意妄为程度不亚于对待自身作品，但他仍由衷钦佩那些大师以超乎常人的耐心精心构筑的画面——这种耐心是他自己无法忍受的。（他创作《格尔尼卡》时如此急切而混乱，以致在基本灵感仍在涌现时就完成了作品，错失了融入新意的时机。）
A man so lacking in the ordinary printmaker’s patience could achieve prints only when he found technicians to take on the methodical drudgery. In 1958 he wearied of the delays in sending etchings and lithographs from the south of France to Paris for proving, and so began to cut some of his boldest and most expressive prints in linoleum [ 736 ] simply because a neighbor could prove the blocks overnight. In the rationed postwar winter of 1945/46 he left his icy studio to work for four months in Mourlot’s heated lithographic pressroom. This sharing of work with assistants
一位如此缺乏普通版画家耐心的人，唯有找到技术人员承担繁琐的机械性工作时，才能完成版画创作。1958 年，他厌倦了将蚀刻版画和石版画从法国南部寄往巴黎试印的漫长等待，于是开始用油毡板雕刻出他最大胆、最具表现力的版画[736]——仅仅因为邻居能在一夜之间完成试印。 在物资短缺的 1945/46 年战后寒冬，他离开冰冷的工作室，前往穆尔洛的石版印刷车间工作四个月。这种与助手分工协作的模式——
Figure 224: 737 Women of Algiers. Zinc lithograph by Picasso after Delacroix, 1955. First variation
图 224：《阿尔及尔的 737 名妇女》。毕加索根据德拉克罗瓦原作创作的锌版石版画，1955 年。第一变体版。
may be what made Picasso shy of depicting his family in prints, as he did in the paintings that he worked on in solitude.
这或许正是毕加索不愿在版画中描绘家人，却在独自创作的油画中如此表现的原因。
Whether feeling tender, truculent, impish, or tragic, Picasso strikes us with as “primitive” a shock of joy as the Altamira cave painter and the carver of an African mask, who assault us so directly because they worked for the demons rustling in their thatch and flickering in the fire that cooked their supper. Picasso had indeed deeper affinities with African sculptors than any non-African artist. In Africa the violence of man’s energy never took the leap into intellectuality, be it into science, architecture, or the mere writing of words. No records of history, no plans for the future mitigated the helpless passing of the moment. Thus compressed into the now of his body, a force like implosion drove the African sculptor to evade his anxieties by remodeling his features with a visceral compulsion not found anywhere else. Picasso, indifferent to landscape, blind to architecture, and ignoring theories, invented fewer schemes to suggest the human body than the sum of all African sculptors but still contrived more innovations than any other single artist. And, again like the African, he exploited each discovery in busywork series.
无论是温柔、倔强、顽皮还是悲怆，毕加索都像阿尔塔米拉洞穴画家和非洲面具雕刻者那样，以"原始"的喜悦震撼着我们——他们之所以能如此直击心灵，是因为他们为那些在茅草屋里窸窣作响、在烹煮晚餐的火光中闪烁的妖魔而创作。毕加索与非洲雕塑家的精神共鸣，确实比任何非非洲艺术家都更为深厚。 在非洲，人类能量的暴力从未跃升为智性表达——无论是科学、建筑还是文字书写。没有历史记录，没有未来规划能缓解当下无助的消逝。这种被压缩在身体当下的力量，如同内爆般驱使非洲雕塑家以别处罕见的本能冲动重塑面容，借此逃避焦虑。 毕加索漠视风景，无视建筑，藐视理论，其构思人体的方案远少于所有非洲雕塑家的总和，却仍比任何其他单一艺术家创造了更多革新。而他同样效仿非洲艺术家，将每项发现转化为繁复的系列创作。
Picasso shows us ourselves in the free and lonely roles into which he transformed
毕加索向我们展现了我们自身——那些被他转化为自由而孤独的角色。

himself. From the supple circus performer camping in vacant lots with his girl and their child he became the brilliant harlequin in the commedia dell’ arte [ 739 ]. He revealed his inmost life of work in the sculptor fondling his mistress while he reconsiders his carving [ 735 ], and in the frowzy painter drawing, not what he sees, but what he wants to make us see through the fiction that convinces of the truth [740]. In inner anguish, he is both the slayer and the slain, knotted in the struggle of the picador lancing the bull who gores the picador’s horse [ 741 ]. Picasso then split this triple image into the man-horse or centaur, and the man-bull, or Minotaur, who overwhelms a woman with the cataract of his muscles as the picador overwhelmed him when he was all bull.
他自己。从那个带着女友和孩子在空地露营的柔韧马戏演员，他蜕变为即兴喜剧中的璀璨丑角[739]。 他将内心最深处的工作状态，刻画在雕塑家抚摸情人时重新审视雕刻的瞬间[735]，也呈现在邋遢画家笔下——他并非描绘所见，而是通过虚构的真实，让我们看见他想让我们看见的[740]。 在内心煎熬中，他既是屠夫亦是牺牲品，在斗牛士刺穿公牛与公牛刺穿斗牛士战马的搏斗中纠缠不清[741]。毕加索随后将这三重意象拆解为半人马（人马体）与半人牛（牛人体）——后者以肌肉瀑布般的姿态压倒女子，正如斗牛士当年将纯粹的公牛压制在地。
Picasso has described how art invades actuality. “A glimpse of two people generates the sensation for a painting; then little by little their presence blurs; they become a fiction, and then disappear, or rather, are transformed into all kinds of problems. They are no longer two people, but forms and colors that prolong the tremor of their lives.”
毕加索曾描述艺术如何侵入现实："两个人的一瞥便催生出绘画的灵感；随后他们的存在逐渐模糊；化作虚构，继而消逝——或者说，转化为种种问题。他们不再是两个人，而是延续生命颤动的形式与色彩。"

The expressionists (表现主义者)


From about 1900 to 1950 German art was hagridden by the foreboding and the aftermath of national catastrophes. Anxiety drove artists from villages to group and regroup themselves at Cologne, Dresden, Weimar, Munich, and Berlin, scattered in a land that has always lacked a political and intellectual center. In ignorance and contempt of the outer world, these young artists twisted things into the shape of their introspection, deforming individuals into the imagined types of the Worker, the Sufferer. They created for the proletariat, who ignored them, while despising the middle class, who bought their works, exhibited them, and for them organized the pioneer museum of contemporary art in 1919. The Italianate restraint of balance, imposed by Dürer 400 years before, was at last broken by the examples of Matisse, Delaunay, Gauguin, and Munch. Even while Cézanne was leading young French painters to analyze shapes, Munch dominated young Germans by the ache of his introspection, his sexual pain, his withdrawn portraits, and by his revival of the color woodcut as a plank boldly gouged by the designer himself. Munch’s color and Matisse’s flared when blown by the German emotionalism of Corinth and Kokoschka. Corinth expressed his ever intenser anguish in paintings, and even more in prints, that finally match Grünewald’s halluci-
表现主义者从 1900 年至 1950 年间，德国艺术始终笼罩在民族灾难的阴影与余波之下。焦虑驱使艺术家们从乡村聚集到科隆、德累斯顿、魏玛、慕尼黑和柏林，在缺乏政治与思想中心的土地上四散游走。 这些年轻艺术家对外部世界既无知又轻蔑，将万物扭曲成自我内省的形态，将个体变形为"工人"、"受难者"等想象中的类型。他们为无视他们的无产阶级创作，却鄙夷购买其作品、举办展览并于 1919 年为他们筹建先锋派当代艺术博物馆的中产阶级。 马蒂斯、德劳内、高更和蒙克的作品，终于打破了 400 年前丢勒强加的意大利式平衡克制。 当塞尚引领法国青年画家剖析形体时，蒙克却以内省的痛楚、性苦闷、疏离的肖像，以及将彩色木刻重塑为设计师亲手凿刻的木板画，主宰着德国青年艺术家。 当蒙克的色彩与马蒂斯的绚烂被德国柯林斯与柯克施卡的情感主义之风吹拂时，更显璀璨。柯林斯在画作中倾注愈发深沉的苦闷，其版画作品尤甚，最终与格吕内瓦尔德的幻觉艺术相媲美——
742 Crucifixion. Lithograph by Lovis Corinth, about 1920
742 绞刑。洛维斯·科林斯石版画，约 1920 年
743 Walter Hasenclever. Lithograph by Oskar Kokoschka, 1918
743 沃尔特·哈森克莱弗。奥斯卡·科科施卡石版画，1918 年


nations in their desperation [742]. The more operatic abandon of the Austrian baroque reappeared in Kokoschka, who was run out of Vienna as “degenerate” when he was only 22. After 1904 he traveled widely, painting and lithographing obsessive and shaken portraits [ 743 ] and riotous landscapes.
各国在绝望中[742]。奥地利巴洛克那种更具歌剧式放纵的特质在科科施卡身上重现——他年仅 22 岁便因被斥为"堕落艺术家"而遭维也纳驱逐。1904 年后他四处游历，创作着充满执念与震颤的肖像画[743]与狂放不羁的风景画。
The first closely organized German artists’ group, Die Brücke (The Bridge) formed itself at Dresden in 1905 around Kirchner, who was then 25. At 18 he had started making woodcuts after seeing Dürer’s and then turned to architecture and painting. In a vacant store he and his young friends painted, drew, and cut woodblocks with a visionary fever that for seven or eight years fused their personalities into a common style like that in a medieval guild shop. They authenticated their sincerity by “Gothic” slashing in woodcuts that were even more fractured than their paintings [ 744 ]. But since an artist can feel sincere without convincing others, the bulk of expressionist art registers as a routine of agony as automatic as the 18th-century routine of charm. In 1906 the Bridge group was visited by Nolde, an intractable North Sea peasant some 15 years older than the others, with a longer experience in drawing, carving, and painting. The ecstasy of the younger men broke through into Nolde’s stubbornness to release his deepest powers. Seawater surged through his veins when he etched tugs buffeting the chop of squalls [ 7.45 ]. Gauguin inspired him with a longing to escape from cities into the supposed purity
德国首个组织严密的艺术家团体"桥社"于 1905 年在德累斯顿成立，核心成员是当时 25 岁的基尔希纳。18 岁那年，他受丢勒作品启发开始创作木刻版画，随后转向建筑与绘画领域。 在空置的店铺里，他和年轻伙伴们以狂热的艺术激情进行绘画、素描和木版雕刻，七八年间他们的个性在这种共同创作中熔铸成统一风格，宛如中世纪行会作坊的集体创作。他们通过木刻中"哥特式"的凌厉刻痕来证明真诚——这些刻痕甚至比他们的绘画更显支离破碎[744]。 然而艺术家的真诚未必能打动他人，表现主义艺术的多数作品，终究沦为痛苦的机械化表达——如同十八世纪魅力的机械化生产。1906 年，年长其他成员约十五岁的诺尔德造访桥社。这位顽固的北海农夫在素描、雕刻与绘画领域拥有更深厚的积淀。 年轻人的狂热冲破了诺尔德固执的防线，释放出他深藏的力量。当他刻画拖船在暴风骤雨中颠簸前行时，海水仿佛在血管里奔涌[7.45]。高更激发了他逃离城市的渴望，向往着传说中的纯净之地。

The expressionists  表现主义者
746
Saint of the Inner Light. Color lithograph by Paul Klee, 1921
内光圣者。保罗·克利彩色平版画，1921 年
of primitive peoples, a longing that Nolde satisfied in 1913 by crossing Russia to the German colonies in the South Pacific. After the Bridge group broke up in 1913, some of its members regrouped in Berlin around the periodical Der Sturm (The Tempest), which published their work from 1910 to 32.
对原始民族的向往，诺尔德于 1913 年横越俄罗斯前往南太平洋的德国殖民地时实现了这一渴望。1913 年"桥派"解散后，部分成员在柏林围绕期刊《风暴》重新集结，该刊物从 1910 年至 1932 年持续发表他们的作品。
From 1919 to 32 several young German artists taught at the Bauhaus in Weimar, where they contributed little compared to the school’s far-reaching innovations in architecture, furniture, and typography. But the school’s spirit of innovation certainly stimulated a Swiss member of the teaching staff, Paul Klee, as he explored and subtly readjusted the drawings of children and the insane to unveil a world of endless unexpectedness [ 746 ]. Theoretical, like almost all Germanic artists, Klee modernized the emblem [ 221 ]-the unit of picture plus caption-as images “pushed themselves” upon his waiting watchfulness along with the titles that clue us into his secret wit. Perhaps because Klee was Swiss, he escaped the expressionists’ slavery to hatred. The German artists had heroism thrust upon them by the torment of two vast defeats and a dictatorship that exiled the lucky ones and suppressed and killed the rest.
1919 至 1932 年间，数位年轻的德国艺术家曾在魏玛包豪斯任教，相较于该校在建筑、家具和排版设计领域的深远革新，他们的贡献显得微不足道。 但包豪斯的创新精神无疑激发了瑞士教师保罗·克利的创作灵感，他通过探索并微妙调整儿童与精神病患者的绘画，揭示了一个充满无限意外的世界[746]。 与几乎所有日耳曼艺术家一样，克利以理论化手法革新了图标[221]——即图像加标题的组合形式。当画面"主动涌现"于他凝神的等待中，那些标题便如线索般揭示其隐秘的机智。或许正因瑞士血统，克利得以摆脱表现主义者对仇恨的奴役。 德国艺术家们被迫背负英雄主义，源于两次惨败的折磨与独裁统治——它放逐了幸运者，压制并屠杀了其余人。

The American scene (美国社会景象)


After Whistler’s death in 1903 North American etching followed his lead for a generation. Though, as usual, painters did lively work as a sideline [ 747 ], specialist etchers flooded the market with a dependable product that was bought-even subscribed to sight unseen-by collectors in the United States and England who were lured by the rise in price of Whistler’s prints. This industry collapsed when the market for etchings disappeared in the financial crash of 1929. Many American artists then lost their livelihood, or perhaps, as the painter John Sloan put it in 1933, “Artists have always been in a depression. It’s just that other people have joined us now.”
惠斯勒 1903 年逝世后，北美蚀刻艺术界整整一代人都追随他的脚步。尽管画家们照例将蚀刻作为副业进行创作[747]，专业蚀刻师们仍以稳定的产品充斥市场——这些作品被美国和英国的收藏家们争相购买，甚至在未见实物的情况下就预订订购，他们被惠斯勒版画价格的上涨所吸引。 1929 年金融危机导致蚀刻版画市场崩溃，这一产业随之瓦解。众多美国艺术家因此失去生计，或许正如画家约翰·斯隆 1933 年所言："艺术家始终处于萧条状态，只不过如今其他人也加入了我们的行列。"
In 1931 a committee of New Yorkers, and then the state legislature, began to pay artists to decorate public buildings. The Treasury in 1933 and the Congress in 1935 enlarged this start in the first great test of John Maynard Keynes’ economic theories by voting federal funds for creating jobs “to help men keep their chins up and their hands in.” The pioneer relief agencies for artists coalesced in the Works Projects Administration (WPA), which was soon financing some 350 centers in 44 states where over 5000 artists could count on subsistence pay and free materials of all kinds. Many printmakers profited by the chance to experiment without fear of
1931 年，纽约市民组成的委员会及州议会开始资助艺术家装饰公共建筑。1933 年财政部与 1935 年国会通过拨款创造就业岗位，将这项计划扩大为约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯经济理论的首次重大实践，旨在"帮助人们昂首挺胸，双手不闲置"。 艺术家救济先驱机构最终整合为公共工程管理局（WPA），该机构迅速在 44 个州资助约 350 个艺术中心，为逾 5000 名艺术家提供基本生活补贴及各类免费材料。众多版画家借此机会得以无忧尝试创新——
Figure 228: 747 The Lonely House. Etching by Edward Hopper, 1922
图 228：747《孤独的房子》。爱德华·霍普蚀刻版画，1922 年
The American scene  美国社会景象

748

Laisser-faire. Silk-screen print by Ben Shahn, about 1950
放任主义。本·夏恩丝网版画，约 1950 年

749

Abstraction 1947. Engraving and texture etching by Stanley William Hayter, 1946
《抽象》1947 年。斯坦利·威廉·海特 1946 年创作的雕刻与纹理蚀刻作品。
cost and to make pictures of social protest in quantities ( 11,285 were printed in generous editions) that no free market could have absorbed. Some printmakers continued to etch, more turned to lithography, and still others tried silk screen [ 748 ], which had recently been taken up by artists in New York. This most versatile form of stencil printing, patented in England in 1907 and widely used for commercial posters since the 1920s, prints colors more simply than any other process. Germans call it “sieve printing.” Silk gauze, stretched on a frame, is varnished wherever whites are to result. When a paste of pigment is scraped across the silk, the color is held back where the varnish has sealed the weave, and seeps through everywhere else onto the paper beneath. Each color is added through a separate screen.
成本，并以自由市场无法消化的大量（11,285 幅作品以宽裕的印数印制）制作社会抗议画作。 部分版画家继续使用蚀刻技法，更多人转向平版印刷，还有些人尝试丝网印刷[748]——这种技法刚被纽约艺术家们采用。这种最灵活的模板印刷法于 1907 年在英国获得专利，自 1920 年代起广泛用于商业海报，其色彩呈现比任何工艺都更为简便。 德国人称之为"筛网印刷"。将丝绸纱布绷在框架上，在需要呈现白色的区域涂上清漆。当颜料浆料刮过丝网时，清漆密封的网孔阻挡颜料，其余颜料则渗入下方纸张。每种颜色都通过单独的网版添加。
The WPA’s swoopstake rescue naturally gathered up some amateurs and wouldbe artists, thus contributing to the subsequent anomaly that while scientists are required to study more and more, a few “artists” manage to make a brief effect with less and less preparation. Although the WPA produced much heavy-handed clumsiness, soured by the gloom of the depression, it built up a tidal wave of printmaking and technical experiment that swept on past 1941, the year when Congress stopped the funds. At this opportune moment the helter-skelter enthusiasm found a direction when S. W. Hayter came from Paris to the United States for most of the 1940s, bringing the free copperplate engraving that Paris had started in the 1920 s. Instead of the old laborious conventions evolved for copying oil paintings, the graver now got its head to explore. Hayter started from the doodles called “strikes” [172] that writing masters used to swirl with all the relish-and absence of pas-sion-of a skater cutting a figure 8 on ice. Hayter charged these empty loops with violence and printed them by combining and inventing techniques-no matter how farfetched or homegrown-and by mixing colors with a skill learned from his early training in chemistry [749]. While he did not teach, his endless ingenuity and his eloquent force magnetized mature artists around him and inspired them to experiment. His impact on American printmaking-the first generative push since Whistler-resulted in the spreading of American art through prints rather than through paintings.
WPA 的大规模抢救行动自然吸纳了不少业余爱好者和准艺术家，由此催生了后续的异常现象：科学家们需要钻研得越来越深，而少数"艺术家"却能以越来越少的准备工作博得短暂的轰动效应。 尽管 WPA 项目充斥着笨拙粗糙之作，更因经济萧条的阴霾而黯然失色，但它掀起的版画创作与技术实验浪潮却持续涌动，直至 1941 年国会中止拨款后仍未停息。 值此关键时刻，当 S·W·海特尔于 1940 年代从巴黎赴美，带来二十年代巴黎兴起的自由铜版雕刻技法，这股狂热的创作激情终于找到了方向。雕刻师摒弃了临摹油画时繁琐的传统规范，开始自由探索。海特尔从被称为"试刻"的涂鸦出发 [172]——即书法大师们以溜冰者划出冰上 8 字般的兴致盎然却毫无激情的挥洒。海特赋予这些空灵曲线以暴力张力，通过结合与发明各种技法（无论多么牵强或本土化）以及运用早期化学训练[749]习得的调色技巧进行印刷。 虽未传授技艺，他无穷的创造力与雄辩的力量却如磁石般吸引着周围的成熟艺术家，激发他们进行实验。他对美国版画艺术的影响——自惠斯勒以来首次具有开创性的推动——促使美国艺术通过版画而非绘画得以传播。

The world within (内在世界)


The photomechanical processes that developed from the 1840 s to the gos rerouted printmaking by ruining the bulk of printmakers, those who had lived by engraving reproductions of other men’s pictures of famous faces, views, scientific specimens, and other facts. To survive, printmakers had to turn from what they saw to how they saw, the rare birthright of personality. (African carvers similarly changed functions when they ceased to make equipment as useful as X-ray tubes for detecting the unseen and fighting sickness and began instead to tempt tourists with curios. The new African souvenir can be as skillfully made as
1840 年代至 19 世纪末发展起来的光学机械工艺，通过摧毁大批以复制他人作品为生的版画家——那些靠刻印名人肖像、风景画、科学标本及其他纪实作品谋生的人——从而重塑了版画艺术。 为求生存，版画家不得不从"所见之物"转向"观察方式"——这恰是人格特质的珍贵天赋。（非洲雕刻师同样经历了职能转变：当他们不再制作如 X 光管般探测隐疾的实用器具，转而用奇珍异宝吸引游客时，新生代非洲纪念品的精巧程度可与前者比肩。）

750 Color lithograph by Wassily Kandinsky in Kleine Welten, Berlin, 1922
瓦西里·康定斯基的 750 色石版画，出自《小世界》，柏林，1922 年
751 Silk-screen print by Jackson Pollock, 1951
751 杰克逊·波洛克丝网版画，1951 年
the old magical mask, but it is cut off from the vitality of service to a higher power. Among us, no painter has for centuries sat down to his easel with a prayer, as Cennini recommended around 1400.) The Russian painter Malevitch said, “Old works of art do not reveal their value as art until life has left them for other aims, but new works of art begin by being art without practical usefulness.”
那古老的魔力面具，却已断绝了为更高力量服务的生命力。在我们之中，几个世纪以来再没有画家像切尼尼在 1400 年左右建议的那样，带着祈祷坐到画架前。（俄罗斯画家马列维奇曾说：“古老的艺术作品只有在生命离开它们去追求其他目标时，才会显露出其作为艺术的价值；而新的艺术作品则从一开始就是没有实用价值的艺术。”）
Art began the final abandonment of practical use in 1913 when Malevitch’s friend Kandinsky entered his Munich studio one evening at dusk to be astonished by the shapes and colors on a canvas propped against the wall. A second look showed him that it was a half-finished canvas of his own, unrecognized on its side. Such a double glimpse happens to all of us, but Kandinsky pressed his surprise for its implications: “I realized that objects interfered with my painting. An abyss opened before me. What should replace the object? I saw the danger of decorative painting, and shrank from the fiction of stylized form.”
1913 年，当马列维奇的朋友康定斯基在暮色中走进慕尼黑工作室时，被倚在墙边的画布上那些形状与色彩震撼了——艺术由此开启了对实用功能的最终背离。 再看时才认出那是自己半途而废的画作，侧卧时竟令人难以辨识。这种双重视觉体验人人皆有，但康定斯基却深究其中启示："我意识到物体干扰了我的绘画。深渊在我眼前敞开。何物能取代物体？我洞见装饰性绘画的危险，并畏惧风格化形式的虚妄。"
To jettison the object may have been less hard for a Russian than for western Europeans, who have concentrated since Giotto on organizing appearances. Byzantium, on the other hand, permanently directed the Russian toward states of soul, first expressed in hieratic formulas, then with the witness of naturalistic detail as corroborative as Tolstoy’s descriptions. Kandinsky did not aim at adding a new style but at vaporizing all representational styles the way the new physics was then vaporizing the world’s solidity. In 1922 he expressed states of emotion without depicting objects in the first abstract prints, which he called Small Worlds [750].
对俄罗斯人而言，抛弃物象或许比西欧人更容易——后者自乔托以来便专注于组织表象。而拜占庭则始终引导俄罗斯人关注灵魂状态，最初通过神圣公式表达，继而借助自然主义细节的佐证，其确证力堪比托尔斯泰的描写。 康定斯基的目标并非创造新风格，而是要消解所有具象表现形式——正如当时的新物理学正瓦解世界的实体性。1922 年，他在首批抽象版画《小世界》[750]中，通过不描绘物体的方式表达情感状态。
To organize these shapes and colors required traditional training, but in the next step, when the artist tracks the path of a gesture [ 751 ], he has withdrawn into the dead center of instinct, where everyone becomes more or less alike. (Our skulls look more mass-produced than our colored eyes and hair.) Unable to penetrate deeper into the engulfment of personality, artists then fled from all personality with found objects [ 752 ] or imitations of machine tooling. All these innovations break equally with the past, for none requires the artist to submit to a discipline as rigid as a ballet class in the hope of eventually infusing some strain of his own into a revered tradition. We may have to wait until the end of our age of fossil fuels to see just where the new vision will lead, but it clearly will change art as totally as the Western Christians did when they flattened and wasted classical form.
要组织这些形状和色彩需要传统训练，但在下一步，当艺术家追踪一个手势的轨迹[751]时，他已退缩到本能的死寂中心，在那里人人都变得大同小异。 （相较于彩色眼眸与发色，我们的颅骨更似批量生产。）当艺术家无法更深地穿透吞噬个性的洪流时，便转而逃离所有个性，投身于现成物[752]或机械加工的仿制品。这些创新同样与过去决裂——它们都不要求艺术家像芭蕾课堂般严苛地服从训练，以期最终将自身特质注入受尊崇的传统。 或许我们必须等到化石燃料时代的终结，才能看清新视野将引领何方，但它显然将彻底改变艺术——正如西方基督徒摧毁古典形式时所做的那样。
